author: skyphusion-rollins
body:
## What (#740 S4)

The `send_as` power, per Conrad's S4 rulings (RFC 5322 as designed; fail closed on the Cloudflare transport). Contract: `docs/DELEGATION.md` section 4.5.

An agent holding an active `send_as` grant names the human address as `from` on `POST /api/send`, `/send` or `POST /api/reply`:

| header | value |
|---|---|
| `From:` | the granted address, with the HUMAN's display name from their account (the caller's name is ignored) |
| `Sender:` | the agent identity's own address and display name |
| `Reply-To:` | the human (a caller `replyTo` only inside the grant, else 400) |

- **Response:** reports `from` (the human) and the new `sender` (the agent).
- **Audit:** one `delegation.send_as` row (actor = identity id, target_kind `address`, target = the address, detail `{op}`) is written BEFORE dispatch; no row, no send.
- **Drafts:** a draft send takes no caller `from`, so it goes out as the identity.
- **Without the grant:** nothing changes; a foreign `from` is overridden by the identity's own address.

**Transport capability.** `Transport.canSetSender` is new.
- `CfEmailTransport` is `false`. Cloudflare Email Sending has no `sender` field, and `Sender` is not on its header allowlist, which rejects the whole send rather than drop the header. That was measured against developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/reference/headers/, updated 2026-11-09; no live probe.
- So on the default transport a send_as send is refused `422 E_SEND_AS_UNSUPPORTED`, before the audit row and before dispatch, never downgraded. `CfEmailTransport.dispatch` also throws if a `sender` ever reaches it.
- `RelayTransport` is `true`. The relay's `OutboundMessage` gains an optional `sender`, and `renderMIME` writes it as the `Sender:` header right after `From:`, parsed and re-rendered like every address header (a malformed one is refused).
- The Cloudflare feature request is #896, assigned to `skyphusion`.

The keys are stable ids only (identity id, address), per the #854 constraint. #740 stays open for S5.

## Tests

`inbound/delegated-send-as.test.ts` (19). The rows come from `ROUTE_TABLE` `scope === "send"`: send, send-alias and reply, with drafts named as not taking a `from`.

- **Relay:**
  - no `send_as` grant (or every other power) sends as the agent with no Sender;
  - with `send_as`: From `{human, human's name}`, Sender `{agent, agent's name}`, Reply-To the human, the response `from`/`sender`, and exactly one audit row;
  - revoke goes back to the agent;
  - a caller display name never reaches From;
  - `replyTo` is only the granted address;
  - a forced audit failure dispatches nothing.
- **Controls:**
  - owner: own address with the grant held, no Sender, no row;
  - operator: the `both` token sends from the human address with no Sender and no row.
- **Cloudflare:**
  - send_as is `422 E_SEND_AS_UNSUPPORTED`, the message names Sender, nothing is dispatched, no row;
  - CONTROL: without the grant, the same request sends as the agent.

Against the base (`0de342f`, `inbound/src` stashed): 13 of 19 fail, and the 6 controls pass. With S4: 19 of 19.

`relay/sender_dispatch_test.go`:
- `renderMIME` writes Sender, writes none when it is absent, and refuses a malformed Sender;
- **end to end**: the real `/dispatch` handler, the real `SMTPTransport`, an in-process SMTP sink; the delivered message parses with `net/mail` and carries From, Sender and Reply-To exactly;
- CONTROL: the same path without `sender` puts no Sender on the wire.

With the header write removed, `TestRenderMIME_WritesSender` and `TestDispatch_SenderEndToEnd` fail and the controls pass.

Updated: the S1 test now pins that a `send_as` grant on the default transport REFUSES (422) rather than sending as the agent, and the delegations shape gains `sendAs`.

## Gates (local, as rollins; run unpiped, push chained on both exit statuses)

- inbound: typecheck exit 0; vitest 1630 tests passed
- relay: `go vet` clean; `go test -race ./...` ok
- mcp: 235 tests passed; clients/python: 126 OK; installer: 0 fail
- contract drift: 0
- dash scan: 0 hits, and a planted control fires 1
- secret scan: 0 hits; the control fires 1

author: ykaitao
body:
## Change

- Require a no-action scope preflight before reusing an idle visible thread for a different assignment.
- After a manager-confirmed re-brief, stop and replace a thread if it resumes unrelated issue/task context.
- After completing an item and sending its final report, stop and wait for an explicit manager brief before opening another issue or PR, even when older batch context lists more work.
- A later user request to the manager does not reassign an active peer until the manager relays a new scoped brief.
- Add required policy checks for these boundaries to `tests/skills-check.sh`.

## Evidence

Four scope leaks in a manager-led batch motivated these rules:

- A reused visible reviewer picked up stale, unrelated review context after a fresh assignment.
- After a manager-confirmed re-brief, a reused implementer resumed an older task; it stopped before changing files or GitHub.
- After completing a Chrome verification assignment and reporting it, a reviewer began unrelated review work without a new manager brief.
- During an active implementation, a peer began a read-only branch/worktree inventory for a manager-level cleanup request outside its issue assignment. The manager stopped it before any branch, worktree, PR, or repository mutation.

The latest incidents show that issue scope needs explicit start and end boundaries, and that only the manager can relay a new assignment. Managers still need to verify scope and agent reports; these rules do not grant an agent authority to pick its next task.

## Validation

At exact head `d0d9671e74527856177b85636518b6ac106def5b`:

- `bash tests/skills-check.sh` — passed, including the new manager-relayed reassignment check.
- `bash tests/review-event-guard-test.sh` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

author: willibrandon
body:
The net11.0 validation matrix turned up two failures that came from the tests and test harness, not from the runtime. Ankus.Testing clusters log statements slower than a second, and PostgreSQL then formats each bind parameter as text for that log line. PostgreSQL 13 can't format an interval whose hours exceed 32 bits, so the logging raised "interval out of range" and replaced the statement's own result. IntervalSignMatchesPostgresComparison hit this in the Windows x64 run against PostgreSQL 13 once its first binds took about 1.5 seconds, and an extension author's test with such a value would fail the same way whenever a statement ran slowly. Test clusters now set log_parameter_max_length = 0, so slow statements are still logged, without their parameters, and a new test forces that log line for the maximum interval. On PostgreSQL 13 it fails with 22008 without the change and passes with it.

FreshEditorLoadPreparesDependenciesAndCompilerOptions has failed both rows on Intel macOS since it was added, with net10.0 and net11.0 alike, because the stub build tool could not load its own project reference. That runner's temporary directory sits under /var/folders, which macOS reaches through the /var symbolic link. Restore records a referenced project by its real path while MSBuild loads it by the path it was given, so the referenced library never reaches the executable's deps.json. A plain SDK solution reproduces this on Linux under a symlinked TMPDIR. The test now resolves the links in its directory first; under a symlinked TMPDIR its rows failed before and pass after. Ankus extensions are libraries that run the packaged build tool, so extension builds are unaffected.

author: bpmcginley
body:
P-2.1f adds a dormant pure matcher for the approved company/field/state follow scope. It accepts bounded UTF-8 bytes for a versioned, complete recent-role snapshot, validates exact authoritative UTC coverage, and returns deduplicated roles, scope references and proposed watermark advances. Invalid, incomplete, oversized or out-of-coverage input returns no progress.

Stacked on frozen #243 at 7ffca463340a81f2dc3987a2c05d350e115a5884. Draft, needs-bruce. The internal producer contract in notes/product/P-2.1f-follow-matching.md is not a published feed. No producer, production limits, route, schema, dispatcher or live source is selected.

The caller supplies canonical catalogs, an exact expected upperBound and explicit positive byte/row/follow/match/result/text/window limits. Fatal UTF-8 decoding follows the byte check. IDs retain existing 16-character lowercase hexadecimal listing semantics. canonicalFollow validates stored scopes. Matching uses exact employer keys, OR within each field/state dimension and AND between dimensions, with first_seen strictly after max(confirmation, prior watermark) and at or before the snapshot upper bound. There is no wall-clock fallback; parsed times are reused. Coverage gaps require an authoritative wider recovery snapshot or approved operator recovery, never silent clipping.

Public role fields align with renderer #256. Posting URLs share its unsafe-character, userinfo, HTTP(S) and canonical 2,000-character checks; display facts share its 200/300/300 character ceilings. Scope references preserve overlap for consent while output roles deduplicate IDs and preserve producer order. Returned confirmation and prior-watermark guards are proposals only: future consent checks and atomic queue/progress coordination must succeed before persistence. Producer completeness, eligibility, source authenticity and catalog construction remain separate integration obligations.

- Before edits: 36 existing follow Node tests passed.
- Final: 3 focused Node tests, 378 aggregate Node tests and 22 local Workers tests in 11 files passed, including all three new matching scenarios.
- Coverage includes OR/AND/exact keys, overlapping/pending/no-match follows, exact time boundaries, repeats/gaps, leap/ambiguous/invalid dates, malformed UTF-8, duplicate IDs, unsafe or oversized links/text, explicit limits and no mutation/partial progress.
- Pinned Prettier, focused ESLint, diff and scope checks pass. The shared Node registry is untouched; Workers CI discovers the new wrapper.

Six files add 471 lines: 180 implementation, 264 tests and 27 internal note/tracker lines. Public assets/data, both goldens, producer, routes, existing follow modules, schema/migrations, dependencies and shared registry match the parent byte-for-byte. No golden refresh or UI/startup changes; changed visible strings: none. Final independent review and CI remain pending. No deployment, sending or provider requests occurred.

author: sinemacula-ben
body:
## Summary

Everything the package keeps for one request or job is bound with `scoped()`, so Laravel's queue worker and Octane forget it with the rest of the scoped state. A long-running command that does several units of work in one process can't call `forgetScopedInstances()` between them: that would also drop what Laravel or another package keeps scoped, such as the command's context and the callbacks deferred with `defer()`. laravel-iam's worker reset therefore kept its own list of this package's scoped bindings, and the list went stale whenever the package added one, as it just did with BL-77's `DecisionMemory`.

`Support\RequestState::forget($app)` now forgets exactly the scoped instances held under the package's own names: its class names, `authorization` and the `authorization.` keys (the seam defaults among them). It works out the names from what the container scopes, so it stays right as the package changes and the caller keeps no list. The package's state after boot (`PackageState`, the declarations, the binding registry) isn't scoped and is kept, as is anything another package or Laravel scopes. `RequestState::abstracts($app)` lists what it would forget. Both are `@api`, and the README describes them in the section for suite packages.

`Diagnostics\ContainerState` gains `scopedAbstracts()`, which reads the container's scoped names without building anything.

## Testing

- `tests/Unit/Support/RequestStateTest.php`: only the package's names are forgotten, and another package's scoped name, a name that merely starts with the word, and the package's own singletons are kept.
- `tests/Feature/Support/RequestStateTest.php`: in a booted application, the manager, last-decision store, resolution cache and resolved tenant are built afresh, while `PackageState` and the application's own scoped state are kept.
- `tests/Unit/Diagnostics/ContainerStateTest.php` covers `scopedAbstracts()`, including a container that isn't Laravel's.
- All three pass on PHP 8.5 and 8.3. `qlty check` (without cache) and `qlty smells` against master report no issues.

author: jagerzhang
body:
## 背景：v1.3.3-legacy / 48 在 Android 4 上无法启动

线上 legacy 通道当前指向 versionCode 48。用户实机反馈安装后打不开，已用 SDK `api-versions.xml` 与编译产物逐项定位到两个独立根因：

1. **主题资源超纲**：application 主题解析为 `@0x01030241`（`Theme.Material.Light.NoActionBar`，API 21+），Android 4 framework 无此资源，Activity 创建即中止；已验证可运行的旧低配包 38 用的是 `@0x010300f0`（Holo，API 14）。
2. **dex 含 12 个 API>14 框架类**：`JobService` / `JobInfo` / `JobParameters` / `JobScheduler` / `AudioAttributes`（21）、`NotificationChannel` / `AudioFocusRequest`（26）、`Notification$Style` / `$BigTextStyle`（16）。`GuardWatchdog extends JobService`、`MediaPauseController` 的 `AudioFocusRequest` 字段类型在**类加载阶段**就失败，运行时 `SDK_INT` 守卫来不及执行。旧低配包这个数字是 0。

修复代码在独立分支 `fix/android4-compat-r2`（`333a06e`，已推送）：以 main 为基线保留 bank-v9 / 9,544 题、三套学制进度表、手机端 25 项设置，把主题改 Holo、JobService 改纯 AlarmManager、音频焦点改 API 1 三参重载、通知去 BigTextStyle，并新增 `NotifCompat`（仅 `SDK_INT>=26` 时反射建 channel，类名不进 dex 类型池，避免 Android 8+ 前台服务通知 `Bad notification for startForeground`）。新增硬门禁 `tests/android4_compat_check.py`：构建前查源码/manifest，构建后扫成品 dex，断言 `high-api=0`。

**该分支刻意不合入 main**：低配的主题/服务/通知裁剪会改变主线行为，与既有 `release/v1.3.3-legacy` 独立低配分支的做法一致。

## 本 PR 改动（仅站点清单与文档，不含主线代码）

| 文件 | 变更 |
| --- | --- |
| `site/update.json` | legacy 通道 `versionCode 48 -> 49`，sha `1ab3b312…`、size 2,430,743、notes 改为修复说明；`publishedAt` -> 2026-11-11 |
| `site/dl/latest-legacy.apk`、`site/dl/PoHW-1.3.3-legacy.apk` | 替换为 versionCode 49 修复包 |
| `site/script.js` | v1.3.3 卡片如实描述 49 修复重发，不再宣称 48 可用 |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | v1.3.3 段落加 `###` 子条目记录根因、修法与验证；不新增 `##` 分组，保持 15 个正式 Release 口径 |

**main 通道完全未变**：versionName 1.3.3 / code 47 / minSdk 21、sha `4b67c23f…`、size 2,397,975、notes 逐字一致；`site/dl/latest-main.apk` 与 `PoHW-1.3.3.apk` 字节未变（故不在 diff 中）。URL 也保持不变，所以已装 48 的设备在线更新会看到 49 > 48 并直接覆盖安装恢复，无需卸载。

## 验证

- 待发布包独立复核：`aapt dump badging` = `versionCode 49 / versionName 1.3.3`，主题 `@0x010300f0`，dex 中 API>14 类 **0**（含内部类），与用户已拿到的测试包 sha 完全一致。
- 门禁：`UPDATE_MANIFEST_OK_STRICT`、`LAYOUT_CONTRACT_OK total=388`、`JVM_TESTS_OK total=416`；修复分支侧另跑过契约 395、变异 103/103、`android4_compat_check --apk` high-api=0。
- 真机（高版本模拟器）覆盖安装 47 -> 49：首页 `9544 题 / bank-v9 / 守护运行中`，实弹出题，`FATAL=0`。

## 边界（如实说明）

本环境**没有 Android 4 真机/镜像**，能证明的是「dex 无超纲类 + 主题与旧可跑包一致 + 包本身正常启动出题」，API 14 运行时行为仍未经实机验证。用户已明确表示无测试环境并要求直接发布，故按止血优先上线，后续如有实机反馈会继续跟进。

主线 v1.3.3 / 47 保持原状；PR #35 合入的四项后台修复（手机端全量设置、学制切换、二维码文案、文字截断）**本次不发版**，仍待 v1.3.4。

The best drivers take the biggest trucks. Every software module now tops out at a similar late price, so in the pacing bot they finish between about 4h and 7.5h. The page keeps its scroll position after those purchases.

How: GRADES and crew() in web/engine.js, a capacity bonus per assigned grade, new tests, new Pro/Veteran trophies, and show(tab, true) in web/ui.js. Older saves with higher software levels are capped to the new maximums. Also merged into v1.1-rewards.

author: xiaoba-dev
body:
## Description

When no `rotifer` binary is on PATH, the server runs a pinned `@rotifer/playground` through `npx`. The pin was 0.33.0, which predates running Wrapped genes in the sandbox (0.36.0) and the fixes in 0.36.1. This raises `PLAYGROUND_FALLBACK_SPEC` to `@rotifer/playground@0.36.1`.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (existing functionality changes)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] Other:

## Verification

A new unit test in `tests/unit/local-ops.test.ts` requires the pin to be at least 0.36.1. It fails with the old value 0.33.0, and also with 0.35.9 and 0.36.0. It passes with 0.36.1, 0.37.0 and 1.0.0.

`npm run build && npm test`: 592 passed, 7 skipped, none failed.

The built server was also run over real stdio against the published 0.36.1. It ran with a temporary `HOME`, a temporary npm prefix and cache, telemetry off, and a `PATH` that had only `node`, `npx` and `npm` (`which rotifer` found nothing). So every CLI call went through the `npx` fallback, and `npx` could only use the `@rotifer/playground` copy it downloaded.

| Step | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `init_gene` (Wrapped, no genesis) | ok, 6.7 s |
| `wrap_gene hello-world` | ok, 1.8 s, phenotype fidelity `Wrapped` |
| `run_gene` before compile | ok, 1.9 s, "Running via Node.js", greeting returned |
| `compile_gene` | ok, 8.0 s, `gene.ir.wasm` written, but only because esbuild and javy leaked in (see below); with the stated `PATH` alone it fails with `E0024` (`esbuild: missing, javy: missing`) |
| `run_gene` after compile | ok, 2.1 s, "Running via WASM sandbox", greeting returned, 495 ms |

The only package in the temporary npx cache was `_npx/0eaff143fd892aec/node_modules/@rotifer/playground`, version `0.36.1`.

`run` only uses the sandbox once the gene has a `gene.ir.wasm`, so the Wrapped gene runs on Node.js until it is compiled.

**Correction after review.** `compile` also needs `esbuild` and `javy` on `PATH`; the npx fallback does not bring them. Run again in the environment described above, `compile_gene` stops with `E0024 … esbuild: missing, javy: missing`, which is what a user who relies on the fallback without the toolchain will see. My compile step only succeeded because the temporary directories were created inside a scratch folder whose `node_modules` already had `esbuild` 0.28.1 and `javy-cli` 3.0.1 from an earlier, unrelated install. The CLI looks for these tools with `npx --no-install`, which searches `node_modules` in the parent directories of the project, so it found them there; the temporary `HOME` then holds the javy 3.0.1 binary that `javy-cli` downloaded on first use. The version check is unaffected: the CLI that ran was the 0.36.1 package from the temporary npx cache. With `esbuild` and `javy` installed, review reproduced compile, the sandbox run, and the `E0026` error for a gene that imports a Node built-in, which only 0.36.1 has.

Not verified: other tools that go through the fallback (publish, arena and similar) were not run against 0.36.1.

- [x] Tests pass locally (`npm test` / `cargo test` / etc. — as applicable)
- [x] Documentation updated (if behavior or API changed): not applicable
- [x] No secrets / credentials / `.env` files committed

## Related Issues

author: agreenspan
body:
## What and why

Aron (2026-11-10): "Muse should be an assistant, and Claude Codex should be coders… We have role types for threads, and they should probably have their own instruction set… maybe you can configure your own roles and default roles." Every main thread used to get the coding executor's prompt ("Active agent: artificer…"), so his Muse thread acted as a coder when he wants it as his day-to-day assistant.

- **Thread roles are composition roles.** Built in: `coder` is the default for `claude-code` and `codex` and takes every general file. `assistant` is the default for `muse` and takes general files only from the computer-level nodes (`managed`, `global`), so repo coding rules never reach it. Users add their own with `composition.roles.<id>.thread` (`label`, `defaultFor`). There is one home and no second registry. A built-in's entry merges slot by slot, and its `thread` field by field.
- **`main` is the shared base.** Its role files compose before the thread role's at each rung, through core `HierarchyLocation.baseRoles`, a minimal extension of the hierarchy planner. `when.roles` also matches base roles. `main` itself takes only `audience`.
- **Harness follows the worker.** The fix: a Muse thread reads neither `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` nor `$CODEX_HOME/AGENTS.md`. Role and worker reach the `instructions` source through the bound `OwnershipScope` (alongside `cwd`), so a role change re-composes on the next turn.
- **`ThreadMeta.role`:** set at creation (the chosen role, else the worker's default) and changeable via `PATCH /api/threads/:id` `role` (null follows the default). A worker switch moves a thread on its old worker's default role to the new worker's. Records with no role resolve at read time, with no migration.
- **Executor `prompt` is retired.** It no longer reaches the session (the `Active agent` standing part is gone). A saved one is refused by name with the fix. Doctor reports the legacy starter before validation, and `setup --remove-legacy-defaults` reads the raw file. Setup and the viewer stop writing executor prompts.
- **Feedback** with no owning Warden goes to the thread's role. The edit form lists thread roles, `main` and the Wardens.
- **API and viewer:** `POST /api/threads` `role`. The launch view and thread payloads carry `role` and `effectiveRole`, and `/api/workers` lists `roles` plus each worker's `defaultRole`. There is a role row in the New thread and Runs on pickers, and the header pill shows the role.
- Agent ids and region ids may not take a thread role id or `main`. A Warden's audience cap is the widest of `main` and the thread roles.

Config example:
```json
"composition": { "roles": {
  "coder": { "instructions": { "exclude": ["inixiative-for-tribe"] } },
  "writer": { "thread": { "label": "Writer", "defaultFor": ["muse"] }, "instructions": { "general": ["global"] } }
} }
```

## Primitives used
- Composition roles: `instruction-settings.ts` (roles, `roleComposition`, validation) and `instruction-stack.ts` (`instructionStackSource`, `sharedRoleView`). `threadCompositionSource` reuses them, and the shared parts are factored out of `compositionSource`.
- Core hierarchy `plan()` and `matches()` gained `baseRoles`. `OwnershipScope` gained `role` and `worker`, bound by `ThreadFactory`'s scope getters.
- `ThreadMeta.worker` routes and pickers (FEAT-007, #309, #316) are the model for role.
- Feedback reuses `routing.ts`/`service.ts`. Settings refusal follows the `refuseHandNamedWardens` pattern.

## Checks
Adversarial review (Opus) found no parallel machinery. Its findings are fixed in the second commit: setup and viewer prompts, the audience cap, role on worker switch, built-in field merge, agent id collisions, when.roles base matching, and partial apply. Full check is green apart from `vcr-freshness`: local claude CLI 2.1.322 against cassettes recorded on 2.1.317, which is environmental and unrelated. The browser `run-picker` suite is green.

author: masarray
body:
## M6 architecture safety — authoritative native FX instance identity

The native CONTROL producer `projectNativeGraph` already validates the installed processor token, catalog identity, bypass and channel IDs, but did not check **duplicate FX instance tokens across two strips** or a rack exceeding eight slots. M5 JS hardening in parallel PR #561 rejects such malformed snapshots. This changes the *native producer* to fail closed before publishing them, reducing cross-side contract drift.

**Two files only:**
- `integration/ApprovedNativeV8Projection.h`: reject duplicate `instanceId` across all channels and >8 inserts/strip before authoritative snapshot mutation. Distinct inserts of the same vendor catalog remain valid (only tokens, not catalog IDs, must be unique).
- `tests/approved_native_v8_projection_test.cpp`: real JUCE projection fixtures for duplicate lease on the same strip, reused lease across MAIN/INPUT, and nine unique inserts, each checking that a rejected graph leaves the accepted snapshot byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Safety**: zero DSP or native audio callback changes; no GUI assets/repaint; no extra graph owner; validation and temporary set allocations only on CONTROL thread. Keeps existing AV8 projection ABI.

**Qualification**: fast native contracts; one exact-SHA Windows C++/CTest after fast green. Native producer is independent of JS M5 #561; reconcile current main before merging. This is M6 guardrail *slice*, not entire M6 or physical ASIO FAT.

author: obra
body:
Broad recall queries currently expand every FTS match into passages and score the entire union. Observed fresh preparations ranked roughly 95,000–113,000 candidates and issued 740–887 explicit-score requests despite needing only one semantic-search page.

Nominate up to 128 distinct admitted identities per text surface using BM25, with an independent shortlist for complete identifiers. Refill past duplicate and orphan rows, then use existing passage scoring, source/revision validation, grouping and packing. Qdrant, semantic retrieval, the context allowance and error fallback retain their existing contracts. This intentionally replaces exhaustive text nomination with a shortlist; a large source can still contain many passages.

The private native-worker evaluator also accepts an optional query so both builds can receive identical input. No production API or storage schema is added.

Validation:
- Two independent Sol code reviews accepted the repair. Real SQLite regressions failed before it and passed afterward across event, original and note surfaces, covering ordering, duplicate/orphan refill, identifier rescue and fallback.
- 91 focused recall tests, agent typecheck and commit hooks passed.
- CI passed on `9a0231da15a620a4e4ddfc1daa3bbaa4dcdbae1e`: build, lint, format, 110 protocol tests, 4,379 agent unit tests, 336 agent end-to-end tests and 14 CLI tests. Preserved local emulated failures were not represented as passing.
- A 196,574-vector paired test used identical frozen inputs, with Qdrant, the root and two native workers under a combined 2-CPU/6-GiB limit in emulated Linux. Fresh preparation fell from 32.493 to 7.859 seconds on the development question and 40.019 to 3.479 seconds on its delegation wrapper. Explicit scoring fell from 269/386 to 8/12 batches. Both completed without OOM/restarts and supplied the required original. This is one sequential pair, not a production latency estimate; the wrapper is not an independent question and other selected context changed.
- Four fresh questions over an identically expanded, frozen synthetic corpus produced correct delivered answers in 3/4 baseline and 4/4 repair cases according to both blind Sol reviewers. Persistent writes were graded separately; reviewers differed on two ancillary repair overstatements. Initial selected-evidence metadata matched within all four pairs, so the different answer outcome does not demonstrate a causal recall-quality gain.
- All eight completed sessions were interviewed in private copies; original runs and inputs remained unchanged. Both independent conclusion reviews support a guarded Reeve-only rollout. Four cases establish an observed regression check, not general quality equivalence.

Existing live-baseline HTTP 408/socket errors and one long semantic query remain unresolved. This patch's unchanged HTTP path is not a demonstrated transport repair. All runs and failures are preserved privately.

Deployed to Reeve only at Sen `f6efd47e` / Lace `1fd6ba5c` after the guarded upgrade succeeded. Installed refs, healthy core/search services and no post-deploy OOM/restarts were verified. Reeve acknowledged Slack and collected a native worker's successful `uname -s` result; root inspected the saved tool output. Root recall remains on and extraction off. The first two fresh live preparations were hybrid with partial coverage and took 54.94/23.77 seconds; semantic search accounted for 42.79/14.14 seconds, while 30/27 explicit-score batches took 1.13/1.03 seconds. Background publication HTTP 408 recurred, followed by successful publication. Two independent Sol reviews checked these bounded observations; the remaining semantic latency and transport failures are unresolved. Doctor passed runtime and credential checks but its host Git freshness check lacked noninteractive GitHub credentials; installed refs were verified independently.

author: labasubagia
body:
### Summary

- Sync processing now runs through a bounded-concurrency pool (`SYNC_CONCURRENCY=4`) instead of a serial per-conversation loop, porting g2n’s collect-then-aggregate model.
- Live, verbose progress everywhere, so the UI never looks stuck: per-conversation discovery, duplicate-check progress, and per-record upload/skip/fail updates.

### Changes Made

- `lib/sync.ts`: add `mapWithConcurrency` bounded pool (workers pure, `Promise.allSettled` — all siblings settle before any error surfaces); state mutates only via a serialized promise queue (no lost increments, live progress); fatal-auth/cancel abort handled via chained `AbortController` + drained queue on worker rejection.
- `lib/notion.ts`: `findExistingNames` accepts optional `onProgress(done, total)` callback (source×filter chunks).
- `docs/architecture.md`: document concurrent processing + progress reporting.

### Testing

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Tests passed (`npm test`) — 48/48
- [x] Typecheck passed (`npm run typecheck`)
- [x] Build passed (`npm run build`)

### Review

author: loktoto
body:
## Why
Wallet Tap and Wallet/credit-card notifications can report the same payment with different merchant/card/source IDs. Requested behavior: when an existing transaction has the same signed numeric amount within ±180 seconds of an incoming one, skip the incoming one regardless of merchant, card, source or currency.

## Implementation
- Apply 180-second inclusive amount-only check before appending to `transactions.json`, including batch and manual form paths. Use original event time, falling back to `createdAt` if absent.
- Canonicalize floating-point artifacts such as `663.91999999999996` to `663.92` without globally enforcing two decimal places.
- Verify only newly inserted rows, set `status=duplicate` and `shouldAppendNumbers=false` for suppressed entries, prevent a second Numbers row, track duplicate reasons in local audit.
- Maintain mirror and release VERSION/CHANGELOG/docs, add end-to-end tests.

## Known tradeoff
Different legitimate purchases with identical amounts within 180 seconds will be ignored. Currency is intentionally not part of the matching key, per requested amount-only rule. Existing ledger entries are not deleted or migrated.

## Validation
GitHub Actions offline Scriptable integration suite will validate the change on this PR. Native iPhone Scriptable execution still requires updating the installed script and testing a real Shortcut event.

author: kingdemond434-cpu
body:
Before: on the box, the expression factory crashed mid-pass (exit 1, its work for the pass lost). The index discovery organ never wrote, because the battery killed it at 150 s while it was still waiting on network routes. Ten other miners finished "ok" but left their seat folders weeks stale, so a miner that ran and found nothing looked the same as a dead one.

After: the expression factory treats a cell the campaign already holds as a duplicate instead of crashing. Index discovery fits its own 110 s budget and always writes. Every one of these miners writes a small counts-only `pass_census.json` (tried, new, duplicate, donated) into its seat on every pass. The candidate compiler reads zero rows from it, so no donation is faked.

How:
- expression_factory: its `seen` set is capped at 50k, but the campaign keeps QUEUED rows. A key that fell out of `seen` re-ran, and `advance(QUEUED->SCREENED)` raised an uncaught `CampaignError`. This was reproduced and is now pinned by a test.
- index_discovery: a new `--budget-s` flag. Request timeouts are cut to the time left, nothing starts after the deadline, and the starting route rotates hourly.
- `proposer_common.pass_census()` is wired only into legs that already write that seat. The per-leg verdicts are in `reports/box_reads/breadth_ok_but_stale_legs.md`.
- The box read's "factor_residual never runs" was a name mismatch: the leg is `residual_factors`, which has 670 runs.

author: hackjsw
body:
## What this does

Four things the Telegram side was missing, plus the one Windows build fix that made them possible to work on:

- **`/restart`** (Telegram admins, Windows desktop only): restarts the whole desktop app, backend included. A detached PowerShell helper first proves it is running under the desktop (`dsh-desktop-host\lib\index.js`, same executable, parent/child relation), arms itself with a ready file, waits for the request, re-checks the process identities, then stops the desktop and the processes it owns and starts it again. Anything that is not the Windows desktop app is refused with a short explanation instead of a half restart.
- **`/effort`**: lists the reasoning efforts the model metadata declares and switches this Session's effort — by button or by exact value — from the next model request on. It refuses when the model declares nothing, and it re-checks the Session, provider, model and previous effort before touching the live Agent, so a stale picker cannot change something else.
- **`telegramReplyButtons`** (new setting, **off by default**): hides the ⏹ Stop button on progress messages and the quick actions under finished replies on Telegram, so the chat stays plain. Menus, approvals and question choices stay; `/stop` still stops a turn. The switch is in the panel under *Messages and notifications*.
- **Bot menu merging**: `setMenu` now reads every scope and language, merges its commands with the ones other tools registered, writes only when something differs, and reads back to verify. Nothing is deleted from other scopes any more, and a list that would exceed 100 commands is reported and left untouched. The menu is also retried when a language switch or late Harness commands make the old list stale.
- **Stale button handling**: reply buttons and progress messages now belong to the line generation that asked for them, so an older chat or turn cannot clear a newer reply or progress message, and an undelivered button request is not retried forever on a dead connection.
- **Windows build**: `scripts/build.mjs` resolved the project root with `URL.pathname`, which yields `/C:/…` on Windows and makes esbuild reject it — so `pnpm install` (which runs `prepare`) failed there. It now uses `fileURLToPath`. The restart helper lives in `resources/` and is copied to `lib/` by the build, since `lib/` is generated.

## Testing

- `node scripts/build.mjs` builds the host and client bundles and copies the restart helper.
- `npx vitest run`: **266 passed, 2 failed, 3 skipped**. Both failures are existing POSIX-only tests on Windows (`validates /cwd and uses it for /new` and `/get … never outside` use `/etc/hosts` and `symlink('/etc', …)`); they fail on a clean checkout here too and are unrelated to this branch.
- New tests cover the effort picker and exact values, the restart gates and commit path (through a fake harness), the reply-button switch, and the merge/verify/limit behaviour of the menu.

## Not verified here

- I could not run `pnpm run typecheck`: `tsconfig.json` maps `@deepseek-ai/*` to a sibling `../deepseek-harness` checkout that this machine does not have (DSH is installed from an asar there). The build and tests pass, but the first real typecheck will be in an environment with that checkout — please treat any type error as mine.
- The whole-desktop restart is exercised only by unit tests against a fake harness and by reviewing the helper protocol; I have not run it end to end against a real desktop app in this branch.
- Nothing here was installed into a live profile; the packaged build was not used to drive a real bot.

author: asuresh8
body:
## What changes for an operator

Before: `hostkeeper-coordinator` had six verbs (`serve`, `backup`, `restore`, `import`, `export`, `host-groups migrate`) and `hostkeeper` had two (`daemon`, `check-repositories`). Moving a fleet from roles to host groups was one offline run of `host-groups migrate`, and `serve --rollout-file` said to run it.

After: `hostkeeper-coordinator` has `serve`, `backup`, `restore` and `export`; `hostkeeper` has `daemon`. A fleet moves from roles to groups through the operator API, with the coordinator running (docs/operations/hostgroups.md, "Moving a fleet from roles to host groups"):

1. Start this release's `serve` without `--rollout-file` (and, until the groups exist, without `--mac-serial-allowlist`). A coordinator that holds no group orders every host nothing; hosts keep running what they run.
2. `hkctl host-groups put` each group.
3. `hkctl host-groups move` each enrolled host into its group.
4. `hkctl services set-repository` / `services set-min-version` where the rollout file set them.
5. `hkctl releases set-desired --host-group <group>` per group and package; CI names `host_group`.
6. Give each Mac allowlist entry its `host_group` and start with the allowlist again.

`serve --rollout-file` now says: `--rollout-file is not read by serve: start serve without it and place hosts with the operator API: HostGroups.Put each group, HostGroups.Move each host, Services.SetRepository and Services.SetMinVersion where needed, Releases.SetDesired per group (docs/operations/hostgroups.md)`.

Unchanged: `serve` and its flags, `backup`, `restore`, `export` (and the monthly restore drill that uses it), `hostkeeper daemon` and every unit, plist and init script that runs it, the operator API, hkctl, and every on-disk and database format. `serve` on a database at release 0.1.252's schema runs migration `0009` and starts (tested below).

## Inventory of hand-run verbs

| binary | verb | called by | decision | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| hostkeeper-coordinator | `serve` | the packaged unit, the compose deployment, the privileged tests | keep | the coordinator itself |
| hostkeeper-coordinator | `backup` / `restore` | operators (docs/operations/coordinator-state.md) | keep | disaster recovery of the file store, which `serve --state-file` still supports; no API call does it |
| hostkeeper-coordinator | `export` | operators: the monthly restore drill (docs/deploy/coordinator/README.md) and the way back from the database to files | keep | a documented operating need; no API call does it |
| hostkeeper-coordinator | `host-groups migrate` | nothing but docs | **delete** | a one-off conversion of roles to groups; the operator API makes the same change, call by call |
| hostkeeper-coordinator | `import` | nothing but docs | **delete** | a one-off conversion of a file store into an empty database. The farm is already on the database |
| hostkeeper | `daemon` | systemd unit, OpenRC script, launchd plist | keep | the host daemon |
| hostkeeper | `check-repositories` | nothing but docs | **delete** | a check verb; the daemon's start already refuses a defective `/etc/hostkeeper/repositories`, naming the file, and `pxe serve` checks its directory at its own start |

Flags that act at start are not verbs and stay: `serve --ca-init` (the CA is made once, at a first start) and the hidden `serve --rollout-file`, which exists only to refuse with the text above.

Verbs of other binaries, outside the two this change covers, are listed for a follow-up and not changed here: `hostkeeper-mdm migrate` (a one-off move of the old kit's MDM stack, called by nothing but its design doc), `hostkeeper-mdm fetch/install/tls/verify/push-cert/dep`, `pxe serve` and `pxe update-hook` (run by the host daemon's hooks), `hostkeeper-measure check/run/analyze` (a development tool), and `hostkeeper-coordinator-update` (run by its systemd timer).

## Public interface changes

- `hostkeeper-coordinator host-groups migrate ...` -> removed: a usage error, exit 2.
- `hostkeeper-coordinator import ...` -> removed: a usage error, exit 2.
- `hostkeeper check-repositories [--dir DIR]` -> removed: a usage error, exit 2.
- `StartError::RolloutFileRetired`'s text: `... convert it once with hostkeeper-coordinator host-groups migrate (docs/operations/hostgroups.md)` -> the text above.
- `StartError::MigrateUnfinished` / `BackupError::MigrateUnfinished` text: `{path}: a host-groups migrate --apply stopped partway; restore the backup taken before it and run it again` -> `{path}: a host-groups migrate --apply of release 0.1.253 stopped partway; restore the backup taken before it`.
- Rust items: `hostkeeper_coordinator::migrate` (module), `config::Command::{Import, HostGroups}`, `transfer::Import`; `hostkeeper_daemon::cli::Command::CheckRepositories`, `repositories::{CheckFlags, check, report, run_check, EXIT_REFUSED}` -> removed. Crate-internal helpers that only `import` or `migrate` used are removed too: `refuse_newer`, `read_only`, `rewrite`, `counts_of`, `manifest_of`, `read_live`, `read_joined`, `MoveError`. The types are unchanged (the variants and structs are simply gone), and no format changes.

## Layer by layer

- **crates/hostkeeper-coordinator/src/config.rs, lib.rs**: the `Import` and `HostGroups` verbs and their dispatch are gone; the module docs say what is left.
- **migrate.rs, migrate_plan.rs, migrate_policy.rs, migrate_apply.rs, migrate_support.rs and their eleven test files**: deleted (about 4,800 lines).
- **transfer.rs, store/postgres/transfer.rs**: `import`, its dry-run plan, its read-back comparison and the read-only and rewrite paths `migrate` used are deleted; `export` stays as it was. `MoveError` had one variant left, a wrapper of `DatabaseError`, so `export` returns `DatabaseError`. `Moved.unread` (lines of the audit files `import` could not read) is gone with it. `export` still reads `imports.audit_pruned_before`, so a database an earlier release imported into still exports its pruned history as a sealed segment.
- **config_error.rs, backup.rs, config_state.rs**: the refusal texts above. The `.migrate-unfinished` marker is still refused by `serve` and `backup`, and `restore` and `export` still take it for state in their targets, because 0.1.253 shipped the verb and a stopped `--apply` of it may have left one (see Decisions).
- **store/postgres/tests/seed.rs, records.rs**: the export tests used to fill their databases with `import`. `seed` writes a whole state in one transaction with the store's own statement builders (`statements`, `records::writes`, the device upsert), so the tests start from the same rows. `records::writes` (a whole enrollment snapshot as rows) is now built under `#[cfg(test)]`, beside the private record statements it uses, since no coordinator path writes a whole store. The test-side `stored` reads a file store as a start reads it.
- **crates/hostkeeper-daemon/src/cli.rs, repositories.rs, crates/hostkeeper**: `check-repositories` and what only it used are gone; `Command` keeps its one verb, `daemon`, which every unit names. Callers that matched it with `let ... else` now use a plain `let`. hostkeeper's `rustix` dev-dependency, used only by the deleted test, is dropped.
- **Docs**: docs/operations/hostgroups.md (the section above replaces "Migrating from roles"), MIGRATION.md (a "Removed one-off verbs" entry), README.md, docs/operations/coordinator-state.md, docs/operations/enrollment.md, docs/operations/network-install.md, docs/deploy/coordinator/README.md, docs/enrollment-coordinator.md, docs/report/hostkeeper.html, and a "Removed" note on each design section that specified a deleted verb (docs/design/hostgroups.md section 10, coordinator-storage.md section 11, packages-repositories.md, packages-tests.md, two-programs.md).

## Compatibility and failure modes

- A unit that still names `--rollout-file` is refused at start, before any file is opened, with the text above (as in 0.1.253, with a new text).
- A script that runs a removed verb gets clap's

It says the prompt-function-boundary render must match "pre-change bytes", but `extension/src/plan-pi-spec.ts:76` ("The problem field is the issue TITLE"), `:234` ("`problem` is t… — proposed: state the fallback chain explicitly (first non-empty, non-`Descriptor:`/`Type:` paragraph of the section → the `Descriptor:` line → the title), define "the section is empty" to mean that chain yields nothing, and gate `PI_SPEC_SECTION_MAX_CHARS`/`piSpecReservation` on whether the Context path can e…** — the filed issue marks this CRITICAL point resolved

## Adversarial review — non-blocking findings

The adversarial gate passed this diff but left these unresolved. They did not
block the commit (only `CRITICAL_ISSUES_FOUND` does); they are recorded here so
they are decided deliberately rather than forgotten.

### default

I'll start by orienting on the repo state and the changed files.




Status: done investigating; verdict below.

VERDICT: MINOR_OBSERVATIONS

CRITICAL ISSUES: none

ISSUES: none

MINOR_OBSERVATIONS:

1. `descriptorProblem` takes the first non-blank line of `## Context & motivation`, so a section with no descriptor line yields whatever prose sits first — which can be a bullet of a following list rather than a statement - `extension/src/plan-pi-spec-descriptor.ts:110`
   Quote: `"  for (const raw of sectionLines(body, \"Context & motivation\")) {\n    const trimmed = raw.trim();\n    if (trimmed === \"\" || /^Type\\s*:/.test(trimmed)) continue;\n    return trimmed.startsWith(DESCRIPTOR_PREFIX)"`

   Quote: `"      if (end >= 0) {\n        i = end;\n        continue;\n      }"`

author: litlfred
body:
Companion to litlfred/cat-harness-tools#1833 (issue litlfred/cat-harness-tools#1830). FHIR IG artefact pages now declare the node they render, as the ArchiMate, OpenAPI, library and todo pages do. This is the last family.

- **Declaration:** `<main resource="<Type>-<id>" typeof="fhir:<Type>" prefix="fhir: http://hl7.org/fhir/">`, a JSON-LD stub in the head, and `rel=alternate` to the node. The page's identity moves from the private `ig-artifact-page` config block to `data-kg-*` attributes on `<main>`.
- **Renderer:** `assets/kg-render.js` (tools' generic renderer) is published beside `ig-artifact.js`. `ig-artifact.js` registers for the FHIR namespace and still reads a config block, which old pages and the artifacts/toc list pages keep.
- **IRIs:** the artefact node `@id` is now extensionless, `artifact/<Type>-<id>` (kind/id, Q-THIN-2 A). Its JSON-LD is the IRI plus `.jsonld`, and its page is the IRI plus `.html`, which Pages serves at the IRI. So no stub page is needed, and the Publisher's page address is unchanged.
- **Fix:** `ig-artifact.js` and `ast-resource.js` counted loads in `window.__kgLoads` as a number, while `ig-footer.js` and the others use the shared object. Both now use the object.
- **Readback:** `isArtifactPage` and `artifactPageConfigOf` read a page back by the node it declares. `stampIgTocNav` recognises declaring pages.

Tests: `ig-thin-pages`, `ig-tab-views`, `gen-ig-pages` and `ig-repo-site` give 165 pass, 0 fail. A generated artefact page grew about 300 B (RDFa, stub, script tag). The e2e budget moves from 3000 to 3400 B.

Not done here: smart-base's committed IG pages regenerate on its own next build.

body:
#Jakobs agent

Buggranskning: Claude Code (Opus 5.5, extra hög), två oberoende granskningar, djup. 14 fynd: 10 åtgärdade, 0 avvisade, 4 går vidare som följd.

## Vad

Våg 1 och 2 i uppdrag B ([planen](docs/plans/BOLAG-SCEN-UI.md)): ett bolag tilldelas dealers, bakgrunder, bord och nivåer i stället för färdiga scener.

**Tilldelning med listor**

- `branding.assignment` kan bära tre valfria listor med id: `dealers`, `backgrounds`, `tables` (`apps/admin/lib/partner-assignment.mjs`). Okänt id, fel roll eller fler än 32 ger 422 med fält, id och skäl.
- `companyAssignment` är enda källan till bolagets gällande tilldelning, med uppgift per lista om den är uttrycklig eller härledd ur scenerna, och märket för en liten bakgrund.
- Med listor räknas scenernas tillåtna bakgrunder och bord ur listorna (`companyAppearance` i `packages/presentation/contracts/appearance-options.mjs`). Ett bord som inte går att placera i en scen redovisas som `notOffered` i stället för att falla bort tyst. En bakgrund under 1920 × 1080 är inte längre spärrad när den står i listan.
- Med listor avgör `assignment.allow` ensamt partnerns rätt, och ett nekat val ger 422 med skäl.
- **Tolerans:** ett bolag utan listor får samma frysta paket som förut (jämfört mot mains kod på sex scenurval av granskaren). Spelmotorn är orörd och behöver inte deployas.

**Bolagets sida Får använda** ersätter Dealers och scener

- Fyra listor med bockar (Dealers, Bakgrunder, Bord, Nivåer och språk), märkena *Liten bild* och *Passar N av M dealers*. En ibockad dealer tar med sin scen; en dealer som ett spelbord använder kan inte bockas ur (prövas på servern).
- **Spara och publicera publicerar listorna, inget annat.** Sparningen bygger på bolagets redan frysta presentation; bara scenernas tillåtna val räknas om, och bara en scen som är ny för bolaget hämtas ur projektet. Sparade men opublicerade scenändringar följer inte med. En ändring av bara rättigheter, nivåer eller språk rör ingen scen.
- Före sparningen säger sidan hur många öppna spelbord som får ändrade val (ny läsande förhandsvisning på servern). Knappen är avstängd när inget skulle ändras.
- Ett pausat spelbord som skulle ändras nekas med spelbordets namn; listor som inte ryms ger ett begripligt besked; ett fryst klipp eller material som tagits bort sedan publiceringen ger en egen text.
- Servern räknar själv vilka scener som får tas bort eller läggas till och nekar en klient som skickar andra (`studio_company_lanes_mismatch`).
- Ta bort och Ersätt av material rensar id:t ur bolagens listor.

## För Kevin (gränssnitt)

Admin: sidan *Dealers och scener* heter *Får använda* och har nytt innehåll (`apps/admin/components/admin/company-allowed*`); den gamla `company-selection*` är raderad. Partnerportalen får fälten `source` och `small` i sin läsning men ingen ny sida. Inget i spelet eller lobbyn ändras.

## Följder

- En av två scener för samma dealer hos ett bolag går inte att ta bort från sidan; löses när scenerna slås ihop till en per dealer (våg 4).
- Partnerns översikt visar id i stället för namn för listat material som ingen scen bär.
- Ett nytt bord i en fryst scen kan få sin mätta rad ur projektets mätning när ingen fryst scen har den.
- En scen som skapats åt en ibockad dealer tas bort igen vid nekad publicering utan kontroll av om någon hunnit börja använda den.

## Prov

Riktade prov lokalt, bland dem nya PGlite-prov för att en opublicerad scenändring inte når publiceringen, att orörda spelbord behåller sin `presentationHash`, pausat spelbord, för stora listor och fel `lanes` från klienten: 359/359 i 21 filer efter sista rättningen, webbläsarprovet 2/2, Admins typkontroll ren. Pre-commit godkänd på varje commit. Ingen DDL, inga nya miljövariabler.

body:
## 类型

- [x] ✨ 新功能

## 变更概述

用药清单新增与最近化验的交叉安全提示：ACEI/ARB/保钾利尿剂与血钾、二甲双胍与 eGFR、他汀与转氨酶、华法林与 INR、地高辛与血药浓度、利尿剂与电解质异常时，在新增/修改药物、健康提示、家庭总览与健康档案中提示「请与开药医生或药师核对」。

## 背景/问题

现有用药安全引擎只检查药物相互作用与过敏史，化验异常则单独陈列。ACEI/ARB 与高血钾、二甲双胍与 eGFR 下降、他汀与转氨酶升高、华法林与 INR 升高、地高辛浓度过高、利尿剂与低钾低钠这些交叉风险完全漏掉，患者只能自己把两份记录对照着看。

## 变更内容

- `core/medication_lab_safety.py`（新增）
  - 规则：RAAS 阻滞剂/保钾利尿剂与血钾 >5.0 mmol/L；RAAS 阻滞剂与 eGFR <60；二甲双胍与 eGFR <45；他汀与 ALT >3×参考上限；华法林与 INR >3.0；地高辛与血药浓度 >2.0 ng/mL；袢利尿剂/噻嗪类与血钾 <3.5 或血钠 <135 mmol/L。
  - 化验项目别名与单位换算：血钾/血钠/肌酐/INR 复用危急值模块；ALT 支持 U/L、IU/L、μkat/L；地高辛支持 ng/mL、μg/L、ng/L；eGFR 支持 mL/min/1.73m²。
  - eGFR 优先使用已登记结果，缺失时按档案年龄/性别与最近肌酐采用 CKD-EPI 2021 估算。
  - 统一文案只建议与开药医生或药师核对，不输出剂量调整、停药或诊断建议。
- `core/medication_safety.py`：新增 `find_drugs` 公开匹配函数与袢利尿剂药物组（呋塞米、托拉塞米、布美他尼）。
- `core/lab_values.py`：新增 `normalize_lab_measurement` / `normalize_unit_key` 公共入口，供用药-化验联动复用。
- `api_server.py`：`_medication_safety_for_profile` 读取近 180 天化验与档案年龄/性别，把化验交叉提示并入现有安全提示；新增/修改药物响应、健康提示、家庭总览（attention 与 CSV）与健康档案自动生效；提示详情在保存状态条中展示。
- `web/app.js`：保存药物后的安全提示展示首条详情（数值与检测日期）与剩余条数。
- `README.md`：更新用药安全与家庭总览说明。

评审加固：ALT 参考上限与数值按同一系数换算；肌酐为 0 不再崩溃；同分钟化验按较新记录取值；尿标本（panel=尿电解质等）不参与血清规则；他汀补充普伐/氟伐/匹伐他汀，保钾利尿剂补充依普利酮/非奈利酮；ALT/AST 比值双向排除；家族总览接入化验联动。

## 日志/验证证据

```text
$ python -m py_compile core/medication_lab_safety.py core/medication_safety.py api_server.py

$ python -m pytest tests/test_medication_lab_safety.py -q
31 passed, 1 warning in 5.52s

$ python -m pytest tests/test_medication_lab_safety.py tests/test_api_family_overview.py tests/test_api_family_attention.py tests/test_api_medication_safety.py tests/test_api_health_insights.py tests/test_api_dossier.py tests/test_web_health_insights.py -q
85 passed, 1 warning in 16.63s

$ python -m pytest -q
1438 passed, 1 warning in 209.03s (0:03:29)
```

浏览器实测：

```text
POST /api/lab-results（血钾 5.8 mmol/L）
POST /api/medications（培哚普利）→ safety.alerts[0]：
  培哚普利与血钾偏高：最近血钾 5.8 mmol/L（2026-11-11）。这类药物可能进一步升高血钾，请与开药医生或药师核对，不要自行调整剂量或停药。
添加厄贝沙坦 → 状态条：
  ⚠ 用药安全提示：培哚普利、氯沙坦、缬沙坦、厄贝沙坦与血钾偏高：最近血钾 5.8 mmol/L（2026-11-11）。这类药物可能进一步升高血钾，请与开药医生或药师核对，不要自行调整剂量或停药。（另有 2 条提示）
```

## 测试情况

- [x] 六类规则命中/不命中、全部阈值等值边界与最新化验选择（含同分钟多条）
- [x] 单位换算（μkat/L 值与参考上限同单位、μg/L、ng/L、IU/L）、ALT/AST 双向比值排除、缺失年龄/性别不估算
- [x] 尿标本 panel、肌酐为 0、他汀/保钾药别名覆盖
- [x] API 集成：新增药物返回化验交叉提示、既有过敏提示不被截断、健康提示包含该提示、档案年龄/性别参与 eGFR 估算、超过 180 天的化验不参与、空档案可用、家族总览 attention 接入
- [x] 浏览器实测：保存药物后状态条显示化验提示详情
- [ ] `python examples/test_all.py`（未涉及真实 LLM 调用）
- [ ] `python scripts/diagnose.py`（非环境相关改动）

author: angelica-boo
body:
## Qué hace

Empaqueta el frontend en una imagen Docker y deja la URL del backend configurable en ejecución (SCRUM-190).

- `Dockerfile` en dos etapas: Node 22 compila y la imagen final solo lleva Nginx sin privilegios (uid 101, puerto 8080) con los archivos estáticos.
- `nginx/default.conf.template`: fallback de SPA, caché larga para los archivos con hash, cabeceras básicas y `/config.json`.
- Configuración `docker` en `angular.json` con `environment.docker.ts` (`runtimeConfig: true`): `main.ts` pide `/config.json` antes de iniciar Angular y `runtime-config.ts` aplica `apiUrl` y `googleMapsApiKey`. Nginx arma esa respuesta con `API_URL` y `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` del contenedor.
- README y `.env.example` actualizados.

## Lo que no cambia

El build de Vercel sigue usando `environment.prod.ts` (URL compilada) y no hace la petición a `/config.json`, para no sumarle un viaje de red al LCP de RNF-01. Ahí la brecha del factor 3 sigue abierta y queda declarada en el README.

## Verificación

- `ng test`: 287 pruebas en verde (incluye `runtime-config.spec.ts`), `ng lint` y `ng build` de producción sin errores.
- Imagen construida y usada desde el compose del backend: registro, inicio de sesión con segundo factor y búsqueda de ruta desde el navegador. Evidencia en el PR hermano del backend (`docs/evidencias/docker/`).

## Orden de merge

Este PR va **antes** que el del backend (misma rama, `feature/SCRUM-190-docker-completo`): el compose construye la imagen desde este repo.

body:
## Summary

Step 28: a label named like a keyword. The lowering fuzz targets (`FuzzParserLowering`, `FuzzExtractLowering`,
`FuzzLabelFilterLowering`, `FuzzLabelFilterAfterParserLowering`) failed on main after 7 to 44 s on a label called
`or`, `OR` or `of`. The inputs hold five separate causes, each fixed where it lives.

| # | Cause | Where it was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | VictoriaLogs rejects a bare `not`, `in`, `contains_*`, `equals_common_case`, `options` (and `and`/`or` right after another filter) as a field name; Loki accepts a label called that | translator and plan wrote it bare: a filter-only query got a 400 ("failed to parse the log query", the VictoriaLogs parse error passed on) | the plan quotes the name; the translator (frozen) is a registered known divergence |
| 2 | the proxy's LogsQL parser was stricter than VictoriaLogs (`delete not`, `filter (OR:>=1 and ...)`) | the fuzz could not read the translator's valid text | parser reads `and`/`or`/`not` as names in pipe positions and `and`/`or` at a filter start |
| 3 | the proxy's LogQL parser accepted 15 words of Loki's lexer as label names and read them in lower case; Loki answers 400 | `{OF="a"}` was `of:="a"` in the plan and `OF:="a"` in the translator | rejected in the 12 places a name stands, with Loki's text. **Breaking** |
| 4 | `ip` and `label_replace` were read in lower case without a parenthesis | `{Ip="a"}` filtered the field `ip` (served from the plan) | a label keeps its case |
| 5 | the translator mangles a json expression for a key called `or`/`and`, a label name holding `detected_level`, a non-ASCII value it reads as a name | fuzz findings (not keyword names) | recognised by content in the fuzz helpers |

## Facts (Loki oracle 3.7.9, VictoriaLogs oracle v1.49.0 and v1.53.0, which agree on every row)

| Input | Loki | Translator text | Plan text | VictoriaLogs reading | Served today (flag default on) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{not="a"}` | 200 | `not:="a"` | `"not":="a"` | bare: "missing whitespace or ':' between "not" and ":""; quoted: field | plan, filter-only: 400 before, 200 now |
| `{app="a"} \| in="x"` | 200 | `app:="a" in:="x"` | `app:="a" "in":="x"` | bare: "the "in" must be put in quotes" | plan: 400 before, 200 now |
| `{app="a"} \| contains_all>5` (also `contains_any`, `contains_common_case`, `equals_common_case`) | 200 | `app:="a" contains_all:>5` | `app:="a" "contains_all":>5` | bare: rejected | plan: 400 before, 200 now |
| `{options="a"}` | 200 | `options:="a"` | `"options":="a"` | rejected only as the first filter | plan |
| `{app="a"} \| _or="x"` under a label function that drops a leading underscore | 200 | `app:="a" or:="x"` | `app:="a" "or":="x"` | `or` after a filter is the operator: rejected | plan: 400 before, 200 now |
| `{app="a"} \| json \| not="x"` | 200 | `... \| filter not:="x"` | `... \| filter "not":="x"` | rejected | translator: 400 (unchanged until the plan serves parsers) |

body:
Fixes #1641

Implements ADR-1032's external-actions default, following the approved plan (revision 1).

## What changes

- **Defaults.** `defaultGrantModes` in `src/core/delivery-levels.ts` gives each action kind the mode a new grant starts in:
  - `allow` for the ten reversible, cab-owned kinds, plus `pr.update-branch` from #1648.
  - `approval` for `pr.merge`, `issue.close`, `issue.edit`, `issue.create`, `branch.force-push` and `branch.adopt`.
  - Settings **Add grant** uses it, and changing a row's Action resets its Mode to that kind's default. This replaces the old `branch.adopt` special case.
  - CLI grants still come from the `--level` presets. A test pins the presets and the defaults together.
- **`pr.edit` no longer forces approval.** It is removed from `DeliveryStore.authorize` and from the Delivery authority note.
  - `issue.edit`, recovery actions and operator publication still require approval.
  - The closing-keyword guard still covers `pr.edit`.
- **Migration** `allow-default-kinds-v1`, at startup level 27, data-only:
  - It switches existing `approval` grants of the frozen ten-kind list to `allow`, once per store.
  - It adds and removes no grant and keeps every other field.
  - It does not bump the policy version. Bindings and settlements compare only that version, so they stay valid and in-flight projects migrate too.
  - An operator reset back to `approval` stays.
- **Readable approval material.** `src/operator/approval-material.ts` turns material into facts, texts and diffs. The task approval review and `cab approval get` both use it.
  - The material is shown before the version and hash, and Exact JSON stays available but closed.
  - Material is read as an action only when the approval's action is its kind. That is the case where the service validated it strictly and bound its target. Other material lists its fields, or is shown literally if it is not an object.
  - Approve still sends the material unchanged, and `--output json` data is unchanged.
- SPEC Delivery and approval paragraphs are revised in place.

## Validation

The branch was rebased onto main 38ac25e5 and validated at head dcbfa17e:
- `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run build` all exited 0.
- The stack-real-adapter, startup-snapshot, both delivery-migration, delivery-policy, branch-ownership, presenter and delivery-presentation tests: 106 passed, 1 skipped.
- `npm run test:built -- --suite=delivery,operations,coordination --profile=service`: 2210 passed, 1 failed.
  - The failure was "concrete offline stack delayed platform rebase …", which ended in `v2-authority-closed` after 80 s under full-suite load.
  - It passes alone in 26 s. It also passed in the pre-rebase run at 4ccc34e6, which had 2211 passed and 0 failed.
- `npm run test:built -- --suite=operator` (Chromium): 1868 passed, 0 failed.
  - Before the rebase, three unrelated browser tests failed there on teardown or locator timeouts. All three passed when rerun alone.

New tests:
- the store migration test file
- a defaults and presets consistency test
- `pr.edit` allow/approval enforcement
- a Settings browser test for the default mode and saving with Require approval
- the presenter unit test
- a task-detail browser test that checks the diff comes before the version, Exact JSON is closed and Approve sends the exact material
- a CLI test that checks the diff comes before the hash and the JSON material is exact

One independent read-only review was done before the first push, and a drift review after the rebase. The first verdict was fix-first:
- Fixed: non-object material was hidden; a recognized kind could hide extra keys in generic approvals; a stale test comment; an over-broad SPEC sentence.
- Deferred: the `DiffColumn` duplication (see residual risks).

The re-review verdict was ship. The drift review covered the rebase resolution, interactions with #1605 and #1656, migration order and the schema-pin files; its verdict was also ship.

## Residual risks

- `DiffColumn` and the compare markup are copied from `web/src/issue-improve.tsx`. Sharing them means editing a file outside this ticket's scope, so it is left as a follow-up.
- No browser test covers rendered Markdown text in the review. The 390px overflow check uses only unrecognized material, so the diff and text layout is not checked at phone width. The CSS is contained (`min-width: 0`, `overflow-wrap: anywhere`).
- `MIGRATION_LEVEL` 27 repeats level 26's schema digest, because this migration only rewrites data. Open PRs #1657 and #1659 also take levels, so whichever merges second must renumber.

author: kshot3000
body:
## Summary

Adds the Wave 3 gated-swap demo: a Compact contract and a local UI where a swap only fills after the holder privately proves a ShieldPass credential.

`contracts/src/gatedswap.compact` admits the same salted leaves that ShieldPass issues (`credentialLeaf` is byte-identical) and `swap()` re-proves Merkle membership plus the pool policy (KYC, sanctions, age, country, expiry) before it moves demo units at a constant-product quote. Compact 0.31 cannot read another contract's ledger, so the UI also keeps the swap closed until `@shieldpass/verify` reports `isSessionVerified` for that session.

The existing ShieldPass contract, Preprod deployment, and 0.31.1 toolchain pin are unchanged. This branch does not deploy the swap to Preprod (that needs the shared testnet wallet, which stays outside the repo). Please do not merge until it has been reviewed.

## How to test

```bash
# compactc 0.31.1, Node 22.18+, pnpm 9
pnpm install
pnpm test            # 27 contract + 7 SDK + 3 demo-world tests
pnpm compile         # full ZK build of both contracts
pnpm demo            # http://127.0.0.1:8787
```

In the demo: prove the compliant credential, swap 1000 A for B, then try a failing profile (under 18, blocked country, expired, not sanctions-clear) and confirm the gate stays closed.

## Safety

No secrets, keys, seed phrases, emails, or physical addresses are in the code or this PR. Demo credentials are fake; only salted leaves sit on the simulated ledger.

author: vishvananda
body:
Preserve explicit LowIR pointer bounds, forward private storage across ordinary joins in computed-goto functions, and merge provably equal cyclic phi state. Repair packed floating-field reads with a bounded, single-use load projection that preserves memory snapshots, volatile/atomic widths and alias semantics. Add student requirements, Perl reducers and exported references; publish the validated internal test count instead of the static 9,832 badge.

This includes #126 and the committed LLVM aggregate checkpoint `cf3e0fca5`, as requested. The broader integer-only and full-width bitcast experiments are excluded.

On the quiet EPYC host, the isolated field repair measures **1.150× Fasta 1 CPU speed**, **1.024× Fasta 2**, **1.026× Fasta 3**, and **0.998× Fasta 6**. All 81 public output checks pass; 76 executables remain byte-identical, and aggregate instruction efficiency improves **1.0054×**. The frozen compiler workload adds **0.33% instructions at -O3**, with effectively unchanged -O0 work. Myc's allocated code/data and layout remain identical to the aggregate baseline.

Godot's repair-only screen averages **0.995×**; **arrays is an unfavorable 0.977× local screen** that needs CI/focused confirmation. Earlier LLVM inliner losses in Mandelbrot 0 and re2-test-re2 remain separate follow-up work. [Measurements, calibration, provenance and remaining gaps](https://github.com/vishvananda/cppgm-extended/blob/opt/godot-epyc-followup/docs/performance/godot-epyc-followup-20261111.md).

Validation: **10,626/10,626 strict tests**, architecture/source-set/scaffold/format/IR/file/placement/harness audits, PA36 smoke, debug-info, self-host through PA5, byte-identical inception, and a fresh student export with **256 documents and all 43 reference wrappers passing**. The pre-fix compiler fails the new field-quality bounds; positive/negative runtime checks and optimizer pass validation pass. GCC and Clang 21 compile the new module with warnings as errors. Native macOS qualification remains for CI.

author: dalton-cole
body:
> **Do not merge or deploy.** Stacked on #7 (`claude/sec-f04-cable-tickets`, F-04 one-time cable tickets) — review/merge that first. Server-side correlation acks, if ever needed here, would depend on primeta #60 and then the new F-09 server PR; this extension does **not** send correlated `type: "reply"` messages (it is a TTS/avatar surface), so no outbox was added. No streaming is involved.

## What changed

**1. Watchdog / reconnect race** (`src/cable/actioncable-client.ts`)
- The watchdog now detaches the socket (`this.ws = null`) **before** `terminate()`/`close()`, via `teardownSocket(force = true)`. The socket's close handler then hits the existing `this.ws !== ws` guard and does nothing, so the watchdog is the only reconnect path.
- `scheduleReconnect` still allows at most one pending timer.
- F-04 ticket auth is unchanged: every connect mints a fresh ticket with `POST /cable/tickets`, the socket URL carries `?ticket=`, and there is no `?bridge_token=` fallback.

**2. No auto-claim of an arbitrary bridge** (`src/extension.ts`, new `src/bridge-selection.ts`)
- `autoConnectBridge` used to fall back to `bridges[0]` when no bridge matched the workspace name, which could voice another project's session. It now uses `selectAutoConnectBridge()`, which returns an exact workspace-name match or `null`. The `bridge_status: connected` handler uses the same helper.
- When there's no match, the panel stays on the waiting screen, adds "or pick a session from the menu", and the dropdown gets a disabled "Select a session…" placeholder. Without the placeholder, picking the first session would not fire `change`.
- `AvatarPanel.updateBridgeList(bridges, null)` now means "nothing selected". `undefined` still falls back to the loaded bridge.

## Tests
- Watchdog fire with a socket that emits `close` synchronously schedules exactly **one** reconnect timer and makes exactly **one** connect (mint) attempt, with nothing left pending afterwards. This fails on the pre-change code, which scheduled 2 timers.
- When the terminated socket's `close`/`error` events arrive late, after the new socket is open, they are ignored.
- The socket is detached before `terminate()` is called. This also fails on the pre-change code.
- `selectAutoConnectBridge`: exact match; no fallback to the first bridge; no workspace folder; a single non-matching bridge; no bridges; no prefix or case-insensitive matches.

`npm test`: 27/27 pass. `npm run build` and `tsc --noEmit` pass.

author: neo-opus-grace
body:
Resolves #20748

`AGENTS.md` is a pointer in git and the generated rules in every installed checkout. Git keeps a short note, the operator's one-liner: the file is generated, `npm install` writes it, and a fork's agent can print the contributor rules with `npx`. The `agents-md` stage writes the maintainer rules into the same path at `prepare` and on every `seat:start`. A clean filter maps the working copy back to the pointer, so `git status` stays clean. It is Git LFS's pattern.
- **One path for every tool:** Claude, Codex, Antigravity and any other agent read `AGENTS.md`.
- **Visible:** scanners and directories that look for a root `AGENTS.md` still find it.
- **No commit on a bump:** a skills bump changes the rules a session loads without anyone committing a file. The tracked copy used to need a hand catch-up (#20739).

Evidence: L3 (unit specs, a real-git round trip of the filter, and `npm run prepare` / `npm run seat:start` run live in this Engine checkout) → L3 required (AC-1 to AC-6). The Fleet-driven Start is Post-Merge Validation.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Coverage |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | Outside CI, at the head in this checkout: `npm run prepare` prints `✅ neo,neo-agent-brain/maintainer → AGENTS.md (23408 B, 392 B headroom)`. The file equals `npm run generate-agents-md`'s output, and `git status` lists no change to it. CI: `agentsMdPointer.spec.mjs` "generated rules in the working copy leave git clean, and git keeps the pointer" |
| AC-2 | CI: `prepare.spec.mjs` "husky runs, then the skills materializer, then the pointer filter and AGENTS.md with the arguments of this checkout's own script". `git grep "neo,neo-agent-brain"` outside `test/` finds only `package.json:45` |
| AC-3 | CI: `prepare.spec.mjs` "a bump moves the file: the stage writes what the installed version generates" (a fixture package bumped from 1.3.3 to 1.3.5) |
| AC-4 | CI: `seatStart.spec.mjs` "a deleted AGENTS.md is back after the next Start, with nothing reinstalled". Outside CI: `rm AGENTS.md && npm run seat:start` prints `[seat:start] AGENTS.md generated`, and the file equals the generator's output |
| AC-5 | CI: `seatStart.spec.mjs` "a failed generation rejects with its reason, after the theme check has run", "a generator that exits non-zero fails the Start…", and "the entry point exits 1 and names AGENTS.md when the generation fails" |
| AC-6 | The two blog links and `CONTRIBUTING.md:165` point to `agents-md` in neomjs/neo-agent-skills. CI: `agentsMdPointer.spec.mjs` "the committed AGENTS.md is the pointer" pins the tracked file to the constant, and its filter attribute |

## Deltas from ticket
- **`AGENTS.md` stays tracked, as a pointer; it is not untracked.** This follows the operator's input on discoverability, and it makes Skills #342/#343 unnecessary: a CI tree always holds the file, so `.claude/CLAUDE.md` never dangles.
- **No stage step writes file content to the index.** Git trusts a changed size without reading the file. So after each generation, the entry is re-set to its own blob, which clears the cached stat, and `git update-index -q --refresh` runs with no pathspec. The index re-reads the file through the filter, and nothing is staged.
- **The filter is required, and its registration fails closed.** The stage makes sure `clean` and `required = true` are registered before it writes, and stops when they cannot be. A filter that cannot run makes git refuse to store the file, never store it raw.
- **It composes with the Fleet's home projection** (neomjs/neo-agent-brain#644). The install and `seat:start` run before the preparer (`startAgentProvisioned.mjs:716` → `:760`), so the preparer finds the generated file and writes no home copy. Two Fleet changes follow under their own leaf: count `AGENTS.md` as Claude's project file, which must land before `.claude/CLAUDE.md` can go, and read the pointer marker as "not supplied", so that a failed generation still gets the home copy.

## Slot rationale (`/turn-memory-pre-flight`)
- **`AGENTS.md`, delivery only:** the loaded content is the generator's output, byte-equal at pin 1.3.3 to the tracked file it replaces (23,408 B), so the always-loaded delta is 0 B. The committed bytes shrink to the 328 B pointer.
- **Decay mitigation:** the loaded file can no longer lag the installed sections, and the pointer has nothing in it to go stale.

## Test Evidence
`agent-preflight`: not hosted here. Ran locally at the head:
- `prepare.spec.mjs`, `seatStart.spec.mjs` and `agentsMdPointer.spec.mjs`: 36 passed;
- mutations, in a separate worktree: restoring the refresh's filename operand fails "without a filter, the refresh stages nothing", and registering the filter without `required` fails "a registered filter that cannot run refuses to store the file";
- red-first, earlier in this branch: in a base worktree, the 5 new `seatStart` arms failed and the 5 existing ones passed;
- `check-substrate-size` at the pinned `v1.3.3`, run against the checked-out index (what CI sees): `AGENTS.md` 328 B and `.claude/CLAUDE.md` 328 B, exit 0;
- `check-package-contents`, `check-relative-links`, `check-file-sizes --base origin/dev` and `check-ticket-archaeology --base origin/dev` all pass;
- the live `prepare` and `seat:start` receipts are under AC-1 and AC-4.

All other coverage runs in CI.

## Post-Merge Validation
- [ ] The first Fleet Start of an Engine seat after the merge logs `[seat:start] AGENTS.md generated`, and its start row carries no `seatStart` failure.
- [ ] neomjs/neo-agent-skills#335's other halves land under their own leaves: the Brain's `IdentityFirewall.md` link (neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1593) and `devindex` (neomjs/devindex#135).

## Commits
- `d2d5b2b` — the `agents-md` stage in `prepare` and `seat:start`, its specs and the doc links
- `93ca039` — `AGENTS.md` stays tracked as a pointer, behind a clean filter
- `a6dfced` — the filter is required and registered before the write; the refresh never writes file content to the index

## Evolution
The first commit untracked `AGENTS.md`. Its baseline reddened on the substrate-size guard, which reads a dangling `.claude/CLAUDE.md` as a seat without rules. author: jfrancolopez
body:
Two commits, deliberately separate.

## 1. The inert-key class

The dead-key audit (#206) cannot see this one by construction: the key appears in
the code, so *"is it referenced"* answers yes. What makes it inert is that **every
occurrence is plumbing** — its own export, its `load_cfg` default, or a
`configure`/`config_set` that **writes** it — with nothing reading the value to
decide anything. It's the worse half: `configure` **prompted** for all three, and
being asked a question asserts the answer matters.

**`DOMUM_TS_IP` is removed.** Its comment claimed it was *"used by docs and
dynamic routes"* — **both halves false**: nothing in `compose/proxy/` references
it, no document mentions it. Its neighbour `DOMUM_LAN_IP`, under the *same*
comment, genuinely is used (`traefik.yml:19` + two docs) — that contrast is what
makes this a finding rather than a guess. The prompt and export go with it, or
`configure` would re-add what the example dropped. Measured: the CI compose
render is identical with and without it, and sourcing the example still returns 0
with nothing executed and no comment leaking into a value.

**`IMMICH_HOST` and `IMMICH_BUNDLE_ROLLBACK_ENABLED` are exempted, not wired.**
The first needs the Traefik rule changed — a compose change, deployment-
affecting. The second is a **rollback gate**: wiring it makes it obey a value
never obeyed, and the production config is `0600 root`, so it could silently turn
bundle rollback **off**. Operator decisions, not cleanups.

**Joining continuations is the whole reason the audit works.** A `config_set`
whose prompt default sits on the next physical line puts `${KEY:-...}` on a line
with no `config_set` on it — measured **0** inert keys before joining, **3**
after. That's the pipefail audit's blind spot in a third place.

The exemptions double as its negative control: a marker on a key that has become
live **fails**, so dropping the join is caught instantly (both read `NOT inert any
more`). Also controlled: a new inert key, and both vacuity guards. A setter
missing from the helper list yields a false *negative*, never a false alarm.

## 2. A test that depended on the host's timezone

My own, from #192. It asserted `SENT_DATE=$(date -I)` in the **test's** shell,
while `record_weekly_report` computes it inside the CLI — which exports
`TZ="${TZ:-UTC}"`, and that leaks into its own process.

Measured 2026-11-10 21:47 EST: `date -I` is `2026-11-10` locally, `2026-11-11`
under UTC. So it failed on this host every evening after 19:00 and passed in CI,
which runs UTC — the **"passes in CI, fails locally"** inversion, and the fourth
dimension of host dependence after PATH, speed and awk.

**Production is unaffected**, verified: writer and same-day guard both run inside
the CLI, so both see UTC and agree. The fix mirrors the production derivation and
additionally requires `TS` and `SENT_DATE` to agree — true whatever the clock
says. Both negative-controlled; verified passing in the window that was failing.

Local: 78/78 shell suites, 15/15 audits, shellcheck clean, compose render `rc=0`.

The observed loose-file A2 install contains `Armada2.exe`, `odf/` and `bzn/`, but no Data child or root ZFS archive. The actual client therefore reported NoData and zero maps. Shared `Vfs::mount_install` now recognizes that complete file/directory combination, case-insensitively, when no mod was requested, and mounts it through the existing `push_dir` loader.

Data keeps priority, including errors and the mod chain. Flat A1 archive recognition and all indexing/archive/profile/loose-file semantics are unchanged. Incomplete or wrong-type marker combinations remain unsupported; an explicit mod, including an empty string, is never silently discarded. Markers identify a layout, not executable authenticity or a complete installation. No executable is read or launched for recognition.

The pre-code contract and WORKPLAN row were pushed in `40c8a36`; implementation is `c667f5f`, based on main `14ce742` independently of the unmerged selected-map seam #302.

Validation:
