author: lbarrosby
body:
Fixes #1398

A latency SLO whose total is written as the `+Inf` bucket instead of `_count` (the filesystem validator only warns about it) generates broken rules:

```yaml
total:
  metric: http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{application="test-api", le="+Inf"}
success:
  metric: http_server_requests_seconds_bucket{application="test-api", le="0.5"}
```

1. `increaseRuleLatency` built the success labels as `{"le": <success le>}` and then copied the total rule labels on top, so `le="+Inf"` from the total overwrote `le="0.5"`. Both increase rules record `http_server_requests_seconds:increase4w{application="test-api",le="+Inf",slo="api-latency"}`, i.e. two rules writing the same series. The second `SLOMetricAbsent` alert got the same wrong label.
2. The generic `pyrra_availability` rule, the `performance_over_accuracy` total subquery and the UI queries (`QueryTotal`, `QueryErrors`, `QueryErrorBudget`) append `le=""` to the total selector to skip the success bucket. With a total that already has `le="+Inf"` this gives `{le="",le="+Inf"}`, which never matches.

The fix keeps the success `le` on the success rule, and adds `le=""` only when the total selector does not already match on `le` (new helper `appendEmptyLeMatcher`). Nothing changes for `_count` totals or native histograms.

Reproduced with `pyrra generate --generic-rules` on the SLO above. Diff of the generated file, before and after:

```diff
@@ success increase rule
-      le: +Inf
+      le: "0.5"
@@ second SLOMetricAbsent
-      le: +Inf
+      le: "0.5"
@@ pyrra_availability
-      or vector(0)) / sum(http_server_requests_seconds:increase4w{application="test-api",le="",le="+Inf",slo="api-latency"})
+      or vector(0)) / sum(http_server_requests_seconds:increase4w{application="test-api",le="+Inf",slo="api-latency"})
```

Tests: added `TestObjective_LatencyBucketInfTotal` (increase rules, split rules, generic rules, UI queries). All four subtests fail on `main` and pass with the change; `go test ./...` passes.

I used an AI assistant (Claude Code) to help trace this and write the test. I reviewed and ran everything myself.

author: stickerdaniel
body:
Closes #31

## Problem

The plugin downloads the Convex local backend from the release's anonymous github.com link, in one attempt. On 2026-11-08 that link answered 503 and 504 for hours, so cold dev server starts failed. The REST asset endpoint served the same bytes.

## Solution

The download uses the asset's REST `url` with `Accept: application/octet-stream`, plus `GITHUB_TOKEN` when set. Fetch drops the token on the redirect. Once the API's rate limit is spent, the remaining attempts use the github.com link without the token. Other 429s fail at once. The archive must match the release's SHA-256 `digest`. The listing and the asset get 3 attempts on 408, 409, 5xx, network errors and damaged archives.

## Verification

12 new tests drive `ConvexBackend.spawn()` with a stubbed fetch. Disabling the digest check, the fallback, its reuse or the 429 fail-fast fails one each. `bun qa` and `bun run test:run` pass.

Implemented with Claude Opus 5.5 (high) and reviewed with GPT-6 Pro (Pro) in Claude Code via T3 Code.

author: ronishrohan
body:
Code changes: +3 -1  
Tests: +0 -0  
Others: +0 -0

## What

Artifacts page section headers (Recent, Pinned, each project, Scratchpad) now use the same type as a Settings section heading instead of the page title's type.

## Why

Team feedback (Aditi): the type sizes on the Artifacts page looked inconsistent. The scope tabs (All | On this machine | Cloud) were small, the section headers were much larger and bolder, and the page title was a third size.

In the code, `ArtifactSection` copied `topbarTitleClass` almost exactly (`text-brand font-semibold tracking-tight leading-none`, 16px/600). So every section header was as large as the page title and well above the 12px tabs next to it. No other page uses `text-brand` outside the topbar. The rest of the app keeps 16px/600 for the route title only:

| Element | Where | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page title | `PageTopbarTitle` (all pages) | 16px / 600 / tight |
| Section heading | Settings `SettingsSection` | 14px / 500 / 20px leading |
| Project rows | Sidebar | 14px / 500, 14px icons |
| Section heading | Automations "Templates" | 13px / 500 |
| Scope tabs | `Button size="sm"` (Artifacts, Usage, Automations) | 14px / 400 as rendered (see note below) |
| Card title | `ArtifactGalleryCard`, list rows | 13px / 500 |

DESIGN.md: "500 medium for controls and small hierarchy; 600 only for headings, selected values, and genuinely primary emphasis", and 21–22px is reserved for "route-level title only". A collapsible group label is small hierarchy, not a page heading.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Section header text: `text-brand` 16px, `font-semibold` 600, `tracking-tight` -0.01em, `leading-none` | `text-sm` 14px, `font-medium` 500, normal tracking, `leading-5` 20px |
| Header icons 14px beside 16px text | 14px icons beside 14px text (same as sidebar project rows) |
| Rendered: title 16/600 = section 16/600 > tabs 14/400 | Title 16/600 > section 14/500, tabs 14/400 > card title 13/500 > caption 11/400 muted |

Unchanged: the "Updated 13h ago" caption (11px, muted, tabular), the 13px muted chevron, the 44px header row height (`min-h-11`), section spacing, the scope tabs, and the page title. No layout or behavior change other than the smaller header text.

No screenshots: I did not run the app for this PR. Please capture before and after by hand (see Testing).

## How

One class string in `ArtifactSection` (`frontend/src/renderer/components/ArtifactsView.tsx`). `leading-none` became `leading-5` because the label truncates (`overflow: hidden`), and at `leading-none` descenders such as the "p" in "Scratchpad" can clip.

Shared-style notes, not changed here:
- `topbarTitleClass` (16px/600) is shared by every page title and is correct for that role, so I left it alone.
- The scope tabs use the shared `Button size="sm"`, which asks for `text-xs` (12px). In the running app they render at 14px/400. An unlayered `button, input, textarea, select { font: inherit; }` rule in `styles.css` (since #3518) beats every layered Tailwind font utility, so all buttons, inputs and selects inherit the body's 14px/400 regardless of their `text-*`/`font-*` classes. Confirmed via CDP matched styles in the dev app. Fixing it (moving the rule into `@layer base`) would resize most small buttons in the app, so it belongs in its own PR. With it in place, the 14px/500 headers and 14px/400 tabs read as siblings, which is what this PR is after.

## Testing

I did not run tests, typecheck, lint or builds. After opening the PR I ran it in an isolated dev app with seeded artifacts; computed styles: section headers 14px/500/20px, page title 16px/600, scope tabs 14px/400. No test asserts these classes. Please check by hand on the Artifacts page with at least two projects that have artifacts:

1. Dark and light themes: the Recent, project and Scratchpad headers read as siblings of the All / On this machine / Cloud tabs, clearly smaller than the "Artifacts" title, and still a step above the card titles.
2. Project avatars, the Scratchpad file icon, the Recent clock and the Pinned pin sit centered on the header text at the same size.
3. "Scratchpad" and project names with descenders (g, p, y) are not clipped. Long project names still truncate, and the "Updated …" caption stays on the row at a narrow center width.
4. Collapse and expand a section: the chevron rotates, the row height does not change, and the hover pill and keyboard focus ring look as before.
5. The selected "All" tab pill is unchanged, and switching tabs or filtering down to one project (non-collapsible header) causes no layout jump.
6. Switch between gallery and list views: both use the same headers.

## Checklist

- [x] Change scoped to the Artifacts page section headers
- [x] Uses existing type tokens only
- [ ] Before/after screenshots (to be added by hand)

## Summary

```diff
 dependencies
-  sp_rtk_base_relay>=4.2.1,<5
+  sp_rtk_base_relay>=4.2.2,<5     # Bluetooth input data_timeout
 version
-  0.13.1

```

Relay 4.2.2 (rodenj1/sp-rtk-base-relay#76) reconnects a Bluetooth input that stays open but stops sending. Under 4.2.1 the Relay only warned about no data, for 27 hours on vaio-base, until someone restarted it (rodenj1/sp-rtk-base-relay#75). sp-rtk-base doesn't set `data_timeout`, so the Relay's 60 s default applies.

## Evidence

- **Before:** locked `sp-rtk-base-relay 4.2.1`, which has no `BluetoothConfig.data_timeout`.
- **After:** locked `4.2.2`, with hashes matching PyPI (`65cdb156…` wheel, `d1f1cd09…` sdist). `BluetoothConfig().data_timeout == 60.0`, and the full suite passes against it (3,422 passed, 1 xfailed, 96% coverage).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

The dependency floor can be lowered again.

**Blast Radius:** Bluetooth-inputs

A Bluetooth input that sends nothing for 60 s while connected now has its link dropped and reconnected each minute, instead of staying open and silent. Nothing changes under `deploy/`, so hosts need no setup step.

body:
## Work package

**M1.2c: the conformance suite says what a harness cannot do.** Commits `1cf646d` and `09fc8f2` (the answer to the review) on `skyzfs-coding` (base 6cffc8e).

The suite of `skyzfs-blk` is to be driven against a real block device with the daemon behind it. Such a rig cannot cut the power at a chosen record, build a base, fail the log, or get an invalid request past the kernel, and almost every case failed there for a reason of the harness. The alternative, a list of runnable cases kept in the rig, would be a relaxed check hidden outside the suite.

## What was done

- `Harness::capabilities()` returns a set of `Capability`: `PowerCut`, `Base`, `ReadOnly`, `FailLog`, `InvalidRequests`, `ReopenFailed`. It has no default: each harness says what it can do.
- Every `Case` declares `requires` (the capabilities its rule needs) and `weaker` (those it uses only to check more, each with what is left out).
- A case that requires a missing capability is reported as `Status::NotExercised` with the capability as the reason, **before it runs anything**: the harness is not asked for a device.
- A case that only used the capability to check more runs without it and is reported as `Status::Weaker(what was left out)`; `Report::weaker()` lists them, `Report::unexercised()` gives the unexercised cases with reasons, and the printed report has `WEAK` lines beside `SKIP`.
- The random programs leave out the steps the harness cannot do (power cut, log failure and reopen, invalid request), run on an empty volume without `Base`, end without the power cut before the last read-back, and the report says which and how many programs ran.
- The suite never calls a hook the harness lacks. A guard in the driver fails the case if it would (a base, a read-only device, a power cut, a log failure, a reopen, or submitting an invalid request); the guards are tested on a harness that silently complies.
- `Harness::reopen_failed` returns `Result<Target, HarnessError>`; its former "cannot" value is the capability. `Needs::Reopen` is gone.
- Nothing changes for a harness that can do everything: `MemTarget`, the reviewer's target and the store (both drivers) pass as before, and their tests now also assert that nothing ran in a weaker form.

**Every case** (P power cut, B base, R read-only, F log failure, I invalid requests, O reopen):

| Case | Not exercised without | Weaker without (what is lost) |
|---|---|---|
| parameters_are_as_the_contract_fixes_them | | P (not checked after a power cut), R (the read-only flag), B (read-only device on an empty base) |
| fresh_device_reads_as_its_base | | B (only an empty volume) |
| rejects_misaligned | I | |
| rejects_out_of_bounds | | I (only: the last block can be written and read) |
| rejects_empty_and_oversize | | I (only: 1 MiB is accepted; discard and write-zeroes span the device) |
| read_your_writes | | B |
| write_zeroes_hides_the_base | B | P (not checked after a cut) |
| discard_leaves_old_zeros_or_base | | B (the base is zeros), P |
| discard_never_hits_later_writes | | B, P |
| flushed_operations_survive_power_cut | P | B |
| flush_covers_what_was_acknowledged_before_it | P | |
| flush_covers_an_earlier_instance | P | |
| power_cut_at_every_point_leaves_a_prefix | P | B |
| recovered_state_is_durable | P | |
| first_request_after_power_cut_may_be_a_write | P | B |
| queue_depth_requests_complete_in_any_order | | |
| overlapping_operations_in_flight_apply_whole | | P (the order is checked in memory, not in the log) |
| kill_keeps_acknowledged_operations | | B |
| reissue_after_kill_is_idempotent | | P (not checked after flush and cut) |
| failed_volume_fails_every_request | F | I (no invalid request in flight or after) |
| reopened_failed_volume_holds_what_was_flushed | F, O | B, P |
| restart_after_the_log_failed_recovers_nothing | F, O | B, P |
| read_only_target_refuses_mutations | R | B |
| prop_invalid_requests_are_rejected_without_effect | I | B |
| prop_concurrent_programs_match_model | | B, I, P |
| prop_failures_match_model | | P, F, O, B, I |

With every capability missing: 13 cases are not exercised, 12 run in a weaker form, and one (`queue_depth_requests_complete_in_any_order`) runs whole. Both kill cases run, and two of the three random-program cases (the rejection property does not).

## Acceptance criteria

- **(a)** `tests/capabilities.rs`: `Limited`, `MemHarness` without a set of capabilities. It records any call for something it lacks, and any invalid request that reaches its target when it lacks `InvalidRequests`. `a_missing_capability_leaves_out_exactly_the_cases_that_need_it`: without each capability in turn, without all, and with all: no case fails; nothing is recorded; the unexercised and the weaker cases are exactly those of a table written down in the test (not derived from the suite); each reason names the capability. `a_case_that_is_not_exercised_runs_nothing`: no device is created. `the_random_programs_say_what_they_left_out`. `the_random_programs_have_every_kind_of_step_the_harness_can_do` (in the suite's own unit tests).
- **(b)** The 24 faults of `MemTarget` against the limited harness, in three columns.

  | Without | No fixed case notices (asserted, any seed) | Of those, invisible to random programs at three seeds (asserted) |
  |---|---|---|
  | a power cut | FlushDoesNothing, FlushJoinsOldSync, FlushForgetsEarlierInstance, CutDropsMiddle, RecoveryNotDurable | none |
  | a base | WriteZeroesShowsBase, ReopenLosesFlushed, StrayWrite | WriteZeroesShowsBase, StrayWrite |
  | a read-only device | ReadOnlyAcceptsWrites | the same |
  | a log failure | FailedServesReads, FlushSucceedsOnFailedLog, FailureForgottenOnKill, ReopenLosesFlushed | the same |
  | invalid requests | AcceptMisaligned, AcceptOutOfBounds | the same |
  | a reopen | ReopenLosesFlushed | the same |
  | all six | the faults above and TearOnCut: 15 of 24 | the same 15 |

  Every fault not in the middle column is noticed by a fixed case, at any seed. The faults in the middle column and not in the right one were noticed only by random programs, and not at every seed. At seeds 0x5ca1ab1e, 7, 0xC0FFEE, without a power cut: FlushDoesNothing yes, yes, no; FlushJoinsOldSync yes, no, no; FlushForgetsEarlierInstance yes, yes, yes; CutDropsMiddle no, no, yes; RecoveryNotDurable yes, no, yes. Without a base: ReopenLosesFlushed at all three. That is reported and promised by nobody: a random program sees these faults only if it happens to fail the log and reopen. So a rig without a power cut must not count on the suite for the faults of durability, and a rig with none of the six capabilities sees none of them at all. Still caught by a fixed case with nothing: StaleReads, ShortWrite, WriteZeroesDoesNothing, DiscardCorrupts, DiscardAppliedLate, SplitWrites, KillLosesUnflushed, RejectReissued, DropWriteBuffer.
- **(c)** `Case::defect_run_without_its_capabilities` (hidden): a case runs although its capability is absent. `a_case_that_runs_without_its_capability_is_stopped_by_the_suite`: on a harness that would comply silently, exactly the cases the table lists fail.
- **(d)** The `Harness` documentation: what leaving a capability out means, a table of what a kernel-level rig is expected to answer for each, and that a harness must not claim a capability it imitates loosely, with examples. The module documentation has the case table.
- **(e)** Every test's doc names its property; no `unwrap` outside tests; no `unsafe`; fmt and clippy clean on rustc 1.99.1.

author: wydrox
body:
Hardening of the Connect account protocol (ADR 0037 stage 7, unit FA2), on `feat/connect-stage7`. Unreleased; the contract changes with it.

## The signed device list

- Each account keeps a **signed, versioned device list**. Version 1 is the root key (the first device, or the device of the last recovery). Each later version is one change, an `add` (a confirmation) or a `remove` (a revoke), signed by a device of the list over `apassy-connect device-list v1` with the hash of the entry before.
- `GET /v1/account` and the join answer carry the list; device answers no longer carry chains.
- The confirm and the revoke take `{"version","statement"}`: the entry that the device signs after the head that it verified. A stale version is `409` (the client reads the list and signs once more), a bad statement `400`, a list past 256 entries `403 account_limit`. A recovery starts a new list.
- Clients verify the list from the root they pinned. They pin the highest version and hash they verified, and an older list or another history verifies no device. The account file goes to version 3: root, pin, devices of the list, keys that left.
- A device confirmed by a device that later left stays a device: its `add` comes before the `remove`, also for clients that join later.

## Signers of a vault store

- The keys that may sign heads come from the client's own trust store only: the devices of the verified list, and a device that left only for versions up to the store's anchor. A store goes on past a head that such a device pushed before it left.
- No answer of Connect (a group, a store marked shared, a device it lists) adds a signer. A session of the account key accepts no head until it has its policy, and a running session follows the policy of the latest refresh.
- No step of this version pins the root of another account, so devices of other accounts sign nothing.

## Relay

- A revoke and a group removal take the device out of its vault stores in the same directory transaction: the map rows go, with a waiting removal for each store file. The files apply them after the commit, when they open, or at the maintenance pass.
- A store device of another account signs in only while both accounts are active members of one group. The store token step checks the map again after it keeps the token.
- The recovery signature is checked first, and a valid one is never limited. Only failures count and are limited, per account and per client prefix.
- Used sign-in nonces have a bound for each key (`429` for that key only) as well as the global bound. Nonces run on a clock that never goes back.
- Maintenance prunes revoked device rows and recorded brain events after 90 days.

## Client

- `403 device_removed` counts as a removal only when the token call answers it.

## Contract and docs

connect-account-v1 (sections 1 to 15, fixtures regenerated with the device list), SPEC section 33, the Connect section of the trust model, and ios-core-v1 5.14.

## Tests

- Relay: signed list (history kept, `409` on an old head, bounded), recovery limits that never block a valid signature, per-key nonces, the nonce clock, and store sign-in that needs the group.
- App:
  - Rollback, fork, and changed-entry lists verify nothing.
  - A removal reaches other devices, and a restored account file catches up.
  - A device that a later-removed device confirmed still verifies on a later device.
  - In a store, a key that Connect lists signs nothing, also with an active group and a store marked shared.
  - A device that left keeps its merged head and signs nothing later.
  - `device_removed` from another route is not a removal.
- iPhone core: same verification checks, also with an active group.

body:
> **Do not merge before migration `20261110000100` is on production.** The nightly `graph-sync` on `main` would otherwise commit the graph and then fail every night on an RPC that does not exist. Matt's OK is needed for the push.

## What

The nightly Neo4j sync (#174) now computes three signals per Bev **from the graph**, inside its existing transaction, stores them on the nodes, and writes them back to Postgres for the app:

| Signal | How | Stored as |
|---|---|---|
| **Taste family** | `louvainCommunities(attributeProjection(…))`: Bevs clustered on the flavour bases and notes they share, read back from `(:Flavor)` / `(:Note)` | `(:Bev)-[:IN_COMMUNITY {hub}]->(:Community {id, size})`, `Bev.community`, `bev_graph_stats.community_id` |
| **Centrality** | weighted `pageRank` over `SIMILAR_TO` | `Bev.pagerank`, `strength`, `degree` |
| **Bridge** | `participationCoefficient`: the share of a Bev's `SIMILAR_TO` weight going to other families | `Bev.bridge` |

Every formula is `@bevi/ranking`'s (#172, #176); Cypher only extracts the adjacency and the memberships. No `gds.*` call.

**Why taste families and not `SIMILAR_TO` communities.** Measured on the live graph: Louvain over `SIMILAR_TO` rediscovers the root categories (84% category purity), while the flavour projection gives ten families that cut across them (46%): citrus/lemon-lime 50, berry 49, tropical 47, tea 46, orange/grape/apple 41, cola 36, coffee 34, root-beer/ginger/cream 32, mineral/herbal 29, beer+wine 20, and Yakult alone. They are driven mostly by the hand-labelled flavour base plus shared words in names; the clustering merges 23 uneven labels into ten broad families and places Bevs whose base is `other` or missing.

## Changes

- **`scripts/graph/analytics-core.ts`** (pure) and the analytics phase in `sync.ts`: after the mirror sweep, read the Bev ids, `SIMILAR_TO` and memberships back from the graph, compute, write, sweep stale `Community` / `IN_COMMUNITY`, and extend the in-transaction verification to 32 checks (one family per Bev, one hub per family, sizes, property types, Σ PageRank = 1).
- **After the commit**, `replace_bev_graph_stats` writes one generation to Postgres, retried up to three times on a transient error. If it still fails the run exits 1 saying the graph committed and Postgres was not updated; the next night repairs it. A dry run writes neither.
- **Migration `20261110000100`**: `bev_graph_stats` (RLS on, **no client policy**), the service-role-only `replace_bev_graph_stats` (validates the whole payload before deleting; `delete … where true`), and `get_prediction_snapshot()` with one added key, `bevGraph: [[bev_id, community_id, pagerank, bridge], …]`, visible Bevs only, `[]` never null. The function differs from `20261101000100`'s by exactly those added lines.
- **`packages/api/src/snapshot.ts`** maps `bevGraph` onto `snapshot.bevGraph` when the key is present. Nothing reads it yet: `recommend()`'s two options that do are off.
- `schema.cypher`: `community_id_unique`. `graph-query`'s `bev` template returns the three new properties.

**Privacy.** A family's public id is `c_` + 16 hex of an HMAC of its hub's Bev id, keyed with `BEVI_PSEUDONYM_SALT`: a hub can be an alcoholic Bev (on production the beer-and-wine family's hub is a wine), and catalog Bev ids are derivable from the public catalog, so neither the id nor a plain hash may reach a client. `bev_graph_stats` has no client policy because `community_size` counts hidden and alcoholic members; the snapshot is its only reader and emits neither that column nor a hidden Bev's row.

## Verification

| | Exit | |
|---|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck:scripts` | 0 | |
| `npm run test:scripts` | 0 | 307 tests (includes #179's dashboard tests, untouched) |
| `npm run typecheck` | 0 | |
| `npm test -w packages/api` | 0 | 99 passed, 20 live tests skipped |
| `npm run graph:schema` on the live instance | 0 | the one new constraint; idempotent |
| `graph:sync --fixture` on the live instance | 0 | 32 checks equal; rolled back; instance unchanged |

- The `--fixture` run (catalog source, rolled back) gives 11 families, modularity 0.652, category purity 0.47, 286 of 380 Bevs with edges into more than one family.
- Read-only on the committed production graph, this code reproduces the measurement above exactly: 1,422 memberships, 7,306 projected pairs, sizes 50/49/47/46/41/36/34/32/29/20/1, modularity 0.648.
- Stale-family sweep: generation A then a changed generation B in one rolled-back transaction, with a negative control that fails four checks without the sweep and none with it.

**Never executed, and where it first runs**

- All SQL (`20261110000100`, pgTAP `30`, 81 assertions): no local database. **CI's `db` job on this PR is its first execution.**
- The Postgres write-back and the analytics phase's commit path: first real `graph-sync` after the migration is on production and this merges. I will dispatch it as a `dry_run` first.
- `deno check` on `graph-query`: CI.

## Heads-up for Arjun

- Your lane, built from Matt's side; review after the fact is welcome.
- Rotating `BEVI_PSEUDONYM_SALT` now renames every taste family as well as every `(:User)`.
- With this partition `bridge` is non-zero for most Bevs (median 0.62): `SIMILAR_TO` is category-driven and the families cut across categories. A high value is not rare.
- #179's dashboard will show `(:Community)` nodes (named by their opaque id) and `IN_COMMUNITY` edges once a real sync has run; nothing breaks, but its own degree/PageRank shift because every Bev gains a neighbour, and its `degree` overwrites the stored one in the property panel (same key).
- On Neo4j 5.27-aura, a node whose properties were SET and which is then deleted in the same transaction is still returned by a seek on its uniqueness index. The sync never does both to one node; it is documented in `docs/graph.md`.

body:
Closes #664

## What changes

- **Shared run code** (`run.rs`): `POST /api/notebooks/run` now goes through `RunRequest::parse` and `run_notebook(state, request, extra_env)`, and `notebooks.run` calls the same function. The HTTP behaviour is unchanged, and #659's tests pass as before.
- **`notebooks.run`** (`host.rs`) takes `{ path, params?, timeout?, save? }` and returns `{ path, status, results, error? }`.
  - **Grant:** it needs the `[host] run` grant, which defaults to `[]`. A call outside it fails `denied` and names `[host] run` and `ganymede grant … run=`.
  - **Grants narrow:** the run's kernel gets the intersection of the caller's `read`/`run` and the run notebook's, and `edit_self` is off, because a run writes nothing. It also keeps every grant up its chain, and a path must pass each with symlinks resolved, so a grant naming a symlink can't reach past the caller's.
  - **Revokes:** once a slot frees, the caller's grant is read and checked again. A running run keeps the grant it started with (reference.md says so).
  - **Finding the run's kernel:** the server sets a launch variable, `GANYMEDE_HOST_RUN`, naming the run. It reads that from its own record of the kernel's launch variables (`RunningKernel::launch_var`, new in ganymede-api), so the kernel can't claim another run's grant. This also means it doesn't depend on whether `hello` arrives before the call learns the kernel id. The grant entry is dropped when the call ends; a run kernel with no entry gets nothing.
  - **Depth and width:** runs nest at most 3 deep, and each calling kernel has at most 2 runs in flight (a semaphore). Further runs wait.
  - **Cancel:** the comm aborts the call's future. The run's `KernelGuard` then shuts the kernel down, and the slot frees. On the normal path `run_notebook` shuts the kernel down before answering, so a slot frees only once its kernel is gone.
  - **`hello`** lists `notebooks.run` when the run grant isn't empty and the depth allows another level.
- **CLI:** `ganymede grant NOTEBOOK run=PATH`, plus `--revoke … run=PATH | run`.
- **Docs:** reference.md (`[host] run`, the sample config, `grant run=`), docs/host-api.md "What's built", a dev-log note, and the module doc.
- **Not here:** `save: "copy"` still waits on the run contract's copies (#652). Wiring into `ganymede execute` and the apps' granting sheet come later.

## Verification

- [x] Tests (all fail without the change):
  - `a_notebook_runs_another_under_its_run_grant` (tests/host.rs) checks:
    - a granted run returns named results
    - an ungranted path is `denied`
    - the run's kernel has the called notebook as `notebook`, no `self.*`, and reads narrowed to the intersection
    - a nested run from the run's kernel works
    - cancelling shuts the run's kernel down
  - `a_kernel_has_two_runs_in_flight_at_most`: three concurrent runs never have more than two kernels at once.
  - `runs_nest_at_most_three_deep`: `hello` at each level, and the `3 deep` denial.
  - `a_run_reads_through_no_symlink_its_caller_may_not`: a callee grant naming a symlink in the caller's folder doesn't widen the run.
  - `a_run_waiting_for_a_slot_sees_a_revoked_grant`.
  - `intersect_keeps_what_both_grants_cover` (unit test).
  - `grant_stores_lists_and_revokes_a_notebooks_grant` (cli.rs) now covers `run=`.
  - #659's `notebooks_run_answers_with_named_results` still passes on the shared code.
- [x] By hand: none. CI runs all of the above.
- [x] Docs updated. The host API section and the `grant` row already carry the **Unreleased.** note.
- [x] New dependencies: none. `tokio::sync::Semaphore` comes from the existing tokio.
- [x] API change: `RunningKernel::launch_var` (ganymede-api, read-only) and the new host method. No REST or websocket change.
- [x] Dev-log note: docs/notes/2026-11-11-host-run.md
- [x] Kind: production. With the default `[host] run = []`, nothing can run.

body:
Closes #980

Fixes the Windows failures on `main` (windows CI only runs on pushes to main, so PR checks never showed them):

- `SystemFileReplacer`: on Windows an existing target is replaced with `File.Replace`; `File.Move(overwrite)` throws `UnauthorizedAccessException` when a reader has the file open, even with `FileShare.Delete` (real bug, introduced with `AtomicFile` in #959). Other systems keep the move. Fixes `AtomicFileTests.GivenAReaderIsOpen_...`.
- `SiteCache`: the disk lock is a non-fair monitor, so a flush could retake it after every file and a read waited behind the whole batch (real starvation, #935). Reads announce themselves and the flush lets waiting reads in before each file step (bounded to 50 ms per step). Fixes `IssueCacheTests.GivenASlowBatchFlush_...`; docs updated.
- `ExternalEditor`: optional `TimeProvider` seam instead of `Stopwatch`; the Windows "returns at once" test depended on real time under 1 s and took 6 s on a cold runner (test assumption). New test for the slow-return case. Not weakened.
- `CancelOffUiThreadTests` failed only on ubuntu in two older runs; already fixed by #969.

Reviewer: approve with comments; all findings fixed (yield for every file step, bounded wait, docs). Not verifiable on Linux: the Windows paths, gated by a `ci.yml` dispatch with `os=windows` on this branch.

body:
For #905

**Galaxy**
- Galaxy was the most expensive mode in the output CPU profile of a real scene. Per frame and per star (2,600): a colour, an rgba string, and a `fillStyle` parse.
- Stars are now sorted once into 48 rings by their fixed radius, and the colour is set once per ring.
- 48 is a multiple of the 16 bands, so a ring's stars share band, energy and size. Additive blending is order-independent. Positions still use each star's own radius.

Measured at 1920×1080 in Electron, old vs new code, five runs each, twice:

| | ms per frame |
|---|---:|
| before | 2.83–3.22 |
| after | 0.40–0.44 |

Pixel cost: colour along the radius now moves in 48 steps.
- Mean absolute difference: 0.036 / 255 per channel.
- 5 % of lit pixels differ by more than 8 levels; most are stars that cross the palette wrap.
- Not visible side by side.
- The Galaxy templates' export changes accordingly; nothing else in `generative.js` changed.

**Cued monitor**
- A scene that had never been live showed only its gradient and a layer list.
- It now shows its MilkDrop preset's rendered thumbnail, or the shipped rendered thumbnail of its top visual or background mode (`modes:thumbs`).
- Verified live: an `sv-thumb://` image, loaded, no console errors.
- A continuous second render of the cued scene was deliberately not built: on the same GPU it would take frames from the live output, which is the main complaint being fixed.

**Gates**
- unit tests 4387 / 1 skip (`tests/galaxy-rings.test.js`, 3);
- self-test PASS;
- 15 Galaxy-owned thumbnails redrawn.

Remove and Block ask for confirmation first. - **Friend Requests** page: Accept / Remove for incoming requests, and Cancel for ones you've sent. - **Search**: live search through `/users/filtered`, with each result's button matching your relationship (Add +, Requested, Accept), plus your matching friends below. - **Other people's profiles**, reached by tapping anyone (friends list, search, requests, or a participant in an activity): - Every Figma state: **Add as Friend**, **Request Sent** (tap to cancel), **Accept Request / Deny**, and **Friends**. - The red **Interests + Hobbies** card. For friends it also shows the tilted WhatsApp / Instagram badges, which open their links. - Friends get **Activities by {name}** (tap opens the activity drawer). Everyone else gets the dashed "Add {name} to see their upcoming activities!" box. - **⋯ menu** with **Add to Activity Type** (pick which of your types they belong to), Remove as friend, copy/share link, report and block. - Accepting a request shows the **Success!** sheet with **Add to Activity Type**. - Pressing Back on any tab other than Home now goes to Home before leaving the app. - Fixes a crash on Home when the feed request fails, for example with no network. # Releases
## @cosyte/ccda@0.1.11

### Patch Changes

- ac7a5bb: `editCcda` holds less memory again on the small documents a feed edits all day. The edited XML, the
  returned document, its warnings and every error are unchanged, and no caller needs to change
  anything.

  - On a source whose XML is in the form our writer gives it, the edit now reads only the elements it
    looks at (the header, the body's sections and every `ID`), not a tree of the whole document, and
    builds the new section and header elements without `@xmldom/xmldom`. It writes them as the same
    serializer wrote them before, so the bytes are the same. A parse records whether its document's
    XML is in that form, so an edit of a parsed document does not read the XML whole to find out.
  - An edit reports whether it was made on the text or fell back to a DOM on the `cosyte:ccda:edit`
    channel of `node:diagnostics_channel`, as `{ path: "text" }` or `{ path: "dom" }`, only while
    something subscribes. Our benchmarks read it.

author: cisterciansis
body:
Phase 1 of `docs/box-scaling.md` (#2957), the agentd half. Stacked on #3001; the two commits here are the last two. `crates/arbos-boxd` is not started: it needs Linux with `runsc` to build and prove.

## `POST /box/prepare-sleep`
Same bearer as `/box/state`. No body.
- **409** `{ok:false, reason}` while the box is starting, a turn runs, sends wait, or a job is running or queued. Checked before the work and again after. A job parked on an approval card does not count, so an open card does not hold a box awake.
- **200** `{ok, files_bytes, scratch_bytes, trash_bytes, active_user_pids, user_pids, purged_bytes, trash_removed, vacuumed}`.
- It truncates the WAL (and vacuums past 25% free pages), removes `/work/.trash` entries older than 7 days, and reads each workspace cgroup's `cgroup.procs`.
- It never exits agentd. SIGTERM already is the flush-and-exit path, so the supervisor reads the report and then stops or checkpoints.

Narrower than the spec's wording, on purpose:
- Caches and `/tmp` are purged only on the clean path (no process in any workspace cgroup). A box about to be checkpointed keeps them: an `npx` dev server runs out of `~/.npm`.
- Playwright's cache is left out: it holds installed browsers nothing re-downloads. Adding it is one entry in `SLEEP_CACHES`.
- `active_user_pids` is `null`, not 0, when a cgroup cannot be read. Unknown must not read as a clean stop.

## SIGUSR1
Drops every relay connection (rooms, HTTP pools, the voice link), skips backoff, and re-posts `/box/hello`. For after `runsc restore`, where sockets are dead but look open. The push poll, keep-alive and goals calls also gain the existing 10 s timeout, since a request caught by a checkpoint never answers.

An agentd older than this dies on SIGUSR1, so boxd must gate on version.

## Approval-card timers
Nothing to remove: main already has "cards never expire".

## Verified
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p arbos-agentd --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p arbos-agentd --locked` on macOS: 10 new tests pass; the failing set is identical to the base's (process-tree tests that pass on Linux CI).

## Not verified (Linux only)
- Real `cgroup.procs` reads, SIGUSR1 through `runsc kill`, and whether sockets hang rather than reset after a restore.

## Needs the owner
- Purge runs only on the clean path, and Playwright's cache is left out: both keep a restored box identical to the one that was frozen.
- "Scratch" on the Machine card is everything under `.arbos`.
- Where runsc gives the sandbox no writable cgroup v2, `active_user_pids` is `null` and the box is checkpointed rather than stopped clean. Measured on a real host in #3008; correct, just not the cheap path.

author: dcshzj
body:
## Problem MDDI's gov.sg SEO/GEO audit (item #19) found that Isomer pages render a visible breadcrumb but emit no `BreadcrumbList` structured data, so search engines get no explicit signal of a page's position in the site hierarchy. Separately, the existing `WebPage` JSON-LD used slash-less URLs (`/about-us`) while the canonical link, `og:url` and `sitemap.xml` all use the served trailing-slash URL (`/about-us/`), because sites are exported with `trailingSlash: true`. Closes ISOM-2698 ## Solution `getPageJsonLd` now nests a `BreadcrumbList` in the page's `WebPage` entity. It is built with `getBreadcrumbFromSiteMap`, the same sitemap walk that drives the visible breadcrumb, so names and order always match what users see. - Emitted on **every** page, including layouts that do not display a breadcrumb (homepage, search). The homepage gets a single `Home` item; Google's Rich Results Test accepts this as valid. - Every `ListItem` has `position` (1-based), `name` and an absolute `item` URL ending in `/`, matching the canonical URL. - If the sitemap walk stops early, the trail is emitted as-is, matching the visible breadcrumb. - `page.tsx` passes the sitemap into `getPageJsonLd`. This runs at build time in a server component; only the serialised JSON-LD reaches the HTML. Expected impact: explicit hierarchy for search engines and control over the breadcrumb trail shown in **desktop** Google results (Google stopped showing breadcrumbs on mobile in Jan 2025). Structured data is not a ranking factor, and there is no evidence it affects AI answer engine visibility, so this is SEO hygiene rather than a GEO lever. **Breaking Changes** - [ ] Yes - this PR contains breaking changes - [x] No - this PR is backwards compatible The `@id` of the `WebPage` entity changes from `…/page#webpage` to `…/page/#webpage`. It is only referenced within the same page's JSON-LD. **Features**: - `BreadcrumbList` structured data on every published page. **Improvements**: - Extracted a `withTrailingSlash` helper, now shared by `getSitemapXml` and `getPageJsonLd`. **Bug Fixes**: - `WebPage.url` and `@id` now use the trailing-slash URL, consistent with the canonical link, `og:url` and `sitemap.xml`. ## Before & After Screenshots No visual change. Example JSON-LD for `/services/grants/startup-grant/`: **BEFORE**: ```json { "@type": "WebPage", "@id": "https://www.isomer.gov.sg/services/grants/startup-grant#webpage", "url": "https://www.isomer.gov.sg/services/grants/startup-grant" } ``` **AFTER**: ```json { "@type": "WebPage", "@id": "https://www.isomer.gov.sg/services/grants/startup-grant/#webpage", "url": "https://www.isomer.gov.sg/services/grants/startup-grant/", "breadcrumb": { "@type": "BreadcrumbList", "itemListElement": [ { "@type": "ListItem", "position": 1, "name": "Home", "item": "https://www.isomer.gov.sg/" }, { "@type": "ListItem", "position": 2, "name": "Services", "item": "https://www.isomer.gov.sg/services/" }, { "@type": "ListItem", "position": 3, "name": "Grants & Schemes", "item": "https://www.isomer.gov.sg/services/grants/" }, { "@type": "ListItem", "position": 4, "name": "Start-up Grant", "item": "https://www.isomer.gov.sg/services/grants/startup-grant/" } ] } } ``` ## Tests - Unit tests in `metadata.test.ts` cover a top-level page, a nested page, the homepage (single `Home` item), a page that does not display a breadcrumb (search), and the trailing-slash `WebPage` URLs. - Verified on the local template dev server across homepage, content, index, auto-generated folder index, collection, article, database and search layouts, plus a broken sitemap walk. On every page the JSON-LD trail matched the visible breadcrumb, all JSON-LD parsed, and a title containing `` stayed escaped. - Rendered JSON-LD passed Google's Rich Results Test with Breadcrumbs and Organization detected as valid and no warnings. **Manual Verification Steps**: - [ ] After release, rebuild a site (e.g. gov.sg) and open a nested page, such as an article inside a collection. - [ ] View the page source and find the `application/ld+json` script whose `@type` is `WebPage`. Confirm it has a `breadcrumb` whose items match the visible breadcrumb in name and order, with absolute URLs ending in `/`. - [ ] Confirm `WebPage.url` equals the `` href, including the trailing slash. - [ ] Open the homepage source and confirm the `breadcrumb` contains a single `Home` item. - [ ] Run the nested page URL through https://search.google.com/test/rich-results and confirm "Breadcrumbs" is detected as valid with no errors.

PR Summary by Qodo

Add BreadcrumbList structured data to every page ✨ Enhancement 🐞 Bug fix 🧪 Tests 🕐 20-40 Minutes
AI Description

>
>• Add sitemap-derived BreadcrumbList data to every page’s WebPage JSON-LD, including homepage and
>  search pages.
>• Align WebPage URLs and identifiers with served trailing-slash URLs.
>• Test breadcrumb hierarchy, page coverage, and URL fallbacks.
>
Diagram

```mermaid graph TD Sitemap["Site sitemap"] --> Helper["Breadcrumb helper"] --> Builder["JSON-LD builder"] --> Entity["WebPage entity"] --> Script["HTML script"] Page["Page schema"] --> Builder Config["Site URL"] --> Builder ```
High-Level Assessment

>Building the list in the existing WebPage JSON-LD generator and reusing the visible breadcrumb’s sitemap traversal keeps both hierarchies consistent. A separate traversal or standalone JSON-LD emitter would duplicate page-hierarchy logic without a clear benefit.

author: ruibincheung
body:
## Why

vLLM lifecycle hooks, operator wrappers, and native fallback handling were managed in separate places, making repeated installation and restoration difficult to coordinate. Introduce a private `HookRegistry` to own declarations, installed bindings, and saved originals, and keep Muse Spark's deferred normalization and expert routes consistent.

## Scope

- Centralize worker hooks in the `bootstrap` phase and operator routes in `device_ready`. Both registration entry points share the bootstrap coordinator; repeated installation preserves wrapper identity, and installation after `restore()` captures the current native targets. Keep `vllm_route` as the public declaration API and make installation/version helpers private.
- Coalesce equivalent hook stacks when different target names resolve to the same `(owner, attr)`, including AITER compatibility module aliases. Preserve every declaration's saved-original handle and validator, reject incompatible hooks or cross-phase writes, and keep distinct re-exported bindings separate.
- Add `vllm_route(..., group=...)` so dependent routes are skipped together if any member does not support the installed vLLM version. Group Muse Spark's deferred norm and experts routes, and use saved originals for the compound fallback: native normalization followed by native experts.
- Update lifecycle, route, and restore tests; add English and Chinese plugin tutorials; and move the existing `_wv_split_krc` route from `layers/gemm.py` to `layers/utils/api.py`. State the removal criteria for AITER GEMM, MoE, and attention routes: the AITER plugin must work inside vLLM custom ops under `torch.compile` and CUDA graphs and preserve measured speedups for all workloads those routes serve. Existing normalization fusion and kernel algorithms are unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

Each phase resolves targets, validates signatures and conflicts, and builds ordered wrappers before writing any bindings. Preparation failures leave targets unchanged, and binding-write failures roll back earlier writes in the batch. This makes incompatible selected hooks fail phase installation; registration and restoration are intended for startup and cleanup, not concurrent runtime reconfiguration.

## Verification

**Environment**: Head `38b263e1dfb7f452e31a0b7c7329d7c1c6d0dcd5`; local Conda environment with Python 3.12.9, PyTorch 2.9.1+cu128, pytest 9.1.1, and Triton 3.5.1. CPU test selection on a host with NVIDIA H200 / CUDA 12.8; no gfx950 or ROCm. vLLM, AITER, and FlyDSL are not installed.

**Gate overrides**: None. No AKLR/AITER environment overrides were used to loosen checks.

### Code

```bash
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 python -B -m pytest \
  -p no:cacheprovider -q -rs \
  tests/core/runtime/test_dispatch.py \
  tests/plugins/vllm/test_hook.py \
  tests/plugins/vllm/test_muse_spark.py \
  -m 'not gpu'
```

Result: **63 passed, 11 skipped, 6 deselected**. Nine checks requiring vLLM were skipped because it is not installed; two checks require a gfx950 GPU. Six GPU cases were deselected.

Tests isolate and restore registry state and provide fake vLLM callers and callees. Worker bootstrap coverage includes feature switches, grouped version filtering, call order, return values, and repeated-wrapper identity. Alias regressions reproduce installation through two module names resolving to one binding, exercise distinct re-exported bindings sharing a native callable, and verify incompatible-hook/cross-phase rejection and every alias validator before writes. Restoration and reinstallation capture replaced natives through both paths.

Muse Spark CPU tests install both actual grouped routes and force the fused op to return `NOT_MEASURED` or `NOT_WARMED`. They assert deferred normalization, exactly one saved-native norm call before saved-native experts receive its output, and the same behavior after replacing both natives and reinstalling. Both full and `device_ready` restoration are covered. Existing fallback and `torch.compile(backend="eager")` guard checks are retained.

All 14 changed Python files passed Ruff 0.15.12 checks, Ruff formatting checks, and syntax checks. Pre-commit passed on the six files updated for review, and `git diff --check` passed. Schema and measurement versions are unchanged; kernel results relative to `main` have not been measured.

## Not run

CI full-schema validation has not run on this change. Actual vLLM/AITER inference, GPU accuracy, CUDA graph execution, and performance were not validated in this local CPU run. The regression tests check preparation failure without binding changes; they do not exercise rollback after a partial binding write.

## Risk

Affects: Worker initialization and all declared vLLM operator routes, particularly Muse Spark's deferred normalization and expert fallback.

If wrong: Hook installation can fail at startup, or fallback can apply incorrect normalization or invoke the wrong native target. The wrapper's performance impact is unmeasured.

Undo: Revert this PR and restart workers to restore the previous implementation. Setting `AKLR_VLLM_PLUGIN=0` and restarting disables operator routes; the core startup hook remains active.

author: jdno
body:
The workflow that updates the tool pins in Renovate's pull requests pinned the action, and the Renovate preset of that action, to the head commit of aonyx-ai/rakko-update PR 2, because the action was not on the default branch of its repository yet. That pull request has merged as a squash, so no branch holds the pinned commit anymore, and GitHub can stop serving it at any time. Both now point at `main` of aonyx-ai/rakko-update: the action through its merge commit with a `# main` comment, so that Renovate moves the pin, and the preset by its plain name.

The action now presents its work as an update, so the workflow follows it. The workflow is named "Rakko", its job is "Update the tool pins", and its concurrency group is keyed on the action rather than on the name of the workflow, as the documentation of the action shows. Only "All checks succeeded" is a required check here, so the new job name needs no change of the branch protection.

author: vantrangradion
body:
Adds optional `sandbox.agent` so each agent session runs in a container from the sandbox image instead of on the host. Closes the "agent session is not sandboxed and can reach Docker" gap from #6.

- Container sees only the clone at `/work` (`.git` read-only), a fresh tmpfs home per session, and the agy login token from a Docker volume
- No Docker socket, `--cap-drop ALL`, read-only root fs, host uid, no host env; network on (agy needs the model)
- `agentic-loop login`: one-time seat sign-in per machine (paste-code flow), saves only the token to `agentic-loop-agy-auth`
- Preflight before each run checks the image has agy and the volume has a login; run record names the agy version
- Shared session helpers pulled out of `AntigravityCliRunner`; CI `run` refuses `sandbox.agent` for now
- Verified with real Docker and a real agy session: file written with host uid, `.git` write refused, no `docker.sock`, no `/Users`
- Remaining gap (README): open network and a readable model token, so the agent could still send repo contents out

author: szeremeta1
body:
## What a listener noticed

With music on a network share over a slow or lossy link, the app sometimes froze (the spinning pointer, Force Quit) right after a song change: after pressing Next or double-clicking a song a second time, or by itself when one song ended into the next. The share was mounted the whole time; it had only stopped answering for some seconds.

## Cause

Two requests to the share were made where the main thread waits for them. Both were reproduced on `main` with a real SMB mount whose server can hold its answers, and the main thread's stack was sampled while it was frozen.

1. **Closing a copied song's file inside the playback cache's lock.** `close` on an SMB mount sends the server a close and waits (measured: 8.3 s for a close made while the server held its answers for 8 s). When play is pressed on another song than the one copied ahead, the cache lets go of that copy (`next = nil`) inside its lock, its last reference ends there, and the file is closed there. Every press of play or skip takes the same lock on the main thread (`PlaybackEngine.play` → `warmStaging` → `NetworkPlaybackCache.warm`), and the engine thread waits for it too (`prefetch`). Sampled stack: main thread in `NetworkPlaybackCache.warm` → `NSLock` wait; the lock's holder in `Entry.deinit` → `Storage.deinit` → `close`. Four presses of Next 0.7 s apart with the server held for 25 s: the second press came back after 23.5 s. The same close also ran on the engine thread when a skip dropped the song before it: the song skipped to did not start and Stop did nothing until the share answered.
2. **Asking the share what a song's path is, from the player's poll.** When a song from a share plays and its copy is complete, the poll on the main thread hands the copy to the offline cache (`NetworkCache.adopt`). `adopt` made the song's URL with `URL(fileURLWithPath:)`, which asks the file system whether the path is a folder (`lstat`): a request to the share, made inside the cache's lock. Sampled stack with the server held while one song ended into the next: main thread in `PlayerController.poll` → `NetworkCache.adopt` → `URL.init(fileURLWithPath:)` → `lstat`. (`Track.fileURL` exists to avoid exactly this; `adopt` did not use it.)

## Fix

- The share's files are closed on a queue of their own (`NetworkPlaybackCache.closing`). A copy hands its open file there when it is torn down or opens the file again after a remount, a file opened for nothing goes there too, and the real handle closes there whoever lets go of it. The hand-over takes the reference out of its owner first, so the queue's release is the last one.
- The cache lets go of entries after its lock, not inside it (`prefetch`, the press-time warm-up).
- `NetworkCache.adopt` and `request` use `Track.fileURL` (made from the path alone). The same in two places that only wanted a name or an extension: the artwork resolver (off the main thread) and the message shown when a scan stops because the share did not answer (on the main thread, about that very share).
- A song whose file the share never opens is given up after two minutes with "The share is mounted but isn't answering", as a song whose reads never return already was. Before, the open was waited for without end ("Buffering from the network"; skip and stop did get through).
- When the share did not answer for a song and the next one would be read from a share too, playback stops there with that reason instead of waiting two minutes for each of up to eight songs in turn. A next song with a copy on this Mac, or one that is not on a share, plays.

Unchanged: at most eight songs in a row are tried when songs fail for other reasons (a missing file fails at once: seven missing songs were passed in 160 ms and playback stopped, with the main thread free).

## Tested

- New `ShareCloseTests` (a share handle whose close can be held). Both fail on `main`:
  - play pressed twice while the copied next song's file cannot be closed: the second press never came back; now it does while the close still waits;
  - the engine: a skip to another song plays, and Stop gets through, while the earlier songs' files cannot be closed yet.
- New `QuietShareTests`: an open that never returns ends with `notAnswering` (before: never); after a song the share did not answer for, the next songs on a share are not opened (before: each was, in turn); a next song on this Mac plays (passes before and after).

There is no failing-first unit test for the `adopt` freeze: `lstat` cannot be made to wait without a network mount. It was shown on the SMB mount, before and after.

- Not run against the share and the outputs the freezes were first seen with. macOS took no sample of those freezes, so their stacks are not known; what matches is the sequence (a song change while the share's health check reports it slow, then no log line from the main thread or the engine thread until the share answers).

- After a share did not answer, a next song on another share that does answer is not tried either (the engine tells a share's song by its cache key, not by which share). Pressing play on it plays it.

author: silthus
body:
## Problem

`fleet packs --remove X` drops X from the plan. Files, provider config, MCP servers, plugins, jobs and T3 parts then go away on the next `fleet apply`, because each keeps a record. Steps keep none. A step's `undo` ran only while its pack was on and its workflow off, so a pack that left the profile left its steps' work behind on every machine.

## Change

- Each machine keeps a **step ledger** in `~/.local/state/fleet/steps.json`. It holds every step that has an `undo` and whose check held in an apply, with the `check`, `undo` and prerequisite probe it had then.
- `fleet apply` undoes each step that the ledger holds and the plan no longer has, for any reason: its pack left the profile, or the machine no longer fits it (OS, role, AI plan). It uses the commands the step had when it last applied, because an off pack's manifest is not in the plan.
- A pack that the profile still lists but cannot load (a source outage, or an unmet `requires`) keeps its steps.
- `fleet doctor` and `fleet apply --dry-run` show these undos as they already show a workflow's undo. A failed undo is reported, and the next apply tries again.
- A ledger that does not parse stops the apply, rather than forget what it would undo.

The ledger is per machine, so each machine cleans its own steps when a pack leaves the shared profile.

## Not in this PR

- A nested `fleet <cmd>` still refuses a command of an off pack (exit 2). The next PR lets it run that command only for an undo the ledger names.
- Human steps and pack secrets stay with a person; `fleet doctor` will list them in a later PR.

## Tests

`src/reconciler/resolve.test.ts`, "a step's undo": pack removed from the profile, step dropped for another reason (using the ledger's undo, not the new manifest's), a pack that cannot load, a step that never held, waiting on the prerequisite, a failed undo retried, and a broken ledger file. Mutation-checked: without the outage guard, or without recording, the tests fail.

`bun run typecheck` passes. `bun run test` on the devbox: the failures are the known environmental ones (gitleaks missing for the privacy scan, the heavy slice, tracker origins); the files that timed out under load pass when run alone.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


## Review round 1 (GPT-6.1 Sol)

Fixed in 8bf1b0a, each with a test that fails without it:
- ✅ Two applies at once lost each other's ledger entries. The ledger now changes one entry per write, re-read from disk.
- ✅ A step that moved to another pack was undone after the new pack's step held. Steps of a pack that is off are now undone before the steps run.
- ✅ A workflow-off undo used the changed manifest commands. The commands the ledger recorded now win.
- ✅ An apply that stopped lost the steps that had already held. Each step is now recorded as soon as it holds.
- ✅ A step that changed state and then exited nonzero was never recorded. Its check now runs after a failed run.
- ✅ Two steps with the same id kept only one undo. A step with an undo now needs an id that no other step of its pack uses.
- ✅ A ledger that is a symlink was followed. The ledger must now be a regular file under real directories.

Decisions:
- 👤 **Undos for workflow-off and "no longer planned" steps still run after the steps.** This keeps main's rule that a pack whose step failed in this apply undoes nothing.
- 👤 **A check of a pack that is off, such as `fleet x check`, exits 2 on this layer alone.** #107 makes it exit 3 (cannot tell). The stack merges bottom-up in one session, so no machine runs this layer alone.


## Review round 2 (GPT-6.1 Sol)

- ✅ Two Fleet processes could still read the ledger at once, and the later write dropped the other's step. Fixed in 910776e: each change holds a lock directory next to the ledger for its read and write. A test with two Bun processes, each recording 20 steps at once, keeps all 40.
- 👤 **No third review round.** The fix is one lock around one read and write, and a test that runs two real processes covers it.

author: hyper-ff
body:
## Why I'm doing:

`SELECT dict_merge(c, 255) FROM t [_META_]` fails with `deserialize chunk data failed`, or crashes the receiving BE/CN in `BinaryColumnSerde::deserialize`. `CacheDictManager` issues this query in the background for low-cardinality dictionaries, so production clusters can crash without any user query.

The meta reader produces `dict_merge` and `flat_json_meta` meta columns as `ARRAY<VARCHAR>`. The `Column` that describes these meta columns keeps the table column's type (`VARCHAR` / `JSON`). The slot built from it (`SlotDescriptor.setColumn` → origin type → `toThrift`) reaches the backend with that type. The receiver builds its chunk meta from the slot types, so it decodes the array stream with the `VARCHAR` layout.

The wrong type only matters when the meta scan's own chunks cross a serializing exchange:
- **One-phase aggregate.** In a two-phase plan the update aggregate is in the same fragment as the meta scan, so only aggregate results cross the exchange.
- **The exchange serializes.** This happens across nodes, or with `enable_exchange_pass_through=false`.

Reproduced on a single ASAN BE on main:

```sql
CREATE TABLE t2 (k BIGINT NOT NULL, c VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL)
  DUPLICATE KEY(k) DISTRIBUTED BY HASH(k) BUCKETS 1 PROPERTIES ("replication_num" = "1");
INSERT INTO t2 VALUES (1,'a'),(2,'b');
INSERT INTO t2 VALUES (3,'a'),(4,'c');
SET new_planner_agg_stage = 1;
SET enable_exchange_pass_through = false;
SELECT dict_merge(c, 255) FROM t2 [_META_];
-- BE: binary_column.h:150 Check failed: _bytes.size() == _offsets.back() (12 vs. 0)
--     ProtobufChunkDeserializer::deserialize <- DataStreamRecvr::SenderQueue::_deserialize_chunk
```

The default settings, and `new_planner_agg_stage = 1` on its own, return the correct result.

## What I'm doing:

Fixes #82831

Give these meta columns their real type in the rules that create them. `count` / `column_size` / `column_compressed_size` already get this treatment (`BIGINT`, see #17619 / #49690):
- `PushDownAggToMetaScanRule`: the copied column for `dict_merge` gets `ARRAY<VARCHAR>`.
- `PushDownFlatJsonMetaToMetaScanRule`: the rule used to put the table's own `Column` object into the meta scan. It now deep-copies the column and sets `ARRAY<VARCHAR>` on the copy, so the table schema is not touched.

Slots for min/max/count/column_size are sent exactly as before. The backend already ignores the slot type for these two meta columns and always builds `ARRAY<VARCHAR>`, so no BE change is needed, and FE/BE version skew is safe.

Observability: reviewed the existing error path (`deserialize chunk data failed ... There is probably a bug here`). This change removes a wrong input; no new signal is needed. Hardening `BinaryColumnSerde::deserialize` against malformed offsets (suggested in the issue, related to #81858) is left for a separate PR.

Tests: new `MetaScanSlotTypeTest` checks the thrift slot type of every meta aggregate across agg stages 0/1/2, and checks that the table schema is unchanged. Without the main-code change, 3 of its 4 cases fail. All existing FE test classes that use `[_META_]` pass, including LowCardinalityTest/LowCardinalityTest2, JsonTypeTest, MinMaxMonotonicRewriteTest, ScanTest, PipelineParallelismTest and AnalyzeStmtTest.

- `msgpackr-extract`: denied. Same: an optional native speed-up with a pure JavaScript fallback.

Entry added under Unreleased, Added, linking this pull request.

None.

body:
Refs #59. Second part after #69: no new API, only tests and CI, so that the next parts are checked on Linux too.

## Why

The `tests (linux)` job builds the static library. The binding tests that need the shared library (`RAVEN_BUILD_SHARED`), `binding_odin` among them, do not exist in that build, and `odin` is not on the runners. So neither the generated Odin package nor `raven_odin` has been run by CI so far.

## Change

- `bindings/CMakeLists.txt`: two tests next to `binding_odin`, with the same needs (odin, the shared library; not on Windows):
  - `binding_odin_wrapper`: the example of `raven_odin` with `--test`.
  - `binding_odin_wrapper_test`: `odin test raven_odin`, one thread (Raven has one UI thread).
- `.github/workflows/build.yml`: a job `odin (linux)`. It takes a release of Odin (`ODIN_VERSION: dev-2026-11`), builds the shared library and runs `ctest -R '^binding_odin' --no-tests=error`. Without `--no-tests=error` a missing `odin` would pass with no test run.
- `bindings/README.md`: the Odin row says tested by the build and names `raven_odin`; the sentence "no Odin compiler was available where it was written" is removed.

The existing jobs are not changed, and `release` does not wait for the new job.

## Verification

- Linux (the new job, on my fork, commit `72f9011`): Odin `dev-2026-11`, 3 of 3 tests pass (`binding_odin`, `binding_odin_wrapper`, `binding_odin_wrapper_test`). This is the first run of the Odin binding on Linux that I know of. All other jobs of that run pass.
- macOS 15 (Apple Silicon), Odin `dev-2026-11`: the same configure options as the job, `ctest -R '^binding_odin'`: 3 of 3 pass.
- `ctest -R '^binding_nothing' --no-tests=error` exits non-zero, as the guard needs.

Not covered: Windows (the binding tests are not registered there), and a checksum of the Odin download (the version is pinned, the file is not verified).

## Next parts

- The rest of the hand-written front door: capture, memory allocator, errors and logging, `run`, frame and error callbacks.
- Generated wrappers for the long tail, with a test that fails when the C API gains a function that is neither wrapped nor listed as raw only.

author: normb
body:
RUNNER-ORPHAN-LISTENER: a read-only check for the state that failed every job on two self-hosted runners on 2026-11-10.

## What happened

- Every job sent to two of the self-hosted runners failed in 2 s in `actions/checkout`.
- Each of the two had two `Runner.Listener` processes, so each job got two workers that wrote one log file.
- A unit had lost its main process (`run.sh`) eight days earlier. The unit sets `KillMode=process`, so systemd left the listener running outside the unit. `Restart=always` started a second `run.sh` about every 4 minutes; GitHub refused each as a second session, 1342 and 1345 times, and then accepted one.

## What this adds

- `scripts/runner-listeners.py` reports, per runner directory: other than exactly one process whose program is `<dir>/bin/Runner.Listener`, and a listener that does not descend from the main process of the unit whose working directory that is.
- Per unit: `NRestarts` higher than at the previous read, from two reads some minutes apart, or from a state file for a timer. A count that fell, or a high count that stands still, is not reported.
- Exit 0, 1 (findings, one per line) or 2 (could not read, or nothing to check).
- It only reads and needs no root. Every command goes through one function that refuses anything but `ps -eo`, `systemctl show` and `systemctl list-units`. It signals no process and writes no unit file.
- `docs/internals/build-ci-release.md` gains the how-to.

## What this does not change

- The units' `KillMode=process`. That is the machine owner's decision. The script prints a note for each unit that has it.
- Nothing runs the script on a schedule yet.

## Tests

- 78 in `scripts/tests/test_runner_listeners.py` (19 success, 39 failure, 20 edge). They give the functions text, and the tests that run the script give it a `PATH` whose `ps` and `systemctl` are stubs.
- 38 mutations, all red. One was green until `test_one_bad_row_among_good_ones_is_refused_not_skipped` was added.
- Run once on the runner machine, reading only: four directories, one listener each, exit 0, and three `KillMode=process` notes.

body:
## Summary

Efficiency is earned standard minutes divided by keyed production-department hours. Several copies of that formula had drifted. This puts them back on one rule (BUG-2026-11-11-501).

```diff
 buildPerfDays({ whe, jobCards, pics,
+  approvedExtraTime,          # required: dashboard route, KPI / board report, Floor Live
   productionDepts })

 dashboard Employees tile, worker rows, dept table (desktop + phone)
-  earned minutes of every day
+  earned minutes only on days with keyed production hours   # hasKeyedHours, same as poolEfficiencyPct
+  labour cost of every day (unchanged)

 Daily Efficiency email
-  efficiency = earned / hours in ALL departments
+  efficiency = (earned + approved extra time) / production-department hours
   printed hours and present/absent: unchanged (all departments)
   low-efficiency lists (compliance, morning brief): only workers with production hours
```

Labels on the dashboard (desktop and phone) and the Employees page:

| Meaning | Dashboard before | Employees page before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| keyed production-department hours | Production time | Prod Hrs / Working hrs | Hours worked |
| standard minutes earned | Prod hours | Production Time / Production hrs | Earned time |

The dashboard feed cache key moves from v8 to v9.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `tests/efficiency-one-rule.test.mjs` on the old code: 0 pass, 5 fail.
  **After:** 6 pass.

```text
extra time 2h approved  ->  day earned 360 -> 480, worker earned 0 -> 120
KPI pool vs tile        ->  tile prod 720 (counted an unkeyed day) -> 480 = KPI
daily email, 4h UPH + 4h R&D, 2h earned + 1h extra  ->  25% -> 75%
warehouse-only worker   ->  0% and flagged -> "—", not flagged, still PRESENT
worker rows             ->  labour cost of a non-production-only day kept
labels                  ->  no old label strings left on either page
```

Full suite: 8277 of 8283 pass. The 2 failing files need `@pdf-lib/fontkit` and `xlsx-js-style`, which the local node_modules lacks; they do not touch this change. Typecheck was not run locally. No browser check yet: the UI change is on main only, so it shows after deploy.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Revert the commit. No schema or data change.

**Blast Radius:** wide

- Efficiency figures move for workers with approved extra time, on the dashboard, KPI cards and board report. KPI and board report are recomputed on every read, so closed months move too.
- The daily email and the "low efficiency" lists change for workers who also keyed non-production hours.
- A failed read of `worker_nonprod_requests` now marks the dashboard employee slice not live instead of silently dropping extra time.
- Still open on purpose: the payslip's PIC 1 / PIC 2 credit split vs the per-piece split, the AI assistant's efficiency tools, the worker phone's daily rows (class C33 in `docs/BUG-CLASSES.md`).

author: mani99brar
body:
Goes into #2604 (`feat/veashi-gateways-master`). Two commits:

### 1. `fix(contracts): address the Veashi gateway review findings`
- Both gateways: a governor-set `minThreshold`, so one compromised oracle cannot forge a dispute or a ruling; duplicate oracle IDs are refused.
- The dispute hash covers the oracle selection, so a copy of a dispute over other oracles is another dispute. The ForeignGateway stores `disputeIDtoHash`, and `relayDispute` checks the recomputed hash.
- ForeignGateway:
  - extraData and the template URI are capped at 1024 bytes;
  - fee-on-transfer tokens are refused;
  - the token bridging share rounds up.
- GatewayLightbulb: `claimRefundTo`.

### 2. `feat(contracts): split the gateway deliveries from dispute creation and ruling`
A Yaru delivery now only records what it carries. A separate public call acts on it, so the delivery depends neither on the court nor on the arbitrable. The `try`/`catch` and the gas guard are gone.

**HomeGateway**
- `onMessage` records the dispute: `receivedAt`, the hash of the delivered message and the oracle selection. It emits `DisputeReceived(hash, DisputeMessage)`.
- `createReceivedDispute(DisputeMessage)`:
  - Anyone can call it.
  - The message must be the delivered one, its template included, because the dispute hash does not cover the template.
  - It calls the arbitrator with no try. Any revert, a low balance included, leaves the dispute received.
- `sendCreationFailure(disputeHash)`: anyone can call it once `creationTimeout` has passed since the delivery without the dispute being created. The timeout is governor-set (`changeCreationTimeout`), 7 days by default.

**ForeignGateway**
- `onMessage` records the ruling or the creation failure in `receivedRulings` and emits `RulingReceived` or `CreationFailureReceived`.
- `executeRuling(disputeID)`, also in `IForeignGateway`, can be called by anyone, once. It calls `rule`, or calls `onDisputeCreationFailed` and records the juror-fee refund.

### Off-chain consequences
- Keeper duties after each Yaru execution:
  - `createReceivedDispute` on `DisputeReceived`;
  - `executeRuling` on `RulingReceived` and `CreationFailureReceived`;
  - `sendCreationFailure` for a dispute still not created after the timeout.
- ABI changes:
  - removed: `InsufficientGas`;
  - changed: `DisputeCreationFailed(bytes32,uint256)` on the HomeGateway, which no longer carries the reason;
  - renamed: `ReceivedDispute.received` is now `created`;
  - new fields: `receivedAt` and `messageHash`;
  - new: the events, functions and errors above.
- The gateways need fresh proxies; this is not an in-place upgrade of 183db56d.

### Tests
- Foundry: 235/235 (the first commit alone: 218/218).
- Hardhat full suite: 163 passing. The draw benchmark, which opens its dispute through the gateways, now creates the received dispute; the shared helper lives in `test/utils/veashi.ts`.
- 32 one-line mutants of the new guards are killed.
- validate-upgrades passes, and the non-IR (coverage) build compiles.
- `KlerosLiquidToV2Governor` and `SafeERC20` are unchanged from #2604.

author: iliangeweilerhsg-blip
body:
## Was und warum

Ticket T2-22b aus `docs/VERTRAEGE.md` §20.12: die Inbox und die Konzept-Ansichten im Core.

- **Endpunkte (§20.6):** `GET /inbox`, `GET /inbox/overview`, `POST /inbox/{id}/accept|reject|reopen`, `POST /inbox/bulk`, `GET /concepts`, `GET /concepts/{id}`, `GET /sessions/{id}/concepts`.
- **Regeln (§20.3, §20.6)** in `services/concept-graph.ts`: Normieren, Namensgleichheit und -ähnlichkeit, Kreisprüfung für `baut_auf`, Annahmen A1–A3, Ablehnen und Rückgängig. Es sind dieselben Regeln wie im Worker (T2-21b), geprüft gegen die gemeinsamen Testfälle in `packages/schemas/fixtures/concepts/`.
- **Sperren (§20.6):** Session `FOR SHARE` → Eintrag `FOR UPDATE` → `pg_advisory_xact_lock(CONCEPT_GRAPH_LOCK_KEY = 70070006)` → Konzepte nach ID sortiert `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` → Beziehungen. Folge-Einträge werden nur mit `SKIP LOCKED` gegriffen. Darf einer nicht übersprungen werden, rollt die Entscheidung zurück und läuft neu.
- **Massenaktionen:** vorab alle Sessions und Einträge nach ID sortiert sperren, jeder Eintrag in einem eigenen Savepoint, Fehler landen mit ihrem Code in `skipped`.
- **Fehlercodes (§20.11)** wie im Vertrag.
- In `app.ts` nur die beiden Routen-Zeilen, in `lib/locks.ts` nur `CONCEPT_GRAPH_LOCK_KEY`. Die Dateien von T2-22a und `services/worker/**` sind nicht angefasst.

**Bitte per Squash mergen:** Der Branch enthält einen WIP-Commit eines abgebrochenen Laufs.

## Wie getestet

- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm typecheck`: grün.
- Core-Unit-Tests: 736 von 736 grün (31 Dateien), darunter `concept-graph.test.ts` gegen `normalize.json`, `name-match.json` und `cycle.json`.
- Integrationstests gegen Postgres 16: 1000 grün, 5 übersprungen (37 Dateien, eine übersprungen: der Leistungstest der Suche mit `SG_SKIP_SEARCH_PERF=1` wie in der CI).
  - `inbox-fixtures.test.ts`: alle 15 Fälle aus `decisions.json` über die REST-Routen.
  - `inbox-concurrency.test.ts`: Graph-Sperre, Sperrreihenfolge, zwei Entscheidungen gleichzeitig, Entscheidung während `concepts.resolve` die Session hält, zweimal Rückgängig gleichzeitig, keine Verklemmung über Folge-Einträge.
  - `inbox.test.ts`: A1–A3, Ablehnen, Rückgängig (auch zweimal und mit `Idempotency-Key`), Massenaktionen.
- Gegenproben (Fehler eingebaut, Test rot, Fehler wieder entfernt):
  - A1 ohne Namensprüfung: 4 Fälle in `inbox-fixtures.test.ts` rot.
  - Graph-Sperre ohne Wirkung: 6 Tests in `inbox-concurrency.test.ts` rot.
  - Rückgängig A1 ohne Prüfung auf Belege anderer Sessions: „Beleg aus einer anderen Session“ in `inbox.test.ts` rot.

## Offene Punkte / Risiken

- Der Worker-Teil des Tests „Entscheidung während der Worker schreibt“ ist im Core nachgestellt (eine zweite Verbindung hält die Session `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`). Das echte Zusammenspiel mit `concepts.resolve` aus T2-21b ist nicht getestet.
- `ai.auto_accept` liest der Core direkt aus `setting` (Schlüssel `ai`). Fehlt der Bereich oder ist er ungültig, gilt `aus`. Der Bereich selbst kommt mit T2-22a.
- Ist ein Folge-Eintrag nach 20 Versuchen (rund 1,7 s) noch gesperrt, antwortet der Core mit `503 inbox_busy`. Dieser Code steht nicht in §20.11.
- Die Namensprüfung in A1 vergleicht in JS über alle aktiven Konzepte (damit Worker und Core `key` gleich rechnen). Bei einem Nutzer mit wenigen tausend Konzepten ist das unkritisch.
- Python-Tests, Swift-Contract und der Web-Build liefen lokal nicht (nicht im Scope, keine Änderung dort).

body:
## 目的

將獨立 iOS App 併入 `ios/`，與渥屋助理 Android 共用同一個倉庫，依 Android 來源及實機畫面對齊介面。iOS 最低版本維持 17；手機及其他 App 控制不在本次範圍。

## 目前變更

- 以 git subtree 匯入舊 iOS repo `a1bf53f`，保留原 Git ancestry。
- 接入 iOS build、release、live model/MCP、worker 及 Android 來源檢查 workflows，調整工作目錄與 artifact 路徑；來源模板與產生器可檢查同步。
- 記錄 Android UI、模型、MCP、記憶、技能、瀏覽器的來源基準與差異，並用 Craft Anything 檢查公開 APK。
- 套用 MacBook 分支 `be41020` 的 iPhone／iPad 原生支援；聊天主畫面／抽屜、設定與模型頁、記憶／技能及瀏覽器入口均已納入 Android 參考樣式；已開始原生驗證與逐畫面比對，介面及功能仍有差距。
- Android 根 README 已還原，iOS 入口放在品牌說明頁，避免破壞既有翻譯檢查。

## 驗證及待辦

- Python 腳本測試 297 項通過；Android 來源清單檢查通過；6 個生成 workflows 通過同步檢查，相關 workflow 通過 actionlint；整合的 Swift 檔案通過語法解析，三語文案檢查通過。
- Monorepo `b42f573`、`3088cf6` 與後續 `3e66cc3` 已在 MacBook 使用 Xcode 27 本機簽章，覆蓋安裝並啟動於 iPadOS 26.6.1；隔離資料的直向 UI 導覽測試 1 項通過，涵蓋抽屜、設定與模型、記憶三分頁、瀏覽器及返回聊天。測試後已恢復 Release 版並保留原有 App 資料。橫向及 iOS 17 真機尚未驗證。
- Android CI 在 `2ec3f24`、`10ff631`、`54e087d` 與 `0c9827e` 通過；`54e087d` 首次下載 Kotlin POM 得到 HTTP 404，僅重跑失敗工作後通過；首次 README 翻譯檢查失敗已透過還原根 README 修正。整合版 `0ebd61e` 的裝置建置失敗：設定頁缺模組匯入，聊天主畫面 SwiftUI 類型檢查超時。`b42f573` 已補匯入並拆分畫面；GitHub Xcode 26.2 及 MacBook Xcode 27 的未簽章 iPhoneOS 裝置建置均通過，較早版本三台模擬器完整工作均失敗；iOS 26 發現兩個 UI 案例失敗、單案及完整套件逾時導致 xcresult 匯出失敗；iOS 18 SE 另有 PDF 及鍵盤定位失敗。已修正 SE PDF 內容遮擋及部分測試定位；完整回歸已改成共用測試產物、三款 iPhone 與 iPad 的分片及結果完整性守門，GitHub 規劃檢查通過，首次原生分片執行排隊中；新版 iOS 模擬器矩陣執行中。較早的部分模擬器工作因推送新版本自動取消。後續設定按 PR commit 分組，保留各版測試結果。
- 已加入多行聊天輸入、受限 Markdown、近期對話抽屜、加密對話改名與草稿／PDF／未保存回覆保護；設定首頁接入記憶及 MCP，並對齊記憶排序與技能刪除確認。新版已於 iPad 完成編譯、簽章、覆蓋安裝及啟動；隔離 UI 實測 5/6 通過，涵蓋近期對話重開、文字草稿保留、導覽、設定中記憶/MCP 入口與設定→記憶→瀏覽器→返回；未完成串流回覆的案例因未啟用專用 fixture，正在補正重跑。未改名封存保留 v2 格式；首次改名後升至 v3，舊版 App 將不能讀取該封存。後續 `0c9827e` 已在 MacBook 完成 iPhoneOS Release 編譯、離線簽章與 8 個框架簽章驗證，未安裝至實體 iPad；新增功能仍待完整 GitHub 模擬器及 iPad 驗證。記憶開啟時的結構化答案串流已合入，撤銷後重送防護與解析器本機回歸通過；僅明確回報不支援 stream 的服務會執行有界非串流回退，非結構化錯誤的 complete-only 服務仍可能無法使用。原生及真實服務測試待完成。歷史對話頁的新對話及刪除目前對話現已加入資料保護；iPad 重測受記憶開關 XCTest 點擊後未切換阻礙：原生控制項顯示可用、左右觸控均未呼叫 Binding；本機 iPad 模擬器以 ad-hoc 簽章重試 1/1 通過，開關 1→0 並保存成功。實體 iPad 需手動確認以區分實際操作與 XCTest 問題。同來源加本機測試診斷的隔離 iPadOS 27 模擬器另完成歷史對話刪除保護及未完成回覆新對話保護 2/2，尚非實機結果。
- 已依使用者提供的測試設定於新 repo 建立 live model/MCP secrets 與 variables。電腦端 MCP 唯讀 probe 初始化、列工具及資源、ping 通過；iPad 上 b42 隔離的真實 HA MCP 唯讀連線、工具及資源目錄、背景中斷、重新連線與手動中斷 UI 測試 1/1 通過，未呼叫工具。初次測試因測試程式從序列化對話擷取 URL 時帶入跳脫字元而失敗，改用原始訊息的網址後通過；模型 JSON/SSE 仍回傳 HTTP 429，模型自主 MCP 仍待實測。手動 live workflows 目前限 main 分支執行。

## 最近診斷（`230749d`）

- 首批 iOS 18 Pro Max 分片：startup 15/19 通過；PDF 入口 0/1，點擊後進入文字稿。`0d15ceb` 已將技能導覽連結分為獨立列，Swift 語法檢查通過，原生重測尚在進行。startup 三項停在記憶開關的測試幾何斷言，一項草稿焦點輸入順序失敗，正在釐清。
