author: ourten
body:
## Summary

A new rite, the **Avenging Reach**, in the Rites constellation (tier 2, after Void Flesh).

- **Getting it:** four altar grafts, Avenging Reach I–IV, all made around an iron sword and each dearer than the last. I uses shards, bone and flesh; II Void Pearls and sin-metals; III Wraith Ink and Rubrum; IV three Memoriam shards. They're eaten in order; one eaten out of turn is refused and kept. No flaw, no attunement.
- **In a fight:** when something within 3 blocks of the player's chest hurts them, one ready arm lashes from the middle of their back. It deals 6 damage (an iron sword's), throws the aggressor back and recharges for 3 seconds. The arm on the aggressor's side answers first, so arms don't cross the back. The blow lands when the drawn claw arrives, 6 ticks after the hit; if the aggressor is out of reach by then, it falls short. An arm's own blow never triggers another bearer's arms.
- **Look:** a pixel-scale segmented black tendril, slightly see-through, with a few dim violet sparks and a three-taloned claw. In first person the root behind the head is hidden.
- **Config:** damage, recharge and extra knockback are in a new Avenging Reach category.

## Testing

- Unit tests: `ReachArmsTest` covers arm choice, side preference, the reach check, graft order and the animation curve.
- New client game test, `AvengingReachClientTest`:
  - grafts are refused out of turn and kept;
  - one hit takes 5.9 health off a husk (6 less its armor) and throws it back;
  - a blow while the arm recharges goes unanswered, and the arm answers again once recharged;
  - nothing reaches a husk 4 blocks away;
  - four arms strike four husks in the same tick, and a fifth blow goes unanswered.
- The full unit and client game test suites passed before the last texture and transparency tweaks. After those, `AvengingReachClientTest` was rerun.
- Screenshots checked in third person, first person and with four arms.

## Not verified

- PvP between two bearers.
- Arrows shot from within 3 blocks.
- How the arms look in the dark, motion smoothness, and Iris.

author: badly-drawn-wizards
body:
Rewrites the separation-logic automation (stage 24d, `lib/HoareTactics.wiz`) on the tactic framework of PR #88 (docs/stages/06-macros.md, 6d–6g). Every example in `lib/HoareExamples.wiz` checks, with shorter proofs.

## HoareTactics.wiz
- **Programs:** one `TacticM.whnfCtorApp` replaces six unification probes against the constructors of `Prog`. All 9 `XT.matchShape` call sites and their helpers are gone.
- **Representation predicates:** unfolded with `TacticM.unfold`, which folds recursive calls back. This deletes `foldAs`, `foldList`, `isRaw`, `arity` and the `heads` bookkeeping.
- **`xapp`:** finds the call by unfolding the program's head.
- **Direct `isDefEq` uses:** 14 → 1, counted together with `matchShape` mentions. The one left is `XT.eqOrConv`.
- **Reading goals:** goals are read with `Expr.view`/`appOf`/`beq`/`nameEq`/`mkApp`. The file's private copies of these helpers are deleted.
- **Star lists are read back:** the list-form lemmas `xs.pure_l` and `xs.exists_l` replace the chain-form `xc.*` lemmas.
- **Restating goals:** done with `TacticM.change`; the `xs.conv` lemma is gone.
- **Names:** variables are named after their binders with `introFresh` (`n`, `l`, `r`, and `hp` for facts), without shadowing. `as …` still works.
- **Contradictions:** a contradictory pure fact closes the goal (`succ n = 0`, or `Not (0 = 0)`).
- **Error messages:** failures print the reason and the goal, for example `xstep: the precondition has no cell at q` and `xapp: the specification is about Prog.incr q, but the program is Prog.get …`. When `xsimpl` stops, it traces why (`xsimpl: stuck: no atom on the left matches b`).
- **Axioms:** an atom headed by an axiom is left alone instead of raising an error.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `lib/HoareTactics.wiz` | 1164 lines | ~1066 lines |
| tactic steps in the example proofs | 44 | 36 |
| `as …` / `[r, hr]` name lists in the examples | 6 | 0 |

The 8 removed steps were all `exact absurd …`; each contradictory case is now `by xunfold`.

## Framework change (Prelude): new `Tac` constructor `isDefinition`
- **Request behaviour:** the `TacticM.unfold` request now returns the term unchanged for a constructor, an axiom or an unknown name, instead of throwing. Libraries can try it without catching.
- **New request:** `TacticM.isDefinition n : Option Bool`, appended to the prelude's `Tac` as tag 32. It returns `none` when there is no constant `n`.
- **The `unfold` tactic** asks `isDefinition` first and reports `unfold: n is not a definition` or `unfold: unknown constant n` itself. The existing tactics test keeps its expectation.
- Docs 6f are updated.
- The two framework commits (24ce272, e3c8b91) may be squashed.

## Docs and tests
- `docs/stages/24-separation-logic.md`, 24d: the "what got in the way" list is rewritten as a section on how the tactics now use the framework, plus the gaps that remain.
- seplogic test group: two failure-message assertions.

## Tests
- `lake test -- '=seplogic' '=tactics'` after merging master (d2c54f9): 40 passed, 0 failed (both groups, one run, seen directly).
- No selfhost/*.wiz changes.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: atqamz
body:
## Summary

- A copied or restored `hand.db` run against another Luvus saw the real terminals as "luvus server restarted" and signalled their process groups by PID. Schema 23 records the Luvus socket path on each attempt and supervisor at launch; a live row whose socket differs from the settling process's (`luvus.SocketPath`) ends `interrupted: terminal belongs to another luvus (SOCKET)` and is never signalled, closed or swept. Rows from before the bump have no socket and keep today's behaviour: nothing proves they are foreign, and treating them as foreign would leave real orphans after a genuine Luvus restart.
- The settle note says `requested by PROCESS` only when that process signalled a root that was alive, and `recorded by PROCESS` when it only recorded an end that had already happened (documented in `docs/vocabulary.md`).
- `hand update` now starts the board first, and the board writes `board.generation` before `board.addr`, then the watchers start, so they hold the new board's generation and the board's 30 s sweep no longer restarts them with a spurious `supervisor.refused`. Restarting after the board was smaller than re-reading the file lazily, which would also defeat the watcher's stale-generation guard.

## Test plan

- `gofmt -l .`, `go vet ./...`
- `go test -race ./...` (the `internal/cli` and `internal/board` packages need `-timeout 40m` on a slow machine)

author: joemattie
body:
Closes #480

Recognized pet sightings now leave the teaching queue and remain on the pet card for correction. Waiting sightings explain their uncertainty, and conflicting guesses cannot share a bulk answer.

The existing restore command now inventories stranded teaching per anonymous pet and performs a genuinely read-only detect/re-embed dry run. It reports missing pictures and unusable crops, preserves all teaching, and adds only recoverable references when explicitly run without dry-run mode. `--inventory-only` counts pictures without loading models.

For configured multi-pet species, calibrated logistic regression averages observed crop probabilities. A retained reference mean is used only when observed crops are unavailable. Training, calibration, and testing are chronological, with a 600-second gap between complete tracks. Calibration permits no observed errors; the independent test must retain the absolute recognition gate and improve or match both decision coverage and error rate. The tested estimator stays frozen, and label changes rebuild its gate. Single-pet species retain the existing gallery rule. Partial negative training did not improve coverage at the chosen operating point, so negative answers remain explicit track exclusions.

Read-only evaluation, with recovered vectors added only in memory:

| Final held-out check | Current right / wrong / unsure | New right / wrong / unsure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cats, 146 sightings | 113 / 2 / 31 | 125 / 1 / 20 |
| Dogs, 103 sightings | 93 / 0 / 10 | 93 / 0 / 10 |

Chronological decision replay using only earlier answers, over the available 29 hours inside the requested seven-day window:

| Species | Automatic before / after | Uncertain before / after | Wrong among owner-checked automatic decisions, before / after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cats, 632 sightings | 369 / 379 | 263 / 253 | 12 of 362 / 7 of 364 |
| Dogs, 426 sightings | 234 / 233 | 192 / 193 | 0 of 233 / 0 of 233 |

This reconstructs decisions, not historical queue membership. Unlabeled sightings have unknown correctness. The restore dry run recovered 10 of 1,995 stranded tracks; 1,985 lack a surviving picture. No live writes or deployment were performed. Near-universal coverage is not established by these results.

Validation: 422 targeted Python tests, 75 frontend tests, Ruff, ty, frontend lint/type-check, both frontend builds, and six headless synthetic-page checks at desktop, 390px, and 320px widths in light and dark modes. Privacy checks pass. The mobile checks include wrapping and readability above fixed navigation, following the modern web text-scaling guidance.

Docs: explain recognized sightings leaving teaching, uncertainty reasons, measured per-pet coverage and its actual time window, stranded-reference counts, and `python tools/restore_pet_references.py --dry-run` / `--inventory-only`. Restoration cannot recover pictures that no longer exist. Add the scikit-learn dependency on deployment while preserving the install's optional extras. New `pets.classifier_min_labels`, `pets.classifier_species`, `pets.classifier_regularization`, and `pets.learning_days` settings require every config-reading service to restart. No state reset or migration is needed.

The dry-run numbers were reviewed and approved for merge. Picture retention for delayed or unreadable teaching images remains tracked in #490.

Written by GPT-6 (Joe's team).

Two things the teacher found while playing the game the day before the lesson.

## 1. Turning a decorated pillow looked wrong

Every vessel was treated as round. On the box-shaped pillow the motifs therefore slid over the faces and bunched up at the corner as it turned.

- The pillow now has a **box cross-section** (0.567 deep per width, measured from its turning pictures) in `surface-warp.js`.

- Marks already saved on a pillow are read with the new shape, so those near the ends of the front face can move; there is no class data yet.

## 2. Glaze colour

Brushing on the glaze turned the vessel celadon immediately.

- Raw glaze is an **ochre coat**: the glazed vessel is ochre and its decoration shows only faintly through it.
- The **second firing** brings the celadon colour.

- The glaze brush, the brushed area and the instruction ("황토색 유약… 재벌구이를 하면 푸른 비색이 돼요") match.

author: vinit2776
body:
Replaces #1169, now closed.

## Why #1169 was wrong

#1169 narrowed this cron to 09:30–10:00 IST, on the premise that everyone starts at 09:30 and the gateway's `fixed` window mode makes anything wider useless. #1166 invalidates both halves of that premise:

- **Shift timings become per branch** — LGF 09:30, Perungudi 10:00, plus per-employee overrides. Starts spread out.
- **`/internal/punchin-reminder` gains a second job.** It now runs the auto punch-out *first, before any email*, due 15 minutes after each shift end. #1166 states this caller is where that gets its timing.

**It never could.** The window was `*/5 3-6 * * 1-6` — 08:30–12:29 IST, mornings only — while shift ends are 18:30–20:00, putting punch-out due times (18:45, 19:15, 20:15) entirely outside it. #1169 would have narrowed it further. The auto punch-out would have fallen back to the gateway's three daily Hobby crons, which stamp the correct time but, at ±59 min precision, can land an hour or more late.

## What this does

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Schedule | `*/5 3-6 * * 1-6` | `*/5 4-5,13-15 * * 1-6` |
| Morning (IST) | 08:30–12:29 | **09:30–11:25** — reminders, 10 min after shift start |
| Evening (IST) | *none* | **18:30–21:25** — auto punch-outs, 15 min after shift end |
| Runs/day | 48 | 60 |
| Runs/month | ~1,250 | ~1,560 |

Morning covers starts from 09:20 to 11:15; evening covers ends from 18:15 to 21:10. Both spans are sized to the branches #1166 actually configures, not a guess. ~1,560/month against Vercel Pro's 1M included invocations is ~0.16%.

### Two deliberate choices

**One entry with an hour list, not two entries sharing a path.** Vercel does not document whether the `crons` array accepts duplicate `path` values with different schedules. #1166 relies on that for its three `/internal/auto-checkout` entries; this sidesteps the question. Ranges and steps are already proven across the other 46 crons in this file — commas are not, but an invalid expression fails the Vercel build, so the check on this PR is the real validation.

**Health threshold 48h → 42h.** The evening window pulls Saturday's last run to Monday's first from ~44h down to ~36h, so the old figure was loose rather than wrong.

### The remaining gap, documented in three places

A shift outside those spans gets nothing from this route — the reminder is simply never sent, and the auto punch-out falls back to the gateway's daily crons. Called out in the route's doc comment, the CLAUDE.md cron table, and the gateway's header comment: **set a shift outside those spans and widen this schedule in the same change.**

## Base: `main`, not `feat/branch-shifts`

Despite being written for the post-#1166 world, this is based on `main` because **the cron entry it edits does not exist on `feat/branch-shifts`** — that branch predates #1164. There is also no code dependency: #1166 touches only `attendance-gateway-code/`, this touches the CRM's `vercel.json`, health route and route docs.

**Merge after #1166.** Landing it first is harmless — the evening window would poke an endpoint that does not yet auto punch-out, which returns early — just premature.

One conflict to expect: the 2-line `server.js` comment fix is in a file #1166 rewrites heavily, though #1166 leaves that comment untouched. Trivial to resolve either way.

## Also

Two gateway comments still claimed reminders were triggered by the biometric device's check-ins. That trigger was removed before #1159 merged; #1166 leaves both stale.

## How tested

- `npm run lint` — 0 errors (225 pre-existing warnings, none new)
- `npm run build` — `✓ Compiled successfully`, route registered as `ƒ /api/cron/attendance-punchin-reminder`
- `npm test` in `attendance-gateway-code` — 101/101 pass
- Schedule expanded programmatically to confirm the real fire times: 60 slots/day, morning 09:30→11:25 IST, evening 18:30→21:25 IST, weekend gap 36.08h

No browser click-through: this changes a cron schedule, a threshold constant and comments, none of which have a UI surface. The verification that matters is the Vercel build accepting the expression (this PR's own check) and then the first scheduled run, which reports itself — `{gateway: {...}}` on success, `502 Gateway refused` on a secret mismatch.

## Migration / rollback notes

None. No schema change. Rollback is reverting the `vercel.json` schedule and the threshold.

body: ## Summary 11/14: adds the Toilet's Resource Pack and Behavior Pack assets. These are a model generated from the owner's reference model with alpha-cut plates, the entity with one seat and the synchronized `yasu_ride:lid_open` and `yasu_ride:flushing` properties, the item and recipe, and property-driven lid and flush animations. There is no sound (#1572) and no engine wiring (#1569) yet, so the Toilet cannot be placed or used in game. **This is a draft: the owner must approve the look against the photos before merge (fidelity gate).** ## Depends on This branch merges the following unmerged branches, so this pull request also shows their commits until they merge: - #1578 ([5/14], `refactor/single-source-kind-lists`) - #1583 ([6/14], `chore/render-preview-cutout-and-views`) - #1580 ([7/14], `spike/alpha-cut-cubes-adr-0246`). Its cut-out probe is still unverified in game, and ADR 0246 says this pull request must not merge until it is. - #1579 ([8/14], `feat/toilet-washstand-domain`) Merging #1579 conflicted in `docs/specs/resort-gear.md` and `tests/domain/resort/furniture.test.ts`. Both sides were kept: the kinds come from `FURNITURE_SPEC`, and the tests add explicit Toilet and Washstand seat expectations. ## Background / Motivation - The Toilet has domain rules (#1567) but no model, entity, item, or animations, so the later wiring (#1569) and scenarios (#1573) have nothing to drive. - The owner's main quality bar is matching the product photos. The design asks for tilted panel rings for curved bodies, and one alpha-cut cube for each flat plate or disc, instead of stair-stepped strips (ADR 0246). - `tests/test-pack/impact.test.ts` already failed on the merged dependencies: #1579 adds `toilet` and `washstand` to `FURNITURE_IDS`, but the impact map had no stems for them. ## Changes ### Generated model and cut-out atlas - New `tools/gen_toilet.py`, run by `pnpm model` through `tools/generators.json`. It ports the reference toilet group at 0.775 px per photo unit with the same ring tables: body 7 rings x 18 panels, interior 5 x 18, seat and shelf 18, tank and cap 16, lid 18. - Each flat plate is one cube with an alpha-cut top face: the base, the interior floor, the seat top with the hole cut out, the shelf, the cap top, the lid top and underside, and the water. The lever boss is a disc, followed by the neck and a three-cube paddle. - The model has 369 cubes; the Beach Parasol has 1,532. - The x axis is reflected so the lever lands on the game's -x side, as in the side photo. - Output floats are rounded to 4 decimals, so `pnpm model:check` matches on the Linux CI runner. - The atlas is 512 x 512 RGBA. Alpha is 0 or 255 everywhere except the water (153). Opaque RGB is kept under alpha-zero texels to avoid fringes, and the chrome bands and radial boss shading are baked in. - Bones: `root`, `body`, `interior`, `seat`, `shelf`, `tank`, `cap`, `lid` (pivot at the hinge, y 8.99, z 1.705), `lever`, `drain`, `swirl` (`swirl_0` to `swirl_15`), `rim_jets` (`rim_jet_0` to `rim_jet_5`), and `water` last. - `tools/resort_gear.json` registers the Toilet after Sofa (Double) with `cutout: true`. `tools/render_preview.py` applies the `rest` animation, which hides the foam bits, before rendering the item preview and the photo views. ### Client entity, materials, and animations - `toilet.ce.json` uses `entity_alphatest` by default and `entity_alphablend` for the `water` bone, through `toilet.rc.json`, as the cut-out probe does. - `toilet.ac.json` has a lid controller on `query.property('yasu_ride:lid_open')` and a flush controller on `query.property('yasu_ride:flushing')`. - `toilet.anim.json` holds these animations: - `lid_open` and `lid_close`: 0.4 s, lid x rotation from 0 to -91 degrees, because the game's positive x rotation lowers the front. - `flush`: 5.0 s of water level and widening, 16 swirl bits, and 6 rim jets, as Molang on `query.anim_time`. - `rest` and `closed_pose`. - The flush follows the reference model's `updateToilet`, which wins over the design text: the swirl orbits around z -2.6 photo units with a z radius of 3.0 (the design says -4.1 and 3.6). ### Behavior Pack, item, and translations - author: hrabbani
body: ### Description Fixes code scan finding `sfind-808d00ebf4ca4645b88cb6da9cba9340`: the chatbot's `generateCoupon` tool in `routes/chat.ts` took any number as `discount`. The 10% limit was only written in the system prompt, so an anonymous user could prompt-inject the bot (`POST /rest/chat`) into minting a 100% coupon, and checkout accepted it. The policy is now enforced in code inside the tool: - `discount` is `z.number().int().min(1).max(MAX_CHATBOT_COUPON_DISCOUNT)` (10), and `execute` checks it again before minting. - New required `orderId`. The tool only mints a coupon if the caller presents a genuinely signed JWT (`getVerifiedUserId`: header `alg` must be `RS256` and the signature must verify; `security.verify` alone accepts `alg: none` tokens) and the order exists, belongs to that user and is `delivered: true`. - Orders now store `UserId` (checkout in `routes/order.ts` and seeded orders in `data/datacreator.ts`), and ownership is matched on `UserId` instead of the masked email, which collides for e.g. `admin@` / `edmin@`. Orders created before this change have no `UserId` and are rejected. `/rest/track-order/:id` strips `UserId` so the public tracking endpoint doesn't expose account IDs. - `security.generateCoupon` zero-pads single-digit discounts. Without it, `NOV26-5` isn't a valid z85 length and `generateCoupon(5)` returned `null`, so 1–9% coupons never worked. Notes for reviewers: - Orders have no "damaged" flag, so `delivered: true` stands in for it. The "customer rejected a return/exchange" rule is still prompt-only. - This code sits inside the `chatbotPromptInjectionChallenge` / `chatbotGreedyInjectionChallenge` snippets. Once this lands, `chatbotGreedyInjectionChallenge` (≥50%) can no longer be solved, and `chatbotPromptInjectionChallenge` needs a real delivered order owned by the user. `chatbotPromptInjectionChallenge_2_correct.ts` now includes the `.int().min(1).max(10)` cap so the "correct" option no longer drops it; `rsn/cache.json` was regenerated with `npm run rsn:update` and `npm run rsn` passes. Whether these challenges should keep a vulnerable snippet is a maintainer decision. - Out of scope: coupons are z85-encoded and not signed, so they can still be forged offline (the separate "Forged Coupon" challenge path in `lib/insecurity.ts`). Tests: added 8 `generateCoupon` cases to `test/api/chat.test.ts`. They cover a discount above 10%, non-integer/zero/negative discounts, no auth, a forged `alg: none` token, another customer's order, a customer with the same masked email as the owner, an undelivered order, and valid 10% and 5% coupons. `test/api/chat.test.ts` passes 16/16, `test/api/track-result.test.ts` (asserts no `UserId`), `test/api/order-history.test.ts` and `test/api/basket.test.ts` passes. `npm run test:server` passes (3 local failures are only the port-3000 precondition specs, port was in use), `npm run rsn` passes, and eslint is clean on the changed files. Resolved or fixed issue: none ### AI Tool Disclosure - [ ] My contribution does not include any AI-generated content - [x] My contribution includes AI-generated content, as disclosed below: - AI Tools: `Devin` - LLMs and versions: `Devin (Cognition AI)` - Prompts: `Remediate code scan finding: chatbot coupon tool in routes/chat.ts has no server-side discount limit; enforce the cap and ownership checks in code.` ### Affirmation - [x] My code follows the [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) guidelines Link to Devin session: https://devin-gtm.devinenterprise.com/sessions/d04068748fd04f929814308b814c0d12 Open in Devin Desktop: https://devin-gtm.devinenterprise.com/desktop/session/d04068748fd04f929814308b814c0d12?variant=devin Requested by: @hrabbani --- 🟢 Devin Review found nothing to fix · [View findings](https://devin-gtm.devinenterprise.com/review/cog-gtm/juice-shop/pull/4392) · [Follow Devin's work](https://devin-gtm.devinenterprise.com/sessions/d04068748fd04f929814308b814c0d12) Devin-Org: engineering

author: quantova-inc
body:
This is the third repo in the same finding. I opened the matching fix for xrpl-py (XRPLF/xrpl-py#1081) and xrpl.js (XRPLF/xrpl.js#3584), both of which share the identical wrong fixture entries this repo also has.

AmountType capped MPT amounts at Long.MAX_VALUE (2^63 minus 1) with an explicit check. An MPT amount carries its sign and type in its own leading byte at serialization, so unlike native XRP and IOU amounts no bit inside the 64-bit value is reserved for sign. rippled documents the real maximum directly as 2^64 minus 1.

The check here was not just wrong, it was redundant once you look at what it is actually comparing against. The underlying value is stored as Guava's UnsignedLong, which already represents the full unsigned 64-bit range by construction, and already throws parsing anything outside it. So the explicit check could only ever reject values the type itself had already decided were valid. I removed it rather than widen its bound.

The two existing tests, encodeMptAmountWithMoreThan63BitAmountThrows and its negative sibling, asserted this exact bug as the expected behavior for 2^63. I corrected them to assert the real, accepted encoding, and added coverage at the true maximum (2^64 minus 1) and genuinely one past it.

The shared data-driven-tests.json fixture encoded the same wrong boundary for the decimal forms of 2^63 and 2^64 minus 1. Corrected those two entries and added a genuine over-the-max case at 2^64. I left the hex forms of the same values (0x8000000000000000, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF) as error cases, since I checked and this codec does not parse a 0x prefixed MPT value at all today, which is a separate and unrelated gap from the one this PR fixes.

Verified locally with Maven, a full clean build and the entire xrpl4j-core test suite pass (74138 tests, 0 failures), and checkstyle reports 0 violations on the changed files.

Machine rules (`phrase:`, `max_sentence_words:`, `max_title_chars:`) are enforced as `lesson_rule #n`, a serious failure. A pack that still repeats a lesson gets "⚠ Do not publish yet".

author: muhannadnouri
body:
## Summary

Fix PDF narration treating presentation hyphens as spoken word boundaries, such as sending `envi- ronment` to TTS instead of `environment`.

The repair happens during PDF narration reconstruction, while line boundaries and original source coordinates are available. Affected saved PDF audiobooks explicitly require regeneration because existing audio cannot acquire corrected pronunciation from a text change.

Matching older audiobooks remain playable. This does not blanket-invalidate PDFs or change the global audio cache/bundle formats.

## Changelist

### PDF narration and source mapping

- Repair eligible line-end word wraps before the shared audiobook chunker.
- Collect intact compound-word evidence across the document before reconstruction. For example, an intact `producer-consumer` elsewhere preserves the hyphen in a wrapped `producer-` / `consumer`.
- Compare compound evidence case-insensitively and expand existing presentation ligatures when constructing comparison keys.
- Remove discretionary U+00AD soft hyphens from narration.
- Preserve U+2011 nonbreaking hyphens while suppressing the intervening layout space at eligible continuations.
- Apply compound evidence and a conservative letter-case fallback to ASCII hyphens and U+2010.
- Preserve en/em dashes, paragraph breaks, backwards column transitions, and rejected page seams.
- Treat Unicode combining marks as part of words, including decomposed accents, Hindi vowel signs, and Arabic marks.
- Preserve original glyphs and UTF-16 source coordinates without normalizing or rewriting the source.
- Remove or shorten only the source run belonging to a removed hyphen; following letters retain their original coordinates.
- Preserve search projections, canonical PDFs, and extracted page sidecars.

### Saved PDF compatibility and regeneration

- Compare the current ordered chunk signature and count with the saved manifest.
- Return a distinct regeneration-required status for readable PDF manifests whose chunks differ.
- Keep missing or corrupt manifests in the existing not-saved flow.
- Keep matching older PDFs playable.
- Make mismatch detection read-only: checking status does not rewrite manifests, prune audio, or start generation.
- Show an actionable reader notice and “Save PDF audiobook again” label.
- Require confirmation before replacement, explaining the target generated speed, interrupted-replacement behavior, and source PDF retention.
- Require confirmation before restarting an affected interrupted PDF job.
- Preserve ordinary resume behavior once the corrected pending manifest exists.
- Reuse cached WAVs only when their index, chunk ID, and text identity match; prune stale files through the existing replacement path.

### Export, import, and saved-version UI

- Check PDF compatibility on demand when exporting or resuming, using that version’s model/chunk profile.
- Independently guard native WAV and bundle export before opening Save As.
- Add a stable native error code and translated regeneration message.
- Display discovered regeneration notices in saved-version menus and the Audiobooks panel.
- Disable exports for known affected versions while keeping entries accessible for opening and deletion.
- Associate asynchronous status results with the selected audiobook identity.
- Preserve notices across registry refreshes only for the same saved generation.
- Recheck status when the selected saved generation changes, including delayed registry responses and completed replacement/import.
- Continue accepting older PDF bundles. Their original audio/source imports normally; current PDF preparation then determines whether regeneration is needed.
- Leave HTML/EPUB/TXT preparation and existing bundle compatibility unchanged.

### Generated speed, readability, and documentation

- Keep every new Save fixed at 1x and select that generation identity after confirmation.
- Fix saving again after selecting legacy 0.8x/1.2x audio: successful 1x generation now selects the generated version and enables playback.
- Keep playback rate independent and unchanged.
- Preserve recorded generation settings when resuming an existing job so cached audio retains a consistent identity.
- Expand UI status/message selection, Save labels, and restart confirmation into explicit branches.
- Remove a redundant native export chunk copy.
- Add function-level comments explaining non-obvious intent, source-offset handling, asynchronous ownership, and replacement behavior.
- Add regeneration strings in all eight locales.
- Update the PDF architecture, compatibility policy, validation results, and manual acceptance checklist.

## Architecture and design

The root fix belongs in the Rust PDF reconstructor, before format-independent chunking. This preserves the line geometry needed to distinguish layout wrapping from normal punctuation and keeps PDF cleanup out of the shared TTS pipeline.

Reconstruction reads validated sidecars twice, one page at a time: first to collect intact compound evidence, then to build narration. This adds a sidecar pass without reparsing the PDF or retaining every page’s geometry.

Unicode Mark classification reuses the already locked `regex` crate through a direct dependency. The lockfile adds only the application dependency edge; no packages or package versions are added or changed.

Compatibility uses the existing chunk-signature contract. The global cache version, durable manifests, and bundle formats remain unchanged. Regeneration notices are derived in memory rather than persisted as a new migration/version marker.

Saved-library checks are lazy; startup does not reconstruct every saved PDF.

## Examples

| Input/context | Narration behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `envi-` followed by `ronment` within an eligible paragraph continuation | `environment` |
| `producer-` followed by `consumer`, with intact `producer-consumer` evidence elsewhere | `producer-consumer` |
| A discretionary soft hyphen inside a word | Soft hyphen omitted |
| A nonbreaking hyphen across an eligible visual wrap | Hyphen retained; layout space omitted |
| A paragraph break or rejected page seam | Boundary retained |
| Decomposed accented letters around a wrap | Marks and original UTF-16 coordinates retained |

## Compatibility and gotchas

- Previously generated WAVs are not repaired in place. Affected PDFs need generation again.
- Detection itself preserves old files and the source PDF. Declining confirmation starts no replacement.
- Replacement is not atomic. The existing save path writes a pending manifest and prunes stale chunks before synthesis finishes. If interrupted or failed, the replaced version is not guaranteed to remain playable.
- Unseen compound words remain ambiguous. Document evidence and conservative fallback improve reconstruction without introducing a dictionary or language-specific model.
- A legacy non-1x saved version and a new 1x save can remain separate entries. Saving at 1x does not automatically delete the differently paced version.
- Resuming an existing job retains its recorded generation speed; this does not expose a generation-speed control or alter playback-rate behavior.
- Old PDF bundle import remains supported, but affected imported audio requires regeneration after current PDF preparation.
- No sample audiobook/PDF payloads are committed.

## Automated validation

- Frontend: 840 passed, 1 skipped across 101 test files.
- Native suite with `native-tts-core` and `sherpa-onnx/shared`: 339 passed, 5 ignored.
- Focused native PDF tests also passed in the default configuration.
- Production build passed, including TypeScript, eight-locale i18n checks, Vite, and Pagefind indexing.
- Strict ESLint on touched TypeScript/TSX, scoped Rust formatting, and Git whitespace checks passed.

Regression coverage includes:

- Discretionary/nonbreaking hyphens, compound evidence on later pages, paragraph/column/page boundaries, and sidecar errors.
- Combining marks, ligatures, emoji, fragmented PDF items, and

author: joepjoosten
body:
## Summary
Moves the repo onto the toolchain used by [Effect-TS/effect](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect) (main). Its root `package.json`, `.oxlintrc.json`, `packages/tools/oxc/oxlintrc.json`, `dprint.json`, `tsconfig.base.json` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` are mirrored where they apply.

This branch includes the commit from #59 (pnpm 11.20.0) and supersedes it.

- **pnpm** `11.20.0` via `packageManager` (same as Effect). `pnpm-workspace.yaml` gains `verifyDepsBeforeRun: error` and `allowBuilds: { dprint: false }`; dprint's binary comes from an optional platform package, so its build script isn't needed.
- **TypeScript** `^7.0.2` (unchanged).
- **Type check:** `check` = `effect-tsgo tsrs -b tsconfig.json` (`@effect/tsgo`), `check-tsc` = `tsc -b tsconfig.json`.
- **Lint:** `lint` = `oxlint -f unix && dprint check`, `lint-fix` = `oxlint --fix && dprint fmt`.
  - `.oxlintrc.json` inlines Effect's shared rule set without the `effect/*` rules and the `@effect/oxc` jsPlugin, which is private.
  - `dprint.json` copies Effect's file, with excludes adapted to this repo.
- **tsconfig.base.json:** adopts Effect's compiler options (`verbatimModuleSyntax`, `erasableSyntaxOnly`, `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`, `noUnusedParameters`, `noImplicitOverride`, `noErrorTruncation`) and its `@effect/language-service` plugin config. It keeps this repo's `lib`, `paths` and per-package emit settings.
  - There was no `baseUrl`. The `paths` were already `./`-relative to `tsconfig.base.json`, so they resolve the same.
  - Every package tsconfig already declares its own references.
- **Removed** `@effect/language-service`: TS 7 doesn't load tsserver plugins, and `@effect/tsgo` reads the same plugin config. Nothing in the repo imports `typescript`, so no `@typescript/typescript6` alias is needed. There was no ESLint to remove.
- **CI:**
  - The setup action uses `pnpm/action-setup@v6`, which takes the version from `packageManager`. Node stays at 24.5.0.
  - New Lint job.
  - The Types job runs `check`, `check-tsc` and `check:examples`.
  - The existing Build job is kept.
- **README:** dev commands updated (`pnpm test --run`, since pnpm 11 forwards `--` literally).

### Fixes for what the new tools reported (no rules disabled)
- **`erasableSyntaxOnly`:** constructor parameter properties in three classes are now explicit fields: `BinaryReader` in core, `BinaryReader` in `node/internal/container`, and `AsyncByteReader` in node's `stream.ts`. None of them is exported from a package entry point, and field order is kept, so emitted JS and `.d.ts` are identical.
- **`effectFnOpportunity`** (an error in Effect's config): `writeContainerFile`, `readContainerFile` and the two `makeAvroNode` methods in `@effect-avro/node` now use `Effect.fnUntraced`.
  - The exported consts carry explicit signatures, so the public `.d.ts` is unchanged. Without them, TS 7 inlines `Avro.ParseOptions` as an object literal.
  - `readContainerFile` is built without a contextual type first. `A` only appears in its return type, and assigning `fnUntraced(...)` straight to a generic signature drops `A`.
- **oxlint:** type-only imports and `Array<T>` in tests and examples, and two empty spread fallbacks removed in an example.
- **`dprint fmt`** across the repo.

## Verification
From a clean tree (`git clean -xdf`, then `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`), each step run on its own after deleting `dist` and `.tsbuildinfo`:
- `pnpm check`, `pnpm check-tsc`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm check:examples` and `pnpm lint` pass.
- `pnpm test --run`: 59/59 pass.

### Built output vs npm (`@effect-avro/*@0.1.1`)
- **File lists:** identical in all five packages.
- **`.d.ts`:**
  - core, schema, schema-registry, kafka: byte-identical.
  - node: the same declarations; only import lines and the specifiers in `export type { ContainerEvent, ContainerHeader }` are reordered (dprint sorts imports).
- **`.js`:** each file pair was run through the same minifier (oxc via rolldown, compression on, mangling off), with imports compared as a sorted set.
  - core, schema, schema-registry, kafka, and node's `stream.js` and `internal/container.js`: identical. The raw diffs are only layout from dprint (line breaks, braces around single-statement `if`s).
  - node `index.js`: the `Effect.gen` → `Effect.fnUntraced` change above. At runtime this is equivalent: both are `suspend(() => fromIteratorUnsafe(body(...args)))`, arguments are captured at call time, and `fnUntraced` keeps `fn.length`.
  - In the three node `.js` files, `@effect-avro/core` and `effect` are now imported before the `node:` builtins. All of these are side-effect-free, so the change in evaluation order can't be observed.
- **`.map` files:** they differ because source line positions changed.

No changeset: tooling only, with no change to behaviour or public types.

author: staticaland
body:
## What A PR body from the `create-pr` skill now has **three short sections** and an issue list. Each section shows **at most two sentences**, then a collapsed `
` block with the longer explanation.
Details
```diff -
-One sentence - -## What is this change? -## Why do we need this change? -## Who is this change for? -## What is the merge danger? -## Which issue(s) does this PR fix? - -
+## What short text +
with a visual +## Why short text +
+## Merge danger Reversible, What can break +
+## Issues ``` - `references/pr-template.md`: the headings are one or two words. The section about the audience is gone. The one `
` block around all sections is gone. - Each block has a `
` below its summary, so the opened block has space above its text. A section has no block when its visible sentences say everything. - `SKILL.md`: a new `Layout` section states the rule. The rule follows the headings. It applies to each heading of a PR body, and to a body rewritten with `gh pr edit`. - `references/visuals.md`: new. It lists the forms for the visual in the What block: diff sketch, tree, diagram, and pseudocode. `SKILL.md` step 2 points to it. - `scripts/pr.py`: `prepare` always prints the skill's template. - The writing instructions in the template now ask for sparing use of bold on key information, so a busy reader can scan the body. - `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`: now the same as the skill's template. The skill does not read it. It stays for PRs that people open by hand.
## Why A reviewer wants the short answer to each question first, and the detail only on demand. The old description gave one sentence when collapsed and a long text with noisy headings when open.
Details
Decisions: - The visible part of a section is at most two sentences, and each sentence is its own paragraph. The limit forces the writer to choose the main point, and it moves the rest into the block. - The outer block is removed. An outer block hides the short sentences, and those sentences must stay visible. - `pr.py prepare` no longer reads a repo's `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`. Every PR body from the skill now has the same sections. This is the breaking change. - The layout rule is also in `SKILL.md`, so a body rewritten with `gh pr edit` gets the layout too. - The audience section is removed because it rarely gave a reviewer new information. - The visual is in the collapsed block. The visible part of each section stays one or two sentences. - The forms in `references/visuals.md` are adapted from the `pr` skill in [mattpocock/skills](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) and the `show-me` skill in [humanlayer/skills](https://github.com/humanlayer/skills). Both have the MIT license. The file itself has no credit line; the attribution comes later in a different form. - The label `Door` with its one-way and two-way answers is now `Reversible` with a yes or a no. The label asks the question directly: does a revert undo the change? - `What can break` no longer starts with a one-word scope such as `local`. The words had no definition in the template. The answer now names what fails and who notices. - The label `What can break` stays. The upstream label is `Blast Radius`, and Vale flags that phrase as an idiom. The literal label agrees with the Simplified Technical English rule of the template. - The visual forms are a separate reference file. Only the What block needs them, so they stay out of `SKILL.md`. Test: `mise exec -- prek run --all-files` exits 0. This PR body uses the new template and layout.
## Merge danger **Reversible:** Yes. **What can break:** A repo with **its own PR template** gets the skill's sections in place of its own, and its reviewers notice.
Details
A revert restores the old template and skill text. The change reaches installed users only after the release PR merges. PRs opened before a revert keep their layout until someone edits the body. A tool that reads the old heading text of a PR body stops finding it. No such tool is in this repo.
## Issues None. **AI assisted 🤖**

author: sarthakaggarwal97
body:
## Why

Follow-up to #149. Of the fourteen failures replayed for that change, two that people fixed were refused, and neither refusal came from running out of attempts: no fix in 28 replays reached the third round.

- **del-node on macOS:** the agent named the function the fix belongs in and listed the real cause as one of three possibilities. It declined because the log did not single one out. The fix a person wrote is five lines and is correct under all three.
- **forkless-write-window under valgrind:** the log the agent was given had lost the failing test's server output, so it could not rule out a product defect.

What limited the fix was what the agent saw and what it did after a rejection.

## What changes

**More for the agent and the reviewer to read**

- **The whole job log.** It was cut to its first 40,000 and last 260,000 characters, although it is a file the agent searches and not prompt text. A long valgrind log lost the failing test's own output.
- **Verification output:** 40,000 characters of a failed run, not 6,000.
- **Existing-fix candidates:** the diff of every candidate, not the first three, and 40,000 characters of each, not 8,000.
- **The reviewer** also reads why the author chose the change and what it ruled out, not only the root cause.

**Fewer refusals**

- The agent refuses only when it can justify no change. Where the evidence leaves a few causes and one change is right under each, it makes that change and says what is not established.
- After a rejection the agent is told that the rejection is of that change, not of fixing the failure. The reviewer says what change it would approve.
- The reviewer does not reject because a failure was not reproduced first. None is, by design, so the line saying so is gone from every report; the docs say it once.

**Gates removed**

- A patch whose author labelled the failure "infrastructure" was discarded and reported as a refusal. The action the agent chose now stands.
- A candidate with an empty root cause or rationale cost a whole round. It no longer does.

**A fix this needed**

- The search for the file paths a log names tried a match from every character of a long run of path characters. That is quadratic, and with whole logs it hung on a 1 MB line. It is linear now and finds the same paths.

## Reviewed and left as they are

- The agent has no shell and cannot list files: a confinement boundary, not a quality check.
- The tree must not change while a fix is verified, so the published patch is the tested one.
- Backport branches take only what is merged upstream.
- Three rounds and the time budgets: never reached in 28 replays.
- The reviewer's veto: every patch it rejected weakened a test.

## Testing

- `pytest`: 2,744 passed, 8 skipped. `ruff` and `mypy` are clean.
- The same fourteen failures are being replayed with this change. Results are not in yet.

## Risk

The refusal rule is looser, so a fix may now be proposed on less certain evidence than before. The reviewer, the verification run and the draft PR a maintainer reads remain the checks, and the report says what the evidence does not establish.

author: piethanegraaf
body:
## Why

A critical usability review of the live dashboard (English, details closed) found:

- **61 tooltip targets and 105 tab stops**, of which only 43 are real buttons, links or selects. Reaching the first "Details" button took 22 Tab presses.
- **Translations underlined as if they were links:** 26 dotted underlines, or 53 with every detail open, each one a tab stop.
- **The same level explanation on 23 chips, the legend and the bar.** At 58 words it was too long for a tooltip, and the card "What do the levels mean?" already has it in full.
- **No Esc to close a tooltip** (WCAG 1.4.13).
- **Raw markdown backticks** in the diary.
- **Chips and meters that do not line up** from row to row.

## What changes

1. **Translations: one switch.** The notice at the top gets a button "Toon origineel" / "Show original" that shows all of the learner's texts untranslated, and back. Per text there is no marker and no tab stop any more. Originals carry their `lang` attribute, and focus stays on the switch.
2. **Levels: short tooltips, in one place.** Only the legend and the level bar have a tooltip, with what the level is, the step to the next one, and a pointer to the card (33 words). The skill chips have no tooltip and no tab stop.
3. **Esc** closes any tooltip.
4. **`code`** in backticks is shown as code, without ligatures, so `>=` stays `>=`.
5. **Aligned rows:** fixed columns for the chip and the button, and the microskill indent on the name only.

- Tab stops with every detail closed: **57** (was 105).
- Docs NL/EN updated.

## Test plan

- [x] jsdom, NL and EN, real and demo data:
  - no per-text markers;
  - no source text visible by default;
  - after the switch, 43/44 originals visible (all details open) and no translation;
  - switching back works;
  - focus stays on the switch;
  - the level tooltip has 3 lines;
  - Esc closes it;
  - no raw backticks;
  - no JS errors.
- [x] Headless Edge at 1200, 820 and 390 px, NL and EN: every row has the same chip x, meter x and meter width, and no chip overlaps or overflows. Screenshots checked.
- [x] The route and card of #20 and the translation check of #15 still pass
- [x] Harness tests: 199/199 pass
- [x] Local `security-check.mjs --range origin/main..HEAD`: nothing in the files of this change. One finding in an existing note from #19 was judged a false positive by the maintainer and is not part of this PR.

author: bobkerns
body:
Follow-up from #502: video 8 gets a scene showing that prices are optional. Bob approved the plan in the project thread.

## The scene

The new scene, `prices` ("Shares or dollars"), sits between `invest` and `growth`.

On camera:
- `sim prices show BALX` lists the fund's stored prices.
- `sim account lot add Asset_Brokerage_Joint fund --symbol BALX --quantity 400` adds a lot held as shares, with no dollar balance.
- `sim account holdings Asset_Brokerage_Joint --opening` shows that lot worth $20,000: 400 shares × $50.
- `sim prices check` shows it worth $19,120 at the latest price.

The narration says:
- A lot can be dollars or shares, and prices are optional.
- A holding with no price to fetch stays in dollars: an employer plan's own fund, a CD, the house.
- Where shares work, next year's update means copying the share counts from a statement and fetching prices.

Fetching a real ticker on camera is left out, because it needs the network at build time. #560 (scheduled background fetches) makes that less of a gap.

## Other changes

- **`setup.sh`:** writes BALX's made-up prices before `stage prices`, using the same prices as video 11's setup. No lot holds BALX shares outside this scene's tape, so the later scenes' runs are unchanged. I checked this by comparing `sim networth` for base between demos built with the old and new `setup.sh`: only the run file's name differs.
- **`script.ja.md`:** the Japanese overlay for the new scene, and a new YouTube contents line in both languages.

## Testing

- `python -m analysis.videos check docs/videos/08-investments` passes for en and ja.
- cspell and markdownlint are clean.
- I ran the scene's commands against the demo at `stage/prices`. `sim prices check` prints a table about 150 columns wide, so the tape uses `Set FontSize 16`, as video 11's wide tables do.

author: niteshbalusu11
body:
Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds with gpt-6.1-sol on high. Sol verdict: approved.

The engine already published ready-to-send frames, but nothing put them on the wire: buyers could not see seat availability change, and HELLO carried a zero chart hash. This PR adds the WebSocket transport, the cacheable HTTP snapshot, PRIVATE frames for the buyer's own holds, and shutdown that closes subscribers. **SSE and polling (RT-007, RT-008) are split out** to keep this near the 2,000-line threshold the brief set (see "Not in this PR").

## What changes

- **Chart hash.** `PgCharts` reads `chart_versions.hash` and gives it to `ChartView::with_hash`, so HELLO carries the version's public hash.
- **`GET /v1/public/events/{event}/state?key=pk_…`** (RT-009) returns the engine's published SNAPSHOT bytes (`application/vnd.cavea.frame`). Headers: `ETag: "<seq>"`, `304` on `If-None-Match`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=CAVEA_SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE, stale-while-revalidate=5`; errors are `no-store`. It never messages the actor. An archived event is still served; an unknown or foreign event is `404`.
- **`GET /v1/public/rt?key=pk_…`** (RT-003, RT-004, RT-010):
  - The key, `CAVEA_CORS_ORIGINS` and the key's origin allow-list are checked at upgrade.
  - SUBSCRIBE must come first, within 10 s. The server then sends HELLO, the engine's first frames, and every publication. Frames are the engine's own `Arc<[u8]>` via `Bytes::from_owner`, never copied or re-encoded per subscriber.
  - A hold token in SUBSCRIBE gets PRIVATE frames after their DELTA. The token must be a live hold of that event and workspace with `max_objects` 1–100; anything else gets CLOSE 5, the same as an unknown event.
- **Slow consumers** (RT-005): each frame is written and flushed before the next, so a connection buffers at most one frame of its own. A stalled reader makes its subscription lag in the engine's shared 64-publication channel. When the write completes, it gets RESYNC, then SNAPSHOT (+PRIVATE). A write stuck for 30 s drops the connection.
- **Liveness** (RT-006): protocol PING every 25 s; 60 s without any client message closes the connection. Each connection has one timer.
- **Actor failure:** the connection resubscribes from its `seq` itself, so the client sees more DELTAs or a SNAPSHOT, never a second HELLO.
- **Hostile clients** (12 T11):
  - CLOSE 6 for a malformed, unexpected or text frame, a second SUBSCRIBE, more than 2 KiB, or more than 10 messages per PING.
  - CLOSE 4 for protocol version 0.
  - Limits per IP (`CAVEA_RT_MAX_PER_IP`, 200, over it `429`) and per node (`CAVEA_RT_MAX_CONNECTIONS`, 60,000, over it `503`). The client IP comes from the socket, via one function that SRV-018 will change.
- **Shutdown** (SRV-021): the serve and shutdown sequence moved into `cavea_server::serve`. On SIGTERM every connection gets CLOSE 3 and closes before the HTTP drain. Blocked writes and pending handshakes end at once. Then the actors stop.
- **Logging:** each connection has its own `realtime {request_id, transport, workspace, event}` span with two info records: subscribed, and closed (duration, frames, resyncs, reason). Nothing is logged per frame; no key, token or frame content is logged.

## Decisions (written into 08 §6.2, §8.2, §8.3, §8.5, §11, §13, §14, §15)

- **D-31: realtime routes take the publishable key in `?key=`.**
  - Why: `WebSocket` and `EventSource` cannot set headers, and event keys are unique only within a workspace. With the key in the URL, the URL is a complete CDN cache key: a simple GET with no preflight.
  - Accepted cost: a CDN hit skips the key's checks. A page whose `Origin` the allow-list would refuse, or a key revoked seconds ago, can get a cached snapshot for up to `max-age` plus `stale-while-revalidate` (6 s by default). The public snapshot reveals only which seats are unavailable (D-12).
  - The hold token never goes in a URL.
- **Protocol PING/PONG, not WebSocket control frames:** browser scripts cannot see control frames.
- **RESYNC on a stream is followed by the SNAPSHOT on the same stream.** The 08 §8.1 row now says so.
- **A secret-key token without a limit, or above 100, cannot be followed** (CLOSE 5), because the renderer refuses PRIVATE sets over 100. A backend handing its token to a browser creates it with `max_objects`.
- **An event archived while subscribed** keeps streaming until the client reconnects, then gets CLOSE 1. CLOSE 2 waits for chart upgrades.
- **`CAVEA_DELTA_INTERVAL_MS` is documented as not read:** the interval is a constant in the engine, which this slice does not change.

## Dependencies

`cavea-server` goes from 184 to 194 crates (`cargo tree -e normal,build`), via axum's `ws` feature:

- Added: tokio-tungstenite, tungstenite, data-encoding, sha1 0.10, rand 0.9, rand_core 0.9, rand_chacha 0.9, ppv-lite86, zerocopy, getrandom 0.3.
- Four of those are second versions of crates already in the tree. tungstenite pulls rand unconditionally for client-side masking.
- No lighter WebSocket implementation was in the tree.
- `tungstenite` is also named directly, at the version axum builds, so an oversized message can be told from a dropped connection. That adds no crate.
- Clean debug `cargo build -p cavea-server` (CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8, shared machine): `main` 10.2, 11.9 and 10.8 s; this branch 13.5 and 12.8 s.
- Dev-dependencies, all already built: tokio-tungstenite's client handshake, futures-util `sink`, tokio `test-util`.
- tungstenite's 128 KiB per-connection read buffer is cut to 4 KiB, and the write buffer to 0.

## Proof

Run locally on an AMD Ryzen 9 7900X (24 threads), against the shared PostgreSQL 18, on head `940052c`:

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo build --workspace`: pass.
- `cargo test --workspace` without the database: pass (the server lib runs 22 tests, 18 ignored).
- `cargo xtask check-deps`: pass.
- `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `bun run lint`, `bun run format:check`: pass.
- `CAVEA_TEST_DATABASE_URL=… cargo test -p cavea-server -- --include-ignored --skip measure_`: 40 + 6 pass, including the new tests:
  - Session tests, run on the in-memory engine with paused time:
    - PING at 25 and 50 s, then close at exactly 60 s.
    - A client answering PINGs is kept until shutdown.
    - A stalled reader gets RESYNC + SNAPSHOT after 80 publications and ends consistent.
    - A client that never reads is dropped at 30 s.
    - A blocked write ends at shutdown.
    - A busy feed cannot starve PING or the idle deadline.
    - Failed and lost-reply commits: the stream continues or resnapshots, with no gap.
  - Database tests over a real socket:
    - `websocket_follows_the_event`: real chart hash; a hold arrives as a DELTA; PRIVATE goes only to its token's subscriber; resume gets only the DELTAs; seven bad tokens and events get an identical CLOSE 5; subscriber count back to 0; log shape checked and no secrets logged.
    - `websocket_refuses_what_breaks_the_rules`: 401, 403 and both origin gates; handshake timeout; malformed, version 0, text, PONG first, oversized, second SUBSCRIBE; 429 past the per-IP limit.
    - `snapshot`: bytes, ETag, 304 for strong, weak and `*` tags, cache headers, 404 and `no-store`, archived event still served.
    - `shutdown_closes_every_subscriber`: `serve` exits in under 3 s with CLOSE 3 on every socket.
  - Tenant-isolation rows added for both new routes.
- **Live**: release server, a uniquely named database (created and dropped), a 5,000-seat chart, a Python stdlib WebSocket client.
  - Frames arrived as `HELLO 26 B`, `SNAPSHOT 10 B`, then `DELTA 1->2 changes=2 (9 B)` and so on for holds made with `curl`.
  - `curl` on the snapshot showed the headers above, then `304`.
  - SIGTERM with a subscriber attached: CLOSE reason 3 arrived, the server exited 0 after 16 ms, and leases were released.
  - Measured locally:
    - Hold response to DELTA, over 300 holds with random gaps of 0–200 ms: p50 6.0 ms, p95 91.2 ms, max 98.2 ms. The budget is 250 ms p9

author: ghbarker
body:
## Summary

Add native Stalker/Ministra sources to Android Mobile. The new source option accepts a portal URL, registered MAC and optional provider-supplied login/device fields. It covers Live TV, native EPG, provider-advertised catch-up, movies and both native/VOD-based series catalogues.

Playback resolves provider references before MIME/player preparation and VPN gating, with bounded link renewal. Credentials are scoped to the authenticated origin through redirects, manifests, segments and keys. Session tokens and resolved temporary links are not saved in playback caches or diagnostics.

Companion TV PR: https://github.com/homelessbrian/NuvioPlusIPTV/pull/108

## PR type

- [ ] Reproducible bug fix
- [ ] UI glitch/bug fix
- [ ] Behavior bug/regression fix
- [ ] Small maintenance only, with no UI or behavior change
- [ ] Docs accuracy fix
- [ ] Translation/localization only
- [ ] Approved larger or directional change

This is a user-requested feature addition. No linked maintainer approval was supplied, so an approved category is not asserted and this is not labeled as a bug fix.

## Why

Current `dev` has no native Stalker/Ministra source path. This adds portal sessions, native guide/archive identifiers and on-demand series coordinates instead of treating the portal as a static playlist.

## Issue or approval

Requested directly by the user for TV and Android Mobile: Live TV, guide, catch-up, VOD and series. No linked maintainer approval or feature issue was supplied. No issue was created, following the user's instruction.

## UI / behavior impact

- [ ] No UI change
- [ ] No behavior change
- [ ] UI changed only to fix a documented glitch/bug
- [ ] Behavior changed only to fix a documented bug/regression
- [ ] UI change has explicit maintainer approval
- [ ] Behavior change has explicit maintainer approval

Adds Stalker/Ministra source setup and provider-specific import/playback behavior. The approval-dependent options above are not claimed satisfied.

## Policy check

- [x] I have read and understood `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- [ ] This PR is small, focused, and limited to one problem.
- [x] This PR is not cosmetic-only.
- [ ] Any UI change fixes a linked glitch/bug and includes visual proof, or this PR has no UI change.
- [ ] Any behavior change fixes a linked bug/regression or has explicit approval, or this PR has no behavior change.
- [x] This PR does not bundle unrelated refactors, cleanups, formatting, or drive-by changes.
- [ ] This PR does not add dependencies, architecture changes, migrations, or product-direction changes without explicit approval.
- [x] I listed the testing performed below.

This is one focused provider feature, but it is a substantial change with cache migrations. Approval/issue/visual-proof items are intentionally not claimed satisfied: implementation was requested in chat, no linked repository approval or screenshots were supplied, and no GitHub issue was created as instructed.

## Scope boundaries

Existing M3U/Xtream behavior is not intentionally changed. Source settings participate in the current backup/restore flow; guide/VOD cache migrations add nullable provider metadata rather than resetting saved sources or profiles. Shared protocol and VPN guard sources are mirrored between TV and Mobile. Uses existing runtime libraries; no new external runtime package or native VPN engine is added. iOS support is outside this change.

Initial Stalker compatibility limits:

- Internal ExoPlayer only. External playback and watch-party stream-link sharing are unavailable; title/episode party metadata can still synchronize without provider artwork URLs or filenames.
- Supported in-app VPN scopes: Off, Full app, or HTTP + HTTPS. HTTP-only is rejected without changing the saved scope. Protected requests do not fall back to an unprotected client.
- On-disk VOD caching is bypassed to avoid saving temporary link metadata. TV's parallel HTTP downloader is also bypassed for these sources.
- Automatic subtitle file hashing, automatic subtitle-sync media downloads, native format preflight and out-of-band chapter lookup are unavailable where their existing transports cannot enforce the scoped policy. Embedded subtitles, normal subtitle lookup and manual timing remain available.
- Ambiguous multi-file movies return an explicit error. Provider-specific watchdog heartbeats are not implemented.
- Extensionless URLs may need a protected format probe: 1.2-second combined budget, at most 8 KiB consumed, cancellation before response close. Known media extensions skip probing; recognized TS/MP4 HEAD responses avoid a second GET.

Guide imports stream programme rows and request the configured coverage without hiding channels or reducing the requested horizon. Actual guide availability still depends on what the provider returns. Archive IDs are bound to the portal that issued them. See [compatibility notes](https://github.com/ghbarker/NuvioMobile-IPTV/blob/04e9afe97a333e7d598d22e1b3459cdaec5d5169/docs/STALKER.md).

This branch targets current Mobile `dev`; it does not include or validate Stalker integration with the separate, unmerged Mobile Multiview PR #17.

## Testing

- Validated head: `04e9afe97a333e7d598d22e1b3459cdaec5d5169`, based on Brian's `dev` at `003e2386435c526e3492fb78f48aebe2eeb5d3b9`.
- Final Mobile host checks: `-Pnuvio.android.distribution=full :composeApp:testAndroidHostTest --tests '*Stalker*'` — **81 passed**, including production SQLite migrations/reopen under Robolectric, atomic guide publication, cache-restored On Demand selection, local HTTP/TLS scoping and probe byte/cancellation limits.
- Broad regression run before the final probe-only correction: **2,287 tests, six failures**. All 79 then-current new tests passed. The same six failures reproduced on clean `dev`: three AutoSync HTTP/subtitle cases, two legacy backup time-shift expectations and one watch-progress legacy payload expectation. The final focused suite covers the last probe correction.
- Included shared protocol checks: **41 passed**, including a generated **16,000-channel / 768,000-programme** streaming guide, paging, auth renewal, both series variants, archive IDs, nested endpoints and credential isolation.
- Identical shared VPN guard tested through TV's standalone module: all four new safeguards passed; full run **38/40 passed**. Both WireGuard parser failures also occur on clean `dev` (**34/36 passed**).
- Shared-source parity and diff checks pass. Local TLS fixtures reuse the existing TV test certificate. The atomic-rename bridge is test-only; Android production filesystem behavior was not changed for the host environment. Independent reviews covered generic On Demand paths and privacy boundaries.

These are synthetic/JVM host and local HTTP/TLS checks, not physical-device playback or frame-performance measurements. No real provider connection, actual VPN tunnel, or protection across process death/revocation is claimed. No signed-in app was cleared, uninstalled or installed over.

## Screenshots / Video (UI changes only)

UI changed: a themed Stalker/Ministra source form is added using existing controls. No screenshots/video or device UI validation were supplied; that visual proof remains outstanding.

## Breaking changes

No breaking change to existing M3U/Xtream source settings is intended. Derived guide/VOD cache formats advance with non-destructive nullable-column migrations; upgrade preservation is covered by the checks above. Stalker capability limits are listed explicitly under Scope boundaries.

## Linked issues

None, per the instruction not to create issues. A linked repository approval is not asserted.

author: benruijl
body:
Repeated nonreal coefficients currently rediscover the image of `i` by factoring `x^2+1` over the field, both during `AlgebraicContext` field discovery and during coefficient conversion. Cache that image per field so warm conversions also avoid factorization in composite fields such as `Q(sqrt(2)+i)`.

- Store successful images in a field-owned `Arc<OnceLock<AlgebraicNumber<R>>>`, populated only for rational extensions and shared by ordinary clones. Equality and hashing continue to depend only on the defining polynomial and selected embedding. The cache dies with its field clones; it does not retain a field or use a global map.
- Consult the cache before numeric field discovery and coefficient conversion. Seed it from known adjunction images and transport it by substitution through compatible extensions. Rename the cached polynomial with the primitive generator; detach it whenever the selected embedding changes. Structural isolated embeddings remain isolated, without canonical indexing for cache maintenance.
- Compute cold images outside `OnceLock` initialization to keep locks out of potentially reentrant factorization. Concurrent cold callers may duplicate work; failures are not cached. Existing context atom caching and coefficient conversion APIs are unchanged.

Validation:

- `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_OPT_LEVEL=1 cargo check --lib` — passed (existing MathML warnings).
- `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_OPT_LEVEL=1 RUST_MIN_STACK=67108864 cargo nextest run --workspace --lib --tests --test-threads=4 --no-fail-fast` — 1,550 passed, 2 skipped.
- After the final degree guard, `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_OPT_LEVEL=1 RUST_MIN_STACK=67108864 cargo nextest run --lib -E 'test(domains::algebraic)' --test-threads=4` — 48 passed, including all seven new cache regressions.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

The focused regressions cover all four embeddings of `t^4-2*t^2+9`, owned/borrowed small and large coefficients, context discovery, shared and concurrent clones, equality/hash stability, indexed and isolated embeddings, seeding, extension transport, renaming, and fields without `i`. Thread-local counters assert one cold discovery and zero warm discoveries across distinct complex coefficients, including the context path. No timing-based speedup claim.

author: jitsusama
body:
### 💡 TL;DR

The slices VM test's systemd-run subtest now sleeps a number of seconds no other subtest uses, so vm-apps-come-first passes again and leaves the net's quarantine. The sorter's behaviour was right throughout; only the test read the wrong process.

### 🧩 Problem

vm-apps-come-first has failed on main since the systemd-run subtest went in, so the net quarantined it. It looks like the sorter stopped taking real time from agents' work; it hasn't. The real-time subtest finds its sleep by the seconds it waits, and the systemd-run subtest left a sleep of the same 1005 seconds running. So the check read that one, never real-time and still under the account's limit of 10, and failed although the sorter had demoted the right process.

### 🔧 Solution

The systemd-run subtest's sleep now waits 1015 seconds, which no other subtest uses, and the helper that finds a sleep by its seconds says each subtest's must be its own. vm-apps-come-first comes off `tools/merge-net/quarantine.json`, so its failure blocks merges again.

For Joel: nothing to try; the test that guards your apps coming first counts again.

### 🔬 Validation

- Red: on a branch from main, vm-apps-come-first failed 1 of 20, at `assert rt_limit(1005) == ["0", "0"]`, reading ['10', '10'].
- Green: `nix-offload there -L . checks.x86_64-linux.vm-apps-come-first` at a271d3e60 passed 20 of 20.
- `nix-offload there --changed` passed at a271d3e60.

author: sargunv
body:
Feature-state sets and removes wait for the next render. Until now that render applied every set first and every remove after it. So when a set followed a remove on the same feature or source before a render, the remove undid the set. And a second key removal in one frame was dropped. ffi's command groups put several calls in one frame on purpose, so this comes up often there. Now the map draws whatever the last call asked for:

```rust
renderer.remove_feature_state("fs", None, None, None); // clear the source
renderer.set_feature_state("fs", None, "2", &selected); // before: feature 2 wasn't drawn selected; now it is
```

This ports maplibre/maplibre-native#4835 (still open; maplibre-native-ffi patch 0081) and its gtests. It sets the behaviour of `mln_map_set_feature_state` and `mln_map_remove_feature_state` when both are called in one frame.

One change goes beyond the patch: reading a feature's state now takes pending removes into account, as GL JS does. A read right after a remove no longer returns the removed state. ffi's `mln_map_get_feature_state` would need the same change.

author: bong-water-water-bong
body:
`Refs #2143` — not a fix for it (that is the fork's dispatch path: the flag must stop changing behaviour), but the part a reader of these pages needs **today**, because two pages teach the flag as a measurement instrument and neither said that using it perturbs the measurement.

## The measurement this is built on

From #2143, same binary, model and request, mask kernels on:

| arm | NaN logits | an 18,782-token `/completion` |
|---|---|---|
| flag **unset** | 2 | **fails** — *"Remote end closed connection without response"* |
| `=1` | 0 | **succeeds**, `prompt_n = 18782` |

and a published rate of mine that is a casualty of the same thing: one plain 18.6k prefill measured **271.75 t/s** unset and **118.86 t/s** set. A 2.3× gap is not "logging cost" — it is a different code path.

## What changed

```
docs/determinism.md  § "What the `hrx` width gate is, by name"
docs/zyphra.md       the bullet that says to take the dispatch histogram before quoting a ratio
```

Both now open with a blockquote carrying the numbers and the two consequences that follow:

> a rate taken with the flag is not comparable to one taken without it, and an A/B that sets it on one arm only is not an A/B.

In `determinism.md` it sits **before** the method rather than after it — a caveat that arrives after the instructions is read after the reader has already started measuring. In `zyphra.md` it sits between the recommendation and the next bullet, which is a clean markdown boundary.

## What I deliberately did not touch

**`docs/hrx.md`.** Five open PRs are editing it (#2157, #2136, #2130, #2126, #2035), and its table row that recommends the flag wants this same sentence — but adding a sixth contender to that file tonight pays the rebase cost for a line that is worth exactly as much tomorrow. Whoever lands one of those five can paste the blockquote in, or I will once the queue drains; the text is identical and this PR is the source of truth for it.

That is the same call as #1979 (eighteen PRs on `CMakeLists.txt`): when a file is the queue's collision point, the right move is to write the finding where it can land rather than to join the pile.

author: 0x1ocean
body:
## Taken over, 2026-11-12

Its Thread had stopped. Rebased on main, where #1459 landed; its eight commits went on clean. One commit added: the fake ssh in `e2e/arc.ts` puts arc's own `bin` first on PATH, as `arc.start` does. Without it, an arc started again from the window's Start ran this machine's `hostname`, so "New shell here" wrote nothing the test could read. The Pane was right all along: a log of its states showed the new boot, `restarted`, `running`, and every key sent.

Run on devbox with the window: `remote-terminal.spec.ts`, `update.spec.ts` and `hosts.spec.ts`, 38 of 38. Picture of the Ended foot, from the test: matches the description below.

Stage 2 of the roadmap, Remote Panes: another machine's Panes run on that machine's engine, and this device only draws them (ADR 0106). This is step 1d, window half, part 1: "Ended" in a terminal, and the update's wait for a program in this machine's terminals. Part 2, a close while the machine is away, is #1475. The engine half (`terminal.running`) is #1319, merged.

## What changes for the Person

- If Banda restarted on arc, arc's terminal no longer gets a new shell silently. The screen stays as it was, and the foot says "Ended: Banda restarted on arc", with a power icon and a "New shell here" button. Nothing starts until the Person presses it, and then the keys go to the new shell. On this machine the foot says "Ended: Banda restarted". A shell closed under the same boot still restarts silently, as before. A program terminal (not a shell) also says Ended, with no button.
- A Pane drawn on a new engine connection, after the old one said goodbye, keeps the boot it ran under. It looks for its shell before it opens one, so a new boot shows Ended instead of a silent new shell.
- An update that waits now also waits for a program running in front in one of this machine's terminals, so a restart no longer kills `cargo build`. Programs in arc's terminals hold nothing here. It counts only once every Project has answered. If a stream or the Project list is refused, as by an older engine, that counts as none, so an update is never held for ever.
- The popover says what it waits for: "Waits for a program in a terminal to finish", or for Threads and programs together. Its warning names terminal programs as well as Threads.

## How it was tested

- Unit tests, each seen failing once with the code broken by hand:
  - `client/web/src/terminal-pane.test.tsx` covers Ended in five cases: under a new boot, on this machine, under the same boot, on a new engine of either boot, and for a program.
  - `client/web/src/bar/Update.test.tsx` (new) covers the update's wait. It does not restart until every Project answered. A program holds it. A refused stream and an unreadable list count as none. Threads hold it. The stream is let go.
  - `client/web/src/bar/updating.test.ts` covers the words.
- e2e, each seen failing with the code broken by hand:
  - `client/desktop/e2e/remote-terminal.spec.ts`: after `banda stop --force` and Start on arc, the terminal says Ended. It starts nothing by itself, and "New shell here" starts a shell on arc that takes keys. Another test checks that a program in arc's terminal does not hold this machine's update.
  - `client/desktop/e2e/update.spec.ts`: `sleep 600` in a terminal here holds the update, says so, and the restart comes once it ends.
- Same-path roads turned on: `ended` and `update-wait`. Both run in `remote-terminal.spec.ts`, which is already in ci.yml's `same-path` list, so ci.yml is unchanged. A reviewer ran the whole spec with `BANDA_SAME_PATH=require`, and it passed.
- Local results after the rebase on today's main:
  - `scripts/check.sh ts` passed. Under load, `sdk/contract` `engine.test.ts` timed out (load average 8.5). It passed 28 of 28 run alone, and this PR does not touch it.
  - `remote-terminal.spec.ts` plus `update.spec.ts`: 16 passed.
  - The full `--no-window` check and the neighbouring specs are left to `ci`.

## Pictures (local, not uploaded)

- `/home/roma/Banda/artifacts/remote-panes/shots/1d-window-half-part-1-/ended-restarted.png` (dark), matching mock frame D4, variant 4A (`png/06-d4-banda-restarted.png`). It shows arc's terminal with its screen kept, the foot "Ended: Banda restarted on arc", and "New shell here".
- `/home/roma/Banda/artifacts/remote-panes/shots/1d-window-half-part-1-/update-waits-terminal.png` (light), matching S3's variant 4B, the note on the update card (`png/06-d4-banda-restarted.png`), with the plan's words. The popover says "0.2.0 → 0.3.0, Waits for a program in a terminal to finish", with `sleep 600` in front. The mock names the program ("cargo build"), but `terminal.running` only counts, so it says the plan's words. #1481 tracks naming the program.

## Words it adds

- "Ended: Banda restarted on arc" / "Ended: Banda restarted"
- "New shell here", and when refused "New shell here was not sent"
- "Waits for a program in a terminal to finish", "Waits for N programs in terminals to finish", "Waits for a Thread to finish its turn and for a program in a terminal to finish"
- "Restarts once Threads and terminals are idle", said before the terminals answer
- The warning "A program runs in a terminal. A restart stops it." (and its plural and combined forms)
- The hover line "Restarts into X once Threads and terminals are idle", in place of "once no Thread works", which would be untrue during a terminal wait.

The last three are not in ADR 0106's "The words". They are my wording, for Roma to see.

## Where it differs from the plan

- `terminalPane.closed`, `closedOf`, the queue and the pill count are not here. They are part 2, #1475.
- The e2e presses Start on arc's sidebar row after `banda stop --force`, because Banda on arc stays stopped until asked.
- `Bar` now takes `engine` instead of `status`, so `Shell` has one prop fewer and `WINDOW_LINES` goes from 954 to 951.

## Issues opened

- #1475 part 2: a terminal closed while its machine is away closes there once it is back
- #1477 a terminal Pane restored after a window restart still starts a new shell silently, even when Banda restarted on its machine
- #1478 an update waiting for idle does not restart by itself while this machine's engine is out of reach
- #1479 "New shell here" opens in the Project's folder, not where the Person was
- #1480 an ended terminal keeps a block cursor
- #1481 the update's wait says how many programs hold it, not which
- #1482 comments in client/desktop still say an update restarts once no Thread works

Part of ADR 0106 (stage 2, Remote Panes).
