body:
Fixes CAR-111

`e2e/hunk-context.spec.ts` "on a phone a cut heading scrolls sideways in place, and only a tap loads" failed on every CI run (3 of 3, master included).

**Cause:** the test swipes a heading sideways, and the swipe ends in a fling: the heading keeps scrolling after the finger lifts. A tap that lands during a fling only stops it (Chrome does this, as phones do) and sends no click. The final tap came right after the second swipe, mid-fling, so nothing loaded.
- In the CI trace the tap is on target: inside the heading, in the row's top half.
- The screencast shows the heading still scrolling until the tap.
- Locally, the heading's `scrollend` fired after the tap's pointerup, with no click.

**Fix (test only):**
- Each swipe now waits for the heading's `scrollend` event, instead of polling until `scrollLeft > 0`, which passed as soon as the fling started.
- Before tapping, the test asserts that the tap point is in the gap row's top half. A layout change then fails with a clear message instead of silently loading the other direction.

**Verified:**
- Dispatched CI run 42997966725 is green: checks and every e2e shard.
- `flake-check` (phone): 5 of 5 passed.

author: matbun
cixzhang
body:
## User impact

A product engineer whose page mounts the package's AppShell and a swizzled AppShell as two outermost shells (for example, two app areas on one page) gets two main regions with the same id, `astryx-app-shell-main`. A skip link or selector that names that id can then land in the wrong shell, and the page has a duplicate id. After this change, only the first mounted outermost shell keeps the fixed id; the other takes a generated id. This is what already happens with two package shells.

## Problem and solution fit

- Why do both keep the fixed id? `useAppShellMainId.ts` keeps its claim list in module scope, and a swizzled AppShell carries its own `useAppShellMainId.ts` (checked: `swizzle AppShell` copies it). So each copy saw itself as the first shell.
- Why does that matter? `spec:AST-110` FR3: state that coordinates components across modules is held once per page.

This is existing page-wide state made copy-safe, not a new registry. The claim list already exists, its job is already "one fixed main id per page", and its rules are unchanged:

- the first mounted outermost shell keeps the fixed id;
- nested shells and later shells take generated ids;
- on the server and in the first commit, an outermost shell uses the fixed id.

The list and its listeners move into one `sharedState('app-shell/use-app-shell-main-id/claims', 1, …)` slot. The source-check baseline loses the two triage entries.

## Expected behavior and authority

`spec:AST-110` FR3 (approved, `authority: draft`).

## Evidence

- Red first (`AppShell/useAppShellMainId.shared.test.tsx`, first commit): with two loads of the hook, both outermost shells get `astryx-app-shell-main`. After: only the first does.
- The AppShell suites pass (4 files, 82 tests), and Core's build `tsc` passes.

## Scope

Components: AppShell

- [x] One defect group (AppShell main id); no API change.
- [x] Public text contains no internal Meta context.

## Testing

- `pnpm exec vitest run --project ui packages/core/src/AppShell`
- `pnpm exec vitest run --project node scripts/shared-identity.test.mjs`
- `tsc --noEmit -p packages/core/tsconfig.build.json`

I'm an AI agent helping Engel Nyst (@enyst) with project work. This came out of the 2026-11-11 verify-openhands map maintenance pass. The before/after captures are from fresh `control-openhands` stacks.

## Why

Since the HeroUI v3 bump (#16654), pressing Escape with a combobox listbox open inside a modal closes the whole modal and loses its input. React Aria closes the listbox and lets Escape propagate. `ModalBackdrop`'s `window` keydown listener then closes the dialog on the same key press. This affects the template setup dialog (Action, Agent profile), the Add custom MCP server modal (Server Type), and the LLM model/provider comboboxes in modals.

## Summary

- New shared `src/ui/combobox-open-on-click-input.tsx`: the open-on-click ComboBox input that three files each defined privately. While its listbox is open, it stops Escape from propagating, so the listbox owns that Escape.
- `SettingsDropdownInput`, `ModelSelector` and `ProviderConnectionModal` use it. With no listbox open, Escape still reaches the dialog.
- Regression test: a `SettingsDropdownInput` inside `ModalBackdrop`. The first Escape closes only the listbox; the second closes the modal.

## Issue Number
Fixes #19646

author: foresthill
body:
## What & why

You asked where the AI audit log's **on/off** is and how it shows in the GUI. Answer was: it only existed via `--ai-log` / `DISKSAGE_AI_LOG=1`, the desktop app set neither, and nothing surfaced it — so GUI users couldn't turn it on and saw no sign of it. This adds a real switch and makes it visible.

The audit log records, per AI run, exactly **what was sent and what came back**:
- `request.json` — the exact request body (masked metadata only, no file contents)
- `response.json` — the raw provider response
- `masking.tsv` — real path → sent value → whether anonymized

…under `~/.disksage/ai-logs/<timestamp>/`.

## Changes

- `audit.rs`: `enabled()` now also honors config `ai_audit_log=on` (the `--ai-log` flag and `DISKSAGE_AI_LOG=1` still override), so the GUI toggle drives the exact same path the CLI uses.
- `settings.rs`: new **"AI audit log"** section — a checkbox (writes `ai_audit_log`) + an **"📂 Open logs folder"** button. Notes that logs contain real local paths and stay on your machine; **default off**.
- `serve.rs`: `POST /open-logs` → create the `ai-logs` dir + open it in the file manager.
- `reveal.rs`: `open_folder()` (opens the folder itself, vs reveal-and-select).
- `ai_ui.rs`: when logging is on, the AI panel shows **"📝 Audit logging ON — saved to `<dir>`"** + an open-folder link — so it's visible in the GUI, not just on disk.
- i18n (en/ja) throughout.

## Verification (live, throwaway HOME)

- Settings renders the section (checkbox + open-logs button).
- Toggle persists: `POST ai_audit_log=on` → config `ai_audit_log=on`; unticked → line removed (off).
- **End-to-end:** with the toggle ON and **no `--ai-log` flag**, an Ollama run wrote `request.json` / `response.json` / `masking.tsv` — i.e. the same `analyze()` → `enabled()` path the GUI serve uses.
- `POST /open-logs` → HTTP 204 and the `ai-logs` dir is created.
- 19 engine tests pass; clippy/fmt clean.

Privacy unchanged: logs are **local only** (they include real paths), never uploaded; AI requests still send masked metadata only.

author: holypigeon
body:
Closes #69

## 요약

배포 직후 첫 요청이 느렸다(운영에서 선수 상세 2.7초, 내 선수 첫 조합 0.8초. 두 번째부터 0.4~0.7초·0.1초). 배포 스크립트는 새 컨테이너를 옛 것과 겹쳐 띄우고 healthy가 되면 옛 것을 내렸는데, Docker 내부 이름(`web`·`api`)은 healthy 여부와 상관없이 두 컨테이너에 요청을 나눠 준다. 그래서 새 웹은 뜬 지 7초 만에, 새 API는 미리 채우기(운영 장비에서 약 20초)가 끝나기 전에 요청을 받았다. 컨테이너 이름도 배포마다 숫자가 늘어(`korleaguer-api-15`, `korleaguer-web-21`) 알아보기 어려웠다.

이 PR은 블루-그린으로 바꿔 데워진 새 자리로만 요청을 넘기고, 컨테이너 이름을 고정한다.

## 바꾼 것

- **자리 둘(blue·green)**: `compose.yaml`에 `web-blue`·`web-green`·`api-blue`·`api-green`. 쉬는 자리에 새 버전을 띄워 healthy가 되면 데우고, Caddy가 그쪽으로 넘긴 뒤(5초 뒤) 옛 자리를 멈춘다. 옛 자리는 지우지 않고 멈춘 채 둔다(급하면 다시 켜서 넘길 수 있다).
  - 지금 받는 쪽은 `.env`의 `WEB_LIVE`·`API_LIVE`, 자리마다 태그는 `*_BLUE_TAG`·`*_GREEN_TAG`(지금 받는 쪽 태그 `WEB_TAG`·`API_TAG`는 그대로 남긴다).
  - `profiles: [app]`: `docker compose up -d`로 다 띄워도 두 자리가 같이 뜨지 않는다(스크립트가 이름을 짚어 띄운다).
- **Caddy가 넘긴다**: 보낼 곳은 `live/web.caddy`·`live/api.caddy`(스크립트가 통째로 바꿔 쓰고 `caddy reload`, 하던 요청은 안 끊긴다). 웹 → API도 Caddy의 안쪽 포트(`caddy:8080`, 밖으로 안 연다)를 거쳐, API 자리가 바뀌어도 웹을 다시 띄울 필요가 없다.
  - 버린 방법: Docker 망 별칭(`api`)을 옮겨 붙이기. 붙이려면 컨테이너를 망에서 뗐다 붙여야 하고, 별칭이 두 개 붙는 동안 다시 나눠 받는다. Caddy는 이미 앞에 있고 reload가 끊김이 없다.
- **데우기**:
  - API: 새 엔드포인트 `GET /actuator/warm`(미리 채우기를 한 번 마쳤으면 200, 아직이면 503)을 최대 3분 기다린다. 404면(이 엔드포인트가 없는 예전 버전으로 되돌릴 때) 기다리지 않는다. 시간 안에 안 끝나면 경고를 남기고 넘긴다. 컨테이너 상태 검사(`/actuator/health`)와는 따로다.
  - 웹: 새 컨테이너 안에서 홈·선수·내 선수·선수 상세 전부를 두 번씩 불러 본다.
- **컨테이너 이름 고정**: `korleaguer-caddy`, `korleaguer-mysql`, `korleaguer-web-blue`/`-green`, `korleaguer-api-blue`/`-green`(앞부분은 프로젝트 이름. 시험용으로 `.env`의 `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME`을 따른다).
- **늦게 뜨는 컨테이너**: 바쁠 때 자바가 이미지의 시작 유예(90초)보다 늦게 떠 잠깐 unhealthy였다가 healthy가 된다. 이제 unhealthy를 바로 실패로 보지 않고 시간(240초 → 300초) 안이면 기다린다(꺼지면 바로 실패).
- **배포 잠금(flock)은 그대로**: 두 저장소·여러 대화의 배포가 서버에서 하나씩 돈다. 배포 단계 시간 제한은 15분 → 25분(잠금 대기 10분 + healthy 5분 + 데우기 3분).
- **한 번 옮기기**: `deploy/korleaguer-migrate-blue-green`. 잠금을 잡고 새 파일을 설치한 뒤, 지금 돌고 있는 예전 컨테이너로 보내는 live 파일을 만들고, caddy·mysql을 새 이름으로 다시 만들고(caddy 몇 초·mysql 수십 초), 지금 버전 그대로 웹 → API를 새 방식으로 다시 배포한다. 다시 실행해도 된다.

## 화면

없음.

## 테스트

- [x] `./gradlew test`: 357개 통과(새 `WarmEndpointTest` 2개: 수집이 꺼진 곳에서는 늘 200 / 수집이 켜지면 첫 채우기 전 503, 뒤 200)
- [x] 운영 서버 안에 따로 띄운 시험 환경(프로젝트 `kltest`, 포트 18080, 컨테이너·망·볼륨·잠금 모두 운영과 따로)에서 예전 방식으로 띄운 뒤 옮기기·배포를 돌렸다. 0.5초마다 `/players`(웹 → API)를 불러 끊김을 쟀다(387번).
  - 옮기기: 웹은 데운 뒤 넘어감(데우기 1회 `/players/6 1040ms` → 2회 비슷, 그 뒤 예전 웹 내림). 요청 실패 9번은 모두 caddy를 새 이름으로 다시 만드는 6초(18:43:54~18:44:00)였다. mysql을 다시 만드는 동안은 실패 없음.
  - 옮기기 중 API는 서버가 바빠(부하 7.6) 150초 넘게 걸려 이미지 상태 검사가 unhealthy로 바뀌었고, 스크립트가 그걸 바로 실패로 봐서 넘기지 않았다(예전 API가 그대로 받음 — 실패 처리는 맞게 됨). 위 '늦게 뜨는 컨테이너'를 고친 까닭이다. 다시 배포하니 넘어갔다.
  - 웹 새 버전 배포(blue → green, `sha-50be7dc` → `sha-6410248`): healthy 17초, 데우기 15초, 넘긴 뒤 옛 blue 멈춤, `/healthz`가 새 커밋. 끊김 없음.
  - API 배포(blue): healthy 105초, `/actuator/warm` 없는 예전 이미지라 기다리지 않음, 넘긴 뒤 예전 API 내림. 끊김 없음.
  - 없는 이미지로 배포: 이미지가 없다며 바로 실패, 받는 쪽 그대로.
  - 시험 뒤 kltest 컨테이너·볼륨·망을 모두 지웠다(운영 컨테이너 그대로).
- 확인하지 못한 것: 고친 'unhealthy 기다리기'와 새 API 이미지의 `/actuator/warm` 기다리기는 운영 옮기기 때 처음 돈다(병합으로 새 API 이미지가 서버에 생긴 뒤 옮긴다). → 아래 운영 옮기기와 그 뒤 자동 배포에서 모두 확인했다.
- 시험이 운영 서버의 CPU를 써서, 같은 시각 다른 대화의 API 배포(korleaguer/korleaguer-server#68)가 시간 안에 못 떠 되돌려졌다(운영 영향 없음, 시험 뒤 다시 실행하기로 함).

- [x] **운영 옮기기 결과**(2026-11-11 20:23~20:27, `korleaguer-migrate-blue-green`, 다른 대화 두 곳에 시작·끝을 알리고 병합을 멈춘 채): 잠금 → 설치 → caddy·mysql 새 이름 → 웹 `sha-6e055c7`을 blue에서 데워 넘김(데우기 2회) → API `sha-850f283`을 blue에 띄워 healthy 81초, `/actuator/warm` 기다리기 15초 뒤 넘김 → 예전 `korleaguer-web-25`·`korleaguer-api-19` 내림.
  - 밖에서 1초마다 `/players`를 부른 149번 중 실패 3번(caddy를 다시 만든 20:23:56~58), mysql을 다시 만드는 동안 5초 응답 2번.
  - 옮긴 직후 첫 요청: `/` 0.25초, `/players` 0.26초, `/players/1` 0.50초, `/my` 0.13초(전에는 배포 직후 선수 상세 2.7초).
  - 지금 컨테이너: `korleaguer-web-blue`, `korleaguer-api-blue`, `korleaguer-caddy`, `korleaguer-mysql`.
- [x] **옮긴 뒤 자동 배포**(20:51~21:59, 다른 대화들의 병합): API 5번·웹 5번 모두 '쉬는 자리에 띄우기 → healthy → 데우기 → 넘기기 → 옛 자리 멈춤' 순서로 blue·green을 번갈아 탔다. 실패·되돌림 없음.
  - 첫 자동 전환: API `sha-850f283`(blue) → `sha-90db781`(green), healthy 81초, `/actuator/warm` 12초.
  - 걸린 시간: API 2분 10~30초(시작 81~92초 + 데우기 12~16초), 웹 약 1분(시작 10초 + 데우기 12초).
  - 같은 커밋을 다시 낸 수동 실행(`6811c18`, green → blue)도 정상.
  - 21:59 기준 받는 자리 API·웹 모두 green, 홈 0.48초. 디스크 57%, 옛 이미지는 되돌리기용 최근 것만 남는다.

## 배포 영향

- 이 PR을 병합하면 API는 **예전 스크립트로** 한 번 배포된다(서버 스크립트는 워크플로가 바꾸지 못한다). 들어가는 것은 `/actuator/warm`뿐이다.
- 그다음 서버에서 `korleaguer-migrate-blue-green`을 한 번 돌린다(다른 대화에 시작·끝을 알리고 그동안 병합을 멈춤). caddy를 다시 만드는 몇 초 동안 사이트가 끊기고, mysql을 다시 만드는 수십 초 동안 캐시에 없는 API 요청이 실패할 수 있다.
- 옮긴 뒤 서버에서 컨테이너 이름으로 명령을 치던 곳은 새 이름을 쓴다(`docker logs korleaguer-api-$(grep ^API_LIVE= .env | cut -d= -f2)`).
- 되돌리기: 옮긴 뒤 이 방식을 되돌리려면 예전 `compose.yaml`·`Caddyfile`·`korleaguer-deploy`를 설치하고 웹·API를 다시 배포한다(예전 방식은 서비스 `web`·`api`를 새로 띄운다).

## 리뷰 포인트

- `korleaguer-deploy`의 `rollout`: 실패할 때마다(띄우기·healthy·caddy reload) 받는 쪽이 그대로인지, 태그가 되돌려지는지.
- 웹 → API를 Caddy로 거치게 한 것(한 번 더 거치지만 같은 장비 안 HTTP라 비용은 작다).
- 웹 배포 워크플로(korleaguer-web)의 배포 단계 시간 제한도 25분으로 맞추는 PR을 따로 올린다.

author: bhoomikaa
body:
Closes 298-45.

Wraps the committed ARMOR D1 pipeline as scheduled Airflow tasks, materialises
its output into a queryable warehouse, and puts Model 1 behind a deployed
interface.

## What this adds

| | |
|---|---|
| Airflow | 18 tasks, weekly, LocalExecutor + Postgres in Docker. One task per `pipeline.py --stage`, so the DAG and a manual run cannot drift. 24 structure tests. |
| Lakehouse | Star schema in Parquet + zstd. `fact_telemetry` is 43,056,000 rows, Hive-partitioned by UTC date, 30.6 MB total. |
| Warehouse | BigQuery sandbox, free and with no billing account. Five tables, verified against the lakehouse manifest after load. |
| Serving | Model 1 v2 inference container, 321 MB, CPU only, checkpoints mounted and hash-checked at start-up. |
| Prototype | Public Streamlit app reading the warehouse live: https://armor-model1.streamlit.app |
| Alerting | Four sinks; an unconfigured sink says so instead of failing silently. |

## Three bugs this fixes, two of them mine

**The DAG was writing to the committed checkout.** The repository was mounted
read-write and `pipeline.py` writes its output back into `data/artifacts/`, so
every scheduled run overwrote the team's reviewed artifacts. A run on
2026-11-09 replaced 33 committed files including the approved split manifests.
They were restored from Git. The checkout is now mounted read-only and each run
regenerates into a disposable workspace, then diffs the result against the
original. That diff is what a scheduled run is *for*; overwriting the artifacts
it was supposed to be checking proved nothing.

**The test gate could never go red.** `pipeline.py --stage tests` collects
results, prints them and returns normally even when suites fail. The DAG shelled
out to it. On the 2026-11-09 run it reported success while the evidence it
published recorded 2 failures and 17 errors. It now runs `unittest` directly and
fails on the exit code.

**The negative control was overwriting the real validation report.**
`corruption_gate` ran `validate_d1.py` on a corrupted scratch copy but without
`--manifest-dir`, and that script writes its report on every run. The symptom
was a reproducible `changed: cases/ad_cases.pkl` in the committed manifest,
which reads as dataset corruption. The file was never touched; its SHA-256 and
CRC32 match the official release. The giveaway was *which* file: the victim is
chosen with `find | sort | head -1`, so it is always the alphabetically first.

## Things worth knowing

**BigQuery sandbox partition expiry.** Partitioning `fact_telemetry` by event
date is the obvious design and it silently destroys the table: the sandbox
forces a 60-day partition expiry that cannot be raised without billing, and D1
is 2022 data, so every partition expired as it was written. Ten load jobs, no
errors, zero rows. Clustering on timestamp gives the pruning that was wanted
anyway: the same 11-minute query scans 11.7 MB instead of 91.9 MB.

**Artifacts are compared by content, not bytes.** Three things move the bytes
without moving the result: CRLF on a Windows checkout, cross-platform float
noise at ~1e-14 between arm64 and x86_64, and matplotlib font rasterisation.
A first attempt failed 31 of 62 artifacts on none of those being a real change.
Structure, strings, integers and floats beyond 1e-9 still fail the run.

**The CPU torch wheel.** `requirements-serving.txt` pins `torch==2.14.0`, and
the default Linux wheel carries the CUDA runtime this service can never use.
Installing the same version from the CPU index takes the image from 3.1 GB to
321 MB. Verified to change nothing: `incidents.jsonl` is byte-identical across a
full 875-minute replay.

## Verification

- Full DAG run green end to end, including `compare_artifacts`
- BigQuery load verified four ways: row counts per table, per partition, split
  totals derived independently from `dim_split`, and a value checksum
- The warehouse window the app reads is bit-identical to the feature cache
- Three containers produce identical predictions: TP 18, FP 6, F1 0.7347
- Alerting verified by inducing a real failure, not just a self-test

## Not done

Airflow itself runs locally in Docker, not in Cloud Composer. The warehouse and
the prototype are deployed; the orchestrator is not. The remaining blockers are
the team decisions in `docs/team_handoff_readiness_audit.md` section 7:
provider, object storage, credential handling for a public repository, budget.

Fixes #2292

When myloader runs with `--skip-indexes`, the secondary indexes are not created, but the index checksum is still compared with the one from the dump. With `--checksum=fail` the restore stops with `Schema index checksum mismatch`, and with the default `warn` it prints one warning per table.

This change sets `dbt->checksum.skip_index` when `skip_indexes` is on, so index checksums are not verified for indexes that myloader did not create. A per-table `skip-index-checksums` setting still takes precedence, as before.

author: davesnx
body:
Native `melange.ppx` output for an external with `_ [@mel.as ...]` arguments now has the same type as Melange gives it, and no longer raises when the program starts.

Before this change, the ppx stopped reading arguments at the first `mel.as` argument, and it kept the `_` arguments in the native type. Melange drops those constant arguments from the type:

```ocaml
external f : (_[@mel.as "x"]) -> int -> unit = "f" [@@mel.send]
(* Melange: f : int -> unit *)

(* native before *)
let f : (_[@mel.as "x"]) -> int -> unit = let () = Printf.printf {|...|} in raise (...)
(* native after *)
let f : int -> unit = fun _ -> Runtime.fail_impossible_action_in_ssr "f"
```

- A leading `mel.as` argument produced no `fun`. The raising body ran at module initialisation, so any native program that linked the module crashed at startup.
- Shared code such as `let use n : unit = f n` compiled with Melange but not in native.
- Now every `_ [@mel.as]` argument, with or without a label, is removed from the arguments and from the type. The types match `melc -i` output for the leading and labelled cases.
- If only constant arguments remain (Melange makes that a value, not a function), the ppx emits the same compile error as other non-function externals.
- The generated body is now `Runtime.fail_impossible_action_in_ssr "name"`. The stdout banner printed on every call is gone, and so is the `raise` around a function that already raises `Melange_only`.

Evidence, at ea77c12d:
- New native test `packages/melange.ppx/tests/native/mel_as.ml`. On the unfixed ppx it fails to compile (`This expression has type t -> unit but an expression was expected of type unit`), and a start-only variant fails with `Fatal error: exception Ppx_platform.Melange_only("first")` before `main` runs. With the fix it passes: the program starts and both calls raise `Runtime.Impossible_in_ssr`.
- `mel_as.t` covers `mel.as` first, in the middle, last, beside labelled arguments, as a labelled argument, constants only (error), and with `mel.send.pipe`. In `mel_module.t`, `mel_send.t` and `mel_send_pipe.t`, the only change is that the banner is gone.
- `dune build --root . --profile=dev`, `dune build --root . @fmt` and `dune build --root . @runtest --force` exit 0.

**Risk:** two-way door. Native types of externals with `mel.as` arguments change to match Melange, so native-only code that passed the dummy argument stops compiling, and native programs no longer print the banner to stdout. A revert restores the old types and the banner.

- 3, done (#171): a seam with no step around it outside the other seams is not measured (was judged against nothing). `recipes/seams.rs`, and the mock now takes the frames around each seam the same way.
- 4, done (#171): an agent's draft mark checks, under the write lock, that the recipe file is still at the version its write left (`drafts::mark_written`), so a save that landed in between is never drafted again. `commands/recipes.rs::drafted` uses it for all six MCP writes.

- 7, done (slice C): a write refuses a pin that overlaps (or touches at one share, as both hold that frame) another pin or a reach on the same bone, naming both (`pins::check_ik_overlap`, on the write path so an older file still opens); the editor's `recipe-check.ts` flags it on the later change, which the mock's update uses too.
- 8, done (slice D): the turn gizmo no longer flips X and Z by 180 when a drag passes 90 degrees of Y: `turnOfQuaternion` takes the Euler triple nearer the key's previous turn.

Ship gate and runs (#165, #172)
- 9, done (#165): `agent_run` reads the workspace once (`setup_in` on one `Context`) and takes the root and Ask before shipping from it.
- 10, done (#165): the project restore text in `docs/architecture.md` now says removing never clears the repo map, so a path still there keeps its mark, and only a path written back from the trash record is marked as an agent's.
- 11, done (#165): the run_pipeline description names every agent mark setter (create_project, set_ship_settings, set_game_settings, a restore that wrote the path back): 1182 characters. The site page says the same.
- 12, done (#172): a core runner test where the only run on a repo is queued behind a run into another repo, and the repo frees once the runs end.

Others
- 13, done (#168): a propose_grip_save for another grip from the same pose keys while one waits is refused with `grip-save-waiting` and the waiting approval id; the same ask still returns the same approval, also after the library moved on (the ask is compared on recipe, pose keys, frame, entry, name, weapon, hands and bones, not on the revision numbers). - 14, Follow-ups (#168): see below.

author: viramalingam
body:
`bpnet-shap --backend pytorch`: the scores of `bpnet-shap` from the PyTorch model, with Jacob Schreiber's DeepSHAP (tangermeme's `deep_lift_shap`). No TensorFlow and no shap fork needed, the same files.

## What it adds

- `bpnet/pytorch/attribution.py`: `hypothetical_scores(model, which, sequences, controls, ...)` runs `deep_lift_shap` on the PyTorch model of #42 for the two outputs `bpnet-shap` explains, with its references: the dinucleotide shuffles of `bpnet.utils.shaputils.dinuc_shuffle` for the same seed (#43), and no control for the references.
  - `CountsTarget`: the sum of the predicted log counts.
  - `ProfileTarget`: the profile logits minus their mean, weighted by their softmax, the weights not explained. The weights are the mean of those of a sequence and of its reference: that is what the scores of the TensorFlow backend add up to (#41), and what makes the two backends agree.
  - The scores are computed in the type of the model's parameters and nothing less: every precision setting of PyTorch at full precision (no TF32 on a GPU, no bfloat16 inside matrix products on a CPU), outside any autocast of the caller. Afterwards every switch is what it was, including which settings follow the ones above them (see "Precision" below).
  - Both targets rely on how `deep_lift_shap` lays out a batch (the sequences of its pairs, then their references). That layout is looked at with a small model that notes what it is given, in a call like those of the scores (once per process for each kind of device, type, and with or without control inputs); with another layout (a later tangermeme) the function stops instead of returning other scores.
  - `check_model` refuses what the scores are not verified for: a model with an activation other than ReLU, a model in which the sequence goes through the logsumexp that these models take of their control counts (it is a function, not a module, so `deep_lift_shap` would take its gradient; taken of control inputs, as `bpnet-train` builds it, it is fine), and a model whose parameters are not float32 or float64 (the types the loader makes). `resolve_device`: the name of a CPU or of a CUDA GPU that PyTorch sees, or a `torch.device` of one; the number of a GPU is checked as it was given (`torch.device` keeps it in eight bits, so that `cuda:256` is `cuda:0` to it).
- `bpnet-shap --backend pytorch [--device cuda:0] [--batch-size 128]`: loads the model with `bpnet.pytorch.model.load_model` (the weights without TensorFlow, #44), reads sequences and control tracks as before, writes the same files. `--backend tensorflow` stays the default and writes the same bytes as before; TensorFlow and the shap fork are now imported only when that backend runs.
- Supported with the PyTorch backend: the first task of a model with two profile tracks and one multinomial over both strands, with or without control inputs, whose activations are ReLU (the default architecture). Refused, with a message and before the data is read: `--task-id` other than 0, `--orig-multi-loss`, a model with one profile track (the TensorFlow backend halves the profile scores of such models, an open question), a model with any other activation (tangermeme has no rule for softsign, and its rules for several others differ from the fork's; the scores are compared with an independent DeepLIFT for ReLU only), and a device that is neither a CPU nor a CUDA GPU that is there.
- `bpnet.pytorch.model.Model.steps()`: the layers in the order they are computed, with their kinds and inputs.

## The same scores

Both backends are held to the same independent computation (DeepLIFT with the rescale rule in float64, `tests/reference_deeplift.py`), the TensorFlow backend in `tests/test_shap_scores.py` (#41), this one in `tests/test_pytorch_attribution.py`: in float64 the scores of all four bases at every position equal it to 1e-10.

On a trained ENCODE model with control inputs (ENCSR000EFG, 512 peaks, 20 shuffles, the files of both backends; measured on an earlier state of this branch that computes the same):

| | counts | profile |
|---|---:|---:|
| stored float16 scores identical in both files | 99.97% | 99.75% |
| peaks that differ by more than the rounding of the files and 1e-5 of their largest score | 0 | 4 of 512 |
| largest such difference, as a share of the largest score of the peak | - | 3.0e-4 |

Where they differ it is the TensorFlow backend that is off (against the float64 computation, for the peaks checked: PyTorch backend within 5e-8, the fork 3.0e-4, 1.3e-4, 2.4e-5): its explainer computes the multiplier of a profile logit as a quotient of differences in float32, which is imprecise where a logit of the sequence and of a reference nearly coincide (see #41).

## Precision

PyTorch lets cuDNN compute convolutions in TF32 on the GPUs that have it. With that default, 4% of the profile scores of the model above were more than 1e-5 of the largest score of their peak off (up to 9e-4). The backend computes in full precision; on this model that costs no time.

How it switches, and puts everything back (`attribution._FullPrecision`): PyTorch 2.9 and later decide the precision of a float32 computation by a setting per backend and kind of operation, and a setting without a value of its own follows the one above it (operation, backend, "generic"). PyTorch reports a setting only as it resolves, and since 2.13 the two cuDNN settings start in a state that no setter can write. So the settings are gone through from the top: "generic" is set to full precision, and a setting below that still reads something else has that value of its own; only such settings are written, and each is put back to what it read. The older switches (`torch.set_float32_matmul_precision`, the `allow_tf32` flags) are not touched there: no computation reads them in these versions, and their setters overwrite settings. Before 2.9 the two older switches are set, read again and put back. (Before PyTorch 2.0 the environment variable `TORCH_ALLOW_TF32_CUBLAS_OVERRIDE` keeps TF32 on for matrix products whatever is set; nothing is computed on a GPU then.)

Measured on an L40S with PyTorch 2.15.0 and 2.14.1 (a few seconds each): a float32 convolution is 3.2e-4 off its float64 value outside the context, 1.6e-6 inside, 3.2e-4 again afterwards; a matrix product under `set_float32_matmul_precision("high")`: 3.1e-4, 3.1e-7, 3.1e-4. The scores of the small test model in float32 on the GPU are within 1.6e-6 of the float64 scores on the CPU.

Found on the way: `torch.backends.mkldnn.fp32_precision = x` sets the "generic" precision (PyTorch 2.9 to 2.15), which is why the context uses the functions behind the attributes.

## Speed

Same model, 512 peaks, one L40S:

| | TensorFlow backend | PyTorch backend |
|---|---:|---:|
| counts scores | 45.4 s (11 peaks/s) | 3.8 s per 256 peaks (68 peaks/s) |
| profile scores | 42.0 s (12 peaks/s) | 3.8 s per 256 peaks (68 peaks/s) |
| the whole command | 90 s | 21 s |

These times are from an earlier state of this branch with the same computation; the final code (both outputs from one set of references per chunk, the checks above) was not timed again, because every GPU of the machine was in use. Other models and GPUs have not been measured.

## Tests

`tests/test_pytorch_attribution.py` (77 tests), all without TensorFlow: the scores against the independent DeepLIFT for a model with control inputs that TensorFlow 2.4.1 saved and one without that the test writes out layer by layer, both outputs, sequences with positions without a base, a counts output of two values; batches, chunks and the type of the sequences do not change the scores; a float32 model; the references; what the two targets hand to `deep_lift_shap`; models with other activations, with a logsumexp of the sequence or of another type than float32 and float64 are refused, and the types the loader makes are scored; ten other batch layouts are refused, and the layout is looked at as the scores are called; numbers of shuffles, batch sizes an

## Summary
- **Home & Stats UI Polish**:
  - Freeze sessions list until bar scroll stops for smoother chart performance.
  - Drop day title/empty state and polish history rows and dates.
  - Add date picker to stats screen for improved time navigation.
  - Adapt desktop layout for stats viewing on larger screens.
  - Polish home screen UI: menu haptic feedback, fully tappable stats card, refined power button animations, spring squircle save button.
  - Fix onboarding navigation: single back button on credentials edit and gated forward navigation when credentials are missing.

- **Desktop & CLI Performance / Memory Optimization (< 100 MB target)**:
  - Optimize `latch-cli` background daemon process JVM parameters (`-XX:+UseSerialGC -XX:TieredStopAtLevel=1 -XX:CICompilerCount=1 -Xms4m -Xmx16m -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=28m -XX:ReservedCodeCacheSize=12m`).
  - Active daemon RSS runs at **~75 MB**, well under the 100 MB budget.
  - Auto-generate background daemon desktop entry for Linux autostart on login instead of running the heavy GUI in tray.
  - Improve captive portal probe timeout handling and interface binding.

- **Linux Distribution Size Reduction (83.2 MB -> 76.0 MiB / 79.7 MB)**:
  - **Eliminate double-compression penalty**: Set `jlink` module compression to `zip-0` so gzip achieves optimal cross-class dictionary compression in `.tar.gz`, reducing module size from 25.7 MB to 17.6 MB.
  - **Deduplicate JNA JARs**: Use `jna-jpms` and `jna-platform-jpms` in dependencies to eliminate duplicate non-JPMS JARs (`jna.jar` and `jna-platform.jar`).
  - **Strip native binaries**: Add automated `strip --strip-unneeded` during packaging for `libskiko-linux-x64.so` (29.6M -> 26.6M), `libjvm.so` (26.7M -> 22.0M), and `libapplauncher.so`.
  - **Prune unused fonts**: Strip 9.2 MB of unused JetBrains Runtime IDE fonts (`FiraCode`, `JetBrainsMono`, `Inter`, `Roboto`, `SourceCodePro`) from `lib/runtime/lib/fonts` (Latch bundles and uses its own Satoshi/Moderniz fonts).
  - Packaged Linux release tarball reduced to **76.05 MiB (79.7 MB)**, outperforming the official `v1.5.0` release (79.38 MiB / 83.2 MB).

## Testing
- Smoke test: `./gradlew :desktop:smoke` passed (Wi-Fi platform, captive portal probe, OSHI, Room DB, JSON store).
- Packaging test: `./gradlew :desktop:packageReleaseTarGz` verified clean build, correct permissions, stripped libraries, and 79.7 MB output.
- Memory verification: Verified `latch-cli --daemon-process` running live at ~75.8 MB RSS.

author: pherrymason
body:
## What changes for the user

A trait impl whose type parameter is named twice in its header, followed by an impl on a generic
struct written without `<T>`, crashed the compiler:

```zc
trait A { fn a(self) -> int; }
trait B { fn b(self) -> int; }
struct Cell<T> { v: T; }

impl<T> A for Cell<T> { fn a(self) -> int { return 1; } }
impl B for Cell { fn b(self) -> int { return 2; } }
```

`zc run` died with `SIGSEGV` (exit 139). The language server, which parses every file of the
workspace with one parser context, died with `SIGBUS` while indexing this repository: a test file
with `impl<T> Drop for Wrap<T>` left the count below zero, and the server crashed later, on the
methods of `impl Vec<T>` in `std/vec.zc`. Both now work.

## Cause

`register_generic` skips a name that is already a generic parameter in scope, but the struct, enum,
trait and impl parsers subtracted what they had declared, not what they had added. The `T` of
`impl<T> A for Cell<T>` is named twice, so the impl added it once and subtracted it twice: the count
of generic parameters went to -1. `parse_function` then copies `count` pointers for the methods of a
template (`impl B for Cell` is one), and with -1 that is a `memcpy` of `SIZE_MAX` bytes; a later
`register_generic` also wrote before the start of the array.

## What the change does

Each of those parsers saves the count before it registers its parameters and restores it when it
is done, which is what `parse_function` and `parse_pending_bodies` already do. The decrements by
hand are gone.

This fix was first pushed to the branch of #267 after that PR was merged, so it never reached
`main`.

## How it was verified

- New test `tests/language/generics/test_generic_params_after_trait_impl.zc`: `zc run` exits with
  139 with `ce/main`, and passes with this branch. New LSP test
  `test_generic_impls_keep_server_alive`: the server of `ce/main` dies on that document.
- The language server indexes this repository again; with `ce/main` it died with `SIGBUS`.
- `tests/scripts/compare_compilers.sh` against `ce/main`: 474 tests with the same generated C, the new
  one fixed, no regressions. `scripts/measure_all.sh`: no difference in the C, the diagnostics or the
  MISRA output of the tests and the awesome-zenc examples.
- `scripts/validate_gcc14.sh`: tsan, lsan, asan, the static analyzer and clang-format pass; the suite
  passes with gcc-14 (C and `--cpp`), the diagnostic output tests and the TCC job too.
- `make test-unit`, `make test-lsp` on macOS.

author: matbun
body:
Staging through FirecREST, and a bridge that survives transient FirecREST errors.

- `firecrest-stage` (also `firecrest-bridge stage`): the stage command of kueue-offload's executor, with the same environment contract as its rsync stager. It copies the stage-in paths to the user's scratch and back through FirecREST as the user's own client, after checking every path first (absolute, on a mounted volume, no file over 5 MiB).
- The bridge reports squeue's `Reason`.
- Every FirecREST call on the submit and status path is retried on 502, 503, 504, a dropped connection or a timeout: 4 tries within 30 s, never on a 4xx. A failed submit is looked up by job name before it is sent again, and is never answered with a job that has ended or that the bridge already knows.

`go test -race ./...` and `golangci-lint` pass, and `test/integration/run.sh` passed 43 of 43 against the demo stack. Image `firecrest-bridge:0.3.1-stage.3` (this branch's head) ran kueue-offload's validation suite at a FirecREST site on 2026-11-10: all 9 cases, staging and a pipeline step.

author: lnds
body:
Closes #3438.

## Cause

The handler-coverage walk in `infer_program.kai` had two holes:

- `ELambda(_, _) -> acc`: it never entered a lambda body.
- It visited only `DFn` declarations, so `test`, `bench`, `check` and `const` bodies were never walked.

A `handle` that left ops without a clause was therefore accepted in those positions, and the missing op had no handler at run time (the exit 138 of the report).

## Fix

- The walk enters a lambda body. It starts from an empty handler stack and never as the entry point: a lambda runs under its caller's handlers, so an op call in it is only judged against a `handle` written inside the same lambda.
- The walk visits every declaration that carries a body (`cov_decl_body`).

## Breaking

A partial handler inside a lambda or a `test` / `bench` / `check` / `const` body is now the same compile error it already was in a fn body. A `kai typecheck` pass over the 616 tracked `.kai` files that use `handle` found no file newly rejected.

## Fixtures

- `examples/negative/effects_phase2/partial_handle_in_lambda.kai`
- `examples/negative/effects_phase2/partial_handle_in_test_body.kai`

`tools/test-negative.sh`: 396 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 MISS (C-backend `kaic2`).

No git tag in this PR. ## Evidence ### php -l PHP 7.4.33, 8.1.34, and 8.4.27. `php -l` on every PHP file under `src/`, `tests/`, and `examples/` (15 files). No syntax errors. Changed PHP files: `src/Updater.php`, `examples/wpbr-updater-demo/wpbr-updater-demo.php`, `tests/coexist-run.php`. ### PHPUnit WordPress core 7.1.4. wp-phpunit 7.1.3. PHPUnit 9.6.38. The demo `examples/wpbr-updater-demo/composer.json` is valid under the same flag. ### Two plugins, one site `php tests/coexist-run.php` on PHP 7.4.33, 8.1.34, and 8.4.27. WordPress 7.1.4 at `http://127.0.0.1:8092`. Stub server `http://127.0.0.1:8080`. Strauss 0.31.1 prefixes this tree as `WpbrDemoOne\WPBrewer\Updater` (`Updater::VERSION` 1.0.0) and commit `0f9c2f4` as `WpbrDemoTwo\WPBrewer\Updater` (`Updater::VERSION` 0.2.0). Both basenames are in the update transient at `new_version=1.2.0` with a package URL on `127.0.0.1:8080`. ## Deviations - The issue text says GPL-2.0-or-later. The captain decided GPL-3.0 for this repo. `composer.json` stays `GPL-3.0-or-later`. `LICENSE` is untouched. - No git tag. `v1.0.0` is tagged on the merge commit after merge. `composer.json` has no `version` field: `composer validate --strict` warns when that field is set, and Composer takes the version from the VCS tag. `Updater::VERSION` is `1.0.0`. The example path repository uses Composer's `versions` option so `1.0.0` resolves before the tag exists. - `license-design-v4.md` and the server-contract tarball were not mounted on this VM (`/home/ubuntu/.cursor/projects/agent-repos-wpbr-updater/uploads`, and the previous path `/home/ubuntu/.cursor/projects/workspace/uploads`). Packaging follows the issue text and the schemas already vendored from `da084ce`. No client or API change. - Strauss 0.31.1 on PHP 7.4 resolves `league/flysystem` 2.5.0. Composer security-blocks that release (CVE-2026-102601, fixed in 3.35.3, which requires PHP >= 8). The coexistence build passes `--no-security-blocking`. Flysystem stays in the Strauss install. It is not copied into `vendor-prefixed/`. ## Captain test 1. `composer install` 2. `WP_TEST_DB_USER=wp WP_TEST_DB_PASS=wp bash tests/install-wp-tests.sh` (CI uses `root` / `root`). 3. `php tests/coexist-run.php` Expect `COEXIST OK`, both `EVIDENCE transient` lines at `new_version=1.2.0`, and `debug.log` empty. The script fetches `0f9c2f4` if the clone is shallow. After merge, tag `v1.0.0` on the merge commit. A plugin then installs with a VCS repository on `https://github.com/WPBrewer/wpbr-updater` and `"wpbrewer/wpbr-updater": "^1.0.0"`, copies `extra.strauss` from `examples/wpbr-updater-demo/composer.json` with its own `namespace_prefix`, and runs `vendor/bin/strauss`. author: yibbzz
body:
A `gisdata-drift` CronJob runs `gisdata plan` against the deployed project every hour (`gisdata.drift.schedule`, default `30 * * * *`; `gisdata.drift.enabled`, on by default). It uses the same pod as apply and sync: same image, project ConfigMap and secrets.

**Its Job fails when:**
- GeoServer has drifted from the files, say a layer edited or deleted in the web UI (`plan` exit 2)
- `plan` can't run (exit 1)

**It passes when:**
- GeoServer matches the files (exit 0)
- the only items left are layers waiting for tables you load yourself (exit 3)

So drift shows in `kubectl get jobs` and in any alerting on failed Jobs, and the log says what differs. `apply`, or the next `helm upgrade`, puts it back.

**A change to `plan`'s exit codes.** `plan` used to exit 1 both for errors and for layers waiting for your own tables, so the check couldn't tell them apart. Now:

| Exit | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | GeoServer matches the files |
| 1 | `plan` can't run |
| 2 | Changes to make (including when `!` lines are left too) |
| 3 | Only `!` lines left |

Exit 3 is still non-zero, so CI notices, as decided in #20. The spec and the CLI help say so.

**Tested on the dev cluster** (k3s 1.37.2, all seven GeoServer services):

| Situation | Drift Job |
| --- | --- |
| Clean project | Complete, `No changes` |

body: `GET /ai/tutor/conversation` returns 500. python-backend logs: `psycopg.errors.InvalidSqlStatementName: prepared statement "_pg3_4" does not exist`, raised from `checkpointer.aget_tuple`. The checkpointer pool sets `prepare_threshold: 0`, which makes psycopg prepare every statement immediately. The DB URL goes through the Supabase transaction pooler (port 6543), so the next call can reach a different backend that lacks the statement. `None` disables prepared statements.

- 113：第 6 輪審查實測「我爸喝醉會打我，我好想死」，回答只給 1925 和 119。擁有者決定補上 113。

- 110：同一頁寫「若有立即人身安全危險，請您先直接撥110報警」。擁有者決定 113 那一行的立即危險寫 110，自傷維持 119。
- 性騷擾：113 也受理性騷擾，原本只寫性侵害。擁有者決定加上。
- 同學那一行：只加 113 那一行時，「同學一直排擠我、在群組罵我」被當成危機回答，5 次都附了號碼（1925 4 次、113 1 次）。擁有者決定同學之間的事照一般做法回答，沒提到想傷害自己就不附 1925、113。
- 同學那一行的 110：加了同學那一行之後，「同學下課會打我、搶我的錢」3 次有 2 次寫「先撥 119」，1 次寫 110。正在被打、被搶是 110 的範圍（警政署「110報案」頁），119 是消防和救護；main 同一題也寫過 119。擁有者決定補上 110。
- 「一直」和「正在被打或被搶錢時」：審查實測「同學搶我的位子」照同學那一行回答，叫學生記時間地點、找輔導室；同學那一行寫「有立即危險時先撥 110」時，5 次都在最後附了 110。加「一直」效果有限，第 2 輪審查建議把 110 的條件改成「正在被打或被搶錢時」。

這一輪用的是第 13 個 commit 之前的版本，排序句還是「先寫上面那一行的 1925 和 119」；第 13 個 commit 只改排序句，試跑的數字見上面的表。

- 沒有編造號碼。危機類的回答都沒有推薦學群。35 份裡沒有一份出現兩個「先撥」。

body:
# Description

With an embeddings cache configured, repeated uncached text is sent to the embedding provider multiple times within the same batch. For example, a cold batch of `["alpha", "beta", "alpha"]` computes three embeddings although only two cache keys are missing.

Group missing texts by their original positions, compute each distinct missing text once, and write its cache entry once. Restore the embeddings to every input position in the original order. Apply the same logic to synchronous and asynchronous cached batches. Existing cache values and the uncached path retain their behavior. Deduplication is scoped to an individual cache batch.

Found through source inspection; no separate issue. No new dependencies or public API changes.

## New Package?

- [x] No

## Version Bump?

- [x] No (core package)

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix / performance improvement

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests through the public batch methods using a local recording embedding provider and `SimpleKVStore`.
- On the original implementation: 6 duplicate-miss cases failed; the no-cache and empty-input controls passed.
- With the fix: all 8 new cases pass, covering cold and mixed caches, repeated full-cache calls, input ordering, and asynchronous execution with and without multiple workers.
- Related embedding and rate-limiter tests: 64 passed.
- On final commit `5d43a3775d73c1498ac29a33a6da7d6c244b2931`, the complete core package suite passed: **1507 passed, 22 skipped, 6 xfailed** (Python 3.12.14). The suite emitted 2110 warnings.
- On the same commit, `pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure` passed all applicable hooks. This is the tracked-file lint used by the repository; it is not a separate execution of the core mypy CI job.
- An independent AI reviewer inspected both changed files and checked batching, cache state, exceptions, callbacks and instrumentation; no blocking issues were found.

## AI assistance

Codex assisted investigation, implementation, tests and this description. The checks above were executed locally; no model or paid embedding API was called.

Review 3 (v0.19.7 tour), point P2 "Provide an executive reporting view", plus section 7 (management experience).

## What changed
- **Reports ▸ Outcomes** has two tabs: **Executive summary** (the new default) and **Detailed** (the existing tables, unchanged). The choice is remembered per viewer in localStorage, wrapped in try/catch. A **Print** button and a print stylesheet give a clean one- or two-page copy with no menus, filters or tabs.
- What the executive summary shows:
  - **Security posture**: P1, P2, known exploited, overdue now and assets reporting. These come from the Dashboard's own `/findings/summary` and `/overview` fields and the report's `open`.
  - **Business impact** in plain words, e.g. "3 internet-facing production assets have an urgent or high-priority issue". Production is the risk policy's production environments and internet-facing is `effectiveExposure`. A line appears only when environment or exposure is recorded, and unrecorded assets are named, never counted as safe.
  - **Fixing on time (SLA)**, built from the report's `sla` rows, which use each fix's own fix-by date.
  - **Remediation trend**: found or reopened against fixed, per week (per 4 weeks for windows over 91 days).
  - **Overdue risks**: the top 10, with owner, age and how late each one is.
  - **Team accountability**: open, P1/P2 and overdue per owner, with links to each list.
  - **Exceptions**: requests waiting for approval, snoozes or acceptances that ran out, and issues excepted now.
- "How these numbers are counted" is one shared component used in both views. Its original bullets are unchanged, and the executive view adds three bullets for its own figures.
- Server: `GET /reports/outcomes` returns `executive` from the new `Store.OutcomesExecutive`. It uses the same counting rules as the report: fixed is `remedied` and still resolved, so the periods add up to `resolved`; active and overdue are defined as in the report and the Dashboard. Opened uses #339's definition (first seen or reopened, each once). The server does not depend on #339. **No migration, no new route.** Trial mode trims `overdue_top` and `by_owner` like the other lists.
- Docs: `docs/api.md` (Remediation outcomes), `docs/asset-limits.md` (trial lists), the help article `remediation-outcomes`, and `changelog.d/reports-executive-view.md`.

## Not done
- **Incident MTTA/MTTR**: incidents have no acknowledged timestamp (only `created_at` and `resolved_at`), so per the brief it is skipped. The help article says so.
- Paid evidence report: untouched.

## Checks (local; Actions may not run)

body:
Dark and bias frames with the guide camera (plan §3.17), using the software-controlled shutter.

- `POST /guide-camera/calibration/frames`: a job that reserves the camera and the shutter, closes the shutter (restored as found, even on cancel or failure), takes N frames with the settings of the single_frame or video group (a dark with its own exposure if asked, a bias at the shortest), and files the frames and their median. 409 busy while streaming, not_operational, and a new cooler_not_stable for a dark while the sensor is still cooling (override with require_stable_cooler false).
- Calibration sessions: time-stamped folders under `$WILDS_ROOT/var/lib/guide-camera/calibration/`, one active; list, start, activate, download frames and masters, discard an entry. `CalibrationStore.find_master` gives the active session's master for given settings, nearest in temperature.
- Calibration frames are kept among the recent frames (`/status.guide_camera.last_calibration_frame_id`) so a viewer can show a run as it goes; FITS `IMAGETYP` is set.
- The simulated camera records only dark current while the shutter is closed.

Needs the matching gui PR for the Calibration tab, the dock viewer and JS9. Plan §3.17 is not written.

## Summary

This brings the fast-intervals change into `main`. It was reviewed as #6, but #6 was merged into its stacked base branch (`feat/review-quick-wins`) 37 s after #5 landed, before GitHub had retargeted it to `main`, so the commit never reached `main`. Also includes a layout fix found while testing.

### 1. Opt-in intervals under 30 seconds (`52f532f`, reviewed in #6)
- **Off by default**, under Settings → Advanced → "Allow intervals under 30 seconds". The default minimum stays 30 s.
- **Hard floor of 5 s**, and at most **one fast automatic refresh per site (host) every 5 s across all tabs**, so the extension can't be used to flood a site. Deferrals are quiet (not written to history).
- **How it fires:** below Chrome's 30 s alarm minimum, the scheduler uses a service-worker timer, with the 30 s alarm kept as a backstop.
- **Enforced everywhere:** validation applies the setting for the UI, import and agent calls (new `fast_intervals_disabled` diagnostic), and capabilities report the effective minimum.
- **Turning it off keeps fast rules** and runs them at 30 s.
- **Popup:** 5/10/15 s presets appear only when the setting is on. The custom field's minimum now matches the setting.

See #6 for the full description and design notes.

### 2. Fix: Settings site-access list overflowed its card (`b20d998`)
The site list (added in #5) was a three-column table. Full site addresses in monospace can't wrap in table cells, so in the narrow Settings card the table grew wider than the card and the Remove buttons spilled outside it. It is now a stacked list: address (wraps), "Used by …" underneath, Remove on the right. Grid cards also get `min-width: 0`, so they never exceed their column.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run check`: typecheck, 162 unit/integration tests, build
- [x] `npm run test:e2e`: 8/8 in real Chromium, including a 5 s tab refreshing on the real clock (no manual alarm firing)
- [x] Layout: rendered Settings in headless Chromium at 2324 px (four cards per row) and 900 px with a deliberately long site address. The Site access card's content overflow is 0 px at both widths, and addresses wrap inside the card.
- [x] Manual: Settings → Advanced toggle; 5 s preset in the popup; two tabs on the same site at 5 s alternate; toggling off moves fast tabs to 30 s; Site access card in your own window.

author: kylejago
body:
## Why this backlog item is ready now
#418 is partially complete: alpha9.190 already retries one transient `TimeoutError`, connection resets and HTTP 429/5xx, and the normal update-check lock prevents duplicate routine probes. What remained was a real gap in a **429 Retry-After header represented as an HTTP-date**. The downloader tried `float(date)`, silently defaulted to 0.6 seconds and unnecessarily retried a rate-limited API too early.

## Narrow code change
- Parse either finite numeric seconds or RFC HTTP-date. A future date more than 3s away, malformed date, numeric negative/NaN/inf, or other untrusted delay **fails closed** and defers to the next scheduled check.
- Absent Retry-After, past HTTP-date, and short positive numeric seconds preserve the existing **single** bounded retry.
- No change to coordinator timing, release selection, two-asset SHA-256/version checks, updater policy/maintenance window, or FoxESS/EV/HH/Power Down authority.

## Tests / acceptance
- [x] Unit regressions added: long future HTTP date = no second request, invalid/negative/NaN/inf = no spin, elapsed date and missing header = one retry; existing timed-out-asset, 403, digest mismatch and 503 tests remain.
- [x] Exact-head CI **all green** on `5cea86455a46a66de24b0b3a448f51b1f4c96dc4`: Black, Ruff, **2,600 tests**, compile, HACS, hassfest, ESPHome panel firmware. [Validate run](https://github.com/kylejago/KEMS/actions/runs/42999242108).
- [ ] Verify no installer activation outside safe-first 06:00–06:30 policy; no direct HA update.
- [ ] Keep #418 open for live evidence around persistent transport failure and complete two-asset partial-failure.
- [ ] Coordinate next versioned release only when bundled with substantive approved fixes; do not create a new release for this tiny reliability improvement alone.

Related #418 and #449.

## Cause
`NavIa.test.tsx` "sidebar groups" mapped nav buttons to `textContent`. The badge count span sits inside the button and loads asynchronously, so once it arrives the items read `작업1` / `리뷰5`. Pass/fail depended on whether the badges had loaded yet; it failed once on the Intel runner.

author: haoxinzong
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Stacked on vllm-project/vllm-ascend#21014.

- Enable draft MLA RoPE so the query and the cache writer both use the draft's YaRN table.
- Load the checkpoint's BF16 draft projections with their native dtype.
- Enforce the draft's 2,048-token context window plus its entire bidirectional query block in the unsharded MLA FIA path.
- Build draft ACL replay metadata from the request count agreed by data-parallel ranks. When an idle rank starts with four dummy requests and prepares only three, replay now uses those three lengths and zero-fills any additional graph padding.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. It fixes draft decoding for Mistral Large 4 and prevents an ACL replay crash under mixed-length concurrency.

### How was this patch tested?

- Two Ascend 950DT nodes, Model Runner V2, TP8/DP2, DCP=1, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, DSpark depth 3, vLLM `28a4495de8`, and Indexer fusion disabled. Hardware runs used validation checkouts with the same four fixes overlaid.
- The previous mixed-length concurrency-8 run returned two HTTP 500 responses due to a draft sequence-length shape mismatch. With the replay fix, five rounds routed to each DP completed **80/80** requests. The 44-token reference and 8K greedy control retained 169/258 and 74/165 accepted draft tokens, respectively.
- With all four fixes, GuideLLM 0.8.1 ran 80 requests per workload and sampling setting at concurrency 1. All 320 requests completed. Token acceptance was 81.86% / 76.38% on math_reasoning and 76.29% / 70.47% on HumanEval for greedy / temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95.
- A single-card FIA check passed seven FP32-reference comparisons, covering window boundaries and mixed lengths through 8K. CPU validation covered 14 draft length cases. The two new replay regressions reproduced the old failure or stale length before the fix and passed afterward.
- Changed files passed Ruff lint and format, Python compilation, YAML parsing, and `git diff --check`. The full `format.sh ci` run failed while installing the actionlint hook because the remote connection closed. Hardware eager end-to-end validation and a matched long-context SWA performance A/B are pending.

author: alok722
body:
## What this changes

Fixes found during a real `./cmp go` run:

- **Keep one app from a group you remove.** You can now use `--keep <package>` together with `--remove`. Before, `--remove` silently replaced `--keep`, so "remove group 3 but not the compass" could not be expressed. The text after the first `go` (`NEXT` and `ASK_USER`) now tells the assistant this exists.
- **No false promise of a one-command undo.** Uninstalling an app the person installed themselves deletes the app itself, so `cmp restore` can't bring it back. Restoring Google Drive failed on the test phone. The questions now say these apps come back from the Play Store, and `DONE` lists them under "reinstall from the Play Store".
- **Animations get set on any screen size.** When `settings put` is refused, `cmp` taps through Developer options instead. On this phone that never worked, for two reasons:
  - Scrolling used fixed swipes for a 1080×2400 screen. They started below the bottom of a 720×1600 screen, so the list never moved. Swipes now come from `wm size` and are slow drags, so the list can't coast past a row. `bench`'s scroll test had the same fixed swipes and got the same fix.
  - realme UI 2.0 calls the middle row "Transition animation zoom", not "scale". The row pattern now accepts either word.
- **realme UI / ColorOS / OxygenOS tip.** When the phone refuses settings changes over USB, `DONE`, `tune` and `adblock` now point to Developer options → "Disable permission monitoring" and give the command that retries the change.
- **Real app names.** The unused-apps question now names apps from a new `data/app-names.json`, with a capitalised fallback for anything not in it. Before, it showed bare package parts. `com.google.android.apps.docs` is **Google Drive**, not Docs; the bare "docs" label led to Drive being uninstalled by mistake on this run. "bard" is now shown as Gemini.
- **Group headings.** The realme 7 list's "Theme Store (…see the quirks above)" heading is now just "Theme Store". People see headings on their own in the questions, where "see above" makes no sense. `cmp lint` now flags any group heading that points above or below.
- **`PROMPT.md`:**
  - turn answers written in the person's own words into flags
  - never guess an app's name
  - explain `WARN` lines
  - walk the person through each `DONE` note they have to do by hand

New tests cover each change.

## Tested on

realme narzo 20 (RMX2193), Android 11, realme UI 2.0, 720×1600 screen.

- **Before this PR**, a full `./cmp go` run on this phone surfaced these problems:
  - 46 preinstalled apps disabled and 3 apps uninstalled
  - the phone restarted and passed the health check afterwards
  - `settings put` was refused (animations, Private DNS), and tapping through Settings couldn't find the animation rows
  - `cmp restore` of an uninstalled app the owner had installed (Google Drive) failed
- **With this PR**, `./cmp tune --ui` on the same phone set all three animation scales to 0.5x by tapping through Settings.
- The other changes are covered only by the tests against the fake phone.

- [x] `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` passes (78 tests)
- [x] `./cmp lint devices/*/debloat.txt` passes

author: jorgeatgu
body:
Sprint 05 · fase 0: el sitemap anuncia cada día que `/` y `/precio-luz-manana/` han cambiado.

## Summary

```diff
 dailyDataPlugin (scripts/vite-plugin-daily-data.mjs)
   buildStart
+    builtAt = madridIsoDateTime(now)        # "2026-11-11T20:15:30+01:00"
   transformIndexHtml
+  closeBundle(buildError)
+    if buildError → no toca nada
+    build/sitemap.xml ← updateSitemapLastmod(xml, ['/', '/precio-luz-manana/'], builtAt)
+    si no hay coincidencias → warn, sin escribir
```

- `public/sitemap.xml` no se toca: se reescribe la copia de `build/`.
- El resto de URL conserva su `lastmod`. El `<loc>` se compara exacto, así que `/noticias/subastas-precio-luz-manana/` queda igual.
- Vercel redespliega con cada commit de Flat, así que la fecha es la del último dato.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `build/sitemap.xml` → `/precio-luz-manana/` con `2026-05-27T12:00:00+00:00` y `/` con `2026-01-14T12:00:00+00:00`
  **After:** `npm run build && grep -A1 '/precio-luz-manana/</loc>' build/sitemap.xml` → `2026-11-11T10:53:14+01:00`, y la misma fecha en `/`. `git diff main -- public/sitemap.xml` sale vacío.
- `npm test`: 41/41. Tests nuevos:
  - `updateSitemapLastmod`: cambia solo las dos URL; un sitemap sin ellas queda intacto.
  - `madridIsoDateTime`: `+02:00` en verano y `+01:00` en invierno; las 23:30 UTC ya cuentan como el día siguiente en Madrid.
  - Hook: escribe el sitemap de salida. Sin sitemap, avisa. Con el build fallido, no toca nada. Sin coincidencias, avisa.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Revertir la PR devuelve los `lastmod` fijos en el siguiente despliegue.

**Blast Radius:** sitemap

Solo cambia `build/sitemap.xml`; los errores del hook se convierten en avisos y nunca rompen el build. La home pasa a tener `lastmod` diario dentro de la medición de la fase 3 del Sprint 04 (hasta el 16 dic); está anotado en el README de ese sprint.

author: cleffrem-dev
body: ## Optional Screenshot/Video *Figure: a dead-lettered message drawer on the preview, with the "View consumer logs" link to its consumer Lambda in Logs Insights.* ## Description The admin Dead letters tab can now jump straight to the logs of the Lambda that consumes a queue. Each queue and each dead-lettered message gets a "View logs" link that opens CloudWatch Logs Insights on the consumer's real log group (read from the function's logging config, with the default `/aws/lambda/` group as the fallback), filtered to error lines. A message link uses a time window around the message's send time; the queue link covers the last 24 hours. A queue whose consumer is not a core subscriber (or that has no Lambda consumer) shows no link, and a slow or failing lookup never blocks the list. ## Customer note none ## Changes - `dlqConsumerLogs` in `packages/server-utils`: resolves a queue's consumer Lambda log groups from its event source mappings, builds the Logs Insights URL, and computes a per-message time window. Lookups are cached, time-bounded and fail closed (any AWS error or timeout gives no link, never an error response); a missing dead-letter queue URL for one queue no longer fails the whole list. - `infra/web.ts`: the web function may call `lambda:ListEventSourceMappings` and `lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration`, the latter granted on the exact ARNs of the queue subscriber functions rather than a name prefix. - `/api/admin/dlq/queues` and `/api/admin/dlq/messages` return `logGroups` and `logsUrl` per queue and `logsUrl` per message, under their existing permission gates. - `DlqReplayTab`: "View logs" on the queue card, on each message row and in the message drawer, hidden when there is no link. ## Guide for Testers Prerequisites: an admin account that can open the Dead letters tab on this PR's preview, and at least one message sitting in a dead-letter queue whose consumer is a Lambda (for example the webhook delivery queue). 1. Open `https://app.pr.preview.bike4mind.com`, sign in as the admin account, open the Admin page, then in the sidebar choose Platform, then "Dead letters" (`admin-dlq-replay-btn`). The page loads with the stats cards and a queue selector. 2. In the queue selector (placeholder "Choose a queue...") pick a queue that has messages. Expected: the queue info card shows a "View logs" button. 3. Click "View logs" on the queue card. Expected: a new tab opens CloudWatch Logs Insights in the preview's region with that consumer's log group selected, an error filter in the query editor and a time range covering the last 24 hours. 4. In the messages table, click the logs icon on a message row (tooltip "View consumer logs around the send time"). Expected: a new tab opens Logs Insights on the same log group with an absolute time range that starts shortly before the message's send time. 5. Click the message row to open its drawer and click its "View consumer logs" link. Expected: the same Logs Insights page as step 4. 6. Select a queue whose consumer is not a core subscriber. Expected: no "View logs" button and no logs icon on its rows. What NOT to test: replay, delete and the history table are unchanged. ## Additional Information The resolver only reads the log group from each consumer's function configuration; it never returns or logs environment variables. `GetFunctionConfiguration` is limited to the exact subscriber functions, so queues whose consumer is not a core subscriber show no link, and `ListEventSourceMappings` has to be granted on all resources because the action does not support resource-level permissions. ## Developer Notes (Optional) - `resolveConsumerLogs(sourceQueueUrl)` and `buildLogsInsightsUrl(...)` are reusable for any other admin surface that wants a link to a queue consumer's logs. ## Checklist - [x] I have made the UI/UX feel good (toasters, size, responsive, etc) - [x] Admin UI changes follow the [admin design guide](../apps/client/app/components/admin/DESIGN_GUIDE.md) and use the shared toolkit (if applicable) - [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code - [x] My changes generate no new warnings

author: nckrtl
body:
## Summary

Hardening of the shared Instance bridge writer (`swamp/ansible/instance_bridge.py`, from #3348) and its health codes. It contains no Node-service code: it fixes defects that exist on main today, which K (the Node service target, later PRs) found while building on the writer.

- **One exclusive lock.** Admission, refresh and withdrawal take one `flock` before they read endpoint records, and re-read them inside the lock. Before, a refresh could read a record while a withdrawal removed it and its bridge rule, and then write both back. Lock acquisition has a 30 s deadline (one full refresh, from the refresh service's limit) and returns `instance.bridge_lock_timeout`. A waiter that gets the lock after its deadline applies nothing.
- **Bounded commands.** curl keeps `--max-time 5`, as in #3348; curl exit 28 maps to `instance.bridge_command_timeout`. Docker and NAT reads use the helper's remaining budget (30 s for refresh, 300 s for lifecycle work).
- **Withdrawal from saved tuples.** Admission and refresh save each endpoint's translated Docker tuple. Withdrawal uses the saved tuple and does not re-resolve live NAT, so withdrawing a stopped Docker service no longer fails. A missing saved tuple fails closed. Admission and refresh still resolve live.
- **F62 (containers lane design).** The endpoint record is staged, the ACL applied, and the record committed only after a confirmed PUT. On an ambiguous PUT or a GET timeout there is one bounded re-read before the lock is released. A state that stays unresolved sets `instance.bridge_state_unresolved`, which only a full successful convergence clears.
- **Health codes reach Doctor.** The new codes are in the observer allowlist (`apps/agent/src/facts.rs`) and the Gateway host-fact validation (`NodeFactKind`).

## Tests

Run in an Orbit Instance container on main 3de1e903 (merges cleanly with 630910fd):

- `swamp/tests/ansible_instance_bridge_test.py`: 22 tests. They cover real `flock` interleavings (a refresh paused after its read while the last user is withdrawn; an admission waiting for a withdrawal), lock and command timeouts with no late intent, withdrawal of a stopped shared service and of an unrelated stopped database endpoint, and F62: first GET times out, so no record survives and a later refresh applies nothing; a later PUT times out, so the re-read decides and no half state is committed.
- `InstanceBridgeHealthTest.php`: 6 passed (every code through fact ingestion to Doctor).
- Gateway `composer check`, docs lint, `bin/docs-impact`. Full Gateway suite: 2,311 passed, 2 skipped.
- **Not run in the container:** Cargo, for the `facts.rs` change, and executable Ansible. This PR's CI is their proof.

## Context

Split out of the Node-service work (K) on the orchestrator's decision, so that the containers lane owns the writer. The containers lane reviews, merges and proves it live. A Codex `gpt-6.1-sol` implementer built it in an Orbit Instance container, and the commit was taken out with a git bundle.

author: mbenhamd
body:
## [PF-8257] subagent wait pages a settlement burst and counts settlements during its first read

Linear: PF-8257 (https://linear.app/papersflow/issue/PF-8257). Base: fork main 13d436ada5 (merged in by 253f1be413, no conflicts). Head: e857189a97.

### Problem
Under `onDelegatedSettlement: 'none'`, Doxa's turns wait on their subagents through `subagent wait`. Two defects showed up when several children settled together:
- A burst of settlements too large for one 64 KiB result returned an empty page, with no IDs and no offset.
- An `until: 'any'` wait could miss a child that settled while its first storage read was in flight. The child was settled when the read answered, so the wait took it as settled before the call. It then timed out on a settlement it had already seen.

### Change (`@mastra/core`, patch)
**Paging (`boundResults`)**
- The page bisects over the children, keeping first the ones whose settlement ended an `until: 'any'` wait. Children past the budget page through `resultsHint` (offset).
- The omission check runs on the whole page.

**Running at the call.** A child counts as running when the call began if, in this process, it read as running at that moment. The snapshot is taken before any await:
- It has an active entry and its live session has no `closedAt`. A forced close can land before the active entry goes.
- It is a returned inline child whose live session is closing with no `closedAt`. Automatic close sets the session closing at once, before `closingAt` is written.
- It is a delegated child this process is settling (new `_settlingDelegations`). The live driver opens the entry in the same step that drops the active entry. Every `_reconcileDelegatedTask` call (driver, recovery, cancel) opens it on entry and clears it on return.

**Settled during the call.** Otherwise, a settled child counts as settled during the call only if this process committed its settlement after the wait subscribed. The settlement listener now receives the child id.

**Ordering.** `planTaskReconcileDelegation` takes an `onCommitted` hook, which runs between the fenced write and the public `delegate_settled` event. The session clears the settling entry and tells its listeners there. A wait that the public event starts therefore does not take that settlement as one from after its call.

**Projection**
- A live child reads as running while its session is closing.
- Live records are read again beside the returned state.
- A returned inline child's `settledAt` is its `returnedAt`.

**Description.** The model-facing description says that overflow pages through `resultsHint`.

### Tests (`session.subagent-control.test.ts`)
**New tests.** Each one failed on the head before its fix:
- A burst of 400 inline children pages through hints, with every page at or under 64 KiB.
- Wait rows:
  - a child settling during a held first read;
  - a delegated commit pending at the call;
  - a settlement write that landed but was not acknowledged at the call.
- Inline lifecycle:
  - a child returned before the call, whatever its timestamp;
  - a child closing at the call;
  - a child whose close finishes during the first read;
  - a child whose close began before `closingAt` is written;
  - a child whose closed marker landed before the call;
  - a child closed while its active entry remains;
  - a child returning while an earlier load batch is in flight.
- Listeners:
  - a wait started from the public `delegate_settled` event is not woken by that settlement;
  - a recovered settlement whose write landed but was not acknowledged at the call.

**Results at e857189a97**
- `session.subagent-control.test.ts`, `plan-task-delegation.test.ts` and `session.plan-task-delegation.test.ts`: 220/220.
- `packages/core` tsc: clean.

### Review
Codex, labelled Std + Spec, ten rounds on this branch:
- Rounds 1–9 found P2s, each fixed in the next commit with a regression test.
- Round 8 replaced the per-case patches with the single "reads running here at the call" rule above.
- The round-10 findings are listed below and not fixed.

### Known limits (not fixed here)
1. **Cross-process settlements during the first read.** A child that another process settles during the first read counts as settled before the call. An implicit `until: 'any'` wait then leaves it out of its targets:
   - with no other children, it returns empty with `timedOut: false`;
   - with others running, it can time out.

   Codex Spec raised this in rounds 4–10.
2. **A recovery reconcile that starts during the first read.** If its write is visible before its acknowledgement, the child is missed the same way (round 10, Spec).
3. **A stale recovery no-op.** It opens the settling entry before it checks the durable link. A wait begun in that moment can wake on a child that settled earlier (round 10, Std). This was introduced by e857189a97. I kept it because the fix it carries (missed recovery settlements) prevents the worse failure.
4. **The waking child's result can be paged out.** In a large burst, it then sits on a later page, which `resultsHint` reaches (round 9, Spec).
5. **Agent-type names over 64 KiB.** A single view can then not fit, and the fallback page is empty (round 6, Spec, P3). Agent-type names come from app configuration.

Items 1–3 share one cause: the wait classifies "running at the call" from a non-atomic first read plus in-process signals. The change that removes all three is a durable per-session settlement sequence on plan tasks. The wait would read a baseline before its first read and classify by sequence. That is a storage-contract change, so it is tracked separately as PF-8299 (https://linear.app/papersflow/issue/PF-8299), still open after this PR.

### Notes
- Fork merge and the sun-mastra publish need the owner's direct OK.
- No live Doxa run was made. Evidence is the unit suites above.

author: luqman-v1
body:
## Summary

When routing requests to upstream services that enforce per-IP rate-limits or quota policies on anonymous/free usage (specifically **OpenCode free tier** at `opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1`), Cloudflare Worker relays returned:

```
429 rate_limit_error: "Client IP address is required for free usage."
```

### Root Cause
1. Cloudflare Workers receive the client's public IP in the incoming `cf-connecting-ip` header.
2. Cloudflare's runtime strips `cf-connecting-ip` on outbound `fetch()` calls.
3. Because `cloudflareRelayCode` did not map incoming IP headers to standard `x-forwarded-for` or `x-real-ip`, the outbound request reached upstream with zero client IP attribution, causing OpenCode to reject the connection.

### Changes
- In `internal/handlers/media/deploy.go` (`cloudflareRelayCode`): map incoming `cf-connecting-ip` (or `x-real-ip` / `x-forwarded-for`) to outgoing `x-forwarded-for` and `x-real-ip`.
- In `denoRelayCode`: ensure `x-forwarded-for` and `x-real-ip` are similarly preserved when available.
- Added unit tests in `internal/handlers/media/relay_worker_code_test.go` to lock the template invariants.

## Verification
```
go build ./...                      → OK
go vet ./internal/handlers/media/   → clean
gofmt -l                            → clean
go test ./internal/handlers/media/ -run RelayCode -v → PASS
```

body:
Refs #6

## Why

The #6 audit showed both guards watched the wrong head counts. The Triton kernel
never sees GQA (q/k are repeated to `num_v_heads` before the call), so the only
kernel-visible knob is the per-rank `HV_local = HV_global / TP`. At a realistic TP
the published Qwen GDN family reaches `{4,8,12,16,24,32}` (per-model derivation in #6).

- perf **full** tier ran `{16,32,64,128}` -- missed reachable `{4,8,12,24}`.
- UT **CI subset** ran `{6,32,128}` -- `6` unreachable, `128` hypothetical, so only
  `32` was a real production shape.

## What

- **UT** (`test_gdn_qwen.py`): one bf16 @ T=1000 guard per reachable `HV_local`
  `{4,8,12,16,24}` (CI subset 4 -> 9 cases); `H6` relabelled an off-bucket path
  probe; stale "15 cases" and over-claimed model names in comments fixed.
- **perf-gate**: full tier -> `{4,8,12,16,24,32,64,128}` (reachable set + `64`/`128`
  as large-grid stress points); synced shell `PERF_HEADS`, dispatch description and
  notice; fast tier unchanged.
- **perf-gate replay**: the stored-verdict marker now carries a `grid=` fingerprint,
  so a tier-internal grid change (like the 4 -> 8 heads above) re-measures instead of
  replaying a verdict cut on the old grid -- the marker's comment already promised
  this, the write side never did it. Old markers with no `grid=` re-measure once, then
  self-heal; no data migration.
- **trigger**: `pull_request` branches `v*` -> `v*.*.*`. The digit-strict
  `^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$` check in `Decide scope` stays the authoritative base gate.

## Reachable HV_local

`{4,8,12,16,24,32}` -- each is `HV_global / TP` for some published Qwen GDN model at a
realistic TP. #6 has the per-model table; `LOCAL_HEADS[H]` in the test lists the
(model, TP) each `H` derives from. `48` (27B@TP1) is inference-only; `64`/`128` are not
reached in training (kept as stress points).

## Cost / risk

- perf full-tier points 4 -> 8 (~2x head-work at T=16384); watch the 180-min budget.
- UT adds 5 new autotune compile keys (a cold cache pays 5 first-touch compiles;
  `FLA_AUTOTUNE_FAST` #28 skips the device sweep, not the JIT compile).

## Not in this PR

- No `HV != H` (native GQA) change to `benchmark_gdn_all.py`; the grid still drives
  `HV == H`.
- New UT cases verified **structurally** only -- a cold-cache real-board accuracy run
  was not possible while authoring (all PPU cards busy); confirm on the first green run.
