author: mrrenaud
body:
## Pourquoi

Dans le piano roll, l'outil (et le magnétisme) revenaient à Dessiner / Auto à chaque clip ouvert, et le clic fait pour donner le focus à la grille posait une note, parfois hors de la vue : seul le compteur de notes changeait (#835).

## Ce qui change

- L'outil et le magnétisme du piano roll sont gardés pour la session, d'un clip à l'autre (même mécanisme que la longueur et la vélocité de dessin : `ui.remember` / `ui.recall`, rangés dans la disposition du projet). Une valeur inconnue retombe sur Dessiner / Auto.
- Un clic dans la zone des notes, quand le clavier était sur un autre élément de la page (hors du piano roll), ne fait que lui donner le focus : aucune note n'est posée. Le clic suivant dessine.
- Toute note posée est visible : une note dessinée à la souris est annoncée (« Note ajoutée, G5 », ou « …, coupée à la fin du clip »), seulement si la commande a été appliquée, et la vue défile jusqu'à elle. Les copies de Dupliquer, Répéter, Coller et du générateur euclidien sont aussi amenées à l'écran (sans déplacer le focus) quand le clavier n'est pas dans la grille.
- Texte EN et FR : l'info-bulle de l'outil Dessiner dit qu'un clic venu de l'extérieur ne fait que donner le focus.

## Décisions prises (déléguées au lead)

- Outil et magnétisme gardés pour la session, sur tous les clips. Ce sont des états de vue de la page, pas des données du projet : aucune commande à ajouter (la note posée reste `clip.notes.add`).
- Un clic qui ne fait que donner le focus ne pose jamais de note. La règle est limitée au cas « le focus est sur un autre élément de la page » : sans aucun focus (page vide), un clic reste un clic normal. Une première version (tout focus hors du piano roll) cassait 24 specs existants et aurait coûté un clic à qui crée un clip puis dessine.
- La longueur de dessin (liste « Longueur ») était déjà gardée ; le mode « suit la dernière note » revient au pas du magnétisme à chaque clip, comme avant (inchangé).

## Vérification

- `node scripts/agent/verify.mjs --fix` : RESULT OK en 13 min (scripts agent, prettier, svelte-check, eslint, vitest 131 fichiers ; Playwright : 34 specs de la zone piano roll, `grid` et `piano-roll-edit` en entier, 12 specs de base). Depuis, seule l'info-bulle a changé de formulation (prettier, eslint, svelte-check, vitest i18n et piano-roll OK).
- Tests de régression : `roll.test.ts` (relecture de l'outil et du magnétisme, règle du clic), `piano-roll.test.ts` (piano roll reconstruit avec l'outil et le magnétisme laissés), `piano-roll-edit.spec.ts` (Playwright : Sélectionner et magnétisme gardés quand le piano roll est reconstruit ; un clic Sélectionner puis un clic Dessiner venu de l'extérieur n'écrivent rien ; le clic suivant écrit une note et l'annonce ; console sans erreur ni avertissement).
- Deux specs (`grid`, `piano-roll-edit` « Repeat ») ont reçu un `focus()` explicite : le piano roll y est ouvert depuis une autre vue, le premier clic ne fait donc que donner le focus.

## Revue de Judge Dredd (livraison)

- Annonce « Note ajoutée » sans vérifier que la commande a été appliquée, et deux annonces qui s'écrasent : corrigé (annonce seulement si la note existe, message combiné `saidAddedCut`).
- « Toute note posée est visible » faux pour Coller, Dupliquer, Euclidien, Répéter hors cellule : corrigé (`revealNote` sur ces chemins).
- Aucun focus : la note est encore posée sans focus (page vide) : risque accepté, c'est la décision ci-dessus ; la note est maintenant dite et amenée à l'écran.
- Le test e2e ne rouvre pas un second clip : rejeté, le test reconstruit le piano roll par un changement d'onglet, ce qui passe par le même chemin d'initialisation (vue recréée, états recalculés) ; l'ouverture d'un second clip passe par le même composant.
- `lastLength` revient par clip : inchangé, voir plus haut.
- Info-bulle de Dessiner trop large (« venu de l'extérieur ») : corrigé, reformulée selon la règle réelle (EN et FR, à valider par le fondateur).
- Deuxième passe : mêmes réserves sur `lastLength` (au lead de dire s'il veut un texte), sur la révélation de la seule première note d'un lot (faible), et sur deux types d'outil (`RollTool` et `Tool`, faible) : acceptés.

## Hors périmètre

Aucun défaut hors périmètre trouvé.

## Commit message

```
fix(piano-roll): keep the tool and snap across clips, a focus-only click writes no note

The piano roll recalls its tool and snap from the page's view memory, so a
clip opened later keeps them. A press on the notes area while another element
of the page holds the focus only moves the focus. A note drawn with the
pointer is said and scrolled into sight, and so are the copies made by
duplicate, repeat, paste and the euclidean generator when the keyboard is not
in the grid.

Closes #835

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016MUT29q8jE1VkEeht8DfgP
```

body:
Tester feedback, items 4 and 13.

**Item 4, identity fields looked optional.** Product name, SKU and Category are required, but LaField printed only a screen-reader "(required)", so nothing showed until a save turned the empty fields red.

**Item 13, the barcode blocked progression.** Saving never needs a barcode, but Amazon refuses a create with no barcode and no GTIN exemption (IDENTIFIER_MISSING). The review screen's Identity gate then blocked approval with no way forward, and the exemption was a small switch that was easy to miss. Amazon's rule stays. This PR fixes the guidance.

What changed:

- `LaField required` shows a quiet "Required" word next to the label, in ink-3 caption text. It is never red and has no asterisk. Screen readers hear it in the control's description, so accessible names stay the plain label. A string swaps the word, e.g. "Needed for Amazon". The calm first visit stays: an empty required field still turns red only after a save attempt.
- Guided form: Product name and SKU get the mark. Category already passed `required` and now shows it. The product editor marks Product name and Category while Category can still be changed. Brand name on setup was already `required` and now shows the mark too.
- Barcode field: a two-option choice, "Has a barcode" or "No barcode: my brand has an Amazon GTIN exemption", followed by "Amazon approves GTIN exemptions per brand and category. Choose this only if yours is approved." When Amazon is ticked in List on, the label says "Needed for Amazon" and the hint reads "GTIN-8, 12, 13 or 14: an EAN, UPC or GTIN from the pack. Amazon needs one to create the listing." The SI12 "Amazon needs this" chip is not repeated next to it. Styles get "Variants have barcodes" / "No barcodes: …".
- Variants page: the same choice and mark replace the "No barcodes (exempt)" switch.
- Review: when IDENTIFIER_MISSING blocks the Identity gate, its row says "Amazon needs a barcode (EAN, UPC or GTIN) to create this listing, or a GTIN exemption if Amazon approved one for your brand." It lists up to three variant SKUs, then "and N more". People who can edit products also get "Add barcode or exemption". That button opens `/products/$id?edit=barcode`, which starts the editor on Overview (after the variants load, so a style gets its exemption choice) and focuses the barcode.

No API change.

Tests: la.test.tsx (the mark, its words, its description), barcode-field.test.tsx (the choice, the Amazon mark and hint, no duplicate chip, the style choice), guided-identity.test.tsx (marks on first visit, no red on blur, the Amazon-only mark, the exemption choice), identifier-fix.test.tsx (the gate helper, the reason, the SKUs, the link, no action without edit rights), detail-tabs.test.ts (`?edit=`). Typecheck and lint are clean.

author: mfx1590
body:
Refs #809 (follow-up from #815's admin review). Window 1 (core).

## The problem
A just-onboarded store did not appear in the owner's `GET /admin/me` `stores` for up to 30 s, and the admin e2e waited it out with a 45 s reload loop.

`/admin/me` builds `stores` from `scope.storeIds`, which `KeycloakStaffTokenVerifier` caches per staff user in hq-rbac's `ScopeCache` (30 s). Onboarding writes the store's OpenFGA object, but nothing dropped the cached scopes.

For organization-level users, `storeClientFor`, `listStores` and the `x-permission` checks (`fga.check`) never read that cache. So `/admin/me`, and anything else reading the cached `storeIds`, was the stale part.

## The change
- `KeycloakStaffTokenVerifier.invalidateAll()` (`src/http/staff-auth.ts`) clears the verifier's `ScopeCache`. It goes through the `cache` the scope middleware already exposes; hq-rbac / auth-sdk (window 2) is unchanged.
- `buildStaffAuth()` returns it as `onStoreScopeChange`.
- `mountCoreMiddleware` passes it to `adminRouter({ onStoreScopeChange })`.
- `POST /admin/onboarding/stores` calls it after `onboardStore` succeeds, for both 201 and 200. It is not called on a 4xx.

**Why every entry and not only the creator's:** the new store's OpenFGA object reaches every organization-level user (owner, finance, analyst, support, operations) through the organization relation. Invalidating only the onboarding user would leave the others stale for 30 s.

This changes **when** cached scopes refresh, never **what** they grant: the next request re-resolves from OpenFGA. Onboarding is rare (a brand every few days), so the cold cache costs one ListObjects per active staff user, once.

**Other processes:** each core process has its own cache. A second process still refreshes within 30 s, as before. The onboarding request's own process, which serves the admin's next call in the e2e and on a single instance, is immediate.

## Tests: `test/scope-invalidate.test.ts`
The setup is the REAL `KeycloakStaffTokenVerifier` with the **default 30 s `ScopeCache`**, a JWT verifier that answers for the seeded owner, and an OpenFGA fake whose visible stores grow when the registrar writes the store object (what the real registrar does).
- The owner's `/admin/me` is cached, then the owner onboards a store. The next `/admin/me` lists it immediately.
- **Control:** the same flow without the callback still lacks the store (the 30 s staleness the e2e waited out), until `invalidateAll()`.
- A refused onboarding (400) clears nothing.

## Gates
- Typecheck 0, lint 0, prettier clean.
- **Local, after the stack came back (2026-11-12):** `test/scope-invalidate.test.ts` 3/3 (the immediate store, the control and the 400); `test/admin-api.test.ts` 41/41.
- On 2026-11-11 the shared Postgres had been down (Docker Desktop wedged, restarted by the owner).
- CI: `unit` green on its own Postgres. `live auth + end-to-end`: every vitest suite passed, but `playwright install` failed on the runner's DNS (also on main). The manager re-ran it.

Window 4 drops the e2e's 45 s reload loop after this lands.

author: kibouakari
body:
## Scope
Stacked on #59, the shared-note revocation hotfix. This branch is not merged to main and is not deployed. No brute-force requests or destructive tests were sent to production.

### Login and abuse prevention
- Verified `POST /api/auth/login` already uses a MongoDB-backed atomic limiter: 60 attempts per client IP and 20 attempts per normalized account in a 15-minute fixed window.
- Counter writes now fail closed if the database cannot confirm them. Evaluate both rate-limit dimensions before returning 429, with Retry-After.
- Parse Vercel-forwarded IPs only under the platform environment, falling back to the socket peer for malformed input.
- Limit authenticated password-change attempts separately (30 per IP and 8 per account per 15 minutes).
- Verify a cached dummy bcrypt hash for absent or passwordless accounts to reduce account enumeration via response timing.

### Injection review
- Inspected Pydantic request types and MongoDB filters across authentication, search, sharing, notes, tasks, calendar and remote calendar feeds. No SQL database is present, and no confirmed exploitable injection was found in the reviewed paths.
- Added negative tests for `$ne`, `$gt` operator objects and regex special characters in search.
- Remaining XSS/browser controls and external SSRF/NoSQL review must be treated as release checks, not proven safe.

### Rankings and privacy
- `GET /api/leaderboard` returns separate `friends` and `participants` rankings.
- Accepted friends always see each other's challenge points even without public consent. Pending and removed friends never receive private ranking access.
- The community leaderboard requires affirmative opt-in for visibility to unrelated users. The viewer can always see their own entry. Other account IDs/emails are not returned.
- A bounded 2,000-record community query is not a globally exhaustive ranking at scale. Scores remain self-reported.
- Frontend shows friends separately and updates on friendship changes.

### Other data leakage
- Stale shared notebook membership no longer reveals notebook titles via notifications after unfriending.

### Documentation
Updated changelog, README, social/calendar, data model, architecture, API integration, deployment, release checklist, roadmap, product brief, security policy and security risk register to reflect current source and unresolved production checks.

### Validation and rollout
- Review and pass frontend, backend tests, typecheck, npm/pip audits and docs CI.
- Verify with two test accounts in a private preview, including friendship acceptance/removal, rankings, account and IP throttling, malformed input and real trusted proxy headers.
- Ensure MongoDB rate-limit TTL indexes exist. Avoid brute-force or denial-of-service tests against production.
- This PR depends on the unfriend fix in #59; the independent realtime collaboration PR #57 is not deployed.

author: melgarafael
body:
## O que aconteceu

Na primeira instalação real (VPS HostGator, Ubuntu 22.04, pelo comando de uma linha), o instalador terminou dizendo que tudo respondia. Não respondia: o Asterisk subiu sem o plano de discagem e sem a interface de controle (ARI), e o processo de voz ficou tentando conectar sem sucesso. Nenhuma ligação seria atendida.

**Causa:** `extensions.conf` e `http.conf` eram montados direto do repositório. Com umask 077, o clone os cria legíveis só pelo dono, e o Asterisk roda com outro usuário dentro do contêiner (`Parsing '/etc/asterisk/http.conf': Not found (Permission denied)`).

**Por que ninguém viu:** a checagem de saúde considerava o Asterisk bom se ele respondesse a um comando, sem conferir se o processo de voz conseguia falar com ele.

## O que muda

- Tudo o que o Asterisk monta sai de `deploy/asterisk/generated`, gravado pelo instalador com permissão explícita, qualquer que seja o umask.
- Linha essencial nova na checagem de saúde, **Controle da telefonia**: falha quando o processo de voz não está conectado ao Asterisk, com o motivo e a causa provável. Como o instalador espera as peças essenciais, ele deixa de dizer "pronto" nesse estado.
- `DESKVOICE_PANEL_LOCAL_ONLY=yes`: sem domínio e com 80/443 de outro proxy, o painel abre só de dentro da VPS, por túnel SSH. Reinstalar mantém a escolha.

## Como foi verificado

- `install/test/02-env-and-templates.sh`: sob umask 077, os cinco arquivos existem na pasta montada com 644 e a pasta continua 700. Falhava antes da correção.
- `install/test/07-healthcheck.sh`: voz sem conexão com o Asterisk dá código 1, também no modo essencial. Falhava antes.
- `install/test/04-dry-run.sh`: painel só local e valor inválido da variável.
- Suíte do kit: 411 verificações. `shellcheck` limpo.

## O que não foi verificado aqui

A correção ainda não rodou na VPS onde o defeito apareceu. É o próximo passo, depois do merge.

## Requer atenção

Quem já instalou precisa rodar `bash install/install.sh` de novo depois de atualizar.

author: adamsalves
body:
Closes #43

## Contexto

A #43 audita o protótipo (`docs/design/`) contra o app. As 5 divergências de comportamento foram decididas pelo dono — todas "o app está certo" — e viram linhas na ADR-0013; os defeitos de copy, o da pílula do logo e a falta dos links de favicon foram corrigidos no próprio bundle do protótipo, e o site ganhou os ícones derivados do logo.

## O que muda

- **Protótipo (1 edição, 2 arquivos):** os dois HTML são bundles self-extracting do Claude Design — o desktop guarda o app num template JSON e o responsivo embute o arquivo desktop inteiro como gzip+base64. A edição do template é regravada nos dois com a mesma codificação. Muda copy ("membros" → "clientes" nas 28 ocorrências visíveis, com as 11 ocorrências de rota/id mantidas), a contagem de estado no padrão do app com singular ("1 cliente"), o logo sem os 272px (a coluna é do grid; a pílula e o foco envolvem só a imagem, como o `AppHeader`) e os 3 links de favicon no head. Round-trip provado: decodificados de novo, os dois arquivos dão o template editado byte a byte, e o asset do responsivo descomprime no desktop novo.
- **ADR-0013:** saem as 3 linhas dos defeitos corrigidos no bundle (a dos textos, que a ADR-0020 já registra, a da pílula do logo e a da contagem "membro(s)"); quatro linhas que citavam copy antiga do protótipo passam a citar a atual ("Ver N membros", "membro não encontrado", "página do membro" e "nav do membro"); entram 5 linhas novas com as decisões de hoje (Enter na busca, limite de 100 caracteres, os 27 estados fixos, fonte vazia como erro e o detalhe que suspende em vez de esqueleto).
- **Favicon:** `favicon.ico` (16/32/48 embutidos como PNG), `apple-touch-icon.png` (180×180, logo centrado sobre o `--header-bg` claro opaco, porque o iOS achata transparência em preto) e `favicon.svg` (o PNG como data URI num `<svg viewBox>`), todos gerados do `public/logo.png` por script Node descartável, sem dependência nova. `nuxt.config.ts` ganha os 3 links, na ordem SVG → ICO → apple-touch.
- **E2E:** `tests/e2e/favicon.spec.ts` — o HTML do SSR de `/customers` carrega os 3 links, e os 3 arquivos respondem com os bytes do repositório e o content-type certo. O Nitro responde `/favicon.ico` com um GIF embutido (200) quando o app não manda o arquivo, por isso a prova é pelos bytes.
- **`ai-journey/registro.md`:** entrada da #43, com o resultado pendente de review.

## Como verificar

**Preview:** https://customer-directory-git-chore-43-pro-474c90-adams-alves-projects.vercel.app (deploy da branch; o link atual também está no check do PR).

- [x] Nos dois HTML: abrir e conferir que a interface diz "clientes" em vez de "membros", o logo em pílula curta a partir de 960px e o tab da moldura navega como antes (as rotas `#/membros` ficaram, por serem internas do protótipo). — **fechado 2026-11-11:** desktop aberto nos dois temas e em 375/768/1280 (prints no comentário de evidência), zero "membro" visível (a11y); pílula do logo só na imagem ≥960; moldura com as 6 frames rodando o app novo e navegação íntegra.
- [x] `node -e` com o decode do plano (ou o do corpo do commit `6488581`): decodificar os dois bundles e conferir o template editado; o asset do responsivo descomprime no desktop novo, byte a byte. — **fechado 2026-11-11:** template novo com 15 "clientes" e 9 "membros" (rotas/ids internos), título "Lista de clientes"; `gunzipSync` do asset `38f1883d` == desktop novo (`cmp` byte-exato).
- [x] No preview: `curl -I https://<preview>/favicon.svg`, `/favicon.ico` e `/apple-touch-icon.png` — 200 com `image/svg+xml`, `image/vnd.microsoft.icon` e `image/png`; e o HTML de `/customers` traz os 3 `<link>`. — **fechado 2026-11-11:** 200 × 3 com os content-types exatos (bypass de SSO) e os 3 `<link>` presentes no HTML do SSR.
- [x] ADR-0013: as 3 linhas tiradas, as 5 novas e o status com a re-sincronização de 2026-11-11. — **fechado 2026-11-11:** diff −8/+10 — 3 defeitos tirados, 4 linhas reescritas para a copy nova, 5 decisões do dono acrescentadas e status atualizado.

## Decisões e desvios

- Sem ADR nova: a ADR-0013 registra as 5 decisões e a ADR-0020 já cobre o termo "clientes".
- Favicon sem dependência nova (não há ImageMagick nem vetor do logo para rastrear): o SVG embute o PNG como data URI, e o redimensionamento é reamostragem por média de área num script descartável fora da árvore.
- As rotas hash `#/membros` do protótipo ficam, porque são identificadores internos do bundle.
- O h1 da moldura do responsivo continua "Diretório de membros — responsivo": é a identidade do artefato, como o nome do arquivo (ADR-0020).
- A conferência lado a lado (375/768/1280, dois temas) foi feita e está documentada com prints no comentário de evidência deste PR (sem divergências novas).

## Checklist

- [x] Título em Conventional Commits, ~400 linhas no máximo (sem lockfile, fixture, snapshot e SVG) — +75 −11 pela conta do GitHub (os dois HTML do protótipo contam 1/1 cada pela marca de gerado, e o numstat local os lê como binários)
- [x] Labels da issue aplicados ao PR (o `release.yml` agrupa as notas por eles) — `fix` e `ui`
- [x] Dependência nova tem ADR — nenhuma dependência nova
- [x] Testes do que foi adicionado (se for bug: teste de regressão) — E2E do favicon com mutation testing: cada link tirado do `nuxt.config` e o `favicon.ico` ausente derrubam um teste
- [x] CI verde (lint, typecheck, test, e2e) — portão local verde em todos os checkpoints (lint e typecheck 0, `npm test` 990/990 duas vezes na árvore final, E2E completo 399 passam e 85 pulam); no GitHub Actions, os 4 passos até o `npm test` passam (lint, typecheck, 990/990), e o job falha só no `playwright install --with-deps` — DNS do runner (`Temporary failure resolving 'azure.archive.ubuntu.com'`) em 3 tentativas seguidas, passo que o workflow roda em todo PR e que a `main` passou 1h antes; nada do diff toca o workflow ou os browsers
- [x] a11y: teclado, nomes acessíveis, contraste — nada de markup do app mudou; os `aria-label` do protótipo seguem os textos do app
- [x] Conferido no preview contra `docs/design/`, nos dois temas — conferência lado a lado do agente principal documentada no comentário de evidência (375/768/1280 × dois temas × lista/sheet/detalhe/vazio/erro/404), sem divergências novas
- [x] Entrada da issue em `ai-journey/registro.md`, com o resultado depois do review — entrada feita, resultado pendente de review
- [ ] `ai-journey/` atualizado (se o PR fecha o milestone) — a #43 não fecha milestone

author: jkdesignpro
body:
Stage 1 of the spec (version 0.3.0), complete. It is stacked on #2 (0.2.0): merge #2 first, then point this one at `main`.

## What is in it

**Speeds and feeds advisors**

- **Milling advisor**: material, end mill and kind of cut give a starting speed and chip load from published tables, a suggested width and depth, chip thinning, then checks against the machine (top speed, top feed, power and torque at that speed) and tool deflection. Three plain-word sliders, plus a stick-out slider linked to the stick-out box. A ball nose runs at the speed of the largest diameter in the cut. Shows the theoretical finish the feed leaves on the wall.
- **Locks**: an empty width, depth or feed box shows the suggestion; a typed value is locked and is never changed. Limits are met by reducing the depth, then the width, then the feed.
- **"What is limiting this cut" card** with one fix, and status tiles (amber at 80 % of a limit, red above it). It names deflection, power, torque, top speed, top feed, and chatter when everything else fits but the cut is above the stability line.
- **Stability chart** in the milling advisor: where chatter starts against spindle speed, a speed marker to drag (or a slider), the nearest best speeds, and a button to run the advisor at the marked speed. A simple model that says so: the tool alone as a round bar, one vibration mode. In Expert you can enter a tap test instead.
- **Turning advisor**: speed for HSS or carbide, feed from the nose radius, depth, force, power and torque against the lathe, finish left by the feed. Optional **chip breaker range** of the insert: the feed and depth are held inside it and a small chart shows where the cut sits.
- **Drilling advisor** with point length, time to depth, removal rate, torque, thrust and power, and a button that fills the drilling cycle.
- **Reaming advisor**: speed and feed from four publishers side by side, stock to leave and the hole to drill first.
- **Tapping advisor**: speed from a published table, feed held at one pitch per revolution, whole RPM so S x pitch = F exactly. Fills the G84 cycle and the tap torque page.
- **Plunge roughing**: speed and feed straight down, cusp between plunges, removal rate, time and a power estimate, with three publishers' rules side by side.
- **Boring bar: overhang and deflection**: bar material, overhang slider, a drawing that bends as you drag, damped bar option, limit card.
- **Slitting saw** starts from a saw maker's sheet by work material and saw material.
- Every advisor ends with a table of what each publisher prints for the material and which one was used. Nothing is averaged.

**Cutting forces**

- **Specific cutting force (kc)**, Kienzle, for 39 material groups (Iscar's table; Sandvik Coromant and Mitsubishi Materials shown beside it, never mixed in).
- **Drill thrust, torque and power**, **tap torque and power**, **chip thinning for entering angle and round inserts**, **slender part deflection** in the lathe.
- **Holder and spindle stiffness** in the deflection checks, typed or worked out from a push test.
- **Material removal rate and power** now checks the active machine at the speed of the cut.

**Machine profiles**: spindle taper or holder, rigidity class (sets where the "How hard is this cut" slider starts), holder stiffness.

**Tool life**: the milling and turning advisors open Tool life and cost per part with their speed filled in, and in Expert show the life from your own Taylor n and C.

Each tool has a drawing, core tests with hand-worked values, a smoke check, formula library entries and its sources in `docs/sources.md` ("Cutting forces", "Advisor", "Stability chart").

168 tools on 135 pages; 324 core tests.

## Acceptance list of the spec

| Check | State |
|---|---|
| At least 10 published worked examples within stated tolerances | 10 as core tests: five from the University of Florida, Mitsubishi Materials face milling power, turning power and drilling, the Open Oregon end mill example, and the Tyler and Schmitz stability limit |
| Every table value cited | `docs/sources.md`, and each page names its publisher |
| Locked values never change | Core tests and smoke checks for milling, turning, drilling, tapping and plunging |
| Limit card names the right limit in test cases | Core tests per limit; smoke checks for deflection, power, top speed, top feed and chatter |
| Standing checks | Rust tests, smoke test of every tool in three modes in inch and mm, `check-versions.py`, CHANGELOG and README |

## Things to know

- **BenchMate's own starting figures, which no publisher prints** (all said on the page and listed in `docs/sources.md`): 1 D depth for shoulder roughing and 1.5 D for finishing; allowed tip deflection 0.05 mm roughing and 0.01 mm finishing; bending force equal to the tangential force unless a ratio is typed; chip load read along a straight line between two printed cutter sizes; which publisher row matches which material class; in the stability chart a damping ratio of 0.03 and a force angle of 62 degrees unless you enter your own (both from one paper's worked example and marked "assumed"); tapping speed rounded down to a whole RPM; the chip thickness used for the plunge roughing power estimate; where the rigidity class puts the slider; when the limit card names chatter.
- **Single publisher**: turning speeds (LittleMachineShop), feed from nose radius (Mitsubishi Materials), the carbide factor of 2.5 and the oil-by-hand factor of 0.6 (University of Florida), drilling formulas (Sandvik Coromant), cutting tap torque (Lubero), forming tap torque (Yamawa), saw speeds and feeds (Gaylee; Kyocera reprints the carbide column), tapping speeds (RedLine Tools), the wording on chip breaker ranges (Seco Tools). Each page says so.
- **Disagreements shown, not resolved**: two editions of the University of Florida table print different drill feeds from 1/2 in up (the lower one is used and both are printed); reaming speed rules differ between publishers; plunging rules differ (University of Florida 25 % of the feed and 75 % of the speed, CGS Tool 35 to 50 % of the feed, MIT under 50 %).
- **Left out because no open source was found**: a factor for dry or mist cutting, a hardness correction, Taylor exponents for tool life (you enter your own), typical holder and spindle stiffness (you enter or measure your own), tapping speeds for forming taps or by coating.
- **The stability chart leaves out the holder, the spindle and process damping**, so at low speeds real cuts are steadier than it shows. The chart and the card word this plainly and do not blame chatter where the model cannot judge.
- Several Sandvik Coromant and Kennametal pages could not be read (they load by script only), so they are named in the sources but not counted as read.
- Fixed along the way: a lock button that swallowed its click when the box had just been typed in.

## Checks
`bash scripts/build-web.sh`, `cargo test --workspace -q`, `node tests/smoke/smoke.mjs`, `python3 scripts/check-versions.py v0.3.0`: all pass locally.

author: michalgrabarczyk
body:
## Bug

With an `exitTransition` set, `clearData()` on a `PointCloud` or `ErrorBarSeries` made the series vanish at once. `animating` still stayed `true` for the transition's duration.

## Cause

`clearData()` stores the empty target data before the transition starts. `count()` is 0 while the transition frame (`dataPoints().setDrawn(...)`) still holds the leaving items. Both `updatePaintNode` implementations returned no node when `count() <= 0`, so they never drew that frame.

## Fix

- Gate `PointCloud::updatePaintNode` and `ErrorBarSeries::updatePaintNode` on the drawn count (`dataPoints().renderCount()`, capped by the render capacity) instead of `count()`, matching `BarSeries::updatePaintNode`.
- Hover stays gated on `count()`, as in `BarSeries::barIndexAt`. Exiting items are no longer data, so hover must not return their indices.
- Add `clearDataRunsTheExitTransition` to `tst_point_cloud_transitions` and `tst_error_bar_series_transitions`, modeled on the `BarSeries` test.

No CHANGELOG entry: enter/update/exit transitions are unreleased.

body:
A Space with spec.archived: true keeps its place but stops costing
processes. An in-process controller watches Spaces and Surfaces and, for
each archived Space:

- deletes its Surfaces and the Dens they point at (the Den finalizer
  stops the dens); a Surface stays until its Den's delete is accepted;
- sets spec.archived on the Spaces under it, which can each be reopened
  on their own;
- sets status.archivedAt once no Surface is left.

Space gets a status, written only on the new spaces/status subresource.
Setting spec.archived back to false clears status.archivedAt.

Implements t8y:/controllers/archive.

body:
## Summary

Keep generated local tooling output out of version control, and run the dependency audit as its own CI job. The repository copies untracked, non-ignored files in `tests/test_init_project.py` and `make smoke-template`, so a stray generated folder can fail them. A new advisory used to fail the `check` job and hide the code checks; now both results show.

## Changes

- Ignore `graphify-out/`, the folder the graphify knowledge-graph tool writes to.
- Ignore `.import_linter_cache`, the cache the import contracts check creates.
- Move `make audit` from the `check` job into a new `audit` job (`Audit 🔒`) in `ci.yml`. `check` keeps its name and its other steps; `audit` also runs in the weekly schedule.
- Describe both jobs in the CI section of the README.

author: odaryo
body:
## 概要
#866: HTML の `<script>` の中に深い入れ子があると、script の中だけ色が付かないまま、案内が出なかった。これを「syntax highlight を適用できませんでした。」の案内に倒す。

## 機序
highlight.js 11.11.1 は safe mode (既定) で、配列の subLanguage の内側の `RangeError` を内部で捕まえる。xml の `<script>` の `["javascript","handlebars","xml"]` がこの配列に当たる。失敗した候補は relevance 0 になり、素のテキストの候補に負ける。トップレベルの `errorRaised` は立たない。#771 の判定はトップレベルの `errorRaised` だけを見ていたので、この部分的な成功を拾えなかった。

## 変更
- `SyntaxHighlightingService` は、`highlight.min.js` を読み込んだ直後に `hljs.debugMode()` を呼ぶ。debugMode では `_highlight` の catch が例外を投げ直す。内側の失敗はトップレベルの JS 例外として抜け、既存の `context.exception` の guard で `nil` になり、既存の `.unavailable` の案内が出る。
- **幅 0 の一致だけは safe mode でやり直す。** debugMode では、文法の幅 0 の一致も例外 (`0 width match regex (<言語>)`) になる。safe mode ならここで1文字送って続ける。例外の `message` がこの接頭辞で始まるときだけ、次の順に呼ぶ。
  1. `safeMode()`
  2. 同じ入力で再実行
  3. `debugMode()`
  
  debug への復帰は、結果の判定より前に必ず行う。復帰で例外が出たら、その context を捨てる (fail-closed)。safe mode のまま使い続けると、#866 の部分的な成功が黙って戻るためである。やり直しの結果は既存の guard (`errorRaised` を含む) で判定する。
- `debugMode()` の呼び出しが例外になったら、context を使わない (fail-closed)。
- 同梱の `highlight.min.js` は書き換えていない。plugin の `after:highlight` はトップレベルの呼び出しでしか発火しない。内側の `_highlight` / `highlightAuto` は closure の参照で呼ばれる。そのため、公開 API を包んでも内側の失敗は観測できない。

### トレードオフ
- これまで色が付いていた HTML の部分も捨て、全文を素のテキストと案内にする。#771 と同じ all-or-nothing で、案内の文言「適用できませんでした」とも合う。部分的に色が無いのに成功と見せるより、案内を出すほうを選んだ。
- 配列 subLanguage の兄弟の候補の1つが幅 0 の一致以外の例外を出すと、main ならほかの候補が勝って色が付いたはずの入力でも `nil` になる経路が、理論上残る。reviewer の 4434 本と fuzz 6 万回では再現しなかった。
- 幅 0 の一致と内側の `RangeError` が同じ入力で両方起き、幅 0 の一致が先なら、safe でのやり直しで main と同じ部分的な成功に戻る。幅 0 の一致は Markdown でしか見つかっておらず、Markdown は inline HTML のタグしか xml に渡さないので、この形は作れなかった (reviewer の計測)。
- やり直しが起きる入力では、時間が約 2〜3 倍になる。reviewer の計測では、約 256 KiB の Markdown でやり直しなしが 0.063 秒、やり直しありが 0.125〜0.183 秒だった。`maximumByteCount` の根拠にした 1 秒の目安には収まる。レビューの Minor で、起票はしない。

## 計測 (生出力は Issue のコメントにある)
同梱の 11.11.1 を、スタック 512 KiB のスレッド上の `JSContext` で計測した。
- **再現**: 深さ 4000 の html-script は、safe では `errorRaised=undefined spans=14`、debug では `exc=RangeError` になった。深さ 600 は両モードで成功した (spans=1217)。
- **新旧の判定の比較**: 7792 本を比べた。main 相当は safe の context で、例外か `errorRaised` なら nil とする。新しい判定は 1 つの debug の context に通し続け、幅 0 の一致のときだけやり直す。
  ```
  files=7792 same=7792 bothNil=0 newOnlyNil=0 mainOnlyNil=0 diff=0 retries=16 retryChecked=16 retryMismatch=0
  final deep html-script nil=true
  ```
  - 対象は、手元のコーパス、upstream 11.11.1 の `test/markup` / `test/detect` の 291 本、`~/workspace` の `*.md` 3000 本、レビューで見つかった退行の 9 本、合成 2 件である。
  - やり直しのたびに、出力を新しい safe の context と比べ、直後に深い html-script が nil になる (= debug に戻っている) ことを確かめた。
  - reviewer も、独立に書いたハーネスで Markdown 2995 本を通した。結果は `same=2995 retries=9 newNil=0 otherExc=0 restoreFail=0` だった。
  - 計測した入力の外で出力が変わらないことまでは保証しない。
- **例外の後の context の再利用**: 例外が抜けた直後の同じ context でも、出力は新しい context とバイト一致した。Director は 4 本、reviewer は 1320 本で確かめた。
- **upstream のテストは debugMode で回っている** (`test/markup/index.js:9` ほか)。
- **文字列 subLanguage の経路**: 対応表の言語からは、内側で `RangeError` に届く形を作れなかった。`cos` で直接測ると、safe でもトップレベルの `errorRaised` が立った。この形は #771 の判定で既に拾える。

## テスト
- 深さ 4000 の入れ子を script に持つ HTML が `nil` になり、直後の Swift は色付けに成功する。
- 陽性対照: 小さな script を含む HTML で、script の中の `let` に xcode テーマのキーワードの色が付く。debugMode で配列 subLanguage の経路ごと `nil` に倒れる退行を止める。
- 幅 0 の一致が起きる Markdown (front matter・setext 見出し) が `nil` にならず、入力を保持し、`hljs-section` の色が付く。
- 同じ service で、Markdown (やり直し) → 深い html-script → Swift の順に呼び、non-nil / nil / non-nil になる。debug への戻し忘れを止める。
- RED: 05cedd5 の前では、深い html-script のテストだけが `failed == nil` で落ちた。05cedd5 の上では、Markdown の3件が最初の `nil` で落ちた。どちらの段でも、ほかのテストは通った。
- **CI (macOS 15 の JavaScriptCore) で `RangeError` に届く深さが違えば、深い html-script のテストは `HighlightJSMarkup` の深さの上限 32 の経路で通る。** CI の緑はこの経路の証拠にならない (#867 と同じ構造)。経路の証拠はローカルの RED → GREEN である。

## GREEN (ローカル、gate-runner、9b6488b)
- `App`: `swift build --build-tests` / `swift test` (226 tests passed)
- `swift format lint --strict` / `swiftlint --strict`: 0 件
- 407390e はコメントだけの変更で、format と lint を通した。
- `AgentWorkflowTerminal/` は変更していない。

## GREEN (この PR の CI)
- `Build & Test (SwiftPM, unit + integration)` / `Build (macOS App)` / `Static checks & iOS build` の3ジョブが、407390e で pass した (run 43038728328)。
- `Build (macOS App)` の `swift test` では 238 tests が通り、追加した4件も走った。
- ただし、CI で深い html-script のテストが `RangeError` の経路を通ったかは未確認である (#867)。上の「テスト」の但し書きのとおり、CI の緑はこの経路の証拠ではない。

## UI の確認
回していない。表示の配線は変えていない。`nil` から `.unavailable` (「syntax highlight を適用できませんでした。」) に至る既存の表示経路に乗るだけである。

## レビュー
敵対的レビュー (reviewer、計測付き) を2ラウンド行った。

- **1ラウンド目、Critical 1 件 (spec の欠陥)**: debugMode にしただけでは、幅 0 の一致で front matter 付きの Markdown が `nil` に退行した。
  - 実ファイルでは、`~/workspace` の `*.md` 2995 本のうち 9 本だった。
  - Director の最初の計測 (Markdown 240 本で 0 件) は、たまたま当たらなかった。
  - Issue の計測コメントは訂正済みである。
  - 9b6488b の、幅 0 の一致のときだけ safe でやり直す変更で直した。
- **1ラウンド目の Minor**: どちらも 9b6488b で直した。
  - `errorRaised` の guard に到達できず、コメントが不正確だった。safe でのやり直しで、再び到達できるようになった。
  - テストのコメント「600 段以下では」が計測の範囲を超えていた。
- **2ラウンド目、Critical なし。**
  - Minor 1 件 (やり直しのコメントが条件より狭い) は 407390e で直した。
  - Minor 1 件 (やり直しで時間が 2〜3 倍) は、上のトレードオフに記録し、起票しない。

body:
Yukon submission `57a8e18f-0321-4717-8fc8-0b06bac3437f` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/dcp at `cdb1ebff130d861e2c61e9cf517ab66c0a56ca7a`.

Current best score: 1. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
Improving submissions stay open until Yukon promotes them, after owner review when enabled. Other results are closed.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: Claude Opus 5.5
Harness: Claude Code

# IFC-BANK-D: fibered seven-input dissection merges in the banked IFC sieve, S_Q = O(2^((149/400) sqrt n)), S_C = O(n), T = O(n^127 2^((1741/1000) sqrt n))

Effort: Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Code, default effort. Main-thread work: a continuous capacity model, a new merge
primitive with its proof, schedule edits and exact-arithmetic checks.

## Result

| resource | declared envelope | index |
|---|---|---|
| T | O(n^127 2^((1741/1000) sqrt n)) | 1/2 |
| S_C | O(n) | 0 |
| S_Q | O(2^((149/400) sqrt n)), no polynomial factor | 1/2 |
| Q | O(n^(7/2) 2^((1741/1000) sqrt n)) | 1/2 |
| tolerance | 0, canonical clean model | - |

The success probability is at least 1 - 2^-8, and all four bounds hold jointly on every branch.

This row has S_Q = O(2^((149/400) sqrt n)), S_C = O(n), tolerance 0 and T coefficient 1741/1000. My local comparator, run over all 1011 accepted rows, finds that no accepted row dominates it and that it dominates 10 of them. It is a new trade-off point in this resource class: the nearest accepted row with a smaller S_Q coefficient at S_C = O(n) is `fc374c6a` (e-man07, S_Q coefficient 7/20, T coefficient 897/500), which has the larger T; the nearest with a larger S_Q coefficient is `7f3d92a7` (e-man07, S_Q coefficient 3/8, T coefficient 1737/1000).

## What is new: fibered MERGE7 (virtual3.md)

IFC-BANK-S (my `3b49ab04` and its siblings) runs the banked IFC sieve below cap ratio 2/3 with saturated four-input
merges. Its T coefficient is 2/(3 sig) + sig/2, which is 1.9760 here. My first IFC-BANK-D rows (`756cdd0e`,
`4541cc56`, `7b5b33ee`, all judged valid) added unfibered seven-input merges at the top of the tree; at this cap ratio that schedule gives 1.8311. This row adds a fiber to MERGE7 so that seven-input levels can start much lower in
the tree.

MERGE7(X1..X7; p, w, b, lam') has the structure of MERGE4I, with triples (x1, x2, x3) in place of one pair and
four-tuples (x4..x7) in place of the other.
1. It measures a w-bit window W0 of the triple sum (fiber X_v) and of the four-tuple sum (fiber Y_v2).
2. It measures the next b - w bits of the seven-label sum. The output is collimated on b = 7 Lam - lam' - kappa - w
   bits and has about 2^(lam' + kappa) tuples.
3. It lists that class by a seven-list dissection (Dinur, Dunkelman, Keller and Shamir, CRYPTO 2012). For each of the
   2^(2 Lam - w) guesses g of the triple residue on 2 Lam bits that agree with v, it builds the class T3(g), cut at
   2L + 1 rows. It streams the matching four-tuples as a Schroeppel-Shamir join of pair classes modulo 2^Lam, each
   cut at 2L + 1 rows, and looks each one up in T3(g) on b bits. A read counter caps the four-tuples read at
   2 L^4/2^w, so the work is O(2^(4 Lam - w)) searches whatever the labels.
4. It re-indexes the listed tuples as MERGE4I does.
With w = 0 this is the MERGE7 of my earlier rows.

The failure bound is Lemma D.1: 9 * 2^-Lam + 2^(-kappa - lam') + 2^-kappa < 2^(2 - kappa). It is proved like
MERGE4I's Lemma B.1:
- BAD fibers (more than twice their mean), by Chebyshev under Hp;
- tuples lost to the class cuts, counted over all outcomes at once;
- overflow of the listing cap Cp = 8 * 2^(lam' + kappa) + 1, under Hp' (Hp plus the W0 digits);
- the block remainder.
On good fibers the read counter never fires (Claim C.1).

## Schedule (virtual2.md Section 8)

- Pool and Phase A are as in IFC-BANK-S.
- Phase I: JI = ceil((57/100) Lam) four-input levels, saturated from ceil((Lam - 1)/2) on.
- Phase M: J7 = ceil(671 r/2000) seven-input levels, level k with fiber
  w_k = max(0, 3 Lam - 2 JI - floor(14 (k+1)/5)).

The fiber is fixed by the time accounting. An attempt at level k costs O(n 2^(4 Lam - w_k)) and consumes
2^(a + 2 JI) 7^(k+1) dl pool qubits. 4 Lam - w_k <= Lam + 2 JI + floor(14 (k+1)/5) and 14/5 < log2 7 (7^5 > 2^14) make
that O(n 2^dl) per dl qubits, as at every other level, so the tree term stays O(n^3 2^(H + dl)).

Level k collimates 6 Lam - kappa - w_k bits, or one Lam - 1 more at the root. Lemma 8.1 bounds the total fiber loss by sum_k w_k <= 5 Y1^2/28, with Y1 = 3 Lam - 2 JI + 1, and gets CP + CA + SM(J7) >= f(Lam) - kappa r with f(x) = (25791/14000) x^2 + (6 (671/2000) r - 24) x. With Lam >= (149/400) r - 81 log2 r - 51 the capacity is at least

    r^2 + r [ (12233191/2240000000) r - (770619979/2800000) log2 r - 522474209/2800000 ].

The bracket is about 36 at r = 2^20 and is increasing from there. Exponents:
- H <= (218919/160000) r + 6, using log2 7 < 45/16 (7^16 < 2^45);
- (8.5): HI (149/400) + 2 (57/100)(149/400) + (45/16)(671/2000) < 1741/1000, exactly, with at least 6/r to spare;
- (F6) still gives Y <= 2r, because e < 2.

## Model

In units of r = sqrt n, per count level s, the gains are:
- pool: min(sig, e - s);
- four-input with fiber l <= min(2 sig, s): (sig + l)/2;
- fibered seven-input with node time t = 4 sig - w <= min(4 sig, s): (2 sig + t)/log2 7.
The seven-input gain passes the saturated four-input gain at about s = 2.21 sig. The continuous optimum is
1.7320 at sig = 149/400; the proved integer schedule declares 1741/1000.

## Checks

- `python dcp_admission.py preflight --root . ...` returns outcome `review` (format admission only).
- Exact-rational checks of (8.5) and of the Lemma 8.1 bracket and its derivative at r = 2^20.
- An exact integer evaluation of the schedule (closed-form sums) at n = 2^40, 2^41, 2^42, 2^44, 2^48, 2^56, 2^64,
  2^80 and 2^120, with r0 = r - 1 boundary cases. It checks capacity >= r^2, a + JI + J7 + 1 <= r, 2 JI + 2 >= 3 Lam,
  CP >= 7 Lam, H >= cb + 1 and the two exponent margins. Capacity/r^2 at this row's parameters: 1.00019 at n = 2^40, 1.00401 at n = 2^44, 1.00543 at n = 2^56, 1.00546 at n = 2^80.
- A scan of the generated text for leftovers of the IFC-BANK-S parameters (H0 and its coefficient).
- All files are below 64 KiB. To make room, Section 9 (BATCH) moved from virtual.md to virtual2.md unchanged, apart
  from the MERGE7 edits.

## Limitations

- Index 1/2 and clean input only. This is a trade-off point, not progress toward 2^(O(n^(1/3))).
- The bank construction (mpjunior92's), IFC-BANK-F's text (kshitij-hash, as re-tuned by kaankolcu) and all lemmas
  other than those named are inherited. Polynomial degrees (n^127) are inherited and not optimized.
- The listing is classical work counted in T. No quantum speedup of the dissection is used.

## Provenance

- `3b49ab04` (IFC-BANK-S at 1/2) and `b7e55543` (at 2/5) are my rows. This archive starts from the latter's text.
- kshitij-hash IFC-BANK-F `f7b12b14` and kaankolcu's re-tune `04f7e018` provide the algorithm, the construction and
  the text. Every dependency they declare is re-declared, including my MW4 `33a6df9d` and CW1 `cfe82a87`, the
  MERGE4I lineage.
- The dissection technique is from the literature (Dinur, Dunkelman, Keller and Shamir 2012; Schroeppel and Shamir
  1981). MERGE7's quantum steps, its proof (Claim C.1, Lemmas C.2 and D.1) and the Phase M schedule are new here.

author: abrichr
body:
SQL effect readback now checks the MySQL session’s result charset before it reads any record. A session that cannot prove `utf8mb4` returns the same named refusal used for frame and history reads. Supported native drivers are recognized directly; opaque adapters that keep one session per connection can declare their dialect. The existing synthetic MariaDB adapters declare it in their configuration.

A connection whose dialect is neither declared nor recognized is refused before the reader opens a cursor.

Testing: 236 synthetic cases passed on hosted Linux with disposable MySQL 8.4.13 and SQLite. Ruff lint and format, mypy, and the file size check passed. The MariaDB benchmark adapters were not run.

Generality: one charset check covers native and configured effect reads, frames, and history, with no app-specific engine code. The checks use synthetic fixtures. No held-out app was run.

Closes #2208

Refs #1914 and #2206

author: cbuchler
body:
Complex Markdown could exhaust host memory despite parser isolation and deadlines. This change gives sandboxed rendering a 256 MiB OS memory budget and refuses to deliver document input when protection cannot start.

Linux uses a verified systemd user scope with no swap, group OOM termination and a task cap. macOS applies a fatal physical-footprint limit through a native helper, then installs the SRT-generated profile with fork/exec denied before signalling readiness. Standalone macOS binaries embed the helper and guard. The explicit --no-sandbox override disables these controls too.

Closes #24.

Validation: [all four native jobs passed](https://github.com/cbuchler/mdview/actions/runs/43091206247) on Ubuntu 26.04 x64/arm64 and macOS 26 Intel/Apple Silicon at 4d9b0ca. Checks cover real allocation failure, pathological source/compiled renders and recovery, missing-guard input withholding, filesystem/network/process containment, parent-loss cleanup, packaged execution without Node/Bun on PATH, and Linux terminal lifecycle. Final follow-up changes only clarify documentation and build prerequisites.

Trade-offs: Linux now needs a systemd user manager with cgroup v2 controls. macOS uses private/deprecated Apple interfaces and depends on SRT 0.0.82's checked profile format. The two platforms account for memory differently; neither bounds the entire viewer or all kernel resources. Older OS versions and notarized/hardened distribution are not claimed as validated. No host policy is weakened and no automatic unrestricted fallback is added.

author: frozenyty
body:
## What changed

`spawn_member` with `replace` composes the successor's brief, hard-coded since ADR 0009. This adds **one** Lead-scoped tool, `handoff_template`, which reads (no `template`), stores (a validated template) or clears (an empty string) one brief template held on that Lead's roster record. A stored template is rendered with the predecessor's real values; the built-in brief is the default template rendered by the same code, so a profile that stores none produces byte-identical briefs. `list_members` rows are unchanged.

- **Placeholders:** `{successor}`, `{predecessor}`, `{label}`, `{assignment}`, `{task_board}`. `{assignment}` is the one required placeholder; the successor's own task is appended after the rendered template and is never a placeholder, so no template can drop it.
- **Refusals at set time:** an unknown placeholder (or an unmatched brace) is refused naming the token — a typo can never reach a child as literal text — and a template without `{assignment}` is refused with the reason.
- **Bounds:** template ≤ 1000 characters, rendered brief ≤ 2000, both refused rather than truncated; the rendered cap is measured only when a template is stored, and it refuses the replacement before the reservation, so nothing is left half-written.
- **Storage:** `handoffTemplate` on the Lead's roster record. Load validates the type only (the facility validates every record of every Lead when it opens a domain, so a preference must not fail the whole roster); the content rules are reported by the read form (`valid`, `problem`) and the composition falls back to the built-in rather than interpolating a bad token.
- **Name:** noun-only instead of `verb_noun` because the call reads, writes or clears depending on its argument; `set_handoff_template` would promise a write on the read and `get_` would lie about the write. ADR 0015 records the surface, the storage and the load-time exception.

The diff is ~720 lines including the bilingual documents and the ADR; the code change itself is ~250 lines. Splitting it would separate the decision from its delivery in the same PR.

## How it was verified

- `node --check index.js actions.js roster.js trash.js host-hooks.js` → exit 0
- `node --test --test-isolation=none tests/*.test.mjs` → **97 tests, 97 passing** (the 87 that existed plus 10 in `tests/handoff.test.mjs`: byte-identical built-in brief, read-back, interpolation with the real values, both set-time refusals, template cap, rendered cap before any child starts, two Leads not sharing, clearing returning to the built-in, load-time type validation)
- `node scripts/check.mjs` → `check passed`
- **Not installed.** No live tool call has run, so activation of the new tool, the wrapper's argument handling and the rendered brief reaching a real child need the owner's install check.

## Affected modules

plugin, roster, docs

## Effect on a running profile

None outside the plugin's own tools: no shipped row is enabled or disabled, nothing migrates, and a record written by any earlier release loads unchanged. Every Lead's tool list gains `handoff_template`; a profile that never calls it behaves exactly as it did.

## Documents touched

- [x] a tool name, parameter or result field → `docs/architecture-en.md` + `-zh.md` §4.5, README pair
- [x] the durable record shape → `docs/architecture-en.md` + `-zh.md` §4.2 and a new ADR
- [x] a document added, renamed or removed → `docs/INDEX-en.md` and `INDEX-zh.md`
- Also: the state-matrix note for "replace with a template set" (§4.3), the composition rule (§4.4), `PLAN.md` P4-02 ticked, a `PROGRESS.md` entry, `0.11.0`.

## README pair — text for whoever owns it

`README.md` and `README-zh.md` are another lane's files in this change, so they still list seven tools. The row for the table (English, then Chinese):

| `handoff_template` | Read, store or clear this Lead's handoff-brief template. Omit `template` to read it; pass one to store it; pass an empty string to clear it. A replacement renders `{successor}`, `{predecessor}`, `{label}`, `{assignment}` and `{task_board}`; `{assignment}` is required. |

| `handoff_template` | 读取、保存或清除本 Lead 的交接书模板。省略 `template` 读取，给一个模板则保存，给空字符串则清除。替换时插值 `{successor}`、`{predecessor}`、`{label}`、`{assignment}` 与 `{task_board}`；`{assignment}` 必须有。 |

And a short note, e.g. after "Replacing a member":

> **Fixing the brief's shape.** If you replace members repeatedly and want a different shape, store a template once: `handoff_template({ template: "Take over from {predecessor} as {successor}. Its role was {label}. Inherited work: {assignment}\n{task_board}" })`. `{assignment}` is required — without it a successor does not learn what it inherited. An unknown placeholder is refused when you store the template, as is a template past 1000 characters; a brief that renders past 2000 characters refuses the replacement instead of truncating it. Call it with no argument to read the stored template, or with `""` to clear it and return to the built-in brief.

## Checklist

- [x] `node --check index.js` passes
- [x] `node scripts/check.mjs` passes
- [x] Bilingual pairs updated in this same PR
- [x] `PLAN.md` task box ticked only for work actually delivered
- [x] A `PROGRESS.md` entry added (append-only, no older entry rewritten)
- [x] No machine-specific path in any shared document
- [ ] If installed for testing: not installed

author: crisprintsstuff
body:
A tester's Finder shows `.oxb` projects with the generic "?" document icon, labelled OXB.

## Cause
The bundle declares the `.oxb` type correctly. The release builds' icon check on macOS 26 shows the OxyBrush icon for `.oxb` once the app is registered with Launch Services. On the tester's Mac the app isn't registered for it, which happens when it was first opened from the disk image or translocated on its first launch.

## Fix
- **At start:** OxyBrush runs the system `lsregister -f` on its own `.app`, in a background thread. It's skipped in `--screenshot` runs.
- **Translocated copies:** when macOS runs it from a translocated copy, it skips registering, because that path disappears, and logs a hint to move the app to Applications.
- **Constraints:** no unsafe code and no network.
- **Test:** `app_bundle` and `is_translocated` are plain path checks with a unit test.

## Docs
CHANGELOG (Unreleased, Fixed) and ROADMAP (known limitations, last updated).

## Not verified
- I haven't run it on a real Mac. The macOS CI job compiles and tests it, but only a tester can confirm the icons change.
- Finder may need a moment, or a Finder restart, to redraw icons it has already shown.
- This only fixes the icon. A **preview** of the sculpt (a Quick Look thumbnail) would need a separate Quick Look extension in Swift or Objective-C, which is a bigger change.

author: charlie-niekirk
body:
Roadmap: 3.6 Layout

## Summary
- Wires the panes together (`panes.rs`): selecting a mailbox in the sidebar shows its threads in the list and closes the open thread; selecting a thread opens it in the reading pane. Removes 3.5's stopgap that opened the newest Inbox thread on its own, so clicking a thread now changes the conversation pane.
- Resizable layout: dividers after the sidebar and the thread list (gpui-component's standalone `resize_handle`). `PaneSizes` keeps each pane within its range (sidebar 160–400 px, list 280–640 px) and leaves the reading pane at least 300 px. If the window gets too narrow it shrinks the panes for layout without changing the saved preference. Sizes are saved to `layout.json` in the data directory (not the mail DB) 300 ms after a drag ends, and read before the first frame.
- Pane states, driven by view-models:
  - Thread list (`ThreadList::content`/`banner`): loading spinner; first-page failure with retry; "No conversations in <label>", with "you're offline" or "still syncing" when that applies; a strip when offline or when loading more fails (with retry).
  - Reading pane: its state moves into the view-model as `ReadingPane`. A failed thread has a retry. Bodies that fail to fetch while offline say so and load again on reconnect.

author: koic
body:
When every cop on a redundant `rubocop:enable` directive was removed, or for a `rubocop:pop` without a matching `rubocop:push`, the cop removed the directive including its `#`. Any text after it other than a `--` reason stayed behind and turned into code:

```ruby
# before
foo
# rubocop:enable Layout/LineLength some text

# after
foo
some text
```

Such text is an ordinary comment, so the directive is now replaced with `#` instead of being removed when text follows it. Text that already starts with `#` keeps the plain removal, so no second `#` is added. A `--` reason after an orphan `rubocop:pop` is removed together with the directive, as it already is for `rubocop:enable`.

-----------------

author: callmefair
body:
## 변경 목적·내용
지금까지는 LLM이 고른 장소 단어 하나로만 곡을 찾아서, 같은 단어가 나온 장소는 늘 같은 5곡을 받았습니다(예: 번화가 12곳이 같은 5곡). 장소 정보를 더 쓰고 칸마다 뽑기를 넣어 같은 종류 장소끼리도 곡이 갈리도록 했습니다.

- **보조 장소 단어 섞기**: LLM이 고른 장소 단어(주 단어) 외에, 근처 지형(300m 안, 산은 거리 무관)과 장소 특징(place_traits)을 같은 보기 단어로 바꿔 최대 2개를 함께 씁니다. 장소 점수 = 주 단어 0.6 + 보조 단어가 나머지 0.4를 똑같이 나눔(1개면 0.4, 2개면 0.2씩).
  - 예: 남한산성 = 숲 산책로 0.6 + 산 0.2 + 돌담길 0.2, 광안리 = 해수욕장 0.6 + 카페거리 0.4
  - 섞은 벡터로 새로 검색하지 않고, 단어마다 찾은 상위 30곡을 합친 후보 안에서만 순서를 정합니다. 섞은 벡터로 바로 검색하면 어느 단어 후보에도 없던 곡이 끌려왔습니다(광안리에서 두 단어 모두 30위 밖인 곡이 2위로 올라옴).
- **칸마다 상위 3곡 중 뽑기**: 사다리 칸·특별 칸 모두 1등 대신 점수 상위 3곡 중 하나를 고르게 뽑습니다. 칸 순서(장소 → 날씨 → 특별 칸)는 그대로라 첫 곡은 여전히 가장 장소다운 곡입니다.
- **도심 한복판 분리**: 상권 규모 very_busy는 번화가 대신 새 보기 단어 "도심 한복판"을 고릅니다(busy는 번화가 유지). 홍대·동성로 같은 곳과 역 앞 작은 상권이 같은 곡을 받던 문제가 갈립니다.
- **기차역 오판 수정**: 이름에 "역"이 들어간 지하철역(개롱역·잠실새내역 등)을 LLM이 기차역으로 고르던 문제를 프롬프트 규칙으로 막았습니다. landmark·region은 이름일 뿐 장소 종류를 고르는 근거가 아니라고 명시했습니다.

주요 파일: `backend/location/query.py`(`support_words`, 보기 단어 연결 표, "도심 한복판", 프롬프트 규칙), `backend/location/blend.py`(`place_vector`, `_pick`, `MAIN_PLACE_WEIGHT`·`PICK_TOP_N`과 근거), `backend/location/service.py`(`_blend_search` 단어별 후보 합치기)

## 검증 결과
- `pytest tests` → **553 passed, 1 skipped**
  - 추가: 보조 단어 순서·거리·강/한강/호수 이름 규칙, 장소 벡터 비중(gemini·v4), 뽑기가 상위 3곡 안에서만 나오는지
  - 기존 사다리 테스트 2개는 `top_n=1`로 고정해 원래 검증 내용을 유지했습니다.
- 35곳 다양성 측정 (모두 맑은 오후 15℃로 고정, 실제보다 불리한 조건)

  | 지표 | 변경 전 | 변경 후 |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | 같은 단어 장소끼리 곡 겹침 (5곡 중) | 5.0 | 1.65 |
  | 서로 다른 곡 (전체 175곡 중) | 61 | 94 |
  | 가장 많이 반복된 곡 | 14곳 | 8곳 |

- 허브 곡 확인: 장소 단어 26개 × 상위 30곡 = 750자리 중 서로 다른 곡 600곡, 한 곡이 걸친 단어는 최대 5개입니다. 기존 v4 허브 보정(β=0.5)으로 충분해서 위치 전용 허브 보정은 넣지 않았습니다.
- LLM 확인: very_busy 번화가 6곳 중 5곳이 "도심 한복판" 선택(나머지 1곳은 0m에 먹자골목이 있어 먹자골목). busy 번화가는 그대로 번화가. 지하철역 4곳은 더 이상 기차역이 아니고, 대전역(기차역)·인천국제공항(공항)·잠실종합운동장(야구장)은 그대로입니다.
- 실제 DB로 같은 장소·같은 조건을 두 번 호출하면 5곡 중 2~3곡이 바뀌고, 장소다운 흐름은 유지됩니다.

## 연동·배포 영향
- **동작 변화: 같은 위치·같은 시각으로 다시 요청해도 곡이 일부 달라집니다(의도된 동작).** 같은 요청 = 같은 결과를 가정한 곳이 있다면 알려 주세요.
- API 요청·응답 명세 변경 없음, 환경변수 추가 없음, DB 스키마 변경 없음
- 요청당 벡터 검색 쿼리가 보조 단어 수만큼(0~2개) 늘어납니다. 장소 단어 임베딩은 프로세스마다 단어당 한 번만 호출하고 캐시합니다. 응답 시간 영향은 따로 측정하지 않았습니다.
- **OSM 파일**: 대학 캠퍼스가 들어간 새 OSM 파일은 이 코드가 배포된 뒤에 전달드리겠습니다. 이 코드는 옛 파일과 새 파일을 모두 읽을 수 있지만, 이전 코드가 새 파일을 읽으면 `KeyError: 'university'`가 납니다.

## 관련 Issue
없음

## 리뷰 요청
- `query.py`의 보조 단어 연결 표(`NATURE_PLACE_WORDS`, `TRAIT_PLACE_WORDS`)는 프롬프트 `_PLACE_RULES`의 연결과 같아야 합니다. 한쪽을 바꿀 때 같이 고쳐야 해서 NOTE를 달아 두었습니다.
- `choose_tracks()`에 `top_n`(기본 3), `rng`(기본 새 `random.Random()`) 인자를 추가했습니다. 테스트처럼 결과를 고정해야 할 때 넘기면 됩니다.
- `_blend_search()` 인자에 `supports`가 추가됐습니다(서비스 내부 함수).

- [x] 작성자가 변경 내용을 직접 확인했습니다.
- [x] 비밀값·개인정보·모델 가중치·데이터셋이 포함되지 않았습니다.

author: quantumexplorer
body:
## Basic explanation

**What this does:** GroveDB has trees that keep a running total of what is inside them (sum trees and count trees). If one batch of writes created such a tree and also ran operations inside it that left it empty, for example deleting a key that was never there, GroveDB stored an ordinary tree with no total. From `GROVE_V5` it stores the tree that was asked for.

**Value:** A tree created this way no longer loses its total silently. Before, anything added to it later was never summed or counted into its parent, and `verify_grovedb` reported nothing wrong, so the error could only be seen as a wrong balance or count much later.

**Risks:** Low. The change is gated on `GROVE_V5`, which no released Platform version runs; `GROVE_V1`..`GROVE_V4` behave exactly as before and that is pinned by tests. Dash Platform's Drive does not build a batch of this shape today. On V5 the stored element differs for that shape, so the root hash and the cost differ, a batch that V4 refused (two wrapped forms, see below) is accepted, and one worst-case estimate grows by a few bytes.

## Issue being fixed or feature implemented

A batch that inserts a Merk aggregate tree (`SumTree`, `BigSumTree`, `CountTree`, `CountSumTree`, `ProvableCountTree`, `ProvableCountSumTree`, `ProvableSumTree`, `ProvableCountProvableSumTree`) and also carries operations at that tree's own path, none of which leaves a key there, stores a plain `Tree`.

The batch runs the level below the inserted tree first, then merges that level's root hash, root key and aggregate into the insert as `GroveOp::InsertTreeWithRootHash`. The apply arm rebuilds the stored element from the aggregate alone, and an empty Merk reports `AggregateData::NoAggregateData` whatever tree it belongs to, so the element comes out as `Element::Tree`.

It happens with default `BatchApplyOptions`, on a path that did not exist before the batch. No open issue covers it. It is related to #779 but does not need an existing tree.

## What was done?

- New version slot `apply_batch.tree_insert_above_emptied_level`: `0` in V1..V4 (the reported aggregate is used as it is, frozen), `1` in V5.
- New `aggregate_above_level` in `grovedb/src/batch/mod.rs`, called where the propagation merges a level's result into an insert, replace or patch op. It only dispatches: `aggregate_above_level_v0` (V1..V4, frozen) returns the reported aggregate, and `aggregate_above_level_v1` (V5) supplies the zero aggregate of the tree's own type when the level reports no aggregate and the inserted element is one of the eight Merk aggregate trees (wrapped or not). Everything else is passed through unchanged: plain trees, non-Merk trees, indexed trees, and every level that reports an aggregate.
- A conditional insert (`InsertIfNotExists`) has its own arm in the propagation and does not go through `aggregate_above_level`: it stores on V5 what it stores on V4 (see Not changed).
- `insert_op_with_propagated_root` and the partial-batch continuation are unchanged. The continuation already refuses an add-on whose type the pending aggregate does not name.
- `CHANGELOG.md` entry, and a note on the #779 row of `docs/audit-non-issues.md`.

### Before and after

```rust
// "parent" is an existing SumTree. "missing" is not stored.
db.apply_batch(vec![
    QualifiedGroveDbOp::insert_or_replace_op(vec![b"parent".to_vec()], b"tree".to_vec(), Element::empty_sum_tree()),
    QualifiedGroveDbOp::delete_op(vec![b"parent".to_vec(), b"tree".to_vec()], b"missing".to_vec()),
], None, None, grove_version);

// A later batch adds 100 under it.
db.apply_batch(vec![
    QualifiedGroveDbOp::insert_or_replace_op(vec![b"parent".to_vec(), b"tree".to_vec()], b"item".to_vec(), Element::new_sum_item(100)),
], None, None, grove_version);
```

| | `parent/tree` after the first batch | `parent` after the second batch | `verify_grovedb` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before, and still on `GROVE_V4` | `Tree(None)` | `SumTree(Some("tree"), 0)` | no issues |
| `GROVE_V5` | `SumTree(None, 0)` | `SumTree(Some("tree"), 100)` | no issues |

Wrapped trees, same batch shape:

| Inserted element | `GROVE_V4` | `GROVE_V5` |
|---|---|---|
| `NonCounted(CountTree)` | stores `NonCounted(Tree)` | stores `NonCounted(CountTree)` |
| `NotSummed(SumTree)` | batch fails with `CorruptedCodeExecution` | stores `NotSummed(SumTree)` |
| `NotCountedOrSummed(CountSumTree)` | batch fails with `CorruptedCodeExecution` | stores `NotCountedOrSummed(CountSumTree)` |

Worst-case batch estimate: it runs the same propagation and its levels never report an aggregate. For "insert a sum tree and write one sum item under it" the estimated added bytes go from 269 (V4) to 278 (V5), the 9 bytes of the sum tree's aggregate. The average-case estimate has sized such a tree as its own type since `GROVE_V4` and does not change.

### Not changed

A batch that inserts a tree over one that already holds rows still orphans those rows (#779). On V5 that tree now keeps its type as well, but the orphaned rows and the `verify_grovedb` failure are the same as before.

A conditional insert (`insert_if_not_exists_op`, `insert_if_not_exists_or_skip_op`) of a tree, in a batch that also carries operations under that tree, is not checked against the stored element on any version: the tree is written whether or not the key already holds one, and the error variant does not fail. That is older than this change and is left as it is. Because of it, this change leaves conditional inserts out: supplying the op's type would turn an empty plain `Tree` the key already holds into the sum tree a skipped insert names.

| Stored at the key before | Batch: conditional insert of `SumTree` + delete of a missing key under it | `GROVE_V4` | `GROVE_V5` |
|---|---|---|---|
| nothing | skip or error variant | `Tree(None)` | `Tree(None)` |
| empty `Tree` | skip or error variant | `Tree(None)` | `Tree(None)` |
| empty `SumTree` | skip or error variant | `Tree(None)` | `Tree(None)` |

### Dash Platform

Drive does not build this shape today. Its tree inserts are queued only when the tree is absent from committed state, its deletes target keys that are in committed state or sit under plain trees, and the aggregate trees it inserts unconditionally either receive an item in the same batch or have no operation under them. This was checked by reading every delete-emitting call site in `rs-drive` and `rs-drive-abci`, not by tests. The token order escrow helpers (create the token's sum tree if absent, remove an order with an unchecked delete) would build it once something places and removes a token's first listing in one batch; they have no production caller yet.

Platform picks this up when its GroveDB pin moves past this change and its next protocol version selects `GROVE_V5`.

## Public interface changes

**`grovedb-version`**

- `grovedb_version::version::grovedb_versions::GroveDBApplyBatchVersions` gains a public field:

  ```rust
  // before
  pub struct GroveDBApplyBatchVersions {
  ```

author: ivcained
body:
## Summary

```text
plugin-catalog/llmux.yaml
  -> ivcained/llmux @ 356118cf7f06dd08352636b2b3cc3795f4cc6e4e
     provider + local routing proxy + Desktop SDK composer card
```

### What this adds

Adds the community catalog entry for [LLMUX](https://github.com/ivcained/llmux), submitted by its repository owner, ivcained.

LLMUX registers one OpenAI-compatible model provider backed by a local routing proxy. It compares Surplus Intelligence, an optional Antseed buyer proxy, and optional Solid offers. A Desktop Plugin SDK composer card shows seller prices, published performance and trust, with explicit next-turn route selection. Hermes continues to own its sessions, streaming client and approvals. The plugin does not patch Hermes core or Desktop internals.

The entry targets Linux and macOS, since detached-child startup uses a Unix process lock. It pins a full immutable release commit. Version 0.1.1 and verification evidence below correspond to the pinned release tree.

## Credentials and profile isolation

- Reads declared marketplace credentials only through `agent.secret_scope.get_secret`: `SURPLUS_API_KEY`, optional `LLMUX_SURPLUS_API_KEY`, `SOLID_API_KEY`, `LLMUX_SOLID_API_KEY`, and `HERMES_CUSTOM_SOLID_API_KEY`.
- Does not read `.env`, `auth.json`, browser profiles, keychains or other credential files. Does not use subscription OAuth tokens.
- Passes scoped source keys to a detached proxy through a scrubbed environment. Unrelated gateway credentials and approval flags are not inherited.
- Hermes and the card authenticate to the loopback proxy with an in-memory profile/configuration-bound capability rather than an upstream API key. Foreign-profile, legacy unauthenticated and mismatched proxy listeners fail closed. Separate concurrent profiles require separate ports. Key or routing-setting changes require stopping the old proxy safely before reuse.
- No extra credential store, wallet custody, funding transfer or on-chain action. Antseed funding and payments remain the buyer proxy's responsibility. Antseed-only operation with no marketplace key is not supported by this version.

## Network and spend disclosure

- Default remote hosts: `api.surplusintelligence.ai` for model, market and performance reads and inference; `accounts.solid.xyz` for authenticated model discovery and inference.
- Optional Antseed buyer proxy: `http://127.0.0.1:8377/v1`. The separately operated buyer proxy handles its network and payment interactions.
- LLMUX listens on `127.0.0.1:8378` by default. The Desktop backend makes authenticated, read-only data and planning requests to this fixed loopback service. Upstream base URLs and the listener port can be configured. Nonlocal binding requires explicit `LLMUX_ALLOW_REMOTE=1`.
- Catalog reads and route planning do not submit completions. Inference sends the conversation context to the selected upstream and bills its funded account. There is no per-request spend approval or hard spend ceiling in this provider plugin.
- Cross-source failover is disabled by default. Explicit `LLMUX_ALLOW_FAILOVER=1` allows additional potentially billable attempts after eligible upstream errors. Budget-exceeded errors, pinned seller requests and partially streamed completions are never replayed to another source.
- Explicitly untrusted sellers are excluded from automatic routing. Selecting one manually requires the card's confirmation. Unpublished trust is not described as verification.

## Background processes and disk writes

- Starts a Python child with `start_new_session=True` when its loopback port is not listening. It can outlive Hermes. It does not launch a shell or a second Hermes agent and does not auto-update its source.
- Refreshes public marketplace data in the background and writes an atomic snapshot under `$HERMES_HOME/llmux/market-cache.json` by default. Proxy output and a spawn lock live under `$HERMES_HOME/logs/`.
- Usage recording is disabled by default. `LLMUX_TRACK_USAGE=1` enables `$HERMES_HOME/llmux/usage.jsonl`, containing model/source/seller identifiers, token counts and cost estimates, not prompts, completions or credentials. No usage telemetry is transmitted.
- May read an optional rewards-description JSON file and Solid's dated price override JSON file. Documented path overrides can place these data files outside the default profile data directory.
- Solid prices are a manual table dated 2026-11-09. Solid speed and trust are unpublished. Seller lists are ranked shortlists rather than full market inventories.

## Evidence

- **Before:** no LLMUX catalog entry exists in upstream.
  **After:** one community entry pins [LLMUX 0.1.1](https://github.com/ivcained/llmux/tree/356118cf7f06dd08352636b2b3cc3795f4cc6e4e); no Hermes core changes.

### Verification and boundaries

Backend tests include synthetic upstream routing, failover guards, opt-in accounting, private endpoint authorization, scoped credentials, source-key/local-bearer separation, detached-child startup and actual Hermes credential resolution. Component tests and rendered browser QA exercise the real card with an isolated test host.

Not claimed: native installed-Desktop switching, a paid end-to-end completion, a real paid-reply ledger row, catalog admission or maintainer approval. No paid inference was performed for this submission preparation. Any isolated-host demo is labelled as such.

Local verification: exact-release unittest discovery passed 194 tests in 53.984 seconds, including the Desktop wrapper. The same 62 Desktop scenarios also pass directly; these counts overlap. Validator passed with zero warnings and host_ready=true; doctor passed. Real-component browser QA covered 11 states at 1280x800 and 390x844 with matching source hashes and no reported clipping findings. Scoped lintapple exited 0 with documented SDK/harness exclusions, not whole-app accessibility certification.


Independent read-only release review found no blocking security or logic issues in the final confirmation-copy correction and its regression, and confirmed correspondence with the credential-boundary approval. This review did not rerun tests; the exact-release rerun above was performed separately.

Reproduction from the plugin checkout with Hermes's Python environment:

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$(dirname "$PWD"):$HOME/.hermes/hermes-agent" \
  "$HOME/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python" -m unittest discover -s tests -q
hermes plugins validate . --install-deps --json
hermes plugins doctor . --ci
```

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way for catalog discoverability. Delisting reverses the listing; it does not uninstall existing copies or reverse any paid requests made after installation.

**Blast Radius:** plugin.

This catalog-only PR does not activate the provider. Users must install and select it. The detached proxy, credential handling, upstream context disclosure, optional retries and absence of a hard spending ceiling are disclosed above and in the pinned README. Native Desktop and paid execution remain unverified. Maintainer review and CI are separate admission gates.

author: heliocosta-dev
body:
Pairing a computer from the desktop app now starts with open defaults the person sees before Allow, and on a Mac goes on to one "Get this Mac ready" step for the permissions agents need. ADR 0165 §7-9.

## Engine
- Commands turned off on a computer whose runner reports access: the agent is told the person turns them on in the agentes.chat app there (Preferences › Tools), not to restart the runner without `--no-exec`.
- `computer_status` says what is off on each computer and who turns it on.
- A person's Mac among the devices: a screenshot is `screencapture` through commands, then uploaded. Screen Recording, and Full Disk Access for a file refused with "Operation not permitted" (what a shell prints for macOS's EPERM) or "Permission denied" (what the runner's file tools say for it), are turned on in the app (Preferences › General › Permissions).

## Web
- Settings in each device row's ⋯ menu, and the Tools card's way to turn tools on in this Mac's app.

## Desktop
- The card after sign-in and a pair link's confirm show "What agents can do here" as switches, prefilled open: Commands on, Claude Code and Codex when found, the browser. Folders come later, in Preferences.
- Prepare this Mac, right after Allow (or Connect, or the site's This computer), and the same rows under Preferences › General › Permissions:
  - **Screen Recording**: Allow (the system prompt), then Open Settings. The row says macOS asks again about once a month, choose Allow.
  - **Full Disk Access**, in place of the Desktop, Documents and Downloads rows, so no folder prompt stops agents mid-task. No prompt can ask for it, so the button always opens System Settings on its list (`Privacy_AllFiles`) and the row says to turn agentes.chat on there. Its state comes from opening the privacy database (`TCC.db`, the user's or else the system's), which opens only with Full Disk Access and never prompts.
  - **Local network (phones over Wi-Fi)**, on macOS 15 and later only: adb, a child of the app's runner, needs it for mDNS and the TCP connect when pairing Android phones over Wi-Fi. Allow raises the prompt with a two-second Bonjour browse from the app (`DNSServiceBrowse` of `_adb-tls-connect._tcp`), then the button opens System Settings (`Privacy_LocalNetwork`). macOS has no call that reads this permission, so the row says "Not asked yet" or "Asked", never On. macOS 14 and older have no such permission, so there is no row there (the app reads `kern.osproductversion` into `app_info`; an unread version keeps the row).
  - The rows have no icon tile: their words run to three lines or more, which a tile's column would squeeze.
- `Info.plist`: `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription`, `NSBonjourServices` (`_adb-tls-pairing._tcp`, `_adb-tls-connect._tcp`, `_adb._tcp`). The Desktop, Documents and Downloads usage strings stay, since they still word any folder prompt.
- Resume after macOS's Quit & Reopen (Screen Recording and Full Disk Access): the step, or Preferences, is kept in `setup.json` and opens again within 30 minutes on the main window's page.
- The pairing dialog's text was over the 120 characters Rust takes for the app's labels in every language (158 in English), so the label set was refused and the site's This computer could not pair. It is shorter in all 14 languages, and the menu label test now covers every language.

## Owner decision left open
The server running on this computer (agentes.chat run here) starts its own homes with commands **on** too, like every other new pairing (decided after review; ADR 0165 §7 and a note in ADR 0060). Commands there run as the person and can reach the server's files; Preferences › Tools turns them off. The one-command install's Mac question keeps its own default.

## Checks
- Local, one file at a time, on e25e1cf3db: desktop `permissions`, `pair`, `styles`, `this-mac`, `popover`, `prefs-hints`; engine `desktop`. Typecheck: desktop, engine. Earlier on this branch also desktop `i18n`, `first-run`; engine `device-tools`, `machines`; web `devices`, `this-mac`.
- `cargo check --lib --tests` (no warnings) and `cargo test --lib` (72 passed, including one that reads macOS's version on the build Mac) in `apps/desktop/src-tauri`.
- Remote CI on e25e1cf3db: every step passes. Geometry did not run (it stays on the Mac, and this change's screens are the desktop app's, which it does not lay out).
- Shots of Prepare this Mac and Preferences › Permissions at the windows' real sizes (720×600, 860×600) in English, German and Russian, light and dark, with a long workspace name. Impeccable's detector finds only what was there before (the dev frame, a 10.5px nav label, a bounce easing).

## Not verified on a real Mac
No signed build ran here. To try on a Mac with a build of this branch:
- Full Disk Access reads Off, then On after turning agentes.chat on in System Settings and choosing Quit & Reopen; the step comes back.
- Allow on Local network shows macOS's prompt, and adb pairs a phone over Wi-Fi afterwards.
- Screen Recording's monthly prompt names agentes.chat when an agent runs `screencapture`.
- On a Mac with macOS 14, the Local network row is absent and Prepare this Mac finishes without it.
