author: edwh
body:
## Summary

- A single mailbox leaving the relay queue is released by two clear scans and not reported as stale. Only a whole provider released without confirmation raises a Sentry event; "probe unreadable" still does.
- The WhatJobs gate forces a rebuild after 10 hours, not 20. With the strict comparison against a rebuild stamped at the end of a 15-minute run, the table is at most about 10 hours old against the 24-hour freshness floor. A test models the schedule and requires 6 hours of headroom.
- `artisan` does not report a mistyped command line (a Symfony console usage error) to Sentry. The check is a plain function that loads nothing, so an autoload failure is still reported.
- The reach evaluation "breaker open" call is logged, not reported; the PHP breaker is only opened by its own evaluation, whose failure reports itself.
- Docs: `ads.md`, `mail-deferrals.md`, `partner-integrations.md` and `moderating-posts.md` updated or marked reviewed.

| Sentry issue | Events in 14 days | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| "Mail suppression released as stale" (7681616921) | 728 | An address row stops refreshing when its backlog drops under 5; the relay expires the rest after five days. That normal exit skipped the two-clear-scans rule and was flagged stale. 280 such rows released in four days, lifetimes 4 to 5 days. |
| "[ScheduledOutcomes] integrations:sync-whatjobs: jobs.seenat last advanced 1469 min ago" (7559821823) | 22 | Syncs run at 04:40 and 09:00 to 21:00 UTC. With a 20-hour skip limit, a 04:40 rebuild is next due at 00:40, when nothing runs, so the next one is 04:40 the next day: 24 hours plus run time, against a 24-hour floor. |
| "The --dry-run option does not exist" (7827340904) | 1 | Someone typing the command wrong. |
| "ripple: reach evaluation unavailable" (7711739056, 7745451379) | 10 | The "breaker open" echo of a failure already reported. |

No screenshot: nothing a member sees changes.

### Deploy

Batch container rebuild. Nothing is order-dependent.

## Test plan

- PHPUnit, run locally through the status API: `DeferralScanServiceTest`, `ScanDeferralsCommandTest`, `SyncWhatJobsGateTest`, `ArtisanUsageErrorTest`, `ReachServiceTest`, `MaxReachServiceTest` (124 passed).

---

### Sentry-sourced?

- **Issue**: the issues in the table.
- **Breadcrumbs read?** Not applicable: server-side messages raised by our own commands; their context was read.
- **Loki cross-referenced?** Production database instead: address suppression rows released in the four days to 2026-11-11, with their `last_seen` and lifetimes; WhatJobs `jobs.seenat` and `posted_at`.
- **Integration gap?** None.

author: sergeytolkachyov
body:
Fresh Linux SQL initialization was disabled because a process group could not prove ownership of every descendant. This change adds an owned user/PID namespace carrier/init with retained pidfds, exact boot/birth/token checks and receipt publication before target execution. Descendants that call setsid remain contained; a new controller can reopen the exact attempt after restart. Windows retains non-breakaway Job objects, and legacy PGID evidence remains conservative.

SQL observation recovers from the native receipt before a wrapper receipt exists. Stop and timeout require positive whole-tree absence. Durable controller decisions survive failed stops and root-exit receipt admission, including Windows CRLF replay; a subsequent status resumes committed stop intent. Linux reopen failures return bounded CLI errors. SQL reservation precedes spawn, and native spawn/signal/wait stay outside SQL transactions. Linux lock owners use host-visible procfs identity for crash/replay. Detached file-only deadlines are enforced on subsequent observation.

Refs #13; release tracker #12. [Ownership model, prerequisites and limits](https://github.com/WebTolk/process-forge/blob/140e3c9cb5f2a5c4951375b734a728249fd53fd5/docs/concepts/linux-owned-execution.md).

Validated head **140e3c9cb5f2a5c4951375b734a728249fd53fd5**, integration base **008f44db1f6636960229fd387a0a3eff86b252f5**:

- Real Windows build 26300, Python 3.11.9: **53 passed, 1 Linux-only skip** in the corrected controller/lifecycle suite. Real Linux kernel 6.18.58.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2, Python 3.12.3: **67 passed, no skips**, including all native boundary tests. Captured changed-source hashes match committed blobs. All nine shared required recovery/deadline cases passed on both platforms.
- [Native Linux CI](https://github.com/WebTolk/process-forge/actions/runs/43069712615), Ubuntu 22.04/Python 3.11: **551 passed, 38 existing platform skips**, no failures. It checks out the exact head. JUnit confirms all six fresh sealed SQL CLI cases, durable failed-stop replay, first stop with a live descendant, interrupted stop/status recovery, fresh SQL collection and governed transition/next prepare. Required scenarios are not satisfied by skips.
- [Public source CI](https://github.com/WebTolk/process-forge/actions/runs/43069712686) passed on Windows and Ubuntu. Isolated public schemas, generated checksum inventory and cleanliness checks passed without private project state.
- Scoped format passed; Ruff and mypy added no diagnostics against the exact base, preserving 320 inherited Ruff and 112 inherited mypy diagnostics under C02. Diagnostic matching retains file/rule/message/source-context hashes and normalizes embedded line references.

Independent PF shell reviews of the earlier candidates found SQL recovery/deadline gaps, Windows marker replay and stop-intent loss. Those findings are fixed and prior failed runs are retained locally; they are not counted as successful qualification. A fresh independent PF shell worker explicitly returned **approve** for this exact head after checking the final five-file correction delta against the comprehensively reviewed predecessor, running independent native Job/replay experiments and verifying the completed platform/CI evidence. All three final findings are closed; no new proven defect was found. The report was natively collected and its review Work completed.

author: abyyxhek
body:
## Description

`continuum --json forget` wrote its three error lines to stdout (`file=out`) instead of stderr: the empty `--tenant` guard, the unknown `--run-id` lookup, and the tombstone target run lookup. The `--json` flag promises machine-parseable output on stdout (`cli/exitcodes.py`: "Text output is for people; exit codes and `--json` are for machines"), and every other command already reports `error:` lines on stderr (58 such prints in `cli/main.py`). A consumer parsing stdout for a JSON object instead received bare text, and a shell inspecting stderr for diagnostics saw nothing.

All three prints in `cmd_forget` now use `file=err`, matching the rest of the CLI. The exit codes are unchanged (`ERROR` for the tenant guard, `NOT_FOUND` for both run lookups), and the success path (including `--json` output) is untouched.

## Related issues

Fixes #2081

## Types of changes

- Type: `bugfix`

## Breaking changes

No. Command exit codes and the `--json` success output are unchanged; only the stream carrying the diagnostic text moves from stdout to stderr, which is where every other command already puts it. Consumers who parsed stdout for error text (against the documented contract) need to read stderr instead.

## How has this been tested?

Regression tests added to `tests/test_forget.py`, one per error site, each asserting the exit code, an empty stdout, and the message on stderr:

```
python -m pytest tests/test_forget.py --no-cov
7 passed in 5.03s
```

All three new tests fail on the pre-fix code (the errors land on stdout) and pass after the fix. Manual reproduction before the fix:

```
empty --tenant -> rc=1 stdout='error: --tenant is required and must be non-empty\n' stderr=''
unknown run-id -> rc=2 stdout="error: no such run: 'typo'\n" stderr=''
```

after the fix:

```
empty --tenant -> rc=1 stdout='' stderr='error: --tenant is required and must be non-empty\n'
unknown run-id -> rc=2 stdout='' stderr="error: no such run: 'typo'\n"
```

Gates run from the worktree against this branch (cut from upstream/main at 31efabc1):

```
uvx ruff@0.16.10 check src/ tests/ examples/
All checks passed!

uvx ruff@0.16.10 format --check src/ tests/ examples/
1 file would be reformatted, 418 files already formatted
(the single failure is the pre-existing src/continuum/recovery/restore.py:108,
also covered by the already-open style PR #2067; this change adds none)

mypy src/continuum
Success: no issues found in 154 source files
```

## Checklist

Tests added or updated for the changed behaviour. Documentation updated where the change affects user-facing behaviour. CI passes on the latest commit. Security-relevant changes state known limitations explicitly in this description.

## Additional context

The empty `--tenant` guard is only reachable by passing `--tenant ""`, since argparse already requires the flag; the test covers that spelling. The tombstone target lookup is defensive (the run was validated moments earlier), so its test monkeypatches `SQLiteStorage.get_run` to fail on the second call.

The largest rise is printed with the other numbers.

**`webviews/test/tray-exit-fold-once.test.ts` (plain).** The comment at `TRACE` said that the second gap comes with the fold's clock at 75 ms. That was true with the old hold. With the hold that never moves the clock back, the clock is at 90.67 ms at the frame before that gap, past the first half, so the frame loop has stopped and the second gap is not held. Only `SOONER` holds a second time (71.67 ms to 88.33 ms). The comment says this now, and one new test states it ("a gap past the first half is not held; one before it is held one frame on").

No product file changes. The WebKit gap after the second painted frame of the fold (cause not found; the lead's decision is no product change and no larger bound) is not touched: this PR adds no retry and changes no bound.

Docs-only. Appends one keeper entry to `docs/homepage-team/image-prompt-library.md` for the §0-P product hero on `/notebook/what-is-an-under-the-bed-restraint-system-and-how-do-you-use-one`, published live by content run 1969 today.

## Why it is worth a commit

The entry records two lessons that between them cost two regenerations this run, and both generalise past this one post.

**Reference-photo choice.** Three of the four Shopify photos for `under-the-bed-restraint-system-black` are box or on-model shots, so `21408D` is the only usable clean packshot. That is the kind of thing nobody wants to rediscover by burning a generation batch.

**The embed-match collision.** `scripts/check-hero-embed-match.ts` flagged this hero three times for naming catalog products the post does not embed, while the hero was in fact depicting the right product. The cause is that on a bondage or restraint topic the category's own vocabulary is also other SKUs' vocabulary. `me-you-us-bed-restraints` needs all of under, mattress, bed, restraint and system; two cuff SKUs need plain + wrist and padded + wrist. Since `isNamedIn` requires every distinctive token to be present, dropping "mattress" and "wrist" from the prompt and the alt clears all three, and keeping black, under, bed, restraint and system in means `heroNamesAnyProduct` still resolves the real subject.

The resolution had to be a regeneration rather than a prompt rewrite. `imagePrompt` has to be the prompt that actually made the image, which is what #2750 and #9369 exist to protect, so editing the stored prompt to satisfy a checker would destroy the record the checker is there to guard. Treating the three flags as false positives was also not available, since the routine says to resolve them "not by loosening the check".

**Finish drift.** "Buckled cuff" makes the model draw a leather buckle cuff, and the real cuff is fabric with a hook-and-loop strap, so the product-fidelity gate blocks it. "Nylon" in the alt trips the unsourced-spec check.

## Scope and risk

One file, eleven added lines, no deletions. No code, no config, no schema, no agent definition, no protected path. Nothing here changes behaviour; it is a note for the next run that art-directs a restraint or bondage hero.

author: njogu-ndegwa
body:
**Needs Dennis: do not merge without him.** It has a schema migration (new columns on `users` and `customers`) and it touches PPPoE router assignment. Requested by Elija (Elgylinkconnect) on 29 Oct and confirmed 11 Nov.

## What changed

**1. Customer register fields (all optional)**
- New `customers` columns: `location` (free text), `id_number`, `house`, `email`, `install_date` (DATE), `notes`.
- Location reuses the existing `latitude` / `longitude` / `location_captured_at` columns. Register and edit accept an optional lat/lng pair.
- `POST /api/customers/register` and `PUT /api/customers/{id}` accept the fields. On edit, an empty string clears a field and an omitted field is left alone. `install_date: null` clears the date. Bad email or over-long values return 400.
- The fields are returned by register, edit, `GET /api/customers/{id}`, `GET /api/customers` and `/api/customers/active`. The admin detail page loads customers from the list, so the list needs them. Changes show in the customer audit log.

**2. Opt-in PPPoE router lock (default OFF)**
- New column `users.pppoe_router_lock_enabled` (default false) and new column `customers.pppoe_locked_router_id` (plain integer, no FK, so `Customer.router` does not become ambiguous).
- `GET/PUT /api/pppoe/router-lock`: read or toggle the setting. Turning it on stamps each of that reseller's existing PPPoE customers with their current router. A customer registered while the lock is on is stamped at registration.
- With the lock on, changing a stamped customer's router in the edit form returns **409** `{"status": "pppoe_router_locked", ...}`.
- `POST /api/customers/{id}/pppoe-router-lock/release` clears one customer's stamp. Their next move is allowed, and the router they move to becomes the locked one. This is recorded as a customer event.
- A whole-router PPPoE transfer (`pppoe_router_transfer`, used when a box is replaced) moves the lock to the target router.
- The new routes have no staff rule, so they stay owner-only.
- This change touches only the database. It does not write to any router and does not change any provisioning path. It works because the app only ever puts a PPPoE secret on `customer.router_id`: the edit path removes the secret from the old router, and the recovery sweep removes moved CID-tagged secrets. So blocking the move is what keeps the login off a second router. RADIUS is not used for PPPoE in this codebase.

**What the lock does NOT cover (for Dennis to decide)**
- A secret a reseller adds by hand on another router in Winbox (no `CID:` comment). The sweep never removes those.
- `scripts/pppoe_customer_import.py --reassign-existing` (ops script) does not check the lock.
- Customers created by the import or by payment paths while the lock is on are not stamped. Each gets one free move, then is locked where it lands.

## Migrations
- `run_pppoe_router_lock_user_migration` runs right after `run_free_setup_column_migration`, before any user reads, and is fatal like that one. It is `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS ... DEFAULT false` (metadata only).
- `run_customer_register_migrations` uses the same lock_timeout retry loop as the grace / pause migrations. All new customer columns are nullable with no default.
- `tests/schema_snapshot.json` is refreshed. `tests/test_migration_standby.py` now stubs the new startup migration too.

## Tests
- New: `tests/test_customer_register_fields_and_router_lock.py` (11 tests). Covers: register saves and validates the fields; edit sets, clears and keeps them; null install date clears; lock off by default; register with lock on stamps and refuses a move; enabling stamps only PPPoE customers; release allows one move then relocks; turning the lock off stops enforcement; hotspot customers are ignored.
- Full local suite (SQLite): the only failure was `test_migration_standby`, which my new migration caused. It is fixed, and that test, the new tests and `test_schema_migrations` now pass. I did not run Postgres-only tests locally; CI runs them.

author: domixayo-gif
body:
## Problem
The EMA strategy correctly aligns fresh signals with the 1-minute EMA20/50 + ADX/DI + CHOP filters and the closed 5-minute EMA trend. However, after a confirmed loss, the existing EMA recovery flow intentionally reuses the previous signal's asset and direction without generating a new pullback signal. If the market regime changes during that recovery sequence, a same-direction follow-up could be sent against the new trend.

## Targeted fix
- Add a read-only current-trend check using the existing EMA20/50 slopes, +DI/-DI direction, ADX minimum, CHOP25 maximum, and closed 5-minute EMA20/50 alignment.
- Re-fetch closed 1-minute and 5-minute candles immediately before every EMA order.
- Block a queued fresh order if the current directional regime no longer confirms its direction.
- If an active recovery follow-up no longer agrees with the current trend (or the trend is unclear), pause recovery and switch AUTO OFF rather than forcing an opposite-trend martingale order.
- Add tests for bullish/bearish confirmation and opposing 5-minute context.

## Preservation
- No changes to EMA entry/pullback rules, thresholds, indicator periods, RSI checks, 2-minute expiry, payout-aware stake sizing, recovery sequence sizing, session target, exposure limits, asset selection, or other strategies.
- No changes to the $2 recovery-sequence target or +$10 AUTO-run target.
- Exact pre-change copies of scanner.py, ema_strategy.py, and test_ema_strategy.py are included under `backups/pre_ema_recovery_direction_guard_20261111/`.

## Validation
GitHub Actions must pass before merging. This PR does not start the scanner or place trades.

author: carlos-eduedu
body:
Entrega a Fase 3 do `AGENTS.md`: o painel da equipe (`apps/painel`) e a API admin (`/admin/*`).

## Aceite
- O atendente assume a conversa e responde, e a IA fica em silêncio até ele devolver. Coberto por `tests/test_painel_api.py::test_atendente_assume_responde_e_ia_cala_ate_devolver`.
- Revelar um CPF grava `revelar:cpf` na `auditoria`. Coberto por `test_revelar_cpf_grava_auditoria`.

## O que muda
- **Estado de atendimento:** fica em `conversas.atendimento` (`ia`, `handoff`, `assumida`), com dono e horário. A decisão está em `docs/decisoes/0003` e os termos no `GLOSSARY.md`.
  - O turno lê esse estado sob a trava.
  - A liberação automática solta só o handoff sem dono.
  - Handoff e erro interno abrem alerta na mesma transação.
- **Login e sessão:**
  - argon2id (`argon2-cffi`).
  - 5 falhas bloqueiam por 15 min e derrubam as sessões abertas.
  - A sessão fica no banco (só o sha256 do token) e dura 8 h.
  - CSRF por HMAC com `SATURDAY_SESSAO_SEGREDO`, que passa a ser obrigatória fora de `pytest`.
  - O primeiro gestor é criado por `saturday criar-usuario`.
- **API `/admin/*`:**
  - inbox por fila, com não lidas e janela;
  - conversa com autor e status de entrega;
  - assumir, devolver, transferir e enviar texto ou modelo, sob a trava;
  - ficha mascarada e revelar auditado;
  - alertas, cota e mídia servida pela API.
- **Tempo real:** `pg_notify` na transação e uma conexão `LISTEN` por processo da API, repassada por SSE em `/admin/eventos`. Os avisos levam só IDs.
- **Worker:** abre alerta de cliente sem resposta há 10 min em conversa assumida. O outbox abre alerta quando desiste de um envio.
- **Front:** React, Vite, TS e `react-router`, servido por nginx com proxy de `/admin` (mesma origem). Entrou no compose e no CI (`tsc` e build).
- **Migração** `5d2e8c41a9f3`. O backfill grava o autor das mensagens antigas pela direção.
- **Log:** o access log do uvicorn deixou de gravar a query string, onde ia a busca por telefone.

## Desvios
- O painel só envia os modelos de utilidade sem botão de link, e sem variáveis. O motivo é que o repositório não sabe os parâmetros de cada modelo, e os links `/l/{codigo}` chegam na Fase 6.

## Verificação
- `pytest` com Postgres: 248 passaram e 1 foi pulado. `ruff`, `mypy` (core e simuladores) e `npm run build` passaram.
- Ponta a ponta local: API, worker, simulador da Meta e o painel no navegador, com as chamadas externas bloqueadas por proxy. Passaram:
  - assumir, responder e entregar a mensagem (`sent`);
  - a IA calada na mensagem seguinte do cliente;
  - a mensagem nova aparecendo por SSE;
  - revelar e devolver gravados na auditoria.

## Riscos conhecidos
- `GET /conversations/{id}` (contrato antigo) mostra o status do grafo, não o estado de atendimento.
- O stream SSE não confere a sessão de novo depois de aberto.
- O caminho real contra o MinIO segue sem teste neste ambiente.

author: kikoveiga
body:
## Motivation

Extract the shared context fix requested in [#252](https://github.com/DataDog/electron-sdk/pull/252#discussion_r4482821687) (RUM-18780). User/account data should be bounded once when updated, rather than on every main-process log.

## Changes

- Sanitize user/account data before storing current values and history, benefiting RUM, logs, and spans.
- Bound identity fields and combined extras separately. Both identities reject oversized standard fields without changing stored data or logging the rejected value.
- Extra-info merges apply shrinking replacements first and preserve accepted values when an update exceeds the budget. Full setters replace extras.
- Document these rules and cover them with unit and Electron end-to-end tests.

This can merge independently before #252.

## Test instructions

1. Initialize the playground SDK and set user or account info with an ID and `extraInfo: { first: 'x'.repeat(120_000) }`.
2. Add `extraInfo: { second: 'x'.repeat(120_000) }` using the matching extra-info API.
3. Read the matching getter and emit a RUM error: the ID and `first` remain, `second` is omitted, and skipping the oversized update produces a warning.
4. Use the extra-info merge API to replace `first` with `'x'.repeat(230_000)`, then try setting an oversized user/account ID or name: the previous attribute and identity should remain, with a single Electron warning that does not print the rejected value.
5. Set `extraInfo: { blob: 'x'.repeat(200_000) }`, then merge `{ note: 'y'.repeat(50_000), blob: 'short' }`: both updated attributes should be kept.

## Checklist

- [ ] Tested locally (playground)
- [x] Added unit tests for this change.
- [x] Added e2e/integration tests for this change.
- [x] Updated related documentation.
- [x] Review findings fixed, or dismissed with a reason.

author: gabriel-darbord
body:
`image_evaluate` compiled its code as a bare script. `leap := Leap new. leap leapYear: 2015` failed with `Undeclared variable named leap`, where a Playground declares `leap` for you, and `Transcript show:` wrote to stdout or a log file the caller never sees, so an agent checking its work by printing got nothing back, and `Transcript contents` is not understood by the `NonInteractiveTranscript` of a headless image.

A lowercase name the code assigns without declaring is now a variable of that call, as in a Playground page. `MCPPlaygroundRequestor` answers the compiler's requestor protocol, which is the same from Pharo 12 to 15; it answers `interactive` false so Pharo 12 does not hand it compile errors as a user interface. Two departures from the Playground: a name the code only reads stays undeclared, since that is a typo or a missing selector far more often than a variable meant to be nil, and the compile error points at its line; and the variables end with the call, since each evaluation gets a new requestor. A capitalized name stays undeclared, so a missing class still fails.

While the code runs, `MCPTranscriptRecorder` stands in for `Transcript`. It keeps what was written, up to the preview limit, and passes every write on to the Transcript it replaced. The answer gives it after the value as `Transcript:`, in `data.transcript`, and on a runtime error in `error.transcript`; `Transcript contents` answers it during the evaluation. The recorder puts the Transcript back only if it is still installed, and a recorder that finished is never put back, so overlapping evaluations cannot leave one behind.

The tool's description and the tool reference say both.

author: codegoddy
body: The studied build's export is fast because it composites the whole stage on the GPU and converts to 4:2:0 once there. This ports that to D3D11. `export/compose_gpu.rs` uploads the decoded NV12, converts it to RGB into a mipmapped texture, and composites the output frame in one pixel shader: - the source placed at a card rectangle: the crop stretched over the frame, or the card on a canvas; - its rounded corners and the background zoomed about the camera's target; - the motion blur, ported from `motion_blur.rs` line for line (`CardTrail` for a card, `ScreenTrail` when the screen fills the frame) at the studied 16 samples and 4-texel fetch span (`qualityByMode.export` / `fetchSpanTexelsByMode.export`); - the click ripple: each pixel's source position is displaced by the summed pull of up to three live clicks, as `ripple_preview.rs` does. Two more passes convert to NV12, and the planes are read back for the encoder. The cursor is drawn on that frame inside its box. Every export frame goes through the stage when the machine profile (base PR) finds a hardware GPU the frame fits on. The GPU crop and scale and the CPU compositor stay as the fallbacks for no fitting GPU, a camera layer, or a stage that fails mid-export. `APEXSHOT_EXPORT_GPU_STAGE=0` keeps the CPU compositor. ## Results (release build, development machine) | | GPU stage | CPU | |---|---|---| | 1080p zoom transition with motion blur, per frame | 5.2 ms | ~390 ms | | 2160x1260 canvas card zoom with blur, per frame | 8.7 ms | | | 6 s zoomed canvas export of a 1920x1200 recording, default blur | **5.3 s** | 46.0 s | | Same export, motion blur off | 5.9 s | | On the Iris Xe the same export took 5.6-8.1 s; on the RTX A500 beside it, 9.3-14.7 s. With no GPU it falls back to the CPU path and completes. ## Where the time goes `APEXSHOT_EXPORT_TRACE=1` logs each range's milliseconds per stage frame. Release build, 1080p30, Quick Sync: | | decoder wait | upload | GPU | readback | cursor | encoder wait | per range | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1.6x zoom, 2 ranges | 3.2-4.4 | 1.1 | 2.2-2.8 | 3.1 | — | 2.4-2.8 | 13.2-13.7 | | click burst with cursor and ripple, 3 ranges | 2.8-3.9 | 1.2 | 3.3-3.4 | 4.1-4.2 | 0.9-3.9 | 1.5-1.6 | 15.8-18.1 | The same clip exports at 7.7 ms/frame as a plain passthrough and 9.0 ms/frame zoomed, so the whole GPU path, transfers included, costs about 1.3 ms/frame once ranges run in parallel. Handing D3D11 textures to the encoder would need an in-process encoder (ffmpeg is fed through a pipe) and could save at most that 1.3 ms; it is not worth doing yet. With a camera layer, which still uses the CPU compositor, the same zoomed export takes 27.6 ms/frame against 7.7 without it; moving the camera into the stage is the next export step, after the camera rewrite lands. ## Testing - Parity with the CPU paths: identical crop (PSNR inf), 56.6 dB identity round trip, 54.9 dB motion blur, 56.5 dB click ripple (two overlapping waves), rounded card over the background, background zoom about its pivot. These tests caught a screen-mode bug: anti-aliasing the frame's own edges would have darkened a one-pixel border on every unzoomed export. - A GPU export and a CPU export of the same zoomed canvas recording agree at 35 dB on average. The lowest frames are blur frames where the CPU path leaves the footage over the padding sharp (a visible seam), and the stage blurs the whole card as the studied build does. Resting and zoomed frames were compared by eye. - A click-burst export with the ripple (2 s, 1080p, debug build): 18.6 ms/frame through the stage against 224 ms/frame on the CPU; the two exports agree at 44.7 dB on average and 40.9 dB on the worst frame, with the same ripple shape by eye. - An ignored `stage_throughput_benchmark` times the stage. - When NVENC, Quick Sync and AMF all fail to open, the export now tries Windows Media Foundation (`h264_mf` / `hevc_mf`, hardware forced) before x264/x265. Both open with the export's flags on the development machine (High / Main profile, bitrate within 1% of the target, 180-210 fps at 1080p). - An encoder probe that fails now logs the driver's first error line, e.g. `h264_nvenc unavailable: Driver does not support the required nvenc API version. Required: 13.1 Found: 13.0`. - Clippy clean; all 935 tests and the export integration tests (parallel against sequential, zoomed canvas card, chunked join, GPU scaler) pass through the stage. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

author: tontsa128
body:
## What this fixes

The live dashboard previously had two competing decision paths: the canonical 14-check multi-timeframe Spot strategy and a separate heuristic score that could overwrite the main BUY/SELL/WAIT display. This PR makes the canonical strategy the only source of actionable main-dashboard decisions. The 1m/3m/5m/15m cards are explicitly labelled as technical direction only, not trade signals.

## Live market data

- Adds a real Binance REST fallback when WebSocket trade, bookTicker, or kline streams go stale.
- Validates ticker timestamps, bid/ask integrity, and the currently open candle's OHLC/time alignment before updating the chart.
- Updates the chart from the validated open Binance candle; never fabricates candle data.
- Shows whether the price and order book are sourced from WebSocket or REST.
- Keeps the existing freshness, spread, volume, ADX, risk, and multi-timeframe gates unchanged. Stale or invalid data fails closed to WAIT.

## Cloudflare Worker

- Adds Wrangler configuration with preview support and static assets.
- Adds a Worker handler that serves the dashboard and proxies only the fixed `/api/market` route to the existing Vercel market-data API.
- The proxy does not accept arbitrary upstream URLs and disables caching for market responses.
- Isolates the Worker build under `/cloudflare` and skips unrelated Python dependency installation for this JavaScript-only Worker.

## Verification

Latest head: `b3bd5b3d46f2ca32af1faf1c3c430e238ec96756`

- Trading Engine Tests: PASS
- Fast Paper 5s: PASS
- Fast Paper 15s: PASS
- Python indicator tests: PASS
- Paper-exit and persistence regression tests: PASS
- Cloudflare Workers preview build: SUCCESS; static assets uploaded and preview created:
  https://fix-live-market-rest-failover-ai-trading-pro.toni-jukka4.workers.dev

A fresh 210-second 5s/15s real-Binance paper session on main also completed successfully: both WebSocket streams connected, 94k+ WebSocket messages, 17.9k trade messages, 0 WebSocket errors, 0 REST quote errors, and 0 simulated trades. No trade was forced when entry conditions did not align.

## Production deployment

The Vercel deployment API currently rejects new deployments with HTTP 402 `api-deployments-free-per-day` (100/day quota; retry after 24 hours). The existing Vercel production deployment remains on commit `9af2ba237370c90d1e4a1593589e569268620d27`. This PR's Vercel production deployment has therefore not been verified. Cloudflare's main-branch production build is configured to deploy the same Worker after merge; its production result must be checked separately.

No real exchange orders are sent. This remains Binance Spot analysis and paper trading only.

body:
`pnpm install` on `main` (and every pnpm script, via the deps-status check) fails:

```
[ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION] 1 lockfile entries failed verification:
  @hono/node-server@2.1.7 was published at 2026-11-11T09:07:07.000Z, within the minimumReleaseAge cutoff
```

`@hono/node-server@2.1.7` was published 2026-11-11T09:10Z and PR #90 merged at 2026-11-11T15:43Z, so the lockfile it committed resolved to a version inside pnpm 11's default 24h supply-chain cooldown. The PR title said `2.1.3`; the lockfile actually contains `2.1.7` (`^2.1.3` range hit the newest release).

## Change

Pin the resolved version back to `2.1.6` (published 2026-11-02, well outside the cooldown). `package.json` keeps `^2.1.3`; only the lockfile changes, 4 lines.

## Verification

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` → `✓ Lockfile passes supply-chain policies (505 entries)`, install completes
- `pnpm run lint` → `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors` (also exercises the deps-status check that failed before)

No consumer-visible change: dev-only dependency, `chore` type keeps it out of `CHANGELOG.md`.

前置 PR：#7。与 phone-use 0.2.0 的 connection_id 协议配套，Shell 升为 0.4.0/code 12；需要成对升级，不能单边部署。

过去 HTTP 回传只靠 device_id 找当前连接，重连前的线程可能把旧结果或状态投递给新连接。现在 hello 声明能力，首条 welcome 验证设备和 connection_id 后才标记在线。每个请求线程与异步状态线程捕获不可变的原连接，ACK/response/state 都用该连接 ID；旧线程 finally 只清自身，不能清新连接。ACK 未被接受或执行前所属连接已失效时不开始操作。旧服务端没有合法 welcome 会明确断开，设置显示升级说明。

┌─ SSE A ─┐ → RPC 线程 A → 回传 A
└─────────┘
┌─ SSE B ─┐ → RPC 线程 B → 回传 B
└─────────┘
重连不会把 A 的线程改写成 B；已经开始的外部效果仍可能完成，断连不等于回滚。

验证：assembleDebug、assembleRelease（R8）、HTML JS 语法与 git diff --check 通过。Pixel 7 / Android 16 安装 release 变体并明确更换 UID 2000 助手后，对冻结 phone-use 680069b 的实际 create_phone_app/PhoneBridge SSE 路径完成：ACK/response/state 携同 owner 返回 200；暂挂真实设备 response 后断 SSE，重连生成新 ID，再放旧 response 得 409；旧 state 得 409 且未污染 descriptor；新连接随机中文/emoji 输入和 Submit 经独立 ContentProvider 精确核对；ACK 被拒绝 503 时按钮计数不变。旧 welcome 无 ID 也真实拒绝，协议场景完整重跑通过。

已验证 APK 为 release/R8 变体，遵循仓库已有本机 debug 签名演示约定；不是 GitHub release，也未部署。制品 SHA-256：86683f2ddae7533eafee325eb0e213951e005c20c433112596c46746e3ee52e0。旧线上 APK 签名不同，不能据此承诺原地覆盖；测试机已授权替换。本 PR 不声称解决已开始请求的并发效果或完整主屏隔离，这些在后续边界修复中独立验证。

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
### Description

Fixes JWT algorithm confusion (code scan finding `sfind-a4f45faa3a184b3bb0ca49f541dcd905`). Before this change, `express-jwt@0.1.3` / `jsonwebtoken@0.4.0` / `jws.verify(token, publicKey)` let the token header pick the algorithm. That meant `alg: none` tokens, and HS256 tokens signed with the public `jwt.pub` key, passed `isAuthorized()`, `isAccounting()`, `isDeluxe()` and the other checks as any user. The existing API test `GET basket should accept forged JWTs` confirmed this on `master`.

Changes:
- `package.json`: `express-jwt` 0.1.3 → `^8.5.1`, `jsonwebtoken` 0.4.0 → `^9.0.2`, `jws` `^4.0.0` added as a direct dependency, `@types/jsonwebtoken` → `^9.0.10`. Removed `@types/express-jwt` because v8 ships its own types. Dropped the matching Dependabot ignore entries.
- `lib/insecurity.ts`:
  - `isAuthorized()` now uses `expressjwt({ secret: publicKey, algorithms: ['RS256'] })`.
  - `verify()` now uses `jws.verify(token, 'RS256', publicKey)` and returns `false` for malformed tokens.
  - `updateAuthenticatedUsers()` passes `algorithms: ['RS256']`.
  - `denyAll()` pins HS256 for its random secret.
  - `authorize()` sets `allowInsecureKeySizes: true`, because jsonwebtoken 9 refuses to sign RS256 with the current 1024-bit key. This option can come out once the key is rotated to 2048+ bits (key handling is being moved to env config separately, sfind-c8ff9653). This is the only line touched near the private key.
- `routes/passkey.ts`: ceremony-token verification passes `algorithms: ['HS256']`. Removed the stale jsonwebtoken@0.4.0 comment (v9 still runs the callback synchronously for a string secret).
- `routes/verify.ts`: the `jwtUnsignedChallenge` / `jwtForgedChallenge` detection now checks the signature with `jws.verify(token, <alg>, publicKey)` directly. It still spots forgery attempts but no longer depends on the auth library accepting them. It only marks a challenge as solved and never grants access.
- Tests: new `verify` / `isAuthorized` unit tests check that `none` and HS256-with-public-key tokens are rejected (401) and genuine RS256 tokens are accepted. The basket API test now expects 401 for both forged token types.

Verified locally (Node 24): `npm run test:server` (all passing), `npm run test:api` (all passing), `tsc --noEmit`, and ESLint on the changed files. The RSN was not run: no changed lines are inside `vuln-code-snippet` blocks.

Resolved or fixed issue: none

### AI Tool Disclosure

- [ ] My contribution does not include any AI-generated content
- [x] My contribution includes AI-generated content, as disclosed below:
    - AI Tools: `Devin`
    - LLMs and versions: `Devin (Cognition AI)`
    - Prompts: `Remediate code scan finding: JWT verification does not pin the algorithm; pin RS256 everywhere, upgrading express-jwt/jsonwebtoken as needed, scoped to verification.`

### Affirmation

- [x] My code follows the [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) guidelines

author: gilbert09
body:
## Problem

- A Stripe connection whose token refresh is rejected once can stay broken, also after the cause of the rejection goes away.
- Stripe keeps the answer to an idempotent request for 24 hours, and sends that answer again for each request with the same key.
- The refresh key is a hash of the refresh token only, so each retry of that token gets the saved rejection back.
- The sync fails until the key expires, or until the customer connects again.

## Changes

- After Stripe answers a refresh with a 4xx, the next retry uses a new `Idempotency-Key`. Stripe then checks the token again.
- A retry after a lost response, a 5xx, a 409 or a 429 keeps the same key. Stripe can roll the token in those cases, and the replay still recovers the rolled tokens.
- A `stripe_refresh_key_round` counter in `config` records the key round. A successful refresh or a reconnect removes it.
- Round 0 is the old key, so a retry that is in progress at deploy time keeps its replay.
- Connections that are broken this way recover by themselves at most two retries after deploy. Nothing else changes for users.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** the existing lost-response test (`test_stripe_refresh_retry_after_lost_response_replays_the_same_request`) is now one parameterized test for each kind of first failure. The `rejected` and `rejected_twice` cases fail on master, because the key does not change there. The other cases guard against a key change that loses rolled tokens.

- Ran the Stripe tests in `posthog/models/test/integration/test_oauth.py` locally.
- Not run: the wider backend suites. CI runs them.
- Not checked against Stripe: the replay of a saved 4xx comes from the Stripe idempotency documentation.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5

**Skills:** `/writing-tests`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

- No duplicate: a search for open PRs on Stripe refresh idempotency found none.
- Public artifact: the test data is invented. Nothing from production is in the diff or this description.

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Decisions:** the key changes only on a 4xx answer. A 5xx can come after Stripe rolls the token, so a key change there can lose the new token.
- **Read closely:** `_stripe_rejected_the_refresh` and the failure branch of `token_refresh_patch` in `posthog/models/integration/oauth.py`.

</details>

author: danjboyd
body:
MSI provenance now records each DLL's and EXE's PDB identity. This is the other Roadmap 18C follow-up, next to the DMG one in #129.

- **`Get-GpPeCodeViewId`** (in `scripts/lib/core.ps1`):
  - parses PE32 and PE32+ files: the DOS header, PE header, optional header, the debug data directory mapped through the section table, and the CodeView (`RSDS`) entry;
  - needs no dumpbin or llvm-readobj;
  - returns `guid`, `age`, `pdb` and `symbolKey`. `pdb` is the file name only, because the full path is the build machine's. `symbolKey` is GUID+age, as symbol servers and crash dumps index a PDB.
- **Provenance entries** gain `peCodeView` only for PE files that have the record. AppImage provenance, and MSI entries for DLLs without debug info, are unchanged.
- **Checked against .NET's `PEReader.ReadCodeViewDebugDirectoryData`** on 25 real DLLs, which all match. The one textual difference was the reference keeping a full Windows PDB path, which this code reduces to the file name.
- **Unknown:** whether the MSYS2 clang64 GNUstep DLLs carry a CodeView record. lld writes one with `--build-id` or `-g`. If they don't, those entries simply have no key, and no test requires one.
- **Depends on #129:** this branch now contains #129 via a merge commit (9026383), with the overlapping lines resolved. Merge #129 first; this PR's own diff is then just the CodeView change.

## Tests
`tests/shared/Provenance.Tests.ps1` builds synthetic PE32+ and PE32 DLLs. They cover a Windows and a Unix PDB path, a debug entry that isn't CodeView, a non-PE `MZ` file and an ELF file. The test checks the provenance key's presence and absence, and that no build path reaches the JSON. Ran locally: 9/9 pass.

Draft: not for merge without Dan's go.

author: bitwalt
body:
`RgbLibWasmAdapter.sendAsset` now returns plain values: `{ txid, batchTransferIdx, entropy }`, with `entropy` as a decimal string.

rgb-lib-wasm 1.0.0-beta.4 added `entropy` to the send result. It is a random u64, so it reaches JS as a BigInt, and the adapter spread it into its own result. A host that passes the result through `chrome.runtime` messaging (the extension does) cannot serialize it, so a send that was broadcast came back to the popup as a failed reply. Found in the live Mutinynet run of 1.0.0-beta.84.

A unit test pins the shape and checks it survives a JSON round trip.

author: pvanhouten
body:
**Team index:** each ESPN feed's team list is loaded at startup (daily refresh) and used to pick which scoreboards to fetch for a lookup or names-only search. Typical fetches: NBA 1, Premier League 3, NCAA 5 (was ~38). No index loaded = old behaviour.

**Single-team matching:** a channel name or program title that is one known team plus optional hint words (`Wrexham`, `Wrexham AFC | Live`, `Wrexham | Championship`, `Wrexham FA Cup`, `Miami NBA`) shows that team's live game, else the one nearest in time. Anything else in the segment disqualifies it (so `CNN | Miami Weather Report` does not match), the description is never used, and a hint that contradicts the team's leagues means no match. The client no longer pre-filters on vs/@/at (script now `?v=10`).

25 tests pass.

author: mondaychen
body:
## Problem

The nightly CI has failed since 2026-11-04. There are two causes:

1. `ubuntu-latest` now resolves to Ubuntu 26.04. Playwright 1.58.1 does not support that OS, so `playwright install --with-deps chromium` stops with `Playwright does not support chromium on ubuntu26.04-x64`.
2. On `ubuntu-24.04`, `--with-deps` runs apt. The runners cannot resolve `azure.archive.ubuntu.com` at this time, so the step stalls for approximately 10 minutes and then fails.

## Fix

- Pin the `check` and `live-provider` jobs to `ubuntu-24.04`.
- Install Chromium without `--with-deps`. The runner image already has the shared libraries that Chromium needs. The flag only added font packages, and no test uses screenshots.

Remove the pin after the repository moves to a Playwright version that supports Ubuntu 26.04.

author: photom
body:
CI on main and on #14 failed at `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`. The job log showed the cause: `apt` could not fetch Playwright's font packages because `azure.archive.ubuntu.com` did not resolve (`Temporary failure resolving`). That is an outage on the runner side, and it has since recovered. The last run on this branch is green, including `test:browser`.

This PR runs the browser download and the system packages as two steps:

```yaml
- run: npx playwright install chromium
- run: npx playwright install-deps chromium
```

The behavior is unchanged. If it breaks again, the step that fails shows which half broke, even when the job logs are not available. An earlier commit pinned `ubuntu-24.04`. That did not help, so the pin is gone.

## Summary

#196 made an aged admission waiter reserve its bytes on both axes. When live memory could not admit the waiter (live + claim above half the slice), it froze every newer, smaller request until live memory fell. On 2026-11-11 a 32 GiB soundness-cache compile held the #188 gate's 14.2 GiB compile from 10:05:37 to 10:15:39 local, with bookings over the cap and about 70 GiB of live anonymous memory.

## Change (in `admission_memory.py`)

- **Booking axis:** newer, smaller requests leave the aged waiter's bytes free, as before. This keeps the waiter's place once bookings drain.
- **Live axis:** newer requests are no longer held. They keep the existing half-slice rule (`live + request <= slice_max / 2`) and the 16 GiB ceiling.
- **The waiter's own live bound:** an aged waiter may be admitted when `live + claim <= slice_max - fixed headroom` (20 GiB, the same headroom as the booking cap), above the small-request ceiling, and within the MemAvailable budget.
- **Second bound:** after `ZESU_ADMISSION_BLOCK_BOUND_S` (default 900 s) past aging, the waiter stops reserving bookings. It keeps its place and its looser live bound, and the projection logs `admission waiter … no longer blocks newer requests`.

## Count each byte once

The utilization check at 15:22Z saw 323 GiB booked in `admission-summary`, against 162 GiB of `memory_claim_bytes` in `coqc-reservations` and 135 GiB live. A read-only breakdown of the live ledger located the cause:

- **Queued waiters (the main excess).** #196 reserved the sum of every aged waiter that was older and larger than the request. At about 15:27Z, 40 queued compiles (109 GiB in total, holding no memory) added 46.9 GiB to a 2.4 GiB request's projection and 35.0 GiB to a 4 GiB request's. Both were refused on both axes. The summary publishes that projection, so the queued bytes showed up as bookings. Now only the head of the queue (the oldest qualifying waiter) reserves; the others get their turn in order.
- **Batch holds.** A hold booked its aggregate's anonymous memory plus its running compiles' claims. That anonymous memory already contains those compiles. A hold now books the anonymous memory outside its running compiles, plus their claims. The aggregate stays the cap for its members, not an extra booking.
- Gate claims were already counted once (`sum_gate_compiles`: own claim + member claims, members set to 0).
- The remaining gap between the ledger's compile claims and the reservation files is growth-raised claims (1.5x RSS). Those are real bookings, counted once.

Live-ledger numbers (read-only projections, `ScopeReader` on the live cgroups):

| Snapshot | Request | main (#196) | this branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| ~15:27Z, 40 waiters | 2.4 GiB | 254.2 GiB accounted (46.9 GiB reserved for waiters), refused | first commit (second bound, not yet head-only): 223.4 GiB (16.0 GiB reserved), admitted on live memory. Head-only reserves at most that 16.0 GiB, over 207.4 GiB of real claims (this snapshot was not re-measured, because the queue had cleared) |
| ~15:30Z, queue empty | 2.4 GiB | 235.4 GiB accounted | 227.9 GiB accounted (holds counted once, -7.5 GiB) |

## Why this form is sound

- **No starvation on the live axis.** A small request is admitted on live memory only while `live <= slice_max/2 - request`. At any such live level the waiter's bound `live <= slice_max - 20 GiB - claim` also holds for every claim up to half the slice minus 20 GiB (74 GiB on the 188 GiB slice). So a newer small request can never take a live-memory gap that the waiter could not also take. The waiter is re-evaluated at every release wake.
- **No freeze.** Nothing is held on the live axis. On bookings, a waiter that cannot fit holds others for at most the second bound.
- **Safety unchanged.** The live bound is the booking cap's own headroom applied to measured live memory. The per-job fence, the slice cap, the guard's watch, and the 200 GiB account cap do not change. A job that grows past the slice is still stopped by them.
- **Rejected alternative:** a waiter that keeps the live axis blocked but only until a second bound. It still idles the machine for that whole bound whenever the waiter cannot fit, which is the throughput loss the user wants to avoid.

## Tests

- `test_a_waiter_that_live_memory_cannot_admit_does_not_freeze_small_requests`: a 32 GiB aged waiter that neither axis can admit (bookings 10 GiB below the cap, live memory 25 GiB below it).
  - 4 GiB requests wait on bookings only until the second bound, then pass.
  - Beside the waiter, they pass on live memory whenever live memory is below half the slice.
  - The waiter keeps its place, and live memory admits it once memory frees.
- The earlier starvation test still passes. The 32 GiB waiter is admitted as soon as it ages (step 5), and the 4 GiB requests are never held.
- The young, dead or smaller waiter test and the correctness-gate waiter-record test are unchanged and pass.
- `test_only_the_head_of_the_waiter_queue_reserves`: three aged waiters; only the oldest one larger than the request reserves.
- `test_ledger_total_is_live_claims_plus_unspent_aggregate`: two running compiles (4 + 6 GiB claims, 1 GiB live each) in one batch hold. The booked total is exactly 10 GiB at 2 GiB anonymous memory, and 13 GiB at 5 GiB (3 GiB of the aggregate outside the compiles). The retained-hold test now expects 4 GiB (2 GiB claim + 2 GiB outside it) instead of 5 GiB.
- **Gates on the exact head `1dd84c73a8937a09d51aa8fc97a2bbf9ec3063ef`** (main `591bfaf17`, unchanged since): `make check-fast` at default parallelism is green (gate RESULT success, 1540 s under load): tools 2902 OK (12 skipped), harness 2144 OK, tools/block 146 OK, stock manifest 18 OK, regen 12 OK, stock platform 86 OK, Evidence 309 OK.

author: jdfalk
body:
Linear re-cut of #4595 (dequeued as `merge_conflict` on `scripts/deadcode-baseline.txt` after F7-01 merged; its branch had merge commits the REBASE queue cannot replay). Content = #4595 head `f6e8ce5a5`, baseline reconciled with main. Review and approval carried from #4595.

---

Platform-core **F2-04** (T3): core's task scheduler and the schedule-parity harness, both dark. Brief: `docs/agent-tasks/platform-core/F2-04-scheduler-schedule-parity-harness.md`.

## What this adds

- **`core/internal/scheduler`**, written fresh against `tasks.ClockStore` and the executor's `StartIn`/`WriteRuns`. No code is copied from HEAD's `internal/scheduler`.
  - One poll goroutine (`Run`/`Stop`) and one durable clock per scheduled kind. A due fire stages the clock advance and the run insert into **one batch**, committed by `WriteRuns`. A losing concurrent poll gets `ErrClockConflict`, which means no fire.
  - Timings: `Every`, `DailyAt` and a 5-field `Cron` (Vixie grammar: `a/n`, DOW 7 = Sunday, DOM/DOW OR), parsed by the new layer-0 `core/internal/schedspec`, which `core/tasks` also uses to validate values at config load. Times are evaluated in `core.tasks.timezone`. A skipped wall time fires at the transition instant. A repeated wall time fires once, at its first occurrence.
  - Clock rules:
    - first sight of an enabled kind seeds and does not fire; a kind first seen **disabled** is not seeded at all and waits one period after it is enabled (HEAD parity)
    - `Coalesce` fires once and counts the missed instants; `SkipMissed` fires only when the latest instant came due while this process was up (at or after its previous poll, or its boot), so a delayed poll is not downtime
    - disable stamps `GateClosedAt`; on re-enable the kind's `Missed` policy applies (05-tasks 1140): `Coalesce` fires once, due at the open edge, with nothing counted missed; `SkipMissed` fires only for a fresh instant
    - a closed `When` gate advances the clock and starts no run
    - a held kind is not polled
    - a clock read error skips the kind (`schedule_errors`)
    - a start the executor **refuses** (permission, mode, priority, plan rule, unknown or held kind) commits the advance alone, so the kind doesn't retry every poll; any other start error (storage I/O) aborts the batch, leaves the clock, and the next poll fires
  - Fold: the executor's. `StartIn` applies the kind's `DedupePolicy` (by default a queued or running run of the kind and mode with identical params) and returns `Existing`; the scheduler has no fold rule of its own.
  - `Boot` fires `OnStart` once and stamps the clock in the same batch.
  - Maintenance windows: `WindowDefinition(name, run)` and `RunWindow`. A window's clock always holds an opening's start instant. A window fires once per opening and starts its members one after another in (`Order`, kind) order, each a child of the window run with trigger `window`. Gated and folded members are skipped. A scheduled run stops starting members once the window closes; a manual run runs them all.
  - `ValidateSchedules`: the registration check (namespace, declared, `ScheduleConfig`-typed, declaring owner, one key per kind, `Every` only for `core.outbox.relay`, Live/Preview rules). All refusals are reported, sorted.
- **`core/tasks/window.go`**: `WindowNightly = "core.window.nightly"` (the one declaration), `WindowKind`, `WindowName`, `NightlyWindow`.
- **`core/tasks/taskstest/schedule`**: the schedule-parity harness for F5-14 (`TestScheduleParity_AllDefinitions`, `TestCutover_NoCatchUpStorm`). It runs a real executor that is never started, over pebble on a MemFS, with a fake clock and Steps (`Clocks` import, `Edit`, `Finish`, `Held`, `Boot`, `NoPoll`). It returns the event sequence.
- **Core config**: the 14 `tasks.ScheduleConfig` keys in per-owner `…schedules` sections, and the `core.tasks.windows` map with default `nightly` = 1/4/true.

## Plan (as executed)

1. Base-state greps. 2. Math: cron, daily, `wallInstant`, then the clock `decide`, then window rules. 3. The poll loop and the batch commit path. 4. `ValidateSchedules`. 5. The harness. 6. Config keys. 7. Tests, gates, mutant sweep.

## Decisions (judgement calls; I took the recommended option each time)

1. **`tasks.ScheduleConfig` encodes itself as one JSON value** (`core/tasks/schedule.go`, outside the brief's file list). Config's leaf walk descends into plain structs, so registration failed as written (`no default for key "cleanup.every"`). 05-config's "ScheduleConfig is an ordinary live object key" needs this.
2. **F2-09's `core/kernel/core_sections_test.go` edited.** Its walk now treats a `json.Marshaler` struct as one key. `TestCoreSections_NoLaterRowsKeys` now allows schedule keys only in schedules sections. Schedule keys are exempt from the storage `ProtectOperator` rule. Without these edits, F2-09's tests fail by construction once the keys exist.
3. Defaults helpers live in **`core/kernel/core_schedule_defaults.go`**, so the brief's `grep -c tasks.ScheduleConfig` on `core_sections.go` stays at exactly 14.
4. **`storage.compact` defaults to `{enabled: true, window: "nightly"}`**, with no operator protection (it's a schedule key).
5. **Window kind constant in `core/tasks`, definition built in the scheduler** (`WindowDefinition`, with a run closure the kernel late-binds). Starting members via `rc.Enqueue` would stamp the core actor, and module members would be refused. Members go through `StartIn` instead, so each runs as its own module's system actor.
6. **New `//tasklint:constructor` allowlist entry, for review**: `core/archtest/tasklint/core_test.go` adds `internal/scheduler.WindowDefinition`. That file's comment says "A new entry is reviewed here." The alternative is registering the window kind where tasklint can see a `Registrar` call, and that is F2-16's kernel wiring.
7. **Window due rule: compare local dates against the opening's date, and the clock holds an opening's start.** A window fires when `localDate(LastDue) < localDate(opening)`. This matches HEAD's `hasRunToday`, and the cutover's import of `LastDue` as local midnight of the day HEAD ran it (so HEAD's day-D run is not repeated in D's opening). **Correction (review round 1):** the first version stamped `LastDue = now` on a fire and `now` on a seed, which was NOT safe for a window that wraps midnight (23-4: a fire at 00:30 stamped day 2 and the whole next night was skipped; a seed at noon never fired the 23:00 opening). The clock now holds an opening instant: a fire stamps the opening it fired for; a first sight stamps the start of the latest opening at or before now. A window first seen inside an opening does not run that opening (no boot stampede).
8. Fold is the executor's (see Fold above). A queued manual run with **different** params no longer swallows a scheduled fire (zero `DedupePolicy` needs identical params); `waiting_deps` and `stopping` runs are not fold targets, per the executor's spec.
9. **A hash change keeps `LastDue`**, as HEAD does. An imported clock with an empty hash continues; it is not re-seeded.
10. `SkipMissed` freshness bound = the process's previous poll (or its boot), held in memory; the one-poll bound remains only when `Poll` runs on a scheduler that never booted.
11. Only an executor refusal (`refused()`: `ErrUnknownKind`, `ErrHeld`, `ErrNotPermitted`, `ErrPlanRequired`, `ErrInvalidPriority`, plan/approval sentinels, `tasks.ErrModeUnset`, `tasks.ErrOutsideEffects`) commits the advance alone and adds to `schedule_errors`; a storage error keeps the fire. **Judgement call:** a definition's static `Params` that fail to decode, or a `Dedupe.Key/Merge` error, carry no sentinel, so they are treated as transient: retried and counted at every poll until the definition is fixed. The alternative (a sentinel in the executor) is outside this row.
12. Metrics go through an interface that matches `executor.ScheduleMetrics`, so the instruments follow the executor's switch.
13. The fake zone for DST tests is a hand-built TZif v2 w

## Purpose
Convert the one-tomato/seed principle into a reproducible, finite CANO simulation rather than a claim of real autonomous replication.

## Evidence
- One virtual founder; descendants can continue producing descendants after founder removal at simulated tick 4.
- Equal simulated energy inputs (44 arbitrary units) over eight ticks: solar-only had **2 dormant ticks**, solar+water+thermal **0 dormant ticks** (12-unit storage cap).
- Lower-energy solar-only control (20 units) had 3 dormant ticks.
- Checkpoint serialize/restore readback, SHA-256 accidental-corruption check, energy conservation ledger, source validation, capacity, explicit authorization and extinction behavior.
- **Local Python 3.13 unittest: 10/10 passing.** CI verified: [Core tests #43072281176](https://github.com/aydinefe2025-svg/Benim-AI-asistan-m/actions/runs/43072281176) Ubuntu and Windows unittest jobs both SUCCESS; [Public research checks #43072281231](https://github.com/aydinefe2025-svg/Benim-AI-asistan-m/actions/runs/43072281231) SUCCESS. Live/physical validation not performed.
- Reproduction: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_seed_ecosystem.py -v` and `PYTHONPATH=. python scripts/cano_seed_lab_demo.py`

## Safety and limits
Pure in-memory deterministic model; no real harvesting hardware, AI process spawning, network discovery, payments or production DB. Units are hypothetical; energy/time profiles are not measured watts or physical performance forecasts. SHA-256 is NOT authenticated offsite backup. No auto-deployment.
Preserve P0 production backup priorities and review before any integration.

## Tracking
- Source: CANO main requirements & issue #95
- Canonical evidence archive: `/Research-Evidence/CANO-Operations-2026-11-10/CANO_seed_energy_lab_2026-11-11.zip`
- Tests/doc/report in this PR.

## 2026-11-11: reuse archived research rather than inventing energy credits
- New `core/archived_energy_bridge.py`, `data/cano_research_bridge_evidence.json`, `tests/test_archived_energy_bridge.py`, integration in `scripts/cano_seed_lab_demo.py`, detailed `docs/CANO_ARCHIVED_RESEARCH_TO_ENGINEERING_2026-11-11.md`.
- Reuses archived DOI findings: 0.42 mW modeled piezo peak; 20.29 µW/cm² artificial-sweat lab result; thermal-mechanical actuation cannot be assumed electrical; Tesla motor/induction is transfer, not generation.
- With **illustrative 10 cm²** area, optimistic 0.6229 mW *combined* peaks from different conditions; 24 h hypothetical 14.9496 mWh; low-duty sensor 0.0595 mW candidate pending field measurements; 3 W computer exceeds the combined selected figures. No positive field guarantee.
- Reuses earlier negative Organism Lab adaptation/transfer findings to block unsupported autonomous-improvement claims (not model-weight learning).
- Local TDD: 8 initial missing-feature RED, 1 integration RED, then 19/19 local unittests GREEN; archival exact file hashes and outputs in Library.
- Library: `/Research-Evidence/CANO-Operations-2026-11-10/CANO_research_reuse_2026-11-11.zip`, SHA256 `c84ec501d9df491cec7fc47f7cbb9a86723bca6cf7059bfef6ca0820d9c9ca53`.
- Reuse code is in this draft PR only: no merge/deploy/physical claims; latest CI status must be checked separately.

## Báo cáo thay đổi Sprint 5 (05/11 – 12/11/2026)

Sprint 4 đã chốt nghiệm thu ngày 04/11/2026 (PR #37). Sprint 5 gồm các PR #38 – #43 và #45, đưa vào `main` bằng PR #44.
Báo cáo đầy đủ: `docs/08-sprints/sprint-5/BAO_CAO_TONG_KET_NGHIEM_THU_SPRINT_5.md`

### 1. Rà soát mã nguồn (PR #38, OISMS-47)
- Hoàn thiện Clean Architecture đợt 1 – 4: tách khóa và transaction sang Infrastructure, đưa chuyển trạng thái đơn vào entity, tách luồng đơn hàng.
- Backend chạy đúng sau Caddy (ForwardedHeaders), sửa thứ tự CORS.
- Sửa lỗi giỏ POS đa đơn vị, phân trang, hiện mã đơn trên hóa đơn.
- Docker/CI: healthcheck Redis, `npm ci`. Thêm tài liệu ERD.

### 2. Giả lập đơn sàn qua webhook (PR #39, FR-SIM-01)
- Owner tạo kết nối sàn và nhận secret trên Admin (màn Kết nối sàn).
- App giả lập riêng (cổng 5175): bắn đơn Shopee/TikTok Shop/Lazada, gửi lại, đổi nội dung, bắn tới 200 đơn đồng thời, chọn sản phẩm theo secret.

### 3. Thanh toán VietQR (CS-05)
- Owner quản lý tài khoản ngân hàng nhận tiền (bảng `payment_accounts`).
- POS sinh mã VietQR theo tài khoản của doanh nghiệp.

### 4. Tách POS khỏi Admin (PR #40, OISMS-50)
- Chỉ còn một ứng dụng POS (`pos-app`, cổng 5174). Admin `/pos` chuyển hướng sang POS.
- Tồn kho realtime trên POS; sửa hóa đơn, khổ in, cache PWA.
- Sửa BF-036: đăng nhập không dùng tenant của token cũ.

### 5. Trả hàng từ khách (PR #41, CS-01)
- Phiếu trả gắn đơn gốc, xác nhận hoặc hủy. Chỉ Owner và Staff được thao tác.
- Hoàn tồn đúng giá vốn lúc bán, chống trùng khi bấm nhiều lần.
- Báo cáo và Tổng quan trừ hàng trả. Admin có trang `/returns`.

### 6. Trợ lý OISMS và gợi ý nhập hàng (PR #42, FR-AI-02, FR-AI-01)
- Chatbot hỏi đáp số liệu cho Owner và Staff, chỉ đọc. Staff không hỏi được doanh thu.
- Dùng Groq/Gemini gói miễn phí nên hạn mức thấp (Gemini khoảng 20 câu/ngày).
- Mở lại tab Gợi ý nhập hàng. SKU hết hàng luôn được cảnh báo.

### 7. Hangfire

body:
## Qué

Permite elegir **qué indexers de Prowlarr usa ZascArr**, sin desactivarlos en Prowlarr ni afectar a Sonarr/Radarr/otras apps.

- Ajustes → Prowlarr → **«Indexers para ZascArr»**: botón que carga la lista real de Prowlarr y muestra **multiselección** con nombre y categorías.
- Se guarda como lista de IDs; **vacío = todos** (comportamiento actual).
- `ProwlarrClient.search()` envía `indexerIds`; el orquestador solo pasa los elegidos.
- Los indexers **apagados en Prowlarr no se ofrecen**; si Prowlarr no está configurado o no responde, el panel lo explica.
- No se modifica Prowlarr, no se guardan secretos en la selección y no cambia la búsqueda agregada.

## Por qué

Con 78 indexers activos (Prowlarr compartido), ZascArr consultaba todos en cada búsqueda. Prowlarr ya soporta `indexerIds`; ahora se puede dejar solo Internet Archive/Knaben/MyAnonaMouse para cómics sin tocar las demás apps.

## Pruebas

- Cliente: lista de indexers y `indexerIds` repetidos en la URL.
- Orquestador: solo los IDs elegidos se pasan; con lista vacía no se envía el parámetro.
- Ajustes: carga de checkboxes, omisión de apagados y guardado.

`ContextAssembler`'s four per-entry resolvers now read as short lists of steps, each calling named private helpers:

Behaviour is unchanged: the same text blocks in the same order, the same `findAll` configuration, the same log lines at the same levels, and the same skip-and-continue handling for every malformed entry. body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13700

### Proposed Changes:

`Pipeline.stream()` sent the end-of-stream marker from a `finally` inside the pipeline task. When `aclose()` cancels that task before its first step, the `finally` never runs, so a consumer of the handle waits forever. The marker is now sent from a done callback on the task, which fires on every completion, including cancellation before start; the consumer then gets the cancellation.

### How did you test it?

- New `test_aclose_before_pipeline_starts_ends_iteration`: fails on main `bbe4efe` (TimeoutError), passes with the fix.

- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` on the changed files: clean. Full suite and `hatch run test:types` not run.

The marker now arrives one loop iteration after the task finishes instead of just before; consumers already await the finished task on it, so ordering of chunks is unchanged.

author: cboettig
body:
`fetch_stac_catalog` read every node as a Collection and stopped two levels below the root. Three things followed:

- **Catalog-typed group nodes failed to parse**, along with everything beneath them. That blocks data-workflows#762, which retypes group nodes as Catalogs.
- **Anything deeper than two levels was dropped**: 75 datasets in the NRP catalog, including `woa23-temperature-0m`, `megamove-corridors` and the SWAP layers.
- **Relative hrefs resolved against the server's working directory.** This third cause, not in #433 as filed, was found by geo-query-wasm. Portolan catalogs have no `self` link and only relative hrefs, so the St. Louis source.coop mirror (`https://data.source.coop/tge-labs/st-louis-open-data-mirror/catalog.json`) loaded 0 of 12 collections.

## What changes

- **One read point**, `_read_stac_object`, dispatches on `"type"`. Link and asset hrefs are joined to the URL each document was fetched from, with no network access. pystac's own resolution fetches the `root` catalog, and a mirror's root link points back at the original host. Absolute hrefs are kept as written, so globs survive.
- **`_walk_catalog`** follows child links to any depth in the existing bounded pool, with the retry pass, a visited-href set (one node has two parents) and a depth cap of 6 (`STAC_MAX_DEPTH`).
- **Groups.** A Catalog, or a Collection with children and no queryable asset, is a group. `browse_stac_catalog` lists groups as headings with their datasets indented beneath. A group's details list every dataset under it, and its `get_collection` dict nests its children.
- **Short ids.** `wards` finds `government/wards` only when exactly one id ends that way. Otherwise the answer lists the full ids.
- **Inline catalogs** accept the same depth and node types.

## Checked against

| Catalog | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| NRP `public-data/stac` | 390 entries | 465 datasets in 70 groups, 0 failures, 3–6 s; same set as an independent crawl |
| GLEN source.coop mirror | — | 140 datasets in 21 groups; 1 genuine 404 (`nlcd-2024` missing from the mirror) |
| St. Louis (Portolan) | 0 of 12 | 67 datasets in 12 groups |

geo-query-wasm's `stac.js` produces identical listings, `get_stac_details` markdown and `get_collection` dicts on all three of the trees it compared (GLEN mirror, St. Louis, the fixture). `tests/fixtures/portolan` comes from SchmidtDSE/geo-query-wasm#15, so both test suites use the same tree. `tests/test_stac_walk.py` runs on real files, with a tree four levels deep, a link cycle, the depth cap, and a root link to an unreachable host. The existing mock-based tests go through the new read point. 525 tests pass.

## Worth knowing

- **The browse listing grows from 33 kB to 50 kB**, because of the 75 restored datasets plus group headings.
- **Two NRP collections share the id `coral-reefs`**: a group and a dataset in `public-hawaii`. Only the first is listed. That needs fixing in the catalog data, not here.

Closes #433.

author: tvanreenen
body:
## Why this change

The existing GitHub repository has moved from the maintainer's personal namespace to `tvr-works`. GitHub preserves repository history and redirects ordinary links after a transfer, but PyPI's OIDC publishing identity and repository metadata must name the new owner directly.

This PR completes the source-controlled part of that cutover. It updates canonical links, binds each upload job to a restricted GitHub environment, and moves eligible Linux validation jobs onto the organization runner that will build the distributions.

| Area | Added | Removed |
|---|---:|---:|
| Workflows and runner lint configuration | 14 | 4 |
| Documentation and package metadata | 23 | 67 |
| **Total** | **37** | **71** |

## Repository ownership

The existing repository was transferred rather than copied. Its immutable repository ID remains `1069496689`, and the transfer preserved the public visibility, `main` history, 9 tags, 9 GitHub releases, 31 pull requests, and Actions settings. The old GitHub API path resolves to the new repository, while this clone now uses `https://github.com/tvr-works/numpy-vector-store.git` directly.

Maintained links in `pyproject.toml`, the README clone command, and the changelog release-history link now use the canonical organization URL. The distribution remains `numpy-vector-store`, the import remains `numpy_vector_store`, and no package version, release file, tag, or runtime API changes.

## Publishing trust boundary

The PyPI and TestPyPI projects remain owned by the individual `tvanreenen` account. No PyPI organization, shared login, additional human owner, billing relationship, or ownership transfer is introduced.

Each top-level upload job now names the repository-scoped environment that is part of its replacement Trusted Publisher identity:

| Index | Workflow | Environment | Repository policy |
|---|---|---|---|
| TestPyPI | `publish-testpypi.yml` | `testpypi` | `main` branch only |
| PyPI | `publish-pypi.yml` | `pypi` | tags matching `v*` only |

The environments have no secret and no required reviewer, so the solo maintainer cannot deadlock publication. OIDC still provides a short-lived upload token. Package construction and clean wheel/sdist installation tests remain in the unprivileged `Checks` workflow; the GitHub-hosted upload jobs still only download and publish the verified artifact.

Both replacement publisher records are present on their indexes alongside the previous personal-namespace records. The old TestPyPI record will be removed after a successful qualification upload. The old production record stays temporarily because production uploads are out of scope here; it can be removed after a future authorized semantic release proves the new environment-bound identity.

## Runner qualification

The four eligible Linux jobs now use `blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404`, the established Linux label already running successfully in `tvr-works`. The new actionlint configuration declares that custom ephemeral runner label so local and hosted workflow linting remain strict.

Windows coverage remains on `windows-latest`. The PyPI and TestPyPI OIDC upload jobs remain on GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest`, keeping the short-lived publishing credential outside the third-party build runner.

This PR's hosted checks are the repository-specific qualification for Blacksmith access. The branch should not merge unless all supported Python, minimum NumPy, distribution, static-analysis, and Windows jobs complete normally under the transferred repository.

## Maintainer documentation

`RELEASING.md` now describes the final ownership model rather than requiring an unrelated PyPI organization. It records the exact environment and ref restrictions, the individual package-index owner, the Blacksmith/GitHub-hosted runner boundary, the transferred-repository identity, and the production qualification that must wait for a real release.

## User impact

There is no runtime behavior, public API, dependency range, package version, install command, archive format, or persisted-data change. Users following repository links will reach `tvr-works`; GitHub also redirects the previous URL.

## Verification

Completed locally:

- `uv lock --check`
- `actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml`
- `uv run --locked ruff check .`
- `uv run --locked ruff format --check .`
- `uv run --locked mypy src/ benchmarks/ tools/`
- `uv run --locked pytest` with 340 tests passing
- `git diff --check`

External configuration verified before opening this PR:

- transferred repository ID, visibility, default branch, tags, releases, pull requests, redirect, and Actions permissions;
- `testpypi` environment restricted to branch `main`;
- `pypi` environment restricted to tags matching `v*`;

body:
## Falha observada e correção

O bootstrap autorizado do Execução parou na preparação, antes de gerar plano ou executar Terraform, na tentativa 2 da execução 43070106631. A consulta sqs list-queues em conta sem filas retornou exit 0 com stdout vazio; JSON.parse falhou com Unexpected end of JSON input. Reproduzido em leitura no laboratório atual.

O wrapper agora normaliza somente stdout vazio de sqs list-queues concluído com sucesso para QueueUrls vazio. execFileSync continua propagando falha de processo antes de interpretar saída; outros serviços, JSON malformado e estruturas SQS inválidas seguem bloqueados. Filas do projeto continuam impedindo bootstrap sem cache. Não transforma AccessDenied/token expirado em ausência.

Mantém TERRAFORM_ACTION=destroy e acrescenta somente comentário de retentativa no controle versionado. Isso permite que o push deste PR satisfaça a verificação existente de alteração do próprio controle, sem remover ou enfraquecer o guardrail. Demais alterações são apenas parser e teste inline; nenhum recurso, contrato, código da aplicação ou pasta nova.

AWS_DEPLOY_ENABLED=false foi restaurado após a falha e permanece assim. Nenhum recurso foi criado/removido, nenhum plano de destroy foi aplicado e nenhum cache de state foi produzido pela tentativa que falhou.

Gabriel realiza o merge. Depois, a retentativa do mesmo bootstrap já autorizado deverá usar o novo commit, com nova conferência do inventário/state e restauração garantida do bloqueio ao final. Não inclui provisionamento/retorno a apply. Se houver recursos ou state divergentes, interromper para análise.

## Validação

17 testes Node inline do Execução e nove da referência API aprovados; sintaxe Node e actionlint conferidos (sem shellcheck/pyflakes locais). Teste de regressão cobre saída vazia, JSON válido, erros de acesso/autenticação, saída vazia em outro serviço, JSON/estrutura inválidos e fila do projeto existente. Diff/gate de estrutura aprovados. ## MELI-12 — contrato offline para a primeira fonte oficial de preço

**Objetivo:** preparar a integração com `GET /items/{id}/sale_price?context=channel_marketplace`, sem tratar a autorização do usuário como autorização do Mercado Livre para consultar anúncios de terceiros. **Nenhuma coleta externa ou credencial de produção foi utilizada.**

- `src/historico/mercadolivre-sale-price.ts`: parser rigoroso do JSON oficial, com URL HTTPS fixa e GET para canal marketplace. Não implementa `fetch` de rede nem está registrado no `server.ts`.

- Erros e exceções de transporte sanitizados; sem log de token, corpo privado ou metadados de promoção.
- **Não confunde preço de canal com Pix/cartão, nem confirma estoque ou desconto.** O resultado permanece `modalidadePagamento:nao_informada`, `disponibilidade:indeterminada`, `podePublicar:false`.

author: marc-aurele-besner
body:
## Problem

On Node 26 the multi-org orchestrator answers every `/o/:orgId/...` request with `503 org_unavailable` (`Illegal invocation`) when it is served by the real HTTP listener.

`multiOrgApp.ts` forwarded a request to an org's app with `new Request(url, c.req.raw)`. Behind the node adapter, `c.req.raw` is the adapter's lightweight stand-in for a `Request`: it has `Request.prototype` in its chain but is not a real `Request`. Node 26's `Request` constructor reads `init.duplex`, which on that object resolves to the `Request.prototype.duplex` getter, and the getter's brand check throws. Node 22 and 24 have no such getter, so the same code works there.

CI runs Node 26 but the multi-org tests only use `app.request`, which builds a real `Request` and never goes through the adapter. The orchestrator image is `node:26-bookworm-slim`, so the published image is affected.

## Change

- `forwardedRequest(url, incoming)` builds the forwarded request from named parts: method, headers, abort signal, and the incoming body stream itself (unread, `duplex: "half"`), with no body on GET/HEAD.
- `createHttpServer(handler)` in `httpListen.ts` is the one place the server process wraps a Fetch handler in the node adapter; `server.ts` uses it for all three modes.
- `multiOrgListener.test.ts` starts that listener on an ephemeral port and sends real requests: an org's health, a GET with a query, a JSON POST, a non-JSON POST, and a signed hook delivery with no bearer token. It also checks `forwardedRequest` directly for a streamed body that is not read early, GET/HEAD, and abort propagation. It is in the package's test list, so CI on Node 26 runs it.

No other place in the repo constructs a `Request` from another request object.

## Verification

- Without the fix the four listener tests fail on Node 26.12.1 with `503 org_unavailable` / `Illegal invocation` and pass on Node 22.23.2 and 24.18.1. The second commit on this branch is that state.
- With the fix, `multiOrgListener.test.ts` and `multiOrg.test.ts` pass on Node 22.23.2, 24.18.1 and 26.12.1.

body:
**Question (11 Nov):** if a holding has an average cost, why no Invested on date? Man Industries has a cost but no dates.

**Answer:** having an average cost doesn't mean the book has dates. A broker prints one average figure and no dates. HDFC Securities 3110320's trade report starts on 1 Apr 2026, after every purchase. But the dates **were** in the files. The 30 June review's "Transactions since inception" sheet (HDFC Bank block) has Man Industries: 60,000 @ ₹320 on 10 Jan 2025 and 4,57,317 @ ₹328 on 25 Jul 2025. The investment register has the second purchase. Cost recovery only read those rows for holdings with no cost.

**Change**
- `scripts/lib/reviewPurchaseDates.mjs` adds `Position.reviewPurchases`, a new Invested on source `review-lots`. It feeds the date column only; the statement's cost stays as printed. It applies five gates:
  1. The review block ties to its own Closing, matched first-in, first-out.
  2. The account's trade window opens by the day after that Closing and agrees with the review where the two overlap.
  3. The window's trades carry the lots to exactly the units held: 5,17,317 − 37,317 sold on 23 Sep = 4,80,000.
  4. Where the window ends before the holding's date, every unit must be long-term, both by these dates and by the broker's LONG TERM QTY. Any unit bought in the gap would show as short-term.
  5. The surviving lots' cost is within 0.5% of the statement's cost. Man Industries ₹15.726 Cr vs ₹15.727 Cr; Kingfa matches to the paisa.

- check-pages' independent `INVESTED_ON_BOOK` knows the new source.
