author: peyton-spencer
body:
Hey Tom 👋 — thanks for wiring Ditto Router into BitBull. This PR builds on your integration and takes it the rest of the way: one **Connect Ditto** button sets BitBull up on Ditto, Router models work everywhere SayGM models do, and your Ditto memory and connected apps become the agent's tools without ever leaving BitBull's fences. SayGM stays exactly as it is, one pick away in every model picker.

## What changes for a user

1. **Settings → Integrations → Ditto → Connect Ditto.** Approve in Ditto (BitBull shows the code to check), and BitBull creates or reuses two Router endpoints on that account and saves a key for each:

   | Endpoint | Used for | Memory | Tools |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | `bitbull` | chats | recall and record | every app/MCP server connected in Ditto |
   | `bitbull-review` | plan mode and QA Hound | off | none |

   It also sets `DITTO_API_KEY`, makes `ditto-router/bitbull` the default model and moves background work (titles, compaction) to the endpoint. Everything stays editable in Settings.
2. **Manage connections** opens Ditto's Connections page. Connect GitHub, Gmail, Linear or any MCP server there, and it shows up as the agent's tools here on the next turn.
3. **Router models in every picker**, tagged *Ditto Router*: chats (per message), QA Hound reviewers, subagent models and `DEFAULT_MODEL`.

## Provider keys, kept in Ditto

Settings → Integrations → Ditto → **Provider keys**: pick GM, Engy, Instant, OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic or Google, paste the key and press **Save**.

- BitBull runs the Ditto CLI on the server (`heyditto keys set <provider>`, with the key on stdin) and stores nothing. The key lives in the user's Ditto account, and the provider's check comes straight back ("Saved, and OpenRouter accepted it").
- An optional **Name** saves a second key for the same provider (`heyditto keys set gm --label=work`); saving under an existing name replaces that key, and the panel explains the Ditto plan's per-provider limit.
- Keys can be turned off, on or removed in the same panel, and **Copy BitBull's SayGM key to Ditto** moves the existing `SAYGM_API_KEY` over as the `gm` key.
- Connect Ditto now asks for Ditto's `keys` sign-in, and the approval page says what that allows. On a Ditto that doesn't support it yet, Connect falls back to a plain login.
- Endpoints Connect creates bill with `billingMode: "both"`: your own keys first, then Ditto credits. An endpoint that already exists keeps the billing you chose.
- The CLI child process gets the Ditto account key and the egress proxy settings, and none of BitBull's other secrets. It also gets a fresh config folder per run and never self-updates.

This builds on three Ditto PRs, all merged: ditto-assistant/backend#4526 (the `keys` sign-in and write routes, named keys included), ditto-assistant/ditto-cli#157 (`heyditto keys`, released in `@heyditto/cli@3.17.0`) and ditto-assistant/ditto-app#4129 (the approval page). The image now pins `@heyditto/cli@3.17.0` (was 3.6.4). Saving works once the backend change is deployed to production.

## How it works

- **One model list** (`chatModels()` in models.ts): SayGM's models plus the endpoint's, as `ditto-router/<router id>`. Cost estimates, QA Hound budgets, model details and the picker all go through it.
- **OpenCode** routes Router models by API shape, as it already does for SayGM. Claude models use `@ai-sdk/anthropic` on the Router's `/v1/messages`; everything else uses `openai-compatible`. A second, `-review` set of providers carries the review key for plan mode.
- **Claude Agent SDK** runs on any Router model the way `heyditto claude` runs Claude Code: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points at the Router, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` is the key, gateway hint headers are on. The Router translates Messages for non-Claude models.
- **Tools are attached, not injected.** BitBull reads the endpoint's MCP catalog (`GET /v1/mcp`) and attaches each server as a remote MCP server: `ditto` for memory, `ditto-github` and so on for connected apps. Every inference request sends `X-Ditto-Tool-Surface: mcp`, so the Router adds nothing of its own. That keeps your existing rules in force:
  - Plan mode (and so QA Hound) still gets **no** MCP servers.
  - Its Router turns run on the review endpoint, so nothing a reviewer reads in a hostile repo reaches memory. The chat endpoint's own entry (`ditto-router/bitbull`) maps to the review endpoint's there.
  - BitBull checks the review endpoint through its own key on every refresh, not only at Connect. If its memory or tools are on, if it shares the chat key, or if there is no review key, a plan turn on a Router model is refused rather than run where it could be remembered.
  - Background calls (titles, summaries) run on the review endpoint too, so housekeeping never touches memory.
- **One Router thread per chat.** Every Router request carries `X-Ditto-Session-Id`. A small OpenCode plugin (`agent/opencode-plugin/ditto-router.js`) adds it per request; without it the Router groups chats by a 10-minute idle window.
- **No double memory.** When the endpoint records turns itself, BitBull's per-turn archive skips Router turns. SayGM turns are archived as before.
- **Plan turns are no longer archived.** This one also changes existing behavior: before this PR, QA Hound reviewer turns were saved to Ditto memory whenever `DITTO_API_KEY` was set, including text quoted from the branch under review.
- **Outages don't stall turns.** If Ditto is unreachable, BitBull keeps the last model list, tools and prices it had and retries after a minute.
- **Reconnecting is tidy.** A new Connect revokes the endpoint keys an earlier Connect from this BitBull made, once the new ones are saved.
- **Prices.** The Router's `/v1/models` has no prices, so they come from Ditto's model catalog via the account key. With that key set, QA Hound budgets hold for Router reviewers too; without it, the endpoint's own spend limit is the only cap.
- **Errors name the gateway.** Router 401/402/403 errors, including codes like `insufficient_balance`, point at the Router key and your Ditto credits or endpoint limits, not at SayGM.

## What I fixed in the earlier Router integration

- Router models only worked for background work and the OpenCode engine. They now work in chats, subagents, QA Hound and on the Claude Agent SDK engine.
- `redact()` did not include `DITTO_ROUTER_KEY`, so it could show up unmasked in the activity feed. Both Router keys are now redacted.
- The MCP `timeout` in OpenCode's config applies to fetching the tool list at startup. A long value there would stall OpenCode if Ditto was slow, so Router MCP servers use 15 s.
- The `ditto_review` tool passed `HTTPS_PROXY` to the Ditto CLI but not `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY`, so inside the sandbox Node's fetch skipped the proxy and the review couldn't reach Ditto. It now uses the same CLI environment as provider keys: the proxy settings, Ditto's API origin from `DITTO_MCP_URL`, the image's pinned CLI version with no self-update, and `DITTO_CLI` in host mode.

**Known limit** (in docs/THREAT-MODEL.md R2): on the Claude Agent SDK engine, the chat endpoint key sits in the Claude CLI's environment, the same way the SayGM key does today. Outside plan mode it reaches the same tools the turn already has, behind Ditto's approval gate. Plan turns carry the review key, which reaches no tools and no memory.

## Keys and the referral link

- All keys are **runtime server settings**: `.env` or Settings, saved to the vault when it's unlocked. They're never GitHub Actions secrets or build-time variables, so the published image carries none. Nothing reaches the web UI or the agent's shell: the keys are scrubbed from the engines' environment, the guard plugin hides them, and both Router keys are in `redact()`.
- `DITTO_REFERRAL_CODE` (empty by default): set your own Ditto referral code (like `abcd-2345`) and the **Create a Ditto account** link becomes Ditto's `https://heyditto.ai/r/<code>`, so signups from BitBull count

author: thiesi
body:
Engineer: implements slice P12, [`docs/plan/slices/P12-talk-and-log-fit.md`](https://github.com/Thiesi/Karst41/blob/main/docs/plan/slices/P12-talk-and-log-fit.md), with #202's log rule 5. Closes #204.

The slice names Codex as primary model. This PR was written by Claude Opus 5.5 (the engineer session).

## What changed

- **Talk page (rules 1, 2).** On a talker page, the line starts at the top of the listing area and wraps across the full inner width: 66 × 14 rows at 80x24, 106 × 35 at 132x50 (the new `MenuLayout.talk` rect in `karst41/layout.py`). After one blank row the actions follow, one per row, with an aligned key column and a single `Esc/B  Leave` row. The "Choice" column label is gone. A line that overflows ends its last row with `...`.
- **Menu detail (rule 3).** Every menu detail word-wraps inside its rect, and rows past the rect end with `...`.
- **Log (rule 5, #202).** Both renderers select whole entries:
  - The newest entry always shows. When cut, it shows its first rows ending `... Ctrl-P`.
  - Protected danger/combat entries are taken whole, newest first.
  - The newest entry then takes back free rows, and other entries fill what's left.
  - A protected newest entry takes rows first.
  - The default renderer protects nothing (ruling Q2).
- **Server (the only server change).** `dialogue_runtime.publish()` no longer appends `b Back` to talkers. `b`/`B`/Esc still close the page in the client (`door/model.py:263`).
- **Validator (rule 4).** It rejects a dialogue line that wraps past 4 rows at the 80x24 talk width (66, taken from `compute(80, 24)`, wrapped with the client's own `wrap`), and an offer label over 40 cells. The existing `b` and duplicate-hotkey check is unchanged. All shipped dialogue passes.
- **Shared helpers.** Both renderers use `karst41/door/fit.py`, so P10 inherits one copy. The validator imports it from `door`; content→door imports already exist (`place_validation`), and the door→content guard is untouched.

### Rulings applied (#202 [6805937648](https://github.com/Thiesi/Karst41/pull/202#issuecomment-6805937648))
- The cut marker is ASCII `...` and `... Ctrl-P`, not `…`. Terminal UI canon specifies it, and CP437 has no ellipsis glyph.
- Protection applies only in the presentation renderer, where kinds and arrival times exist. There is no `_arrived` port.
- Talker pages drop "Choice". The 132x50 line starts at y3. A log that isn't full stays top-aligned. The fit check covers dialogue `text` only.

### Rule 5 filling
Steps 2 and 4 say protected entries "fill the remaining rows, newest first, whole only" and other entries "fill whatever is left, newest first, whole only". `select_entries` follows that literally: an entry that doesn't fit whole is skipped, and older, shorter entries still fill the free rows. (An earlier head stopped each pass at the first misfit. That reading had no support in the text and was withdrawn at `854a94b`.)

### Bounded log work (technical review [6808753030](https://github.com/Thiesi/Karst41/pull/206#issuecomment-6808753030))
At `f649335` the default log wrapped all 500 ring lines on every render. Since `bf3e7a6`, both renderers do bounded work per render (`door/fit.py`):
- `select_lazy` wraps newest first, only the entries the passes reach, and stops once the rows are full.
- Unprotected entries are looked for at most `LOG_LOOKBACK_PER_ROW` × height = 2 × height entries behind the newest.
- Protected entries are not bounded out by the lookback. The presentation log digests the newest `log_window(height)` = 4 × (2 × height + 1) lines. If that window cut off a still-protected line, it reaches back for it, stopping at whichever comes first:
  - it holds `height` distinct protected lines (no more can show);
  - it reaches a line older than `PROTECT_SECONDS`;
  - it has gone `LOG_PROTECT_EXTRA` = 100 extra lines, about ten seconds of heavy combat.
- Only a protected line behind a flood of more than 100 newer unprotected lines arriving within 10 s can drop early.
- One visible edge: a run of identical lines longer than the window shows a lower `(xN)` count in the log. Ctrl-P scrollback keeps every line.
- Tests count work on a full 500-line ring, not wall-clock: wraps equal `height` for 1-row entries, at most `2 × height + 1` for entries too tall to fit, and the digest gets exactly `log_window(height)` lines. Another test pins a protected entry behind more lines than the window.
- **Door CPU with a long log is not covered by CI**: the budget runs never fill the ring. Local measurement on a full ring at width 50, height 7, best of 3, Windows:

  | Path | Typical | Worst (2×height+1 too-tall entries) |
  |---|---|---|
  | old default rule (last `height` lines) | 0.30 ms | — |
  | default, at `f649335` (reviewed) | 52.4 ms (technical lead's measurement) | — |
  | default, now | 0.91 ms | 2.23 ms |
  | presentation, now | 3.43 ms | 4.65 ms |
  | presentation, 500 lines of combat spam in 10 s | 0.5–2.0 ms (heights 3–8) | — |
  | presentation, unprotected flood in 10 s plus an old danger line (cap reached) | — | 4.8–8.3 ms (heights 3–8) |

  Without the reach-back cap (at `bf3e7a6`), protected spam cost about 65 ms.

  Before P12 the presentation log digested and wrapped the whole ring, about 85 ms on my measurement (58 ms digest plus 27 ms wrap).

### Offer cap (from the automated review)
The validator also reports a talker with more than 8 offers. 8 is what the 80x24 talk page holds under a 4-row line: `compute(80, 24).menu.talk.height - 4 - 2`. No shipped talker has more than 2.

## Visible changes and moved tests

- **Goldens moved:** `tests/presentation/golden/p5/talker_{80x24,132x50}_{16,256,truecolor}.json` (6 files), the talk page re-laid out. No other golden changed.
- `tests/test_dialogue_runtime.py:74`: talker actions are `{'c','v'}`, no longer including `'b'`. The `b` presses that close the page still pass.
- `tests/door/test_dialogue_render.py`: the synthetic fixture drops its `b Back` action. Added `('vi', 'k', 'key')`, so vi `k` still walks away while `j` takes the offer.
- `tests/world/test_arrival_prose.py:64`: it reimplemented the old row rule and now uses the default renderer's real selector (`default_log_rows`).
- **Vendor, progression and commerce menus:** no asserted text moved out of view. Every test in `test_market_menus.py`, `test_progression_menus.py` and `test_commerce_menus.py` passes unchanged.
- **Actual visible effect at 80x24 vendor pages:** a detail line that used to be cut on one row now wraps. A long last line can therefore end row 4 with `...` (see capture 4 below).

## Tests (what I ran, where)

All runs on Windows with the repo venv (Python 3.12.10) and `PYTHONPATH=<worktree>\src;<worktree>`, after checking that `karst41.__file__` was in the worktree.
- At `5529d73`, which holds every source and test change in this PR (later commits touch only `scripts/accept_p12_netbbs.py` and the workflow): `tests/door tests/content tests/presentation/test_client_foundations.py tests/presentation/test_notices.py tests/presentation/test_p6b_content_pin.py tests/presentation/test_geometry.py tests/test_dialogue_runtime.py tests/test_s42_dialogue.py tests/world/test_arrival_prose.py tests/contracts/test_panels.py` gave **998 passed, 1 deselected** (`tests/door/test_io.py::test_real_module_uses_native_stdio_pipes[True]`, the known Windows exception).
- New `tests/door/test_p12_fit.py` (35 tests) covers every test in the slice's list:
  - the longest shipped line (164 chars) with 0/1/3 actions in both renderers at both sizes;
  - the 20-row fallback;
  - detail wrap;
  - the validator's 5-row, 41-cell, `b` and duplicate-key cases;
  - every shipped line fitting;
  - all the log cases, including #202's three-combat-plus-speech and protected-newest cases.
- **Not run:** the full local suite. I'm relying on hosted CI at the head.
- `python -m karst41.content.validate src/karst41/content` gives `ok`.

author: ju-li
body:
Every install pins the major tag (`:1`: `docker-compose.yml`, the Railway docs, the single container), and `release.yml` moved `X.Y`, `X` and `latest` on every merge into `prod`. So each release reached every self-hosted deployment on its next pull, untested.

## Change
- **`release.yml`** (merge into `prod`) pushes only `X.Y.Z`, `beta` and `sha-<commit>`, and creates the GitHub Release as a **prerelease**. Its `mcp-registry` job moves to `promote.yml`.
- **New `promote.yml`** (manual, `workflow_dispatch`, input `version`):
  1. refuses a version that isn't `X.Y.Z`, has no GitHub Release (that's what tells it all three images exist), or is below the release currently marked latest. Migrations only go forward, so `:1` must never move back. Re-running for the same version is allowed.
  2. retags `X.Y.Z` → `X.Y`, `X`, `latest` for all three images with `docker buildx imagetools create`. No rebuild, so the digest is the one that was tested.
  3. marks the GitHub Release latest (`--prerelease=false --latest`).
  4. publishes `server.json` to the MCP Registry from the `vX.Y.Z` tag.
  - Shares the `release` concurrency group, so it can't interleave with a release still pushing.
- **Docs:** `docs/releases.md` gets the two-step tag table, test and promote steps, and the rollback caveat. `docs/self-hosting.md` says `:1` gets promoted releases and `:beta` gets everything. The `CLAUDE.md` Releases section is updated.

## After merge
- The next release (e.g. 1.3.2) lands as a beta. Run `gh workflow run promote.yml -f version=1.3.2` once it's tested.
- Existing tags are untouched: `:1` and `latest` stay on the current release until the first promotion.

## Checks
- [x] Both workflow files parse as YAML. actionlint isn't installed locally, so it was not run.
- [ ] Not exercised on Actions yet: the first real run is the next release.

author: gilbert09
body:
## Problem

EasyPost sync runs that hit a dropped connection or a read timeout after exhausting the in-process retry budget get reported to error tracking as exception noise ([issue](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/error-tracking/01a1cc6f-7d30-71c0-9427-5eb191c028b5)), even though Temporal already retries the whole activity once that budget is spent.

## Changes

- `EasypostSource.get_retryable_errors()` now classifies an exhausted connection/read-timeout error, and an exhausted 429/5xx, as self-recovering, matching the pattern already used by `close`, `decagon`, `gorgias`, `hubspot` and `notion`.
- Retry behavior, backoff and timeouts are unchanged; this only stops an already-retried, self-recovering failure from being tracked as an exception.
- Mechanical: added a regression test asserting both message shapes match the new classification.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** Added `TestGetRetryableErrors` to `test_easypost_source.py`, parameterized over the connection/read-timeout message and the exhausted 429/5xx message, mirroring `decagon`'s equivalent test. No existing easypost test covered `get_retryable_errors`, so none could be extended.

Ran `pytest products/warehouse_sources/sources/easypost` (71 passed, proxy env unset per the known sandbox caveat) and `ruff check`/`ruff format` locally. Not run: the full backend suite or any database-backed check, not needed for this change.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

**Agent:** Claude Code, Sonnet 5

**Skills:** `/writing-tests`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

**Security review:** not needed

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Decisions:** Classified via `get_retryable_errors` (self-recovering, Temporal retries) rather than `NonRetryableErrors`, since this condition already recovers on retry; matches sibling-source precedent.
- **Follow-ups:** None.
- **Read closely:** `products/warehouse_sources/sources/easypost/source.py`, new `get_retryable_errors` method.

</details>

body:
## Objetivo y alcance

Preparar el modo conectado multiempresa de Davara PLD y el acceso privado de Vicente como superadministrador. El prototipo guardaba datos sólo en navegador, confiaba en controles visuales y perdía revisiones documentales o decisiones al cambiar de pantalla. Esta rama añade servidor, cuentas, sesiones revocables, empresas, permisos efectivos y persistencia compartida con D1/R2/colas, preservando IDs y las llaves de importación locales.

La publicación se orienta a revisión privada del superadministrador: **no declara aceptado el piloto completo para clientes reales**. Mantiene fuera de alcance presentación automática ante SAT, servicios externos no contratados y OCR de PDF escaneados. No incluye contraseñas, tokens, documentos personales ni artefactos QA locales.

## Cambios y contratos

- Better Auth fijado, alta administrada de cuentas, contraseña temporal de un solo uso, cambio obligatorio, suspensión, revocación de sesiones y política MFA inicialmente apagada y exclusiva de superadministrador.
- Organización, empresa y usuario son identidades separadas. Autorización en API/archivos/exportaciones/importaciones; revisión esperada y transacciones evitan sobrescrituras silenciosas. Expedientes privados se reutilizan explícitamente, no por coincidencia de RFC.
- Repositorios compatibles con las colecciones antiguas, migración asistida con respaldo previo, archivos R2 privados por versión, historial y recuperación no destructiva. Ninguna lectura debe borrar registros inconsistentes.
- Actos conserva centavos, moneda original/conversión documentada, identidades estables, borradores, correcciones y snapshots. Avisos guarda folios/acuses vinculados a la revisión exacta, sin presentar datos ficticios como envío SAT.
- Importación Excel/PDF digital con revisión previa, duplicados, mapeos y cola idempotente; 40 fingerprints de formatos, sin macros ni ActiveX. CSV/ZIP/hojas se acotan antes de la expansión; celdas SAT se canonicalizan por layout.
- EBR versionado con metodología/fuentes, factores, riesgo institucional, perfil transaccional, planes, gráficas/PDF y estados incompletos explícitos. Una consulta PEP nueva invalida el uso vigente de la aprobación histórica también en Avisos/CSV/tablero.
- Aprobación/archivo anidados BC/Gobernanza se validan en servidor, con actor real y versión/hash recuperable. Editar contenido reinicia cierres. Referencias documentales sólo activan archivos privados de la empresa; no ejecutan URLs legacy peligrosas.
- Guardas por empresa/generación/autenticación en cargas asíncronas y merges de contenido más reciente. Regresiones ejecutan los callers reales con promesas diferidas, A→B→A y cargas simultáneas.
- Conserva `https://plataforma-de-pld.pages.dev`: `wrangler.jsonc` configura Pages y service binding; `wrangler.worker.jsonc` configura backend/entornos. Preview usa alias estable y recursos/cuentas QA separados. R2 producción sin URL pública ni dominio público. El Worker productivo queda configurado sin workers.dev.

## Fuentes y límites normativos

Consulta documentada 11/11/2026: [LFPIORPI](https://www.diputados.gob.mx/LeyesBiblio/pdf/LFPIORPI.pdf), [Acuerdo 115/2026](https://dof.gob.mx/nota_detalle_popup.php?codigo=5795797), [SAT Actividades Vulnerables](https://www.sat.gob.mx/minisitio/ActividadesVulnerables/index.html) y [esquemas de servicios profesionales](https://sppld.sat.gob.mx/pld/interiores/servicios.html). Detalle por regla, conservación, vigencia y procedencia en `docs/pilot-validation.md` y `docs/pilot-ebr-import-validation.md`. Los pesos EBR son metodología interna; una validación local XML no es aceptación SAT. XIV conserva la vía aplicable sin aviso ordinario fabricado.

## Validación

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`: aprobado.
- `pnpm typecheck` + ejecución sin caché: aprobados.
- `pnpm lint`: cero errores; advertencias de hooks existentes pendientes de deuda específica.
- `pnpm test:pld`: **368/368** en ejecución final, cero fallos/saltos/cancelaciones.
- Regresión final de callers/EBR: **9/9**; integración Worker real local con D1/R2/colas, roles, sesiones/MFA, CAS/rollback, copia y versiones: aprobada.
- `pnpm build` y `pnpm build:worker`: aprobados.
- Un único ciclo independiente de revisión del candidato encontró seis siblings; corregidos con pruebas negativas y controles legítimos. No se presenta como auditoría exhaustiva de la plataforma.
- `scripts/check-sat-xml-programs.ts --verify-workbooks`: **40 plantillas, 1,198 celdas comparadas sin diferencias, macros conservadas, 39 XML válidos con XSD y xmllint**. XIV no genera un XML ordinario. La matriz mantiene expresamente `manualCapture: pending` y `browser: pending`, no convierte ejemplos sintéticos en aceptación humana.
- Preview real: [alias estable](https://codex-piloto-real-multiempre.plataforma-de-pld.pages.dev), Worker `davara-pld-preview`, D1/R2/colas separados. Login con cuenta ficticia probado mediante UI móvil; cookies y origen se mantienen. Pages truncó el alias de rama y se corrigió `BETTER_AUTH_URL` conforme al alias efectivamente asignado. Health responde modo cloud/configurado/preview. El sitio de producción todavía no se ha reemplazado en este punto.
- QA local final: 12 rutas móviles (390×844) sin nuevos errores de consola ni overflow. Captura/recarga desktop en Alta, EUI, Capacitación, Gobernanza, Evidencias y PEP. BC aprobado → declaración nueva → autosave → reaprobación → recarga conservó dos folios, sin 400 ni bucle. Provider impide montar módulos durante snapshots/rutas en transición. Los pendientes se aíslan en memoria por usuario: otro usuario no puede leerlos/exportarlos/reenviarlos, y el titular puede recuperarlos al reautenticar.
- Actos manual: XV borrador → completo con el mismo UUID, `$10,000,000.01`, instrumento buscable y Bandeja SAT. NIF sin RFC para PM extranjera y condición XI-B `99,Otro` en ambos sentidos. CSV de tres filas: grupos explícitos separados aun compartiendo RFC; tres duplicados al reimportar, sin nuevas altas disponibles. No se fabricó presentación SAT.
- **CI aprobado tras autorización del titular:** [ejecución 43106545762](https://github.com/vicvaz074/plataforma-de-pld/actions/runs/43106545762), commit `d63afacd32a057bcf6d5152fe3eeb1206698726a`. Checkout limpio Ubuntu: instalación frozen, `libxml2-utils`, TypeScript, lint, **368/368 pruebas**, build Next y build Worker aprobados (8m33s). La prueba Worker usa `--assets public`, sin depender de un frontend compilado ni omitir validaciones.
- Preview final del mismo commit: Pages `3adde7e7`, Worker `9a2aba93-feb0-4df0-b25b-150d816d2114`. Login real QA 200 con cookie; Actos/EBR/EUI/Avisos recorrieron pantalla sin nuevos errores de consola. El 401 inicial de sesión corresponde al estado previo al login. Health cloud/configurado/preview.
- CRUD manual local final: un borrador CSV ficticio se editó manteniendo ID/revisión y después se eliminó con confirmación. Recarga conservó la operación XV completa y los otros dos borradores, retiró el eliminado de Bandeja y mantuvo su cliente en el índice. Historial conservó revisiones previas y tombstone final; consola limpia. No se borró ningún registro ajeno ni productivo.

## Pendientes de aceptación

Los recorridos humanos completos de las 40 plantillas siguen diferenciados de las pruebas sintéticas y contractuales. El respaldo privado en la misma cuenta no es DR integral; se requiere respaldo externo administrado antes de admitir documentación real de clientes. La rama no modifica ni elimina los datos locales del usuario. Estado y límites: `docs/pilot-release-2026-11-11.md` y matriz de aceptación.

## Publicación privada del superadministrador

Publicación autorizada el 11/11/2026 y comprobada en `https://plataforma-de-pld.pages.dev`, conservando la dirección. Promoción manual del **mismo commit d63afacd32a057bcf6d5152fe3eeb1206698726a** validado por CI y preview; no se ha fusionado este PR ni se declara aceptación para clientes.

body:
Every deploy gave the service worker a new cache name, and install downloaded the whole build (468 files, 1,604 KB decoded) again, even files whose content hash had not changed. Most of that list was route code that offline use never needs.

Now the precache holds only what the shell, /workout (and its run and session pages) and /offline need, plus the render code of the five tabs so they still show their offline state. The list is worked out at build time from Vite's and SvelteKit's manifests. Any other `_app/immutable` file is served cache-first and stored the first time it is used. On install, unchanged hashed files are copied from any older pc-shell-* cache, so only the files that changed are downloaded. `pnpm budgets` gets a new gate on the precache file count and decoded bytes, set at today's scoped size, and it fails if the worker is missing a file from the list.

| Measured on the same `pnpm build:node` | Files | Decoded | gzip-9 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before (whole build) | 468 | 1,604.4 KB | 681.6 KB |
| After (scoped list) | 275 | 994.1 KB | 441.3 KB |

Not measured here: the bytes actually transferred after a deploy, install time, and the offline e2e test. CI measures those.

Behaviour change: offline, a client-side navigation to an (app) route that is not a tab, a workout page or /offline can no longer load its route code, because that code is no longer precached. If the route was opened online before, its files are already in the runtime cache. If not, it falls back to /offline.

Checking the performance review against the code:
- Confirmed: the cache name changed on every build, install called addAll over every file, and docs/performance.md still had stale figures (74 files, 353 KB).
- Different: the review's suggested scope of "206 files, about 350 KB gzip" is smaller than this one, because this list also keeps the five tabs' render code and all of the workout pages' lazy code (sheets, plate calculator), so both work offline.
- Its 443-452 files / 1.46-1.50 MB matches today's 459 immutable files / 1,462 KB, before static files and prerendered pages are added.

## Tests

- Unit tests for the scope (scripts/lib/precache-scope.test.ts) prove that the list holds what the workout pages load on demand, plus the stylesheets and fonts. They also prove it leaves out the tabs' on-demand code and every other route's, and that it fails loudly when a server node has no imports export.
- Unit tests for the worker (src/lib/client/sw-precache.test.ts) prove that unchanged files are copied from older caches and only the rest are downloaded, and that a build file is stored on first use and then served with no network.
- New e2e test in e2e/offline.e2e.ts: an offline cold start with an active workout. Working from the precache alone, a set logs to the outbox and the menu opens. CI runs it.
- Mutation check: I broke four behaviours one at a time (no reuse, no store on first use, scope too wide, whole build precached). Each one failed the matching tests.
- Local gates: `pnpm lint` clean; `pnpm check` 0 errors; `pnpm test:unit` 6800/6803 passed. The 3 failures were load-related, all in backup/store.test.ts, and that file passed 42/42 when re-run alone. `pnpm build:node` passed, and `pnpm budgets` reported "275 files, 994.1 KB decoded (441.3 KB gzip); budget ≤ 275 files, ≤ 995 KB decoded: pass".
- CI runs the e2e specs, Lighthouse and the budgets.

## Docs to add

docs/performance.md, in the service-worker / precache budget section, replacing the stale "74 files, 353 KB decoded" line:

"Service-worker install download (precache, measured by `pnpm budgets` on a Node build): 275 files, 994.1 KB decoded (441.3 KB gzip), down from 468 files, 1,604 KB (682 KB gzip) when it precached the whole build. Gated by BUDGETS.precacheFiles (275) and BUDGETS.precacheKb (995). The list covers the app shell, the five tabs' render code, the workout pages and /offline (scripts/lib/precache-scope.ts). Other `_app/immutable` files are cached cache-first on first use. On install, unchanged content-hashed files are copied from the previous pc-shell-* cache instead of downloaded."

## Round 138: a tune keeps within its token song's notes a bar by the part of the form

The fourth of four items after Song Check 101 (record: `docs/idiom/phase-4-writing.md`, round 138). Stacked on `own-tempo`; merges on hold.

**Found.** Song Check 101's Blackjack tune was "well over twice as busy as the game's". Round 125 gave the backing lines the token song's onsets a bar by the part of the form; the tune kept its own density tier and took only the song's tier against it. On the 59 Song Check 100 songs on their token song's arrangement, the tune's notes a bar were within half to one and a half times the token song's in 131 of 193 parts of the form (47 over, 15 under), bar by bar in 974 of 1,648, and its notes a second were over one and a half times the game's tune's in 8 songs (to 3.75 times).

**Built.**
- Plan: `token_sections` sets `plan.section_onsets` for the tune's line too (the melody's, or the counter's in a band without one), so the tune's writer gets the song's own envelope and tier.
- Writer (`tune.melody`): `keeps`, whether a bar of n notes is within the bar's own onsets, asked by every way a bar is made. A new bar is drawn within them (and is asked neither the tier's running mean nor the pooled `tune_grain` word; among the bar table's bars that fit where no draw does). A bar, a pair of bars or a half bar comes back, and a phrase's rhythm is answered, only where the bar still keeps. The theme comes back as its latest statement whose head keeps, and is stated anew where none does. An earlier phrase comes back, and a phrase is repeated or moved, where every bar keeps. A song without the token song's form is written as before.
- Three cuts, each found by measuring the one before (in the record): the bars that came back were not asked; the grain held to a bar by itself refused every bar of one note (203 such bars fell to 110; the game's songs have 214); a theme of the intro's whole notes came back through 31 bars the game plays three notes a bar in.
- Tests (five; three of them fail with their change taken out); suite 538 (1 skip). No token change, no refit; the vocabulary map is unchanged.

**Measured.** The same 59 songs, round 137's in brackets.
- The tune's bars within their part of the form's own onsets: 1,648 of 1,648 (974). By the part of the form: 193 of 193 in range (131), 131 within a quarter of the game's (75).
- The tune's notes a second within two thirds to one and a half times the game's tune's: 53 songs (46), over in 2 (8). Blackjack's 1.5 (2.8; the game's 1.4).
- Bars that come back 885 (852); the theme's bars back by the letters 85 (77), in 22 of the 23 themed songs (the 23rd brings its theme back by the form's repeat).
- Off the beat, bar for bar against the game's songs: bars of one note all on the beat 0.88 (0.87; the game's 0.90), of two 0.57 (0.40; 0.53), of three or four 0.34 (0.14; 0.35).
- Plans, 400 seeds: all keep their token song, title, tempo and form; 355 of the 360 on their token song's arrangement change their tune (and the parts that take up or double its cells); no kit changes; the 40 others are as they were.

**Open.** The grain is no longer held where the song's own onsets are: song by song the tune's share off the beat is within a tenth of its token song's in 28 of 59 (26); an own word for it would be the vocabulary. The busiest parts of the form run a little under the game's (Battle Theme's tune 2.0 notes a second against 3.2). A theme stated over a thin part of the form is two statements. The counter-line beside a tune still follows the tune's figures.

body:
## What you changed

Scratchpad's message box has a microphone button between the box and Send. Press 'Dictate', speak, then press 'Stop and transcribe' - the words land in the box after whatever I'd already typed. Nothing is sent until I press Send myself.

- The recording is converted to a 16 kHz mono WAV in the browser, then sent to a transcription route the server already had. I didn't add any server code.
- Context has a new 'Dictation' section with a 'Transcription service' choice: this server's own Whisper (no key needed, the default), OpenAI, Groq or Mistral. The remote ones use the API key already saved under API Connections.
- A recording stops by itself after 2 minutes and is transcribed at that point.
- Closing Scratchpad while recording throws the recording away and lets go of the microphone.
- The button only appears in browsers that can record.

## Why

Typing a long question to an assistant on a phone is a chore, and Scratchpad is where I think out loud about a story. The server could already transcribe audio; nothing in the app ever asked it to.

## How to test it

1. Open Scratchpad in a chat and press the microphone button. Allow microphone access.
2. Say something, then press the button again ('Stop and transcribe').
3. The text appears in the message box. Nothing is sent.
4. Under Context → Dictation, pick another service. Without a saved key for it, dictating shows 'No API key is saved for ...' and leaves the draft alone.

## Checks you ran

- [x] Unit tests: `npm run test:unit --prefix tests`
- [x] Server tests, if you touched `src/`: `node --test tests/*.node.js`
- [x] Lint: `npm run lint`
- [x] Frontend budgets: `npm run check:frontend-budgets`
- [x] You added or updated a test that pins the behaviour you changed
- [x] UI changes: you checked a phone (393x852, touch) and desktop (1280x900) in the browser
- [x] Buttons: they follow the accent (no hex colours) and stay readable with a pale and a dark accent profile
- [ ] CSS changes: you bumped `NN_SW_CACHE_VERSION` in `public/sw.js` and the `?v=` on the five core stylesheets in `public/index.html`

Only Scratchpad's own stylesheet changed. It loads on demand with its own `?v=`, which I bumped, so the core cache versions stay as they are.

What I haven't checked, honestly:

- No real microphone and no real transcription service. The browser test uses stand-ins for both, so it proves the button, the request and where the text goes - not that Whisper hears me correctly.
- The phone run is Chromium imitating an iPhone. Safari records in a different format; the WAV conversion is there to cover that, but I haven't tried it on a real iPhone.
- The server's own Whisper downloads its model on first use and is slow on a small server.
- A remote service answering with error 400 is read as 'no key saved', which is the usual cause but not the only possible one.
- The message box is 52 px narrower now that it shares the row with a third button. On a phone that leaves 209 px, which I think is fine, but it's a real cost.
- The chosen service is a per-device preference.

author: teamleaderleo
body:
On a fresh Cloud machine the network attach lands after cmux-host has started. A Cloud request sent before it (the guest bind is the first) could hang in its connect. Nothing failed it until the 10 s connect bound, and then the bind's backoff added more on top. `network_changed` fails in-flight requests only when the global address set changes, so a late route or interface didn't count.

Every cmux-host Cloud request (`JsonPoster`, `cloud_http_transport.rs`) now has a 2 s connect bound, separate from the 20 s request bound. A connect that times out has sent nothing, so it's made again at once for as long as the request's deadline lasts. A connect that's refused still fails at once. The lead asked for this class fix, not a wider `Wake` trigger. It serves Leo's V0 item 1: "A chat starts in a few seconds: ready spare, harness login attached in advance, no 10 s relay credential timeout, no first-boot self-update."

## Evidence

- `cargo test -p cmux-server --lib cloud_http::tests::a_connect_that_hangs_until_the_network_attaches_is_made_again`. A loopback listener with a full accept queue drops the connect's SYN until it "attaches" at 7.5 s. Through cmux-ci (fast-checks run 43116675600): at the base, `answered Err("Cloud request failed") in 10.00s` (red); at this head, `answered Ok(200) in 8.01s` (green, 14 of 14 `cloud_http` tests pass).
- Late-attach netns harness (`cmux-tui/scripts/cloud-attach-compare.sh`). A dummy link drops every packet to 10.9.9.1 until that address is attached, N s after the request starts. The same request runs against the transport at the base and at this head:

Run 43116675600 on a Linux CI runner (root network namespace), 3 runs each, all three identical to 0.01 s:

| Attach after | Base (10 s connect bound) | This PR (2 s, reconnect) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 s | 200 in 1.01-1.03 s | 200 in 1.01 s |
| 4 s | 200 in 4.09 s | 200 in 4.00 s |
| 8 s | **fails in 10.00 s** | 200 in 8.01 s |
| 12 s | **fails in 10.00 s** | 200 in 12.01 s |

At the base, a bind sent before an attach later than about 8 s waited out the whole 10 s connect bound and failed, and then the bind's 2 s backoff came on top. With the fix, it answers within about 10 ms of the attach, at any attach time inside the request deadline. Early attaches are caught by the kernel's own SYN retransmits (1 s, then 3 s) in both.

### Observed / Not run

Observed: the unit test red at base and green at head, and the netns table, all in run 43116675600. Not run: a staging probe with this cmux-host, which needs an image roll after merge.

## Changelog

- Fixed: a Cloud machine's first request to cmux Cloud no longer waits out a 10 s connect timeout when it was sent before the machine's network was ready.

author: bardrop
body:
## This relates to...

Refs #4122

## Rationale

In #4122 the reporter found that a bearer token ended up in plain text in the SQLite cache file, because the response had `Vary: Authorization`. The discussion landed on not hashing keys, and on @metcoder95's idea of documenting this so users know what gets written to disk.

## Changes

Adds a short paragraph to the `SqliteCacheStore` docs saying:

- the database is not encrypted or hashed;
- the URL (with query string), response headers and body, and request headers named in `Vary` (e.g. `Authorization`, `Cookie`) are stored as plain text at `location`;
- responses to requests with `Authorization` are only stored when the response allows it (`public`, `s-maxage`, `must-revalidate`, per RFC 9111 §3.5), and `no-store` keeps a response out entirely.

I checked the plain-text claim locally: writing an entry with `Vary: authorization` and a query-string token, both strings show up in the `.db` file.

author: spaceoceancorp
body:
Each UTM zone uses 8 of the 24 MGRS column letters: A-H, J-R and S-Z in turn. `MGRS.parse()` and `MGRS.isMGRS()` accept any of the 24. A letter from another zone, for example a typo, decodes to a point outside the zone, sometimes past -180: `01CKM4186716915` gives longitude -199.46.

I compared parse() with GeographicLib on 3,694 valid and mutated strings. mgrs-js accepted 812 strings that GeographicLib rejects, and 521 of those had a column letter the zone does not use. With this change, parse() and isMGRS() check the column (and row) letter against the zone's sets, and zones outside 1-60 are invalid there.

Valid strings are unchanged. New test `test column letter not in zone` fails before the change. 32 tests pass. It merges cleanly with the band-northing and Krueger PRs.

The other 291 accepted strings name a 100 km square that exists in the zone but lies outside the latitude band. Checking that needs a rule for how far a square may overlap the band, which GeographicLib applies with a tolerance, so this PR leaves those strings alone.

Paul S. Mamakos
Space Ocean Corp

author: mattpocock
body:
**Size:** ~400 lines changed, about 140 of them in `src/`; the rest is tests. **Reading order:** `src/fork.ts` (`runFork`), then `test/fork.test.ts`, then the two new methods in `src/git-service/git-service-impl.ts` (`getTrackedChanges`, `isShallowRepository`), then `.changeset/fork-keep-history.md`.

Students run `npx ai-hero-cli fork` in the Cohort 005 "Repo Setup" lesson, then `npm run reset <slug>`. Today fork squashes the course into one fresh "Initial commit", so their `main` shares no history with the course, and after a reset git says the branches have diverged (`↓1 ↑53`). With this change fork keeps the course history of the student's `main`, so it shares history with the course from the start and a force-push is never needed. (Matt approved this on 2026-11-11, from a student's report.)

## Summary

```diff
 runFork
   1. gh installed + authenticated
   2. ensureIsGitRepo
+  3. refuse (ForkNotReadyError, nothing changed, nothing asked yet) if
+       HEAD isn't main (or is detached)      -> "git checkout main"
+       tracked files have uncommitted changes -> lists them; commit or restore
+       the clone is shallow                   -> "git fetch --unshallow"
   4. repo name (arg > prompt)
   5. refuse if <login>/<name> already exists
-  5. warn if core.symlinks=false and HEAD has symlinks
   6. confirm
-       "replace this folder's git history with a single fresh commit"
+       "disconnect this folder from the course repo (remove the "origin" remote)"
+       "push your main branch, with its history, to it as "origin""
-  7. removeGitDirectory, initRepo, ensureCommitterIdentity,
-     stageAll, commit("Initial commit"), renameCurrentBranchTo("main")
+  7. removeRemote("origin")            # history, branches, tags untouched
   8. gh repo create <name> --<vis> --source=. --remote=origin --push
+       # gh pushes HEAD only, i.e. main; main now tracks the new origin
-      on failure: "committed as a single Initial commit on main …"
+      on failure: "files and git history are untouched, but no longer
+                   connected to the course repo …" + the same gh command
```

Design calls:

- **Uncommitted changes: refuse.** Committing them on top would publish edits the student may not have meant to share, under a commit message we make up, and put a non-course commit on `main`. Refusing loses nothing and the fix is one command. Only *tracked* changes block: untracked files are in no commit, so the push can't publish them, and blocking on them would stop students over scratch files. (Before, `git add .` published them.)
- **Not on main: refuse**, rather than pushing `main` from another branch. Then the branch gh pushes (HEAD) is always the one the student is looking at, and `main@{upstream}` ends up as `origin/main`.
- **Other local branches and tags** (`live-run-through`, `backup/*`, course tags) stay local and are never pushed. `git remote remove origin` drops their remote-tracking refs and upstream config. Nothing gets deleted.
- **Other remotes** (e.g. a leftover `upstream`) are left alone. reset, pull and the other commands `set-url` it and clean it up themselves.
- **Shallow clone: refuse (new guard).** The old flow didn't care about depth. Pushing a shallow history to an empty repo fails *after* gh has created the repo, which leaves the student with an empty repo that blocks a re-run.
- **Symlink warning (PR #94): removed.** It warned that plain-file symlinks would be "published to your new repo as plain files". That only happened because the fresh commit came from the working tree. The pushed commits now record symlinks as mode 120000 whatever the checkout has, and a test pins this.
- **Hidden-index-flags guard (PR #94): unchanged.** It lives in `reset`, and fork never used it. Fork no longer stages or commits anything, so an assume-unchanged path can't leak a hidden change into the push. At worst it hides a tracked change from the dirty-tree check, and that change isn't published anyway.
- **Dead code removed:** `removeGitDirectory`, `initRepo`, `renameCurrentBranchTo`, `listSymlinkPaths`, `forkSymlinksWarning`, and the three error types used only by them. `ensureCommitterIdentity` stays because `create-pr` uses it.

## Evidence

**Tests** (`test/fork.test.ts`): real GitService on a temp course clone (`origin` = course bare repo, plus `live-run-through`, `backup/main` and tag `v1`). The fake GitHubService now does to the local repo what `gh repo create --source=. --remote=origin --push` does: `git remote add origin <new bare>` (which fails if origin still exists), then `git push --set-upstream origin HEAD`.

- **Before** (new tests, old `src/`): 8 failed | 15 passed
  ```
  × keeps main's history and pushes only main      expected new HEAD 'b2ef02f…' to be 'bb379aa…'
  × publishes untracked files nowhere              ls-tree contains 'notes.txt'
  × refuses … on a branch other than main / detached HEAD / uncommitted changes / shallow clone
  × publishes the course's symlinks as symlinks    expected '100644 blob …' to match /^120000 /
  × says how to finish by hand when create fails   message lacks 'git history are untouched'
  ```
- **After:** `fork.test.ts` 23/23. Full check: `pnpm typecheck` ok, `pnpm lint` exit 0, `pnpm test` 18 files, 205 tests passed.

**Built CLI, stub `gh` on PATH, local bare repos** (no `qa/` script exists for fork, so this was a throwaway harness): course with 3 lessons on `main`, plus `live-run-through` and tag `v1`, cloned. Run `fork my-repo`, then the course adds lesson 01.04 and the student fetches it as `upstream`, the way reset and pull do.

```
                        before (main)             after (this branch)
student main            ffea50a Initial commit    c7cee00 01.03 / ffec550 01.02 / bb876d6 01.01
refs in new repo        refs/heads/main           refs/heads/main
merge-base w/ upstream  (none)                    c7cee00
behind/ahead upstream   4  1   (diverged)         1  0   (fast-forward)
```

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Nothing in the code is one-way. Reverting brings the squash back. Repos students fork after the merge do keep full course history publicly, but that history is already public in the course repo.

**Blast Radius:** fork-only

- Only students who run `fork` after a release. Students who already forked keep squashed repos, and PR #91's unrelated-histories path in `pull` still serves them (untouched).
- Students who edited tracked files, or switched branches, before forking now get stopped with a fix instead of being forked.
- It relies on `gh repo create --push` pushing only the current branch (`git push --set-upstream origin HEAD`). The stub mirrors that; I didn't check it against a real GitHub repo.

## Deliberately left out

- **Tags:** never pushed. One edge case: with `push.followTags=true` in a student's global git config, `git push` also sends annotated tags reachable from main. I didn't override that.
- **Deleting other local branches** (`live-run-through`, `backup/*`). They're harmless and deleting is destructive.
- **Reconnecting the course remote if `gh repo create` fails.** The error says how to finish. `reset`, `pull` and the other commands reach the course through their own `upstream` remote, so a missing `origin` doesn't stop them.
- **Migrating students who already forked.** Out of scope, and `pull` already copes.
- **A `qa/test-fork.sh` script.** The harness above was throwaway and is not committed.
- No release or publish. The changeset is `minor`.

## Summary

A full front-end revamp of the website served by the Worker: the landing page, About, Privacy, Terms, Support, the API key claim page, the browser views of the developer resources (`/health`, `/llms.txt`, `/openapi.json`, …), and the 404. It keeps the MENTION//FORGE brand (canvas, ember, gold, signal) and adds a documented design system. **No pricing, payment, API, or MCP behaviour changes**, and JSON/text/MCP/402 responses are byte-identical to `main`.

### What changed

- **Design system** ([`docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md`](https://github.com/EnkiduHub/MentionForge/blob/claude/mf-revamp-2026-11/docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md)): `DESIGN_TOKENS` in `src/brand/tokens.ts` (colour, fluid type scale, 4px spacing, radius, motion, layout), mirrored by a layered `public/styles.css` (tokens → base → layout → components → pages → motion). Every text colour clears WCAG 2.2 AA on every surface. System fonts only.
- **Shared chrome** (`src/lib/site-chrome.ts`): one head (title, description, canonical, OG, Twitter, icons, JSON-LD), a sticky header with a Developers menu and a mobile menu (native `<details>`, so they work without JS), and a footer linking every product, developer, company, and directory page. Every page uses it; `public/index.html` embeds the same bytes, and a test enforces that.
- **Landing** rebuilt for buyers (developers, founders, marketers, agent builders):
  - hero with live status, one-line install, and an animated forge/signal visual
  - how it works, with the worked costs
  - a server-rendered report of the frozen Cloudflare Workers example
  - what every response includes, plus example requests mapped to tools
  - the free and paid tool gallery
  - quickstart (MCP `mcp.json`, Claude Code, REST curl with presets, how x402 works) with copy buttons
  - pricing with worked costs and the live `/stats` count
  - sources with live `/health` status, the comparison with raw `web_search`, FAQ, and a closing call to action
- **Secondary pages**: About (who it is for, sources, pricing, open source, listings); Privacy and Terms (table of contents, data cards, plain-language summary); Support (topic cards, copyable usage and portal snippets); the claim page (progress steps, key card, quickstart); developer-resource views (tab strip, summary chips rendered on the server, Raw/Copy); and a friendly 404 with technical details tucked away.
- **Copy**: plain, confident language. Prices ($0.02 USDC per call), the 10-call trial, sources, limits, and legal terms are unchanged. Native X and Reddit feeds are described as off by default. Internal jargon and notes are removed from visitor-facing text: "Captured from this Worker with a sandbox call", "this deployment", "payTo is here, not on the marketing landing", "(or Base Sepolia on staging)", and CAIP-2 ids in the status pill.
- **Motion**: CSS-first, using only transform/opacity/clip-path/filter:
  - signal rings breathe and source chips drift in the hero
  - the install command types itself once
  - the header gains depth on scroll (scroll-driven animation)
  - one-shot scroll reveals via IntersectionObserver
  - smooth FAQ expand
  - everything is disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`; without JS, all content is visible.
- **SEO**: unique titles and descriptions; canonical/OG/Twitter tags on indexable pages; and one landing JSON-LD `@graph` with Organization, WebSite, WebPage, SoftwareApplication, SoftwareSourceCode, WebAPI, and FAQPage. The SoftwareApplication offer uses the real `PRICE_USDC` in USDC, and the FAQPage is built from the visible FAQ. About, Privacy, and Terms add WebPage/AboutPage and BreadcrumbList. No ratings or reviews. `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml` were already correct and are unchanged.
- **Small fix**: the "Raw" link on browser views of query URLs (for example `/v1/entity?query=Cloudflare`) now keeps the query string instead of linking to a 400.
- **Tooling**: `npm run pages:render` (`scripts/render-static-pages.mjs`) regenerates the static twins (`public/{about,privacy,terms,support}.html`) from `src/lib/html.ts` and syncs the shared chrome into `public/index.html`; `-- --check` only verifies.

### Commits

1. Website: add design tokens and shared site chrome
2. Website: rebuild every public page on the new design system
3. Tests: leftover-text guard and site-wide page checks
4. Docs: design system, revamp report, screenshots, changelog

Each commit passes `tsc` and the unit suite on its own.

author: sorte1
body:
Some evaluator work grew with the input without being charged to the step or heap budget (review r2-eval-rest findings 3, 4, 5 and limits 8, 9). Each is now charged before the work is done, and refused cleanly when over.

- `replace` builds each `$&`, `` $` ``, `$'` and group expansion into the charged builder, so a template that repeats the subject stops at the string length cap instead of building gigabytes first (the 471-byte probe used to pass through the budget at 2.2 GB peak).
- `own_keys` spends a step per key, checks the array length cap and reserves the key list before building it; `for-in`, `Object.keys`, `values`, `entries`, `assign` and `JSON.stringify` all go through it, each time a loop is entered.
- A `switch` pays the same length charge for a string comparison as `===` (one shared routine).
- `RegExp.prototype.toString` returns a charged string; a regexp subject reserves its UTF-8 copy and offset map first, and an ASCII subject builds no map.
- New rows in `charged_enumeration.rs` and `resource_budgets.rs`, red on main.
- 133 frozen step records move, all from the new per-key, switch-length and replace charges.
- Cost against main: pins (723) identical, both obfuscator matrices unchanged, the four Krunker builds identical, game.js identical (instructions unchanged).

Changelog (Fixed): The evaluator charges `replace` expansions, key enumeration (`for-in`, `Object.keys` and friends), `switch` string comparisons, `RegExp` `toString` and regexp subjects to the step and memory budgets before doing the work, so a small decoder can no longer run past the memory budget or spin uncharged.

macOS window glass now derives its coverage from the theme's tokens, as Windows has since the 2026-10-21 decision. Before, macOS kept fixed numbers (25% frame / 6% sheet on dark Soft). Over a white window, the dark Tint sidebar then composited to a light grey, and its secondary text fell to about 1:1.

| | Before (Soft) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Tint / Zinc / Graphite / Amber Line | 25% | 82–85% |
| Mono / Amber / Gruvbox / Catppuccin | 25% (Catppuccin 55%) | 88–90% |

author: mkolehmainen
body:
Implements https://github.com/org-zpr/zl-zipline/issues/217 (Zodes epic org-zpr/zl-zipline#216). pd plan p15.

Schema-only change to `vs.capnp`. This is the interface contract that zl-zipline#218, #220, #221, #223, #224, #227, #232 and #233 consume.

## Contract

```capnp
struct Link {
  ...
  zprAddr  @4 :IpAddr;
  peerCn   @5 :Text;     # CN on the peer's CA-signed link certificate; the receiving
                         # node accepts the link only from a peer whose verified
                         # certificate carries exactly this CN. Empty = no peer passes.
}

interface VSHandle {
  ...
  visaIdsRequest      @7 () -> (res :Result(List(UInt64)));
  reportLinkStates    @8 (links :List(LinkStateReport)) -> (res :OkOrError);
  updateSubstrateAddr @9 (addr :SockAddr) -> (res :OkOrError);
  getLoginNonce       @10 () -> (res :Result(LoginNonce));
}

struct LinkStateReport { peerCn @0 :Text; state @1 :LinkState; }
enum LinkState { up @0; down @1; failed @2; }
struct LoginNonce { nonce @0 :Text; expiresAt @1 :UInt64; }  # unix seconds
```

Semantics (full text in the schema comments):
- **`reportLinkStates`**: snapshot. Each call lists every topology link and configured initial link, and replaces the node's previous report. A link that is not listed is not up. The node resends after every state change and after every (re)connect. The VS accepts entries for peers in the node's current topology or in the links policy declares for it (initial links included), even before `setTopology` delivers them. It logs and ignores anything else, because a report can race a topology change. Routing uses a link only when both ends report `up` (#224). Operator decision on pd g24: snapshot, and no free-text reason field.
- **`updateSubstrateAddr`**: sent over the existing session, with no re-authentication. The VS updates the address and re-sends `setTopology` to the node's peers. Returns `paramError` for an unspecified IP or port 0.
- **`getLoginNonce`** (scope added by the operator on **pd g27** (p17, #232), q2 = `vsnonce`): the VS mints the nonce for a Zode's own OIDC login. The binding to the calling node's actor and VS-API session lives on the VS side, so the schema carries no binding fields. The nonce is single-use and unusable after `expiresAt`. #232 sets the VS policy: 5 minutes, and at most 4 outstanding per node. A dead handle gets `authRequired`; too many outstanding gets `quotaExceeded`. The reason for the change: with a node-minted nonce, a subverted Zode could replay a stolen id_token.

Compatibility: capnp-rust 0.27 generates a default `unimplemented` body for every `Server` method, so the visa service builds unchanged. The Rust domain types in zl-zpr-common (`vsapi_types/topo.rs` `Link.peer_cn`, plus types for the new calls) are #218.

## Gate

zl-zpr-vsapi has nothing to build. CI here only runs `pr-notify`, so the local gate is the gate.
- `capnp compile -o- vs.capnp > /dev/null`: OK (Cap'n Proto 1.1.0) at c317ce8, 964393e, 3a1e01e and 8e20e82 (review rounds 1-2).
- Scratch, uncommitted zl-zpr-common `feature/zodes` worktree with the `zpr-vsapi` submodule at c317ce8, re-run at 964393e, 3a1e01e and 8e20e82 with the same result:
  - `make check` (`cargo fmt --check && cargo rustc --lib -- -D warnings`): OK
  - `make build` (`cargo build --all-targets -F all`): OK
  - `make test`: `test result: ok. 191 passed; 0 failed`

Deviation from the posted plan: `getLoginNonce` returns `Result(LoginNonce)` (nonce and expiry), not `Result(Text)`, because #232 holds the nonce for a limited time and the node needs the expiry.



Review round 1 (964393e, 3a1e01e): Codex P1 and Copilot both pointed out that the Re-Authorization doc block's exact-set rule contradicted the getLoginNonce login flow. It now documents the self-renewal exception from p17 (pd g27 q3): adapter actors keep the exact-set rule. A node's own actor may gain the user namespace with an unexpired, unused, session-bound getLoginNonce nonce, or drop it. The device RSA proof is always required, and any other mismatch is paramError. Each of the two places now cross-references the other.

Review round 2 (8e20e82): Codex P2 pointed out that a relay-link report sent before the first `setTopology` would be dropped. The VS now also accepts reports for links that policy declares for the node.

author: rahul-sinha1908
body:
## What happened

`pkg/firebase/fauth/delete_test.go` was four lines:

```go
func TestDelete(t *testing.T) { fauth.DeleteAllUsers() }
```

No build tag, no guard, no confirmation, pointed at the live service account. `DeleteAllUsers` iterates every user in the project and deletes each one.

So `go test ./...` — the ordinary gate before opening a PR, and the documented gate for this repo — destroyed the project's entire user pool. **On 2026-11-12 I ran exactly that, and it did.** `trendly-9ab99` is down to a single account, created minutes later by a fresh sign-up.

## Why it is worse than it looks

- **Firebase Auth is per project, not per Firestore database.** `dev` and `prod` share one user pool, so a test run on a dev branch removed production logins.
- **The profile documents survive**, and that is not a consolation. `managers` and `users` are intact, but an account recreated by signing up again gets a **new uid** and no longer matches documents keyed by the old one. The data is present and unreachable.

## The change

The test is deleted. The function stays — wiping a user pool is occasionally a real thing to want — but it now carries a header explaining why it must never have a test again, and has to be called deliberately.

## What this does not fix

Nothing recovers the deleted users; Firebase Auth has no undelete. Re-creating them with their original uids via the Admin SDK is possible and is the only path back to the surviving Firestore data, but it touches production and is not something to do unattended.

author: jeremiepas
body:
## Summary

Finishes and archives the `bunch-search-based-modularization` OpenSpec change (phases 5–7). Phases 0–4 were merged in #241.

- **Build (6.1):** `--cluster-algorithm leiden|bunch`, `--seed`, `--bunch-population`, `--bunch-threshold` (0..100), `--bunch-sa T0,ALPHA|on`, `--bunch-max-iterations`, `--bunch-max-files`, `--bunch-weighted`. Matching `graphos.yaml` keys: `clustering.algorithm`, `clustering.seed`, `clustering.bunch.*`. The CLI wins over the config, and `validClusteringConfig` range-checks the values.
- **Cluster stage:** dispatches through `runClustering`. Leiden output is unchanged byte for byte. Above the file cap, Bunch is skipped, the skip is logged and Leiden runs instead. The final partition (after the size cap) is re-scored and stored as `Analysis.analysisPartitionQuality`.
- **Report (6.3):** `GRAPH_REPORT.md` gains `Partition quality (<algo>): MQ = …, modularity = …, intra-edge fraction = …`, plus a line when Bunch was skipped.
- **`graphos clustereval landscape` (6.2):** reports basins, edge similarity, the random-partition baseline and the Leiden point. Writes `landscape.json` atomically, or prints it with `--json`.
- **Fixes:**
  - `UseCase/ClusterEval.hs` did not compile on `main` (invalid `\|` escape, two type errors), which probably explains the red `main` CI since #241.
  - Basin cluster ranges are now min..max.
  - The infeasible spec scenario `bip:100:0.75` = 3,712 edges is replaced (a bipartite graph on 100 nodes has at most 2,500 cross edges).

## Smoke results (recorded in the archived `tasks.md`)

- **Landscape, Graphos code graph** (170 files / 6,006 file pairs, 100 runs): two basins at MQ 2.45 and 2.50. Zero + High edge similarity is 36.0 %, against 0.8 % for `rnd:100:0.5`.
- **η ∈ {0, 50, 100}, annealing on/off:** final MQ stays in the same band. MQ evaluations are not monotone in η, and annealing *raises* evaluations — the design predicted the opposite on both counts.
- **Scaling (follow-up):** about 6 s per run at 170 files, but more than 18 min per run at 1,494 files. The default `--bunch-max-files 5000` is therefore far above what finishes in practice.

## Verification

- `cabal build --flag dev all` (-Werror): green.
- `openspec validate bunch-search-based-modularization --strict`: valid (before archive).
- `graphos-test` (run with `--skip 'small random graphs'`): 1,628 examples, 5 failures, 4 pending.
  - 44 new or touched examples pass: parser, config, `ClusterSpec`, `ClusterEvalSpec`, report. The golden skill fixtures are updated.
  - The 5 failures are in `tree-sitter grammars` (TypeScript AVI-1440, PHP ×2, Perl, C#). This PR does not touch extraction code; those specs last changed in #247.
  - `BoundedDeltaCommunitySpec` "delta update equals full rebuild on small random graphs (property)" hangs at QuickCheck case 14/100 (still running after 5 min of CPU on `--seed 1`). It only uses `clusterGraphWithResolution` and `boundedDeltaCommunityUpdate`, neither of which this PR changes; I could not confirm on `main` because `main` does not build.
- The other test suites in `cabal test all`: green.
- Lean module `Bunch/MQ.lean`: re-checked (only its path comment changed).

author: ccch1mneyyy
body:
## 来历

这批来自重构线第三波首批十片，在 `8020294d` 上整批跑过完整 Linux CI（run 43093440492，8 个实际 job 全过；汇总 job 因当时 GitHub Actions 故障没执行，本 PR 的 CI 会补上），再按 AGENTS.md「过度防御也是缺陷」「先做最短能跑通的」逐片审查。本 PR 只收判定可合的 7 片，每片一个提交，提交末尾的「Pro 编号」对应补丁编号。其中多数是上一批（#1045）退回后按最短修法重做的。

## 收进来的

- 5400：手机总开关。这是 #1045 里没套上的那一片（原 5200），现在以新 main 重做：不打扰页的 Shizuku/ADB 能力操作占住 `PhonePlugin.io` 时，用户返回主页关总开关，旧实现把关闭排在长操作之后。现改由已有的 `controlIo` 执行关闭，收尾仍排在 `io`，之后的开启排在收尾之后。没有新增状态标记，上一版在测试里自己模拟关闭流程的用例已删，只留两条验证实际 dispatch 函数排队与异常结果的测试。
- 5401：原件库 `collect` 加 `--output`，把已校验的对象平铺输出为 `sha256-<hex>` 并写 `SHA256SUMS`，用于钉死原件从上游下架后复制给自留发布；发布不再被许可材料的缺口挡住，GPL 对应源码的缺口只在文档里说明。另外下载响应超过锁中大小或未知大小上限（1 GiB）时停止写盘，构建源按 UTF-8 读取（非 UTF-8 默认编码下含中文会失败）。
- 5402：伙伴资源打包在 Windows 下（`shell: true` 跑 `npx.cmd`）给每个 esbuild 参数加双引号，framework 或临时路径含空格时不再被拆开。
- 5403：`rtbuild` 三段及以上补丁改同一文件时，第二段落盘后被中断，再次执行 `patch-dsh` 能认出已校验的中间状态并续跑；未知字节、断链仍拒绝。
- 5404：direct 的 DNS lookup 命中 hosts 时返回副本，调用方改动 `all:true` 的结果不再污染配置缓存，后续查询读到原值。
- 5410：Ark 视频任务返回 `OutputVideoSensitiveContentDetected` 时归到 policy 错误，不再报成 `generation_failed`；既有通用失败用例误用了这个码，改为 `InternalError`。
- 5414：Windows 下只设了 `ANDROID_HOME` / `ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`、build-tools 不在 PATH 时，`release_assets.py` 能找到 `aapt2.exe`。

## 没收的

另外三片已退回，各改一两行后再交：

- 5405（日志打码）：计数不再误遮，但带前缀的 token 字段名如 `GH_TOKEN`、`X-Auth-Token` 也不认了，比基底少遮。
- 5406（失败日志）：无条件删 `failure-normal.log` 会丢主配置那次失败的日志。
- 5407（会话级联删除）：读到坏标记会让以后所有删除都失败。

## 验证

- 本 PR 的 CI 以本 PR 为准。
- 各片在基底上的本地验证见补丁说明；这批没有改 `runtime/patches/`，桥和 skill 副本 `--check` 均通过。

#569 のフェーズA（お金の経路）です。申込導線・確認画面・規約などのフェーズBは、このブランチに積んだ別 PR にします。**A と B は一緒にデプロイする前提**です（A だけだと画面の文言が新料金に追いつかない箇所が残ります）。

## 変更点

### 料金と報酬
- 単発の動画添削を 1,500円 → **500円**（`reviewPriceYen`、`coaching_reviews.base_price_yen` の既定値）。
- コーチ報酬は 70% のまま → **350円**。チケットで払った回も 350円（割引前の名目額 500円 × 70%）。
- Web の料金は `lib/review-pricing.ts` に集約。

### チケット
- 旧商品（1枚・5枚）を販売停止にし、**6枚 2,500円**（`six`）を追加（migration 000159）。旧ロットは期限なし・行は消さない。
- 添削1回 = **1枚**（旧仕様の枚数から変更）。
- **有効期限＝決済完了から6か月**（`coaching_ticket_lots.expires_at`）。tick で機械的に失効（`expired` 列・台帳 `expire`、行は削除しない）。延長なし。失効した分は払戻しの対象外。
- 期限前に確保したチケットは、期限後に返却されれば消費、終了すれば失効側に戻す。
- 購入は Stripe Checkout のまま。18歳未満は単発と同じ**購入ごとの宣言**が必須（保護者同意・月上限のチェックは外した）。宣言は `minor_purchase_declarations` に `ticket_purchase` で記録。
- 販売の開閉は既存の `COACHING_TICKET_SALES_ENABLED`（既定は閉）のまま。

### 追加相談（600円）の販売終了
- `CoachingConsultation` を設定で **false に固定**（環境変数を立てても開かない）。Web 側も `coachingConsultationEnabled = false`。

### 決済の二重防止と戻り画面の確認
- 1件の申込みにつき Checkout Session は1つ（申込みの行をロックしてから作成・再利用）。
- 戻り画面は Stripe の Session 状態を取りにいって確認（`POST /v1/coaching/requests/{id}/payment/sync`、チケット購入は `GET /v1/coaching/tickets/purchases/{id}`）。完了なら Webhook と同じ確定処理を通す（冪等）。Webhook が正であることは変わりません。

### テスト
- 新規：失効（6か月）、期限前確保分の消費、戻り画面の同期（単発・チケット）、Checkout の単一化、追加相談の固定停止、6枚商品・価格スナップショット。
- 既存テストの金額期待値を新料金に合わせた。返金の部分計算を見ているテストは、旧料金の依頼を作る fixture（`legacyReviewAmount`）で従来の金額のまま確かめている。
- `go test ./...`・Web の vitest（866件）・tsc・eslint をローカルで通過。

## 判断したこと
- 「申込み時に消費」ではなく、カードの仮押さえ→返却時確定と揃えて「申込みで確保→返却で消費→終了で戻す」を維持。報酬 350円は返却時に記録。
- 旧ロット（1枚・5枚）は期限を付けず、1回1枚で使えるようにした。
- 単発の確認文言は実際の仮押さえ→確定のタイミングどおりに書く（フェーズB）。

- migration 000159 を含みます。

## Release 2.11 — Comprehensive restoration of the original Market Terminal interface

**Draft, not merged.**

### Source of design
The original [Market Terminal](https://github.com/rs88pvyhzz-code/market-terminal) repository is the reference. The exact base CSS from its `terminal_template.html` is copied into `terminal1_original_styles.css` (30 KB). A small compatibility bridge applies the original dark/amber/monospaced typography, cards, tables, inputs, chart styling and page spacing to current components, without copying old financial observations.

The original **10 top-level tabs** are restored: Overview, Markets, Equities, Company Research, Bonds & Rates, Analytics, ETF Trackers, Economics, My Watchlist and Data Quality. Separate Company Research and Analytics workspaces replace Terminal 2's nested navigation. Original market-news and summary flow stays distinct.

### Keep the Terminal 2 engine
The scheduled collectors, financial inputs, dated SEC research, market data, official DMO/FedInvest sources, historical risk/correlation, 14-indicator Overview, 132-ETF catalogue, ETF performance correction, after-tax bond yield calculations, currency conversion, source integrity and verification routines are preserved. **No pricing, total-return, yield or valuation-maths formulas changed.**

Delete access to the editable company DCF/reverse DCF, user WACC/growth/terminal assumptions, stress model and margin-of-safety tools. The **Valuation** tab is removed from navigation. Company Research retains basic sourced valuation **ratios** (P/E, forward P/E, P/B or EV/EBITDA, dividend yield, reported FCF yield and analyst-consensus target comparison) directly alongside company headline facts, without any editable valuation controls. The underlying calculation module stays in the source tree for existing unit-test compatibility but is no longer invoked in the user interface.

### Centralise technical source quality
New Data Quality area groups ETF catalogue/replication coverage, current company source coverage, DMO freshness/retrieval details, issuer/profile warnings and publisher-feed methodology. Security dates and **material investment-risk cautions** remain adjacent to the relevant data for safety and clarity. Simple one-click **SOURCE QUALITY & DATA CHECKS** routes replace repetitive long audit panels in the main research screens. Existing Data Quality sources, logs and audit files are retained.

### Verification before merge
- Full numeric, ETF-history, Shell/SEC, gilt YTM/after-tax, alert, and source-integrity Python tests retained.
- New desktop/iPad/mobile browser acceptance verifies all 10 workspaces and no broken navigation, 14 Overview figures, separate company research and analytics, six sourced read-only ratios, absence of manual DCF/stress controls, source-quality relocation and no horizontal page overflow.
- Existing source-backed original-ETF browser tests still run, including 132-fund catalogue, all four return bases, exact matched-date arithmetic, group/shortlist/cap and side-by-side original presentation comparison.
- Do **not** merge until both research and actual-production browser workflows and independent DMO checks are green. Review screenshots included in build artifacts.

No live site change until merge.

author: chrishargreaves
body:
## What changes

The footer of the Explorer and the custom viewer now reads, for example:

> Explorer 1.6.0 · Knowledge base: commit eac86fbf8 (10 Nov 2026)

The commit links to GitHub. The footer's repeated GitHub link is removed; the header icon still links to the repository.

## How the Explorer version is worked out

It is calculated each time the page is built, from this repository, so nothing has to be bumped by hand or by a bot:

- **Minor:** each entry in `changelog/CHANGELOG_FEATURES.md` with `<!-- explorer: feature -->` directly under its heading. 1.0 is the launch (2026-02-23); the six Explorer features since give 1.6.
- **Patch:** each first-parent commit that changes the Explorer's code (`generate_html_from_kb.py`, `assets/editor.css`, `assets/editor.js`) after the latest marked entry reached `main`.

The seven existing Explorer entries are marked. A comment at the top of the changelog (invisible on the website) tells people and agents when to add the marker. A shallow clone or a copy without git history shows no version rather than a wrong one. Both viewer workflows already check out with `fetch-depth: 0`, so they need no change.

## Date fix

The knowledge base date and commit now follow the first-parent line, so they give the merge into `main`. Previously git returned either the merge or the earlier branch commit, depending on what else had been merged; the two dates differed in 28 of the last 40 data merges.

## Also in this PR

`docs/plans/2026-11-11-001-feat-kb-data-version-plan.md`: the agreed plan for versioning the knowledge base data and schema. Not yet implemented.

## Tests

`tests/test_explorer_version.py` (15 tests) builds throwaway git repositories for each case: direct commits, features merged from a branch, a multi-commit fix branch counting once, marker placement, shallow clones, the merge-date lookup, and the footer. Each was checked to fail against a deliberately broken version of the code. Full suite: 583 passed, 3 skipped.

author: ronijaakkola
body:
## Summary

Adds a notice system: cards stacked above the bus bars that anything holding the stack can push. Notices come in five kinds (tutorial, info, warning, error, incoming call), as designed in the UI style board.

```gdscript
var notice := notices.push(text, Notice.Kind.WARNING, closable, seconds, action)
notice.action_pressed.connect(...)   # the action button; the notice dismisses itself after
notice.close_on(some_signal)         # clears when its cause goes away
notice.dismiss()                     # or clear it by hand
```

- `NoticeStack` (`%Notices` in the HUD) is newest on top, so a new notice never moves the ones showing. It replaces the course hint's `HintBox` and the `TowOffer` scene.
- **Motion:** a notice rises 8 px, grows from 96 % and fades in over 0.3 s with a strong ease-out. It leaves in 0.18 s toward the bus bars, then the cards above glide into the gap (0.25 s). Under Reduce motion they only fade.
- **While a planet or bus panel is open,** the stack hides. New notices wait until it closes, and auto-close countdowns pause.
- **Wired up:**
  - The course hint is now a tutorial notice.
  - Out of fuel is an error notice with "Tow (100 credits)", where it used to say "Request a tow".
  - New low fuel warning (`LowFuelWarning`): it shows when fuel falls to a quarter tank and clears once it's back above or runs dry.
  - Incoming transmission is a call notice whose phone rattles every 1.6 s. Nothing in the game calls yet: the debug panel has "Incoming transmission", "Test notices" and "Low fuel" buttons.
- **Theme:** the red `WarningNoticePanel` is now `ErrorNoticePanel`, `WarningNoticePanel` is the new amber one, and notices are 32 px tall. Action buttons are the quiet `SmallButton`.
- To keep `solar_system.gd` from growing, the nearest-planet search moved to `Planet.nearest_to()` (536 → 534 lines).

## Evidence

![Every notice kind stacked above the bus bars: incoming transmission, out of fuel, low fuel warning, info, a closable tutorial and the course hint](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ronijaakkola/game-off-2026/e092e527746a5c3b9efed53aaf902996c4396133/frame00000059.png)

`uv run tools/check.py all` passes. The updated tow and course hint tests in `solar_system_test.gd`, `planet_panel_test.gd` and `bus_panel_test.gd` pass. Auto-close, the close button, `close_on`, postponing while hidden and the low fuel warning were exercised with throwaway tests that aren't committed, since the feature is still taking shape.

Needs a visual check: `res://test/previews/notice_stack_preview.tscn` (add `-- dismiss` to watch one leave), and in the game the debug panel's notice buttons, including one while a planet is open.

## Blast radius

The solar system HUD: the course hint and out of fuel offer now go through the stack, and the old `TowOffer` scene is gone. `ui/theme.tres` changes the notice styles, which only notices use. `Planet` gains a static helper.
