author: djkcrazh
body:
> **Stacked on #4.** Base is the import branch so this diff is Phase 2 only. Retarget to `main` after #4 merges.

## What this is
A Python harness that measures how well something can work out how to read a farm's spreadsheet, how much human effort that leaves, and how often it gets something wrong **without anyone noticing**. Arm A is the rule-based guesser that ships today; a local AI model and judge arms plug in next with the same scoring. Full explanation, run commands and assumptions: [`evals/README.md`](../blob/djkcrazh/evals-phase2/evals/README.md).

- **Python on purpose** (stdlib + pytest): the evaluations are what people must be able to read and change. The importer stays TypeScript and is called through one JSON bridge (`scripts/eval-bridge.ts`), so scores are for the real code, not a port.
- **Corpus**: 100 generated files, 80 Ghana-style + 20 English stress, 70/30 dev/test. Pigs and answer keys come from **code**, never a model. Reproducible byte for byte from a seed (a test proves the committed files are current).
- **Grader**: read -> propose -> score (silent vs flagged mistakes) -> simulated human -> real importer dry run -> compare every row with the true pig. Two humans are simulated: one fixes only what the app flags (measures silent risk), one also checks every column (measures effort). Arms can never set the "human confirmed" flags.
- **Reference arms prove the grader can fail**: `oracle` must be 100%, `empty` must be bad. 34 Python tests, including mutation tests that corrupt the answer key.

## Baseline (ARM A), 100 files
| | |
|---|---|
| headers it was taught | 100% mapped correctly |
| headers it was **not** taught | **0%** (by construction: it looks names up in a list) |
| imports perfect, human fixes only what is flagged | 46% (rest: pigs imported with silently missing data) |
| imports perfect, human also checks every column | 100%, ~3.7 actions per file |
| files it cannot read at all today | 15 of 100 |

**Do not read the overall "60% of columns right" as the baseline's quality**: it mostly reflects how many unseen headers I assumed (35% Ghana-style / 60% stress). The *unseen* row is the real test for an AI proposer.

## Found by the harness
1. **Optional columns dropped silently**: an unrecognised Weight/Mother/Father/Notes/Castrated header is ignored and the app says nothing.
2. **A hole in the importer's safety net, fixed here** (separate commit): `checkMapping` never verified that a mapped column exists, so a mapping naming a made-up column read blank cells and looked fine. New blocking problem `unknownColumn`; takes the file's real header list because a parser can omit an all-empty column. 5 new TS tests.
3. **Date styles the importer cannot read**: `dd-MM-yyyy`, `dd/MM/yy` (in the real weekly report), `dd-MMM-yy`, `d MMM yyyy`, plus a title line above the headers.
4. `Mother ID` was missing from the alias list.

## Assumptions to challenge
All corpus proportions are **my guesses** (in one place: `evals/nhoma_evals/styles.py`); the unseen-header list is only as hard as my imagination; the simulated human is always right. Replace with real Ghanaian files when available.

## Verification
- [x] `evals`: `pytest` 34 passed; `oracle` 100% under both humans
- [x] TypeScript: `tsc` clean, `eslint` clean on changed files, `vitest` 123 passed, `npm run test:db` 12 checks
- [ ] A human read of `evals/README.md` and a skim of a few generated files in `evals/corpus/cases/` (the spot-check step of the plan)

body: The live job typed the security code and then stopped on “Could not find Verify / Continue / Confirm / Submit”. The retry landed on Send security code again, so the code was never accepted and GHL did not trust the browser. This reads the code from the Google Workspace mailbox that already receives it (the `et***@leadgenisys.com` inbox). There is no new user. ## What the worker does now After Send security code: 1. If a “remember / trust this device” box is on the page, it is ticked. When the label says “N days”, that number is stored on the job. HighLevel commonly labels this about 30 days. That is the usual wording, not a time measured from this login. The last live page did not include the checkbox text, so the next run’s job detail is what will show the real label. 2. The code is typed into one-digit boxes when GHL splits them, otherwise into the single code field, with the input events React expects. GHL often submits on its own once the boxes are full, so the worker pauses, presses Enter, then clicks a verify control. The click matches Verify, Continue, Confirm, Submit, Confirm Code, Verify Code, Login, and Sign in, including an aria-label or a `type=submit` button. 3. The code counts as accepted only after the page leaves the code screen and the agency dashboard path loads. `https://app.gohighlevel.com/?url=%2Fsub-accounts` is still the login interstitial, not the dashboard. 4. If the page stays on the code screen, the job detail records the URL, button labels, input labels, checkbox labels, and a short slice of the page text. Digit codes in that text are blanked. No screenshot is stored. 5. Playwright `storageState` is encrypted with `VAULT_MASTER_KEY` and stored in Postgres `AppSetting` key `ghlSubaccountWorker.session`. Render has no persistent disk, so it is not a file. It is refreshed after the agency dashboard loads. A trusted-device cookie is only present once the code was accepted. ## Automatic code, then the existing paste For about 3 minutes after Send, the worker polls that mailbox every 8 seconds. It keeps only HighLevel security-code mail received after the click (15 seconds of clock skew). The From address has to be `gohighlevel.com`, `leadconnectorhq.com`, `msgsndr.com`, or a HighLevel sender, and the subject or body has to be a security, verification, or login code. Older codes and other mail are ignored. The mailbox is opened with IMAP `EXAMINE` (read-only) and the message is fetched with `BODY.PEEK`. Nothing is marked read and nothing is deleted. If those four env vars are unset, or no matching mail arrives within 3 minutes, the page stays open for the rest of the 12 minutes. Paste the code in Settings → GHL sub-accounts, or `POST {"otp":"..."}` to `/api/webhooks/ghl-subaccount-worker`. ## What to set on Render On the existing mailbox that already receives the codes. Do not create another Google user. 1. Turn on 2-Step Verification for that Google account. 2. A Workspace admin allows app passwords: Admin console → Security → Authentication → 2-step verification → allow users to generate app passwords. IMAP for Gmail also has to be allowed. 3. Signed in as that mailbox: Gmail → Settings → See all settings → Forwarding and POP/IMAP → Enable IMAP → Save. 4. Google Account → Security → App passwords → create one named “Genisys Hub”. The 16-character password is `GHL_OTP_IMAP_PASSWORD`. It is not the account password. 5. Set these on the genisys-hub service: ``` GHL_OTP_IMAP_HOST=imap.gmail.com GHL_OTP_IMAP_PORT=993 GHL_OTP_IMAP_USER=the full address of that mailbox GHL_OTP_IMAP_PASSWORD=the 16-character app password ``` `GHL_OTP_IMAP_USER` is the address GHL already emails. `GHL_AGENCY_EMAIL` should be that same address when that person is the agency login. `HUB_ALERT_CHANNEL` is unchanged: the channel name without `#`, and the Slack bot has to be in it. A failed Slack post still shows on Settings → GHL sub-accounts. ## Checks `npm test`, eslint on the worker files, `tsc --noEmit`, and `npm run build` passed. Not deployed.

author: vincentn-waivern
body:
## What and why

Phase 3 of `docs/eu-gdpr-plan.md`: requests, complaints and breaches for entities under both laws.

**Requests and complaints (decision 2)**
- `data_protection_jurisdiction` gains `uk_eu`. New requests and complaints take their entity's law, so an entity under both gets `uk_eu`. A jurisdiction outside the entity's laws is refused.
- **Strictest-of clock.** A dual request runs the EU deadline: weekends only, no clarification pause. The month is the same under both laws and UK law only ever adds time, so the EU deadline is never later than the UK one.
  - The request page says so.
  - The Schedule 2 and 3 exemptions and the health opinion are still offered. They are marked as answering the UK obligation only; the EU side needs Member State law under Article 23.
- **Proportionate search.** The UK proportionate-search relief is not applied to dual requests, because the EU obligation still asks for the full search. This differs from the plan, which offered it marked as UK only. Applying it would narrow the search the stricter law still requires.
- A dual complaint has the s.164A thirty days, which applies wherever UK law does.
- `regulatorFor('uk_eu')` names both regulators: the Information Commission, or an EU authority on the Article 77(1) terms.
- Existing requests and complaints keep the jurisdiction they were opened under. Their deadlines do not move.
- A law enforcement request to a competent authority under both laws starts under Part 3, recorded as a UK request, since Part 3 is UK law alone.

**Organisation default dropped**
- `organisation.data_protection_jurisdiction` is removed, along with its setting on the requests page.
- The requests and complaints summaries keep `organisation.defaultJurisdiction`, so 1.0 readers are unaffected. It is now read from the default entity (`uk` where UK law applies, else `eu`), and `docs/integration-api.md` says so. The breakdown by law stays in Phase 6.

**Breaches**
- `breach.laws` (from the entity, narrowable on an entity under both) and `breach.affected_states` (EEA codes).
- `breach_decision.authority_code` records which authority a notification decision concerns.
- `authoritiesToNotify` (in `lib/gdpr/establishment.ts`, next to `regulatorFor`) gives one notification target per authority:
  - UK law or Part 3: the Information Commission.
  - EU law, with an EU establishment: the lead authority, or the home State's only authority. Otherwise a placeholder that says to record the lead authority.
  - EU law, with no EU establishment: each affected State's authority (EDPB Guidelines 9/2022). Germany is a placeholder until a Land authority is chosen. A notification to any authority of that State satisfies it.
- Each target has its own obligation and its own seventy-two hours.
  - The breach page lists them under "Notifications to supervisory authorities".
  - The decision form asks which authority a notification went to. A notification must name one where several are owed, and it must be an authority the breach's laws owe. A judgement such as "still deciding" can cover them all.
  - "Not required" and the Article 34 decision stay shared.
  - The breach's headline clock and the sweep use the most urgent authority's clock. The breach becomes "notified" only once every authority owed has been told.
- Narrowing an entity's law narrows its dual breaches as well as its processing records. It is refused while a breach is under the dropped law alone.

**Migration 0104**
- Adds the enum value and the new columns, and drops the organisation column.
- Every breach's laws are set to its entity's (Part 3 breaches to `uk`).
- Existing notification decisions on UK-only breaches are tagged `gb-ico`, as are notifications already made on breaches now under both laws (every breach was handled in UK terms before this release), so they still count and only the EU authority shows as owed.

**Help** is updated in the requests, complaints and breaches topics.

## How it was tested

- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format`, `ALLOW_DEV_SIGN_IN= pnpm build`.
- `pnpm test`: all 1,783 tests pass.
- The new `tests/eu-requests-breaches.test.ts` covers:
  - A dual request due on 25 December 2026, with a clarification pause, gets the EU date, which is earlier than the UK one.
  - s.164A applies under both laws.
  - Both regulators are named.
  - `authoritiesToNotify` for UK, EU and both, Part 3, and no establishment with and without affected States.
  - One obligation per authority.
  - Dual defaults for requests and complaints, and `uk_eu` refused on a UK-only entity.
  - A dual breach that needs a named authority, where notifying one authority leaves the other running.
  - A German Land authority satisfying the German placeholder.
  - Entity narrowing refused because of an EU-only breach.
  - After the code review: a placeholder with no State met by the authority chosen, an authority the laws don't owe refused, a judgement recorded without an authority, "notified" only once all are told, the migration's handling of an earlier notification, and Part 3 for a competent authority under both laws.
- Not checked in a browser.

## Deployment notes

- Database migration included (0104). It drops `organisation.data_protection_jurisdiction`; any earlier change to it remains in the audit log as `organisation.dsr_jurisdiction_set` events.

author: corynezin
body:
## What and why

Agent avatars become GitHub-style identicons: a 5x5 left-right mirrored grid in a pastel colour drawn from the agent's name, on a light gray circle with a hairline border (dark gray in dark mode). They're simpler and easier to tell apart in a list than the Notionists faces. An agent's avatar stays the same whatever model it runs. The company rings and capability backgrounds are gone, and the model is still read out in the VoiceOver label. People keep their Personas faces.

The "Model avatars" toggle is removed entirely, so agents always get identicons.

## Source commits (squashed)

- 43d4f8d Agent avatars use GitHub-style identicons inside the company rings
- 32a5762 Pastel transparent agent identicons without rings
- 9ba69ec Thin neutral circle border on agent avatars
- 2bf4349 Light gray avatar background and border like GitHub

## Fixes made in review

- **Toggle removed:** the Settings "Avatars" section, the `modelAvatars` preference (schema and default), the `ModelAvatarsEnabled` context and its provider in `AppRoot` are gone. So are the avatar steps of the Maestro settings flow and the matching comment in `scripts/maestro-parity.sh`.
- **Stored preference:** an existing `modelAvatars` value on a phone is cleanly ignored. The loader reads only known keys, so it isn't treated as damage, and it's dropped on the next save. A new test covers this. The preference tests that used `modelAvatars` as their sample setting now use `requireFaceId`, `idleFold` and `updateHomeServerId`.
- **Hash quality:** plain FNV-1a barely changes its low bits when names differ only at the end, and those are the bits the cells come from. In 200 names like `agent-0…agent-199`, 13 shared a pattern. I added MurmurHash3's finalizer and now use one salted hash for the cells and another for the hue, instead of four hashes of which two were never used.
- **Misleading parameter:** `identiconSvg(seed, bg, capability === 'flagship')` passed a parameter named `dark` that only made flagship agents a little lighter. I removed it.
- **Dark mode:** the hard-coded `#f0f0f0` circle would have been a bright disc on dark screens. It now has a dark counterpart (`#2c2c2e` / `#48484a`).
- **People's avatars:** the 1 pt border had also been applied to people's avatars. It's now only on identicons.
- **Dead code:** I removed `@dicebear/notionists` (package.json and lockfile), `CAPABILITY_COLORS`, `COMPANY_RING_COLORS`, and stale comments. `avatarModel` stays because it feeds the accessibility label.
- **Tests:** these check grid shape and symmetry, determinism, few collisions and a good spread of hues over 200 similar names, the fill rate of about 3 in 4, and the SVG structure (one square per lit cell, background on request, transparent without one).

## Checks

- `npm run -s lint:imports`: pass
- `npm run -s typecheck`: pass
- `npm run -s test:unit`: 626/626 pass
- `npx expo export --platform ios`: succeeds
- `npm ls --package-lock-only`: lockfile consistent
- No offline journey covers avatars. I haven't run the Maestro parity flow (it needs a simulator), but it's trimmed to match.

## Overlap

Stands alone on `main` (base-5). On the person's main, d415bb9 (settings-rework group) removed only the Settings row and left the preference in place. This PR removes the whole feature, so the settings-rework PR may hit a small conflict at the Avatars section in `features/settings/Screen.tsx` and `model.ts`. That's resolved by dropping both sides.

author: kikobeats
body:
## Problem

`payment:session` and `payment:update` wrote `metadata.country` and `metadata.ipAddress` to Stripe. Nothing reads either field. Behind Cloudflare, `ipAddress` also held the Cloudflare edge instead of the visitor (`request-ip` checks `x-forwarded-for` before `cf-connecting-ip`): 561 of the 796 Microlink customers that had it.

## Change

- Delete `src/get-metadata.js`.
- `payment:session`: the checkout session metadata is only `{ planId }`, which `payment:webhook` reads.
- `payment:update`: sets the default payment method and leaves the customer metadata untouched.
- Commands no longer receive `ipAddress`: `routes.js` stops computing it and `interface/route.js` passes only `headers` (the webhook needs `stripe-signature`).
- Remove the `req-country` and `request-ip` dependencies.

The existing `ipAddress` values were already removed from all 796 live Microlink customers.

## Testing

- Ran against Stripe test mode: `payment:session` (5 tests) and `payment:update` pass.
- New: the session metadata is exactly `{ planId }`. Dropping `planId`, or adding `country`/`ipAddress` back, turns it red.
- New: `payment:update` leaves a customer's existing metadata untouched, even when an `ipAddress` is passed. Writing metadata again turns it red.
- The README no longer claims tom fills customer metadata.
- Through the HTTP route, `payment:webhook` still receives `stripe-signature`.
- CI is green. The Slack test runs nothing in CI, because its file defines no test without `TEST_SLACK_WEBHOOK`; that is unchanged by this PR.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches Stripe checkout/session and customer update behavior in the payment path, but narrows metadata rather than adding new logic; main risk is if anything external relied on `country`/`ipAddress` in Stripe metadata.
> 
> **Overview**
> Removes **IP/geolocation-based Stripe customer metadata** from the payment flow. `get-metadata.js` is deleted along with `req-country` and `request-ip`; the HTTP layer no longer resolves or forwards `ipAddress` to commands.
> 
> **`payment:session`** now attaches only `{ planId }` to checkout session metadata (what `payment:webhook` already consumes). **`payment:update`** updates the default payment method and **does not merge** metadata onto the Stripe customer. README no longer claims automatic customer metadata enrichment.
> 
> Tests assert session metadata is plan-only and that `payment:update` preserves existing customer metadata.

author: axdeontour
body:
## Was

`nc-pre-commit` ruft `nc-timezone-check` auf, sobald die App das Skript `timezone:check` in ihrer `package.json` hat und der Commit `lib/*.php` oder Dateien unter `src/` anfasst. Ohne das Skript bleibt der Schritt aus.

## Warum freiwillig

Der erste Lauf des Checks meldet je App 8 bis 22 Stellen Bestand, die einmal durchgesehen werden müssen. Wäre der Schritt immer an, würde ein Tooling-Sprung jede App blockieren, die das noch nicht getan hat. Mit dem Skript als Schalter stellt jede App den Check scharf, wenn ihr Lauf grün ist. Derselbe Eintrag dient dem CI-Schritt (`npm run timezone:check`).

## Außerdem

README-Korrektur zur Verbreitungs-Messung: Als Vormessung zählt im Workflow nur der eigene Kommentar. Dem Token des Workflows zeigt GitHub die Org-Mitgliedschaft nicht (im echten Lauf vom 11.11. beobachtet: eine von Hand gepostete Messung wurde übergangen).

## Getestet

Drei Tests in einem Wegwerf-Repo: mit Skript blockiert ein `date('Y')`, ohne Skript bleibt der Schritt aus, mit Skript und sauberem Code läuft der Hook durch. Suite: 248 grün.

author: avelino
body: ## Problem Roam stamps pages, not only blocks, with `create-time` and `edit-time`. `RoamPage` did not deserialize them, so every imported page lost its creation date even with `--preserve-timestamps` (5,535 pages on a real graph). ## Fix - `ImportPage` gains `created` / `edited` (the Logseq and Obsidian adapters set `None`). - The Roam adapter reads both fields. - With `--preserve-timestamps` the emitter writes them as `created::` / `edited::` page properties, the same names the block timestamps use. A merged journal (two source pages, one date) keeps the earliest creation and the latest edit. A source attribute of the same name wins and is not duplicated. - Without the flag they count in `timestamps_dropped`, like block timestamps. ## Tests - `page_timestamps_land_as_page_properties_on_opt_in` in `crates/outl-import/tests/roam_e2e.rs` (fails on main). - Ran locally with rustc 1.99.1 (the toolchain pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`, installed via rustup; the cc-task sandbox has rustc 1.85.1 without rustfmt, so nothing ran there): `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p outl-import --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p outl-import --all-targets`, all passing. author: dokyit
body:
## What this changes

Follows #19, which was merged before these commits were pushed.

**Brought to Windows**
- **Dictation on the PC itself, in the Mac's voice row.** Windows' own speech recognizer never answers an app without package identity (seen live: the mic heard a person, and no word came back), and Trek's installer doesn't package it. So the composer's mic now dictates with Whisper (whisper.cpp running OpenAI's multilingual base model) over the microphone as WASAPI records it.
  - Words show in grey italics about once a second as you speak and settle after ✓, with the waveform, ✕ and ✓ as the design draws them.
  - Windows' voice-typing panel (Win+H) never opens by itself any more. It's offered only on a processor that can't run Whisper (no AVX2).
  - The speech model (141 MB) downloads from Hugging Face the first time the mic is clicked. It's pinned to a revision and checked against its SHA-256, and its progress shows in the voice row. ✕ stops it, and the next click carries on from the same byte.
  - It's kept in `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, out of a roaming profile. **Settings › General › Dictation** removes it.
  - Being offline, a full disk, a bad download, and a muted or switched-off microphone each say what to do.
  - Nothing it hears leaves the PC (docs/PRIVACY.md). A packaged Trek would still use Windows' own recognizer.
- **Video transcripts for agents without installing whisper.**
  - `watch_video` on Windows falls back to the same on-PC Whisper, with the model the mic downloaded. Trek names its folder in `TREK_DICTATION_DIR`.
  - It never downloads the model for a video: the agent is told the mic gets it, or to install whisper.
  - The parity ledger now marks this as the same as the Mac: 42 of 65 features.
- **Browser:**
  - a page's dialogs, permission asks and links to other apps go to Trek's bar;
  - Trek answers dialogs for an agent at work;
  - popups keep `window.opener`, and `window.close()` closes them.
- **Computer use by element** (UI Automation): the Mac's outline and refs, press, click or type by ref, and wait for an element.
- **API-key and local-model agents** run commands in Git for Windows' bash, never WSL's. cmd.exe is the fallback, and background tasks end with the session.
- **Share window:** Windows' own share window opens from More….
- **Banners** start Trek when it has quit: they're protocol-activated toasts with the thread's `trek://` link.
- **Video posters** come from Explorer's thumbnails.

**Fixed**
- **Dictation:** a take ended after Windows' 5-second wait for the first words. It now waits a minute.
- **Voice mode's look:**
  - ✕ and ✓ are circles on Windows too.
  - The waveform's silent dots are drawn at the design's shade on both platforms. Their opacity was applied twice, leaving a line that was barely there.
- **Hygiene:**
  - the uninstallers remove Trek's `trek://` and app id keys;
  - the pairing TLS key is the owner's alone;
  - skills keep their links (symlink, junction or copy).
- A thread's link handed to a running Trek no longer brings the main window forward first.
- The PowerShell driver knows the iPhone tool, as the Mac's does, and the `dictate` and `dictate-file` verbs.

**Building on Windows** now needs CMake and LLVM (libclang), because whisper.cpp is compiled from source. It's built through `vendor/whisper-rs-sys`, a patched copy of whisper-rs-sys 0.15 with whisper.cpp's GPU backends left out (5 MB). The patch is three changes to its build script, marked "Trek:":
- **Only the folders its libraries are installed in go on the link path.** Upstream adds all 111 folders of CMake's build tree, about 11,000 characters. On Windows, Cargo puts those on PATH for every program `cargo test` and `cargo run` start. Past cmd.exe's limit, commands stopped being found, and six tests that start cmd failed in CI's Windows jobs.
- **The static runtime (/MT), optimized**, as described below.
- **`GGML_NATIVE` off:** a release is built for the AVX2 baseline and runs on any x86-64 PC that has it, not only on processors like the build machine's.

NOTICE names whisper.cpp, the patched copy and the Whisper model.

**Trek still starts without the Visual C++ redistributable.** Built the default way (/MD), whisper.cpp's C++ made `trek.exe` import `msvcp140.dll`. Neither CI's hardening test nor `release.ps1` would have caught it, because both looked only for `vcruntime140`.
- whisper.cpp now gets the static runtime (/MT) from Trek's copy of whisper-rs-sys.
- Both checks refuse a `trek.exe` that names `vcruntime140`, `msvcp140` or `vcomp140`.
- Tests and examples link the runtime the shipped programs do.
- docs/CROSS_PLATFORM.md has the rule for the next piece of native code.

**Every platform gate belongs to a feature, and a sweep of the rest.** 139 gated files (646 gates) had no ledger feature naming them.
- **The rule (trek-parity):** a file with platform gates must be named in a feature's `code` or `tests`. Files from before the rule are listed as `unclaimed` in `gates.toml`, and that list only shrinks. A new unclaimed file, or one that gains a gate, fails even when the counts are being recorded. It's tested by adding a gate to a legacy file: even the update run refuses.
- **The sweep:** four read-only reviewers read all 139 files and found about 25 differences the ledger didn't have.
  - 8 new features: path-chips, mcp-servers, codex-sandbox, verification-skills, private-files, explorer-names, contrast-fixes and editor-tabs.
  - Notes on computer-use (`open_app` and PC keys), browser-extensions, snapshots, video-transcripts and terminal-previews.
  - 40 files claimed: the list is down to 99.
- **Fixed now:**
  - Windows' browser says why a page failed, and reloads a crashed one (it was a generic page, and a blank one).
  - The Explorer refused `../x` but on Windows took `..\x`, `C:\x`, `todo:v2.md` (a hidden stream) and `nul`. It now keeps names in the folder by Windows' rules too.
  - Settings no longer tells Windows users that transcripts need Python whisper.
  - npm's notices are quiet on the Mac too.
  - A flows test that skipped the Mac now runs there.
  - CI checks the capture build (`--features shots`) on both platforms.
- **Where it stands:** Windows matches the Mac on 47 of 73 features, and the Mac is the weaker side on 4. The rest is listed in the ledger, each with a note on what would close it.

**Every platform split now belongs to a feature, and what claiming them found is fixed** (the last 28 commits).
- **The rest of the gated files are claimed.** Four read-only reviewers read every remaining gate (394 in 99 files). author: jorge-menjivar
body:
This finishes v0.2.0 before it is tagged: Tidy hears the user's dictation context, and the README and links follow the repository's move.

## Commits
1. **Point at the repository's new home.** The coverage badge and report are served from `super-libre.github.io/super-voice-tidy`. `source` keeps the old name, which GitHub redirects and the registry entry's `repo` must match.
2. **Spell the user's vocabulary their way.** Super Voice gives a backend that declares `[capabilities] context = true` the user's dictation context, post-processors included (`instantiate_backend` builds the same headers for stage 2). Tidy now declares it and reads `x-voice-vocabulary`, falling back to `x-stt-vocabulary`. It ignores the prompt, because it is instructions and rules can't follow them.
   - **New rule `vocabulary_spelling`, on by default:** where the transcript has a term in different letter case, Tidy writes it the way the user spelled it, e.g. `iphone` becomes `iPhone`. Only the case of letters already there changes. It runs last, so `iPhone` keeps its spelling at the start of a sentence.
   - **Which terms it applies:** only ones that can't be ordinary words. That means several words with a capital (`Super Voice`), or a word with a capital past its first letter and a lowercase letter (`iPhone`, `GitHub`, `macOS`). A single word that is all capitals, all lowercase or just capitalized (`IT`, `rebase`, `Go`) would recase everyday words, so it's left alone.
   - **Terms are never cut:** the filler and stutter rules leave a term alone, so `Ah Puch` keeps its `Ah` and `Bora Bora` isn't a stutter. A term doesn't protect a stutter on itself: `Rust Rust` still collapses.
   - **Bad headers:** a vocabulary header Tidy can't read counts as no vocabulary, so it never fails a transcript.
   - **Contract:** stays `v2`. OpenAI declares `context` on `v2` too, and its `min_client` is still 0.2.4-beta.1.
3. **Promote Tidy in the README, the way the other backends do.** It's the same short format as Mistral, OpenAI and Deepgram: what Tidy does, with the vocabulary in its example, then what it is. The settings app already describes each rule from `backend.toml`.

## Testing
- `just ci` passes: fmt, clippy on the wasm component and the host (pedantic, `-D warnings`, also clean on Rust 1.99), the component build, and 55 tests. 14 of them are new, for spelling, whole-word and multi-word matching, ordinary words, sentence starts, fillers, doubles, the switch, idempotency, odd terms and the header.
- Super Voice's manifest parser admits `backend.toml`, with `context = true` and one `post_processor` model.
- The built component in wasmtime, given `um i pushed it to github from my iphone iphone in bora bora . super voice uh works`:
  - with no vocabulary: `I pushed it to github from my iphone in bora. Super voice works`;
  - with `["iPhone", "GitHub", "Bora Bora", "Super Voice", "Go"]` as `x-voice-vocabulary`, or only as `x-stt-vocabulary`: `I pushed it to GitHub from my iPhone in Bora Bora. Super Voice works`;
  - with `vocabulary_spelling = false`: `bora bora` survives, but nothing is recased;
  - with an unreadable header: the same as no vocabulary.
- The README's example is the component's real output.

## After merging
1. Tag the merge `v0.2.0`.
2. Then take jorge-menjivar/super-voice#583 out of draft.

author: draarivpatel-ui
body:
Closes #2419

### Summary

When `DirCache` is configured with a positive `max_paths` and `listings_expiry_time=None`, `DirCache.__iter__` yields directly from `self._cache` (an `OrderedDict`). Iterating `items()` or `values()` via `MutableMapping` looks up each key through `__getitem__`, which calls `self._cache.move_to_end(item)` and raises `RuntimeError` (`OrderedDict mutated during iteration`) whenever at least two entries are present.

Snapshot `list(self._cache)` inside `__iter__` when `self.max_paths` is set and `listings_expiry_time` is `None`, matching the existing key snapshot path used when `listings_expiry_time` is configured while keeping unbounded dict iteration unchanged.

### Testing

- Added parameterized regression tests in `fsspec/tests/test_dircache.py` covering `items()` and `values()` across `max_paths` (`None`, `0`, `1`, `2`, `3`) and `listings_expiry_time` (`None`, `60`), including non-default LRU order after reads.
- `python -m pytest fsspec/tests/test_dircache.py -q` (`33 passed`)
- `python -m pytest fsspec -q` (`3,237 passed, 281 skipped, 2 xfailed`)
- `ruff check fsspec` and `ruff format --check fsspec` passed

author: jeremydmiller
body:
Fixes #5520

Three 7.0 default flips from #5344. `RestoreV6Defaults()` restores each one, and an explicit setting always wins.

| Setting | 6.x | 7.0 | Opt-out |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WolverineHttpOptions.RejectUnparseableHeaderValues` | `false` | `true`. It is resolved through `ResolveVersionDefaults(V6DefaultsRestored)`, the same way as `RejectUnparseableQueryValues`. | `opts.RejectUnparseableHeaderValues = false` |
| FluentValidation ProblemDetails for HTTP | needed `UseFluentValidationProblemDetailMiddleware()` | automatic when `WolverineFx.Http.FluentValidation` is referenced and `UseFluentValidation()` is called | `opts.DoNotUseFluentValidationProblemDetailMiddleware()` (new) |
| `WolverineOptions.EnableRelayOfUserName` | `false` | `true` | `opts.EnableRelayOfUserName = false` |

### How it works
- **Header binding:** a nullable backing field, resolved in `ResolveVersionDefaults`. The F# codegen error message and the docs now mention the header option too.
- **FluentValidation:**
  - New internal seam `IHttpVersionDefaults` in Wolverine.Http. `MapWolverineEndpoints()` applies the registered implementations after the user's configuration and `ResolveVersionDefaults`, before endpoint discovery. Wolverine.Http.FluentValidation gets an `InternalsVisibleTo` grant to use it.
  - `UseFluentValidationProblemDetail()` registers the package's implementation. The package's `[WolverineModule]` calls that method, so it also works with `ManualOnly` discovery when that method is called.
  - The implementation adds the middleware only when all of these hold:
    - `UseFluentValidation()` was called (it checks `WolverineFluentValidationMarker`);
    - the 6.x defaults were not restored;
    - the user did not opt out.
  - `UseFluentValidationProblemDetailMiddleware()` is now idempotent, so an explicit call plus the default gives one validation frame. There is a test for that.
  - **Policy order:** the automatic policy is appended after the user's policies. So, like every policy that inserts at index 0, its frames come before middleware that user policies inserted at index 0. An explicit call placed mid-configuration behaves as before.
- **User name:**
  - `EnableRelayOfUserName` getter is `_explicit ?? !V6DefaultsRestored`.
  - Claim hook: `WolverineHttpOptions.UserNameClaimType` (string, null by default). When set, the generated code calls a new overload, `UserNameMiddleware.Apply(httpContext, messageContext, "sub")`, which reads `User.FindFirst(claimType)`. When null, the existing two-argument call is generated unchanged, so code already pre-generated still matches. This stayed a small option, so nothing was split out to 7.1.
- Regenerated the committed `codegen write` output for the `CICodegenDrift` projects. The only change is the relay line `UserNameMiddleware.Apply(httpContext, messageContext);` in 5 files: DeepMiddlewareUsage, StaticCodeGenDemonstrator and AotSmoke Marten/Polecat/Fisher.

### Tests (Alba)
- `restore_v6_http_defaults` has new rows for each flip: the 7.0 default, after `RestoreV6Defaults()`, an explicit setting winning, and an explicit opt-out. It also covers the claim-type hook, including a principal with no `Identity.Name`, as with an Auth0 access token.
- `restore_v6_defaults_tests`:
  - a `CoreRestorations` row for `WolverineOptions.EnableRelayOfUserName`;
  - a theory showing an explicit setting wins in either order.
- `envelope_username_tracking`: the propagation test now relies on the default, and the "disabled" test sets `false` explicitly.

### Docs
- `migration.md`:
  - three new rows in the 7.0 defaults table;
  - the Wolverine.Http section now says "seven" and has bullets for the header and FluentValidation flips;
  - a new section, "The user name travels with every message by default". It says plainly that the user name goes in the `user-name` header to every transport and the outbox, and shows how to turn that off.
- `http/security.md`: the same warning, plus `UserNameClaimType`.
- `http/headers.md`: strict header binding.
- `http/validation.md` and the snippet in `http/policies.md`: the automatic middleware and the opt-out.

No CHANGELOG entry, per CLAUDE.md.

author: jakechampion
body:
## Summary

Part of #14399, item 1.

With no `-target`, `fern` built for arm64-linux on each host. On an x86-64 host:

- `fern -o hello x.fern && ./hello` stopped with "Exec format error".
- `fern x.fern` printed ARM64 assembly.
- `fern -run x.fern` needed qemu-aarch64.

The default is now the target that the compiler itself runs on, from `target_arch()` and `target_os()` (`run_with_gate` in `compiler/fern.fern`). `fern-oracle` has the same default, from the Go runtime. A Go host that is no Fern target keeps arm64-linux.

A build that names `-target` is not changed.

## The sweep

The earlier note on the issue said that the cost is in the tests and scripts that call `fern` with no `-target`. I looked for them:

- The Makefile, `scripts/` and the workflows name the target in each build that has `-o` or `-run`.
- The e2e tests with "default" in their messages (`arm64_native_default_test.go`, `arm64_default_string_reclaim_test.go`, `arm64_darwin_native_test.go`) name `-target`.
- One test read ARM64 assembly from a build with no `-target`: `TestSelfHostCLIWritesAssemblyToStdout`. It now reads the assembly of the host.

The search is by text, so a caller that it did not find is possible. The full suite on this pull request is the check for that.

## Tests

- `TestSelfHostCLIWritesAssemblyToStdout` reads the assembly of the host with no `-target`. It also builds with `-o` and no `-target`, and the host must start that binary.
- `TestHostTargetIsATargetOfThisMachine` checks the default of `fern-oracle`.

Run before the push, all pass:

- `make build`
- `go vet ./cmd/fern ./internal/testing/e2ecompiler`
- `go test ./internal/testing/e2ecompiler/ -run 'TestSelfHostCLI|TestSelfHostFeatureCensus$'`
- `go test ./cmd/fern -run TestHostTarget`
- `make fmt-check`
- By hand on x86-64 Linux: `fern -o`, `fern -run` and `fern-oracle -o` with no `-target` give a binary that runs, and `-target arm64-linux` gives an ARM64 ELF.

Not run locally: the e2e suites and the darwin, android and wasm lanes. CI runs them.

## Docs

The help text, the README, the install tutorial, the tooling reference and `docs/ARRAY-ALGEBRA.md` state the new default. CLAUDE.md names arm64-linux the primary target, not the default target.

Items 3 and 4 of #14399 are not in this pull request.

author: agent-xai-grok[bot]
body:
## Why

An overseer change is proven only live today: merge, wait for a ship, watch the realm. #2281 asks for the offline half, so a change is held to captured realm truth before it merges. This is its first slice: the foundation, with the awaiting-live-check pass left for later.

## Summary

```text
fidelity/record.py     RecordingReader(real reader) -> guarded SELECT reads, in order
        |                 derive.claims(capture)  -> expected claims (credited record)
        |                 verify.problems(fixture) -> refuse if claims do not re-derive
        v
fidelity/scenarios/*.json     provenance, surface, args, reads, expect
        |
fidelity/replay.py     ReplayReader(reads) -> the real Chronicle read path, offline
        v                 compare(expect, projected output)
tests/test_fidelity_*  every scenario on every PR; no realm, database or network
```

- Fixture format: provenance (`realm` or `synthetic`), surface and args, ordered reads, expected claims, and the tickets a realm fixture proves. A synthetic fixture cannot name tickets.
- Recorder: runs an existing read path over a recording reader, guards each statement with the liveproof select-only guard, can alias names, derives the claims from the capture and keeps the fixture only after the verifier agrees.
- Replay runner: answers only the statements the capture holds. A statement it lacks, or a recorded read the code no longer makes, fails the replay.
- Deriver: states the claims from the credited tally (a clear needs every expected encounter credited, whatever the run's own outcome word says). It imports nothing from the overseer, and a test pins that.
- Evidence, before: with the completion-flag shortcut put back in `guildrun.every_boss_fell` locally, the not-a-full-clear scenario fails with "the record says clear False, the overseer said clear True". After: reverted, the scenario passes. The suite also carries this as a mutation test.
- The three scenarios shipped are SYNTHETIC, written to test the machinery, and say so in their names and provenance. They are not realm captures. No realm capture was available to this run, so the seed from one real completed Blackrock Depths run is not here.
- `docs/FIDELITY.md` explains how to capture a scenario and where expected outputs come from.
- `python3 -m fidelity.replay` verifies and replays every scenario by hand.
- Checks: `scripts/check-locally.sh all` passed (16275 tests, ruff clean); the fidelity tests add under a tenth of a second.

## Acceptance criteria

- Meets #2281 criterion 3: the replay suite runs in CI on every PR with no realm, database or network access, inside the existing check job.
- Meets #2281 criterion 5: docs/FIDELITY.md covers capture and the rule that expected outputs never come from the code under test.
- Does not yet meet #2281 criteria 1 and 2, which need a capture from one real completed Blackrock Depths run. This PR lands their machinery: the format and recorder, and a synthetic not-a-full-clear scenario that a mutation test turns red on a completion-flag shortcut. The real capture is the one missing piece and is tracked on the ticket.

Size: M

## Out of scope

- Criterion 4: advancing awaiting-live-check tickets on replay evidence, a second pass after this lands.
- The real Blackrock Depths seed, which needs a capture from the realm.
- Other surfaces (loot attribution, goal transitions, stuck classification) and any change to the liveproof probes, the realm or the bridge.

Refs #2281

author: zm2231
body:
Streaming ASR now uses FluidAudio's 15 s-safe sliding-window preset. Without it, any session longer than about 17 s silently returns an empty or truncated transcript on the pinned FluidAudio 0.14.8.

```diff
-                let manager = SlidingWindowAsrManager()
+                let manager = SlidingWindowAsrManager(config: .streaming)
```

## Why

`SlidingWindowAsrManager()` uses `SlidingWindowAsrConfig.default`. In 0.14.8 that is 10 s left + 15 s chunk + 2 s right, so windows reach 27 s (432,000 samples); the first one is 17 s. Parakeet TDT v3's input is fixed at 15 s (240,000 samples), so every larger window fails.

FluidAudio catches each failure in `attemptErrorRecovery` and only writes an OSLog line. `streaming_asr_feed` keeps returning `Ok(())`, and `streaming_asr_finish` returns whatever text survived, so callers never see an error.

This is FluidInference/FluidAudio#686. Upstream fixed it in FluidInference/FluidAudio#689 by changing `.default` to 2 + 11 + 2, first released in 0.15.3. Bumping to 0.15.3 would also remove Qwen3 (FluidInference/FluidAudio#676, see #16). `.streaming` already exists in 0.14.8 with the same 2 + 11 + 2 layout, so this fixes the bug on the current pin without touching Qwen3 or any Rust API.

## Verification

A 58.7 s, 16 kHz mono recording of continuous speech, fed in 100 ms chunks through `streaming_asr_start` / `streaming_asr_feed` / `streaming_asr_finish`:

| Build | Result |
|-------|--------|
| `main` (186d4e7) | `""`, with 5 shape-mismatch errors logged (windows of 272,000, 379,520 and 432,000 samples) |
| `main`, same recording cut to 8 s and 14 s | Correct transcripts |
| `main`, `transcribe_samples` on the full recording | Complete transcript |
| This PR | Complete transcript, no errors |

Unit and integration tests pass. `cargo test --doc` has one failure, `FluidAudio::init_qwen3_streaming` (`done` is undefined in the example), which also fails on `main`.

## Summary

`_example_ref` in `code-generators/API-Reference-Code-Generator.py` handled a referenced schema with `properties` or a `type`, but returned an empty example for one defined only by `oneOf`. Properties that reference `ParameterSet` rendered as `"parameterSet": ,` or `"parameters": ,`, which no JSON parser accepts.

Changes:
- `_example_ref` builds the example from one of the schema's non-null `oneOf` variants. It picks an object variant first, because it shows the schema's keys, and falls back to the first variant. The table type label and description stay as they were.
- `_example_additional_props` uses a string value for `oneOf` alternatives that include `string`. `0` is both a `number` and an `integer`, and `oneOf` accepts exactly one match, so `{"key": 0}` didn't conform to `ParameterSet`. The examples are now `{"key": "string"}`. The only other schema that reaches this branch is `CreateBacktestRequest.parameters`, so the Create Backtest request example changes the same way.
- `code-generators/test_api_reference_code_generator.py` gets `ExampleRefTests`, next to the `NullableTypeTests` suite that #2879 added to the same file.

Since this PR opened, #2877 changed List Backtests' `parameterSet` to an array of `BacktestParameter`, which fixed that page's examples. author: cmungall
body:
This adds an entry for craniosynostosis 6, named ZIC1-Related Craniosynostosis. It is an autosomal dominant coronal craniosynostosis caused by heterozygous variants in the final exon of ZIC1, a zinc-finger transcription factor; ClinGen classifies these variants as gain of function.

Closes #17042

## Scope
The entry covers only the final-exon variants. A 2026 cohort (Watts et al., PMID:42028696) and ClinGen both separate two other ZIC1 disorders, so neither is part of this entry:
- **Exon 1–2 loss-of-function variants**, which cause a neurodevelopmental disorder without craniosynostosis. This is mentioned in the notes.
- **ZIC1/ZIC4 deletions**, which cause Dandy-Walker malformation. This is listed as a differential.

The name follows the existing gene-named craniosynostosis entries (ERF-, MSX2- and SMAD6-related). It counts as established because MONDO carries "ZIC1 craniosynostosis" as an exact synonym.

## What the entry covers
- **Mechanism:** seven pathophysiology nodes, connected by 24 causal edges.
  - The chain runs from a final-exon variant that yields a stable, C-terminally altered protein, through altered ZIC1 target-gene regulation and disturbed Zic1-Engrailed patterning of the supraorbital regulatory center, to premature coronal suture fusion.
  - Branches cover deficient calvarial ossification, ZIC1-dependent brain development and vertebral patterning.
  - 18 of the 20 phenotypes are connected. Strabismus and downslanting palpebral fissures are not, because both also occur without craniosynostosis and no source proposes a mechanism for them.
- **Variant effect:** recorded as GAIN_OF_FUNCTION, as ClinGen states. A REFUTE evidence item records the reduced reporter activity Watts et al. found for p.Glu402Ter, and a mixed loss/gain model is recorded as an emerging hypothesis.
- **Models:** the Zic1-deficient mouse and a Xenopus embryo ZIC1 RNA-injection assay.
- **Differentials:** Muenke syndrome, Saethre-Chotzen syndrome, TCF12-related craniosynostosis, Dandy-Walker syndrome due to ZIC1/ZIC4 deletion, and Gomez-Lopez-Hernandez syndrome.
- **Treatment:** cranial vault expansion with fronto-orbital advancement.
- **Evidence:** 73 items from 10 PMIDs plus the ClinGen record (Definitive, autosomal dominant). Every snippet is a single sentence.

## Validation
- `just validate-disorders` passes with 0 issues, all 73 snippets verify, and `validate-terms` passes.
- The per-file and whole-KB gates and the cache checks pass.
- After rebasing on current `main`, the six baseline gates pass: snippet length, title snippets, snippet grading, reference titles, retired support prose and gene activity grounding.

## Notes for review
- The brain-imaging and strabismus frequencies come from a cohort that pools both allelic classes, and each evidence explanation says so.
- A 3q chromosomal inversion near ZIC1 is mentioned in the notes but not recorded as a variant, because ZIC1 expression was not measured.
- Deep research: the falcon key was rejected (HTTP 403), so the report comes from the OpenScientist fallback. All 22 of its references resolve, and `preflight-dr` passes.

author: oracle989
body:
Claudit 4.4.0, its last release, runs no audit: `/claudit:claudit`, or asking Claude for Claudit, replies only with a notice that Claudit is retired, to run `/doctor` and then `/doctor prompt-audit`, and why, at https://acoz.dev/blog/retiring-claudit/. This is the plugin PR of the two-PR release; the pointer PR (release lock, retired catalog description, regenerated indexes, README install lines) follows after acceptance and the `claudit-v4.4.0` tag. The plan, reviewed in two rounds, is in [`docs/changes/210-retire-claudit/plan.md`](docs/changes/210-retire-claudit/plan.md).

Refs #210

## Behaviour

- **Skill** (`plugins/claudit/skills/claudit/SKILL.md`): replies with the fixed notice and nothing else, ignores arguments, and has no pre-approved tools or model override. Its description makes Claude load it only when Claudit is named.
- **Package README**: opens with a `> **Retired.**` note as Shipshape's pages do, gives the uninstall command and links the last auditing version at tag `claudit-v4.2.0`.
- **Manifest**: version 4.4.0, the retired description, keywords `configuration`, `best-practices`, `retired` ("audit", "optimization" and "grading" dropped).
- **Removed from the package:** the auditor agent, the scan helper, the shipped feature catalog and the apply reference. The package now holds the manifest, the skill, README and LICENSE.
- **Removed from the repository, because they load or grade the removed helper:** the Claudit eval runner (`bin/claudit-eval`), its suite (`evals/claudit/`), the six `tests/test_claudit*.py` files, their recorded gate reports and the `.gitignore` entry for eval results. They stay in history at the base commit `8a0840f`.
- **Docs:** the acceptance procedure (`docs/acceptance/claudit.md`) is rewritten for 4.4.0, with the candidate checks, the pre-publication gate on the post URL, and the published-artifact checks from the plan. The eval baselines page gets a "Historical" note, and its two links into the removed suite are pinned to `8a0840f`. The repository guide's eval lines no longer name `bin/claudit-eval`. The plan gains the round-2 low: the reviewer's published update path keeps one temporary home from before the pointer merge to after it.

Nothing under `plugins/writing-for-humans/` and nothing in `releases.json`, `catalog.json` or the generated indexes changes here.

## Validation

All on head `066c22c` (tree `602da91`), Claude Code 2.1.322.

- `bin/ci`: exit 0, `Using Python 3.11.15`, `{"version": "2026.11.05.5", "conforms": true}`, `Ran 249 tests`, `OK`.
- Test count: `origin/main` runs 439 tests; the removed `test_claudit*.py` files run 190 of them on `origin/main`; 439 − 190 = 249. (On `origin/main` one of those 190 failed in my worktree run; it is among the removed files.)
- `bin/check-marketplace --base origin/main`: exit 0, `Marketplace valid: 2 plugin(s); package versions checked` (4.4.0 > 4.2.0).
- `bin/sdlc check`: `{"version": "2026.11.05.5", "conforms": true}`.
- `claude plugin validate .`: passed. `claude plugin validate --strict ./plugins/claudit`: passed, with one note that the README has no install line, which is intended for a retired plugin.
- Changed paths outside the plugin and the removed Claudit tooling: only `.gitignore`, the two acceptance docs, the plan and the repository guide.

### Candidate checks (plan's Proof 1 to 4)

Scripts set `HOME` and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to fresh temporary directories for installs; model turns ran on the normal login with `--plugin-dir`, `--setting-sources project,local`, `--strict-mcp-config`, stream-json and `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1`, in a synthetic Git repository. Graders read the whole output.

1. **Install** from a local directory marketplace: `claudit@quickstop` 4.4.0 installed; the cache holds `plugin.json`, `LICENSE`, `README.md` and `skills/claudit/SKILL.md`; no `agents` directory.
2. **The notice, and no audit:**

   | Prompt | Tool calls | Reply has "retired", `/doctor`, `/doctor prompt-audit`, post URL | Init: `claudit:claudit` skill, no `auditor` agent | Cost |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | `/claudit:claudit` | none | yes | yes | $0.057 |
   | `/claudit:claudit --read-only hooks` | none | yes | yes | $0.042 |
   | "audit my Claude Code setup with Claudit" | one: `Skill` `claudit:claudit` | yes | yes | $0.047 |
   | Same plain prompt, no plugin (control) | one `Bash` | no post URL | no `claudit` skill | $0.047 |

   The init agents list was `claude`, `Explore`, `general-purpose`, `Plan`, `statusline-setup`. All three plugin runs replied with the notice verbatim.
3. **Consumer state:** the synthetic repository's status, index and file hashes are identical before and after; no `~/.cache/claudit` exists.
4. **Update from 4.2.0:** installed 4.2.0 (from tag `claudit-v4.2.0`) from a local directory marketplace, then the same marketplace served the candidate. `claude plugin marketplace update` and `claude plugin update` gave "updated from 4.2.0 to 4.4.0"; the 4.2.0 cache stays with `.orphaned_at` (expected), and the 4.4.0 cache has the notice and no agents.

## Docs impact

The acceptance procedure, eval baselines note and repository guide are updated here. The retired notes in the repository README, the repository guide's opening paragraph and the catalog description go in the pointer PR.

## Rollout and rollback

Merge by rebase. Nothing is advertised until the pointer PR merges, so reverting this PR is the rollback until then. After publication, a fault in 4.4.0 is fixed forward with 4.4.1; restoring the 4.2.0 record is only for a failure of the pointer PR. No secret or new credential.

## viewer-annotations-shared: Bun's fs.watch on Linux misses a rename

The annotation store writes atomically: a temp file renamed over the target. Under **Bun on Linux**, `fs.watch` misses that rename, so the test's in-process viewer server never saw the MCP write and broadcast nothing.

GitHub Actions turns colour on, which puts escape codes between `✓` and the element id. The test now strips them. It passes with `FORCE_COLOR=1` on macOS and in the Linux container.

author: harvey-ryan
body:
Fixes the bursts of `[assertGuildManager] 429 … backing off 30000ms` in the admin error log. **v1.25.1.**

### Why it happened
- **Two callers, one tight limit.** Discord limits `GET /users/@me/guilds` tightly per person, and two places asked it separately:
  - `/auth/me` asked on every call, with no cache;
  - `assertGuildManager` asked again whenever its own cache expired.
  
  So the second call often came straight after the first and got a 429.
- **Repeated log lines.** One request runs the manager check several times at once. Those checks shared one Discord call, but each logged the 429, which is why every Ref showed up 4–5 times.
- **Wrong answers after a 429.** The check then stopped asking Discord for at least 30 s, though Discord usually asks for about 1 s. With no cached list it answered "not a manager", so officers could get a 403. `/auth/me` silently returned no servers.

### Fix
`lib/userGuilds.ts` holds one cached server list per person:
- `/auth/me` accepts a list up to 2 min old. `assertGuildManager` accepts 30 min, plus the copy kept in the session, which survives restarts.
- Concurrent callers share one Discord call, and a failure is logged once.
- A 429 asking for ≤ 5 s is waited out and retried once. Longer ones only pause for Discord's own Retry-After and serve the last list meanwhile.
- If nothing is cached, the manager check answers 503 "Discord is busy, try again" (which the website retries) instead of a wrong 403.

### Tests

author: jwinarske
body:
SKIA_REF was `chrome/m150`, and `build-skia.sh` checks it out directly, so every clone took whatever the branch tip was that day. Milestone branches keep moving after a milestone goes stable, because fixes are cherry-picked onto them, so two builds weeks apart were different Skia with nothing in the prefix recording which commit produced it.

Downstreams key their build cache on this value, which turns that drift into a second, quieter bug. acl-cxx's key is `skia-<os>-<arch>-chrome-m150-<wcs rev>`: it carries the branch name but not the commit, so once a prefix is saved the key never changes again. A stale prefix is then served indefinitely, and the first rebuild after a cache eviction picks up a different Skia with no key change to show it.

## What changed

- `SKIA_REF` is now the commit, `59690b53c2d37dd7a3dc7cc8e5718384f51ca200`. That is the current `chrome/m150` tip and has been unchanged on that branch since 2026-06-02.
- `SKIA_MILESTONE` keeps the branch name, since a bare sha tells a reader nothing about where it came from. Bump the two together.
- A guard rejects any `SKIA_REF` that is not a full 40-character sha, so this cannot regress by someone setting it back to a branch.
- The checkout is now `--detach` at the sha, and the script prints the commit and milestone it is building.

## Verified

- `bash -n` clean.
- The guard accepts the 40-char sha and rejects `chrome/m150`, an empty value, a 7-char short sha, and a 40-char string containing non-hex.
- `59690b53` is fetchable by sha from the Skia remote (`[M150][graphite] Guard SDF inset with define`, 2026-06-02), so a full clone plus detached checkout resolves it.

Not verified here: a full Skia build at the pin. The prefix acl-cxx built in CI today came from this same commit, since the branch has not moved since June.

author: jacboy
body:
`./build-xcframework.sh --debug` bricht mit dem bash ab, das macOS mitbringt (3.2.57):

```
./build-xcframework.sh: line 69: BUILD_FLAGS[@]: unbound variable
```

## Ursache

- `BUILD_FLAGS=()` bekommt nur bei `PROFILE=release` den Eintrag `--release`. Mit `--debug` bleibt das Array leer.
- Das Skript läuft mit `set -euo pipefail`. bash vor 4.4 behandelt `"${BUILD_FLAGS[@]}"` bei einem leeren Array unter `set -u` als ungesetzte Variable und bricht ab.
- Das steckt seit dem ersten Commit (32c2186) im Skript. Es ist nie aufgefallen, weil alle Aufrufer (`build.rs`, `ci.yml`, `package-macos-app.sh`, README/CONTRIBUTING) den Release-Build verwenden und mit bash ab 4.4 (z. B. aus Homebrew vorne im `PATH`) kein Fehler auftritt.

## Änderung

Eine Zeile: `${BUILD_FLAGS[@]+"${BUILD_FLAGS[@]}"}`. Das ist die übliche Schreibweise, die in jeder bash-Version funktioniert: Ein leeres Array ergibt nichts, ein gefülltes Array wird unverändert und korrekt zitiert übergeben.

## Getestet

Mit `/bin/bash` (3.2.57) auf macOS:
- `./build-xcframework.sh --macos-only --debug` läuft durch, die Bibliothek liegt unter `target/apple/aarch64-apple-darwin/debug/`. Vorher brach das Skript mit dem Fehler oben ab.
- `./build-xcframework.sh --macos-only` (Release) läuft wie bisher, `--release` wird weiterhin übergeben.

@dr-prinz, magst du kurz drüberschauen? Das Skript stammt von dir, und ich wollte sichergehen, dass `--debug` so gedacht ist und ich nichts übersehe.

author: manfromth3m0on
body:
Fixes what was noticed when comparing with bought patterns: pieces that should match came out slightly different, and outlines were jagged. Four parts.

## 1. Symmetric garments (on by default)
The body model is exactly symmetric: every vertex has a mirror partner to 0.001 mm, 188 vertices lie on the centre line, and no triangle crosses it. `garment::build` now uses that.

**Building on one side**
- The design is cut into the right half of the body only:
  - curves drawn on the left are flipped across;
  - loops such as necklines and waists are clipped at the centre line, with their ends placed exactly on it;
  - curves drawn along the centre (|x| < 15 mm) follow the mesh's centre line exactly.
- Centre-line vertices are pinned in the mesh-editing code: never moved, relaxed or collapsed off `x = 0`.
- The half is then mirrored into the full cut body, so every vertex has a known mirror partner (`BuiltGarment::mirror`).
- Mirrored curves are reversed, so "left of the seam" maps to the same side and allowances land on matching pieces.

**Flattening (`outline::mirror_pieces`)**
- **Pairs** (such as left and right fronts) are matched triangle by triangle. One layout is replaced by the reflection of the other, so they are exact mirror images with identical stretch figures.
- **Pieces on the centre line** are made exactly symmetric: `uᵢ ← ½(uᵢ + F(u_{m(i)}))`, where `F` is the best-fitting reflection.
- **Labels:** pieces show *(mirror image of panel N)* or *(symmetric)*. `PanelReport.mirror_of` records this.
- **Notches** split each seam into equal parts, which is symmetric under reversal, so mirrored pieces get mirrored notches.
- **One-sided designs:** `GarmentDesign.asymmetric` (the web app's **Asymmetric design** checkbox) keeps the old build of each side as drawn.

## 2. Smooth outlines (`outline::smoothed_outline`)
- **Corners kept:** each stretch of outline between corners is smoothed separately. A corner is where the seam or neighbouring piece changes, or where the outline turns more than about 57° measured 2σ either side.
- **The smoothing:**
  - a Gaussian in arc length, σ = 10 mm by default;
  - ends held by point reflection;
  - twicing (`2G − G∘G`) so curves don't shrink;
  - points move only across the outline, never along it.
- **Inside of the piece:** the piece is re-solved with ARAP while its outline is held at the smoothed positions. `arap_pinned` generalises ARAP to pin any set of vertices.
- **Settings:** CLI `--smooth-outline MM`, web "Smooth outlines (mm)", 0 = off.

## 3. Even re-triangulation (`garment::remesh`)
- **Why:** cutting curves into the body leaves slivers. Those caused the max-stretch spikes and stopped seam matching early, because a matching step that would fold a sliver is rejected.
- **What:** after cutting, the garment area alone is remeshed with Botsch–Kobbelt isotropic remeshing, 5 rounds. The target edge length is the area's median edge length, kept within 8–20 mm. Each round:
  - split edges longer than 4/3 L;
  - collapse edges shorter than 4/5 L (along curves only between consecutive curve vertices);
  - flip edges towards Delaunay (`EditMesh::flip`);
  - relax the inner points within their tangent plane and project them onto the body. Projection uses a grid-accelerated closest-point lookup.
- **Fixed:** curves and the centre line. In a symmetric build only the right half is remeshed, before mirroring.
- **Effect:** thin triangles (angle under 15°) drop 3–9×. For the catsuit that's 626 → 80; the remaining ones sit between curve vertices. It takes about 0.3 s natively.

## 4. Body smoothing (`smoothing`)
- **Why:** latex spans the navel, collarbone hollows and nipples instead of following them.
- **What:** before flattening, the inside of each piece is smoothed over σ = 15 mm: `N = 2σ²/(λh²)` umbrella-Laplacian steps, with twicing so the large-scale curvature (bust, shoulders) is kept.
- **Held fixed:** seam and outline vertices. Moving them distorted the tiny triangles where curves meet; an early version reached σ 40+ at the crotch.
- **Pressure map:** still uses the real body.
- **Settings:** `--smooth-body MM`, web "Smooth body (mm)", 0 = off. The flattening library defaults all smoothing to 0, so its analytic tests keep exact geometry.

## Results (default body, 40 % lengthwise)
| | max σ before → after | worst seam mismatch before → after |
|---|---|---|
| top | 12.6–21.7 → 2.2 | 13 mm → 1.7 mm |
| leggings | 9.1 → 1.5 | — → (matched) |
| catsuit | 13.1 → 2.1 | 21.6 mm → 2.5 mm |
| cincher | 1.3–2.8 → 1.7 | 1.2 mm → (matched) |

95 % stretch figures are unchanged (about 1.2–1.3). Pairs are identical, and centre pieces are symmetric.

## Tests
- **Smoothing:** a ±1 mm zigzag on a flat sheet drops more than 5×; corners and width are kept; nothing folds.
- **Body smoothing:** a 3 mm, 10 mm-wide bump on a 60 mm tube flattens to under 1 mm while the tube keeps its radius (±0.5 mm).
- **Templates:** every template builds symmetric, with each vertex's mirror at `(−x, y, z)`. Fewer than 1.7 % of triangles have an angle under 15°; it was 4–7 % before remeshing.
- **Mirroring:**
  - the cincher gives two exact mirror pairs, and the top's two pieces are each exactly symmetric (distances agree to 1e-6);
  - `asymmetric` builds each side as before;
  - `symmetrise` yields an exact reflection.
- **Web smoke test:** the top's pieces show as symmetric; the cincher still gives 4 pieces with Asymmetric ticked.
- **Locally:** fmt, clippy, test, doc and the wasm build all pass with `-D warnings`. The smoke test passes in about 13 s.

- **Sector** `packages/solid-federation-vocab/sectors/environment/`:

author: cyberpunk738
body:
## What changes
Drop could show transfer success before the receiving browser confirmed delivery, cancellation could advance to another queued file, and the completed screen's Send Another File button did not open a picker.

This change adds SHA-256 integrity checks, exact byte/chunk validation, receiver acknowledgements, timeout handling, cancellation from either device, queue stopping on failure/cancellation, retry/removal controls, explicit download links, and working repeat transfers. Files are capped at 100 MB because the portable receiver assembles them in memory. Progress stays below 100% until verified receipt; verification confirms browser receipt, not a completed disk save.

The landing page and shared pairing/transfer surfaces adopt the supplied design reference's silver backgrounds, rounded cards, dark pill buttons and red accents. The hero uses an original CSS/icon device illustration. Zoom, keyboard focus, reduced motion, connection status and transfer errors are supported.

Connection handling now guards stale callbacks, limits each host to one peer, times out incomplete setup, and reconnects signaling when possible. Optional TURN configuration is served by /api/ice. Unused custom HTTP/WebSocket signaling implementations and production demo controls were removed. README, environment examples and GitHub Actions describe the active PeerJS architecture.

## Validation
- npm test: 11 passing protocol tests covering exact payloads, empty/repeated/reverse transfers, corruption, truncation, missing acknowledgements, cancellation/retry from both ends, stalled buffers, channel failures, oversize rejection and Blob URL cleanup.
- npm run build: passed.
- npm run typecheck: passed.
- git diff --check: passed.
- Uploaded Git tree matches the locally tested tree: 076abbeb724cd4afc4a03964aae7baffc70cd66d.

## Verification limits and configuration
Browser visual QA and live WebRTC transfers are unverified: the managed preview service passes --host and --strictPort to next dev, which rejects those arguments. Tests use two engines over an ordered in-memory transport, not two actual browsers. Manual browser/mobile checks are listed in the README.

TURN support requires deployment credentials; no relay service has been provisioned. Without them connections remain STUN-only. Interrupted file transfers require retry from the beginning; lost data connections require a fresh pairing. The 100 MB limit reduces memory pressure but does not implement streaming-to-disk. Pairing still uses bearer session codes without a separate device approval prompt.

author: amalsaidov
body:
Yes, happy to contribute this to Apache SeaTunnel.

### Purpose of this pull request

Closes #13232. Part of #11007 (migrate connector/API validation to declarative `OptionRule`).

`MultiTableSink` checked `multi_table_sink_replica < 1` in its constructor and threw an `IllegalArgumentException`. The range was enforced, but the rule was not declared in `MultiTableSinkFactory.optionRule()`, so `FactoryUtil.createMultiTableSink()` ran `ConfigValidator` against an empty rule and the check only fired later, during sink construction.

### What changed

- `MultiTableSinkFactory.optionRule()` now declares `MULTI_TABLE_SINK_REPLICA` with `Conditions.greaterThan(MULTI_TABLE_SINK_REPLICA, 0)`. `FactoryUtil.createMultiTableSink()` already validates the factory rule before constructing the sink, so `0` and negative values are rejected at that point with an `OptionValidationException` naming the option.
- Removed the duplicated `replicaNum < 1` check and its comment from the `MultiTableSink` constructor. The option is still read there; the lower bound is enforced declaratively upstream.
- The option stays optional, type `int`, default `1`, valid range `>= 1`. No config key, default, or public API changed.

### How was this patch tested?

Reworked the replica-count tests in `MultiTableSinkWriterTest` to exercise the production path:

- `ConfigValidator.of(cfg).validate(optionRule)` rejects `0` and `-1` with an `OptionValidationException` that names the option.
- `FactoryUtil.createMultiTableSink()` rejects `0` and `-1`, wrapping the failure in a `FactoryException` whose cause is the `OptionValidationException`, confirming validation happens before sink construction.
- `1`, `4`, and an omitted option (default `1`) still create the sink.

```
./mvnw -pl seatunnel-api -am -DskipTests install
./mvnw -pl seatunnel-api -Dtest=MultiTableSinkWriterTest test
```

Both pass on JDK 21.

author: perkm
body:
## Problem

With `TZ=Europe/Zagreb`, the 0.46.2 image still runs on UTC:

    Quiet hours (no polling): 23:00-06:00 UTC

Quiet hours and the Sunday digest therefore fire an hour late in winter
and two in summer.

`main.go` embeds `time/tzdata`, but packages initialise in import-path
order (Go 1.21+), so `time/tzdata` registers after the
`github.com/…`, `golang.org/…` and `modernc.org/…` dependencies. One
of them reads the local time in its `init`, which settles `time.Local`
before the embedded data exists. The Alpine image has no zoneinfo, so
that is UTC for the life of the process. A minimal program with the
same import gets CET in the same image; the bot does not.

## Fix

`initTimeZone` loads `TZ` again at the top of `main`, after `initLog`,
before any goroutine starts. An unknown zone now logs a warning instead
of falling back to UTC silently. Unset, empty, `UTC` and absolute-path
values are left to the runtime as before. The CLAUDE.md invariant for
local time explains why the import alone is not enough.

Building with `-tags timetzdata` also fixes it, since the `time` package
then registers the data itself, but only for builds that pass the tag.
The fix in `main` covers `go build` and `go install` too, and can be tested.

## Testing

- `TestInitTimeZone` starts from the broken state (`time.Local` = UTC)
  and covers a zone name, a `:`-prefixed name, `UTC`, empty and an
  unknown zone.
- Built from this branch and run in the 0.46.2 image without zoneinfo:
  `Quiet hours (no polling): 23:00-06:00 CET`, timestamps `+01:00`.
- `task fmt` changes nothing; `go test ./...` passes except
  `internal/fetch`, which already fails on `main`: the surf v1.0.224
  bump in b8f9fb2 moves `Cache-Control` to the end of the login POST
  (`TestPostHeaderOrderMatchesChrome`,
  `TestRedirectHopMatchesChromeWireOrder`). With v0.46.2's `go.mod` it
  passes. I'll send that as a separate PR.
